author: tdebasis
body:
Closes #238.

Adds a fifth listener type, `herdr`, the counterpart of the tmux bell for agents that herdr runs. The address is `<herdr session>/<agent name>`, checked at `subscribe`.

The bell asks herdr for the agent's state instead of reading the pane:

- `working`, `blocked` (a dialog is open) and `unknown` (herdr has not placed the agent yet) are busy refusals, so the bell asks again later. A dialog is never typed into.
- `idle` and `done` have the input box read; only an empty box, or one holding only Claude Code's faint suggestion, is typed into.
- Agent kinds without an input-box reader are refused. Claude Code is the only one for now.
- A bell starting with `-` is refused, because herdr's argument parser takes it as an option and has no `--`.

## Tests

- `internal/mcpserve/notify_herdr_test.go`: a fake `herdr` on `PATH`; no live herdr is touched. Each guard was also broken on purpose and its test went red (11 of 11).
- `go test ./... -count=1` passes.
- Checked by hand against a throwaway herdr session and a throwaway agent: it held at the startup dialog, over a half-typed draft, while working, and at a permission dialog (the command was not approved), and rang when idle with an empty box.

## Docs

`docs/CLI.md` and `docs/OPERATORS.md` list the new type and its address form.

author: gabesud0
body:
From Gabriel's 3DS log and video of the opening.

**Jitter and speed (New 3DS)**
- In the video the forest flyover panned in uneven 6–10 px jumps, about 20 times a second. The log explains it: the geometry ran on core 1, where a program gets 30% of the core, at 18–30 ms a scene, with 3–10 scenes a second left out. The geometry now runs on core 2 by default.
- Engine B's drawer (the lower screen in the intro) moves from core 1's 30% share, where it drew 14–25 frames a second, to core 0, which is nearly idle during the intro. `geometry.txt` `core 1` brings back the old layout.
- The change check compares registers, palettes and OAM first, and only hashes VRAM (864 KB for engine A) when those are unchanged.
- Publishing converts and doubles the pixels in one pass, writing four texels per store.

**Sprites in the wrong places:** each drawer now draws from a copy of the registers, palettes and OAM taken when the frame was handed over, so a slow draw can't mix in the game's next frame.

**HOME / close**
- Nothing is presented while the HOME menu has the screens or while the program is closing, and pending frames are dropped. HOME and sleep are tracked separately.
- The V-blank thread exits before the buffers are freed.
- A crash during close now ends the program instead of waiting for START. That wait is why the close never finished.
- Each shutdown step is logged. If a thread won't stop, the program ends with `svcExitProcess`.
- I couldn't reproduce HOME here; the new `[apt]` / `[quit]` log lines will show what happens on hardware.

**Wide art**
- One layer can have a picture per place it was captured. The game uses the nearest one, if it's less than a screen away. The opening's sky and blue strip are one BG, and the sky picture had replaced the strip's.
- Content drawn in the bands never shows over the DS's part. This was causing the trees to pop into the ball throw.
- Bands show only while the layer is where it was drawn (±8 px), or always when marked `_loop`. This fixes Chimchar's hand showing while his layer waited off-screen.
- A window spanning x 0–255 now reaches the right edge on the wide screen. The running scene's right band was black.

**WideArt editor**
- Pictures are stored per place; a capture taken a few pixels off opens the existing picture lined up, and saving replaces it.
- New "Scrolls round all the time" checkbox (`_loop`).
- Drawing layers are kept per place.

**Tests**
- New renderer tests cover choosing pictures by place, the band rules and the window edge; the upscaler test covers the one-pass publish.
- The editor core tests cover pictures by place.
- Classic render hashes are unchanged.
- Checked on the PC runner with Gabriel's pictures: no trees in the ball throw across 400 frames, a clean slide-in, and the right band filled.

author: schrodingerzhu
body:
Add `#[kernel]` function identity and track it through elaboration, generic specialization, HIR/MIR round trips, dependency interfaces, and the final lowering environment.

Kernels can call kernels. Host code can call a kernel only when its concrete return type is `Tensor`. Ordinary host operations are rejected in kernel bodies; bindings, blocks, and conditionals retain kernel context. Methods preserve the annotation and check agreement with trait declarations. Kernel functions cannot escape as ordinary closures or host trampolines.

Final lowering uses `Env::is_kernel` when dispatching control flow and prevents emitting a kernel or launch as an ordinary host function/call. This PR introduces the boundary and context only; it does not implement kernel operations or launching. Versions remain unchanged.

Validated on Spark with `REUSSIR_ENABLE_OPENXLA=OFF`:
- Rust: core 483, syntax 61, backend 15, codegen 38 plus 22 frontend end-to-end, compiler 11 plus 25 driver and 1 debug-info, REPL 5, and LSP 12 tests passed. The existing optional backend polyffi link test is ignored.
- C++: all 78 unit tests passed.
- LLVM lit: all 636 applicable tests passed; 94 unavailable-feature/platform tests were unsupported. All 6 new kernel tests passed, including source and MIR final-lowering diagnostics, HIR/MIR round trips, imported generic specialization, and trait method metadata.
- Codegen/compiler/REPL all-target Rust compile checks passed.

Integration with #703 was tested on a temporary combined branch: 485 core tests, 39 codegen unit tests plus 22 execution tests, 24 focused lit tests, and additional imported-generic/call-boundary checks passed. The public branches remain independent. Their overlapping signature checks require a merge resolution that preserves kernel signature eligibility and applies host escape checks only to host functions. The tested resolution is saved on workstation in local branch `test/kernel-async-combined-7cc2072a` at `17664c13`.

author: kyleseaman
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** A message sent with Steer while background sub-agents run is answered as soon as the current turn ends, not after the last sub-agent finishes.

With sub-agents running, a user typed a message and sent it with the default Steer action. It showed up as a queued card (hourglass) and sat there while the children kept working, so the session looked impossible to talk to: the only live control was Stop.

## Why it matters

Steer is the composer's default, and long sub-agent waves are common. Every user who steers during the short turn that digests a wave's results gets their message parked for the rest of the wave, sometimes many minutes, without having chosen Queue. The only way out today is spotting the card's Run-now button.

## Not a goal

- Changing what Queue does: a message the sender chose to queue still waits for the wave.
- Changing the hold for anyone but the session's own human in the composer: peer `session_send`, channel, app and Jev-decided `auto` queues keep waiting.
- Any composer or button change.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

A message you send with Steer while sub-agents run now gets answered when the current turn ends, instead of waiting in the queue until every sub-agent finishes. Queue still means wait.

It used to wait because Steer only reaches a turn at that turn's next tool call. The short turn that digests a wave's results often makes none, so the turn ended without taking the message and put it back in the queue. A steer that was unavailable mid-turn landed there too. While sub-agents run, that queue lets only system messages through, so the steer waited as if the user had chosen Queue.

A composer steer that falls back to the queue now carries `meta.steer_intent`, and the sub-agent hold (`releases_past_subagent_hold` in `src/kiro_crew/dashboard/chat_utils.py`) lets it through like a system message. The mark is set in two places: the unavailable-steer fall-through in `chat_api/chat_send` (`queue_for_next_turn(steer_intent=True)` in `chat_delivery`), and the turn-end requeue in `chat_turn/steer_queue`, which reads a new per-slot `_steer_act_now` set in `state`. A hard stop in `chat_api/turn_stop` clears that set with the other per-steer maps. The drain in `chat_runner` strips the mark before writing the row. The `session` system spec (`docs/system-specs/modules/session.md`) gains a bullet for the rule.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: one new optional queue-entry meta key, read only by the sub-agent hold. Entries without it behave exactly as before.

Removes nothing: no path, key, row or validator is taken away. The hold releases more entries, never fewer.

## Tests

`test/test_queue_during_subagents.py`:
- `TestDequeueSteerIntent`: a marked entry drains past an earlier held user message, and only a literal `True` releases.

author: hjewkes
body:
TP-3026 (audio plan slice T6): adds `@titan-design/speech-vet`, tier 2, part 1. It is a TypeScript port of the text-side narration checks, with no Python and no live G2P.

## What it adds

- **Markup** (`plainText`, `g2pText`): parses `[word](/phonemes/)` overrides and `[word](=reading)` declarations. Captions get the plain text. The G2P keeps the overrides and gets the bare word for each declaration.
- **Heteronyms** (`checkReadings`, `readingOf`, `tokenDump`): the 19-word misaki table moves to `src/heteronyms/en.json` and is validated by zod at load. Each heteronym occurrence among the G2P tokens gets one of four statuses: `ok`, `fail`, `forced` or `warn`. A declaration attaches to its own occurrence.
- **lexicon.v1** (`LexiconSchema`, `loadLexicon`, `respellingsOf`): a zod schema with `term`, `spoken`, a single-token `respell`, `phonemes {misaki, ipa}` and `evidence`. It is strict, so unknown keys are refused. `loadLexicon` also upgrades the two older shapes: a flat `{term: respelling}` map, whose `_comment` key is dropped, and an unversioned `{entries}` list.
- **Respelling** (`respeller`, `generateCandidates`): whole-word, case-insensitive and idempotent, with the twelve heuristic rewrite rules.
- **Initialisms** (`spellInitialisms`, `isInitialism`): the shape-based rule. Behaviour change from the original: the built-in list of initialisms that contain a vowel now holds only general English. A product passes its own domain list through `{ spelled }`.

## Tests

There are 57 vitest cases. Every test has a comment naming the mutation it catches.

- **The 7 heteronym and override cases** keep their names and assertion counts. They run on golden misaki 0.9.4 token dumps in `src/fixtures/misaki-tokens.json`, recorded once from `KPipeline(model=False).g2p`. The sentences are synthetic.
- **The 9 lexicon cases and 8 initialism cases** keep their names and assertion counts. Invented words replace the original proper nouns.
  - The two `normalizer ...` cases cover the lexicon and initialism halves of that path. `normalize()` itself is T7.
- **Additions:**
  - candidate goldens recorded from the Python `generate_candidates`;
  - lexicon.v1 upgrade, a respelling with a space refused, and unknown keys refused;
  - the table's 19 words, with every form checked;
  - g2pText's treatment of declarations;
  - the `spelled` option.

These mutations were run by hand, and each fails the named tests:

| Mutation | Fails |
|---|---|
| A declared mismatch is ignored (`status: "ok"`), so `The show is [live](=verb) tonight.` passes | `declared reading the g2p did not choose fails` |
| An override is reported as `warn` | `override forces a heteronym reading against the g2p` |
| Stress marks are kept before pattern matching | 5 HeteronymCheck and override cases |
| A declaration is keyed by its word alone | `declared live in both readings passes`, `declaration attaches to its own occurrence` |
| A respelling may contain a space | `rejects a respelling that is not a single token` |
| The word-boundary lookbehind is dropped | `apply does not match substrings` |
| The sentence-end rule is dropped | `asap is spelled out`, `rule branches: Is it ASAP?`, `normalizer spells initialisms end to end` |

## Notes

- `zod` is a peer dependency, as repo rule R47 requires.
- This branch is rebased on speech-tts (#1569). The `## Speech` family section keeps both bullets.
- Local gates: `build`, `typecheck`, `lint`, `lint:types` and `docs:build` passed, and so did the package's 57 tests.
  - `dag:check` passed its 73 graph rules. The machine-wide lock skipped the dead-code half, so CI runs it.
  - In the full `pnpm test` run, 41 tests failed in factory shepherd/workflows and `test-affected`. These files are outside this diff.
  - The factory files pass once the agent session's `AGENT_CHAT_*` variables are unset. I could not test `test-affected` the same way, because its git-config variables are pinned by a guard.

Ids have gaps: a WAL-replay duplicate (`ON CONFLICT (record_id) DO NOTHING`) or a rolled-back insert uses up a sequence value. When `from_id - 1` was a gap, the anchor fell back to genesis and an intact first entry was reported as a break (design §1 gap 10). Reproduced on the base commit (`6ab8d993`) with a fake chain of ids 1-3, 5-7: `verify(from_id=5)` returned `verified=False, entries_checked=1, first_bad_id=5`. On this head it returns `True, 3, None`.

- **Anchor:** the `entry_hash` of the greatest id below `from_id` (`fetch_anchor_hash`), genesis when there is none.
- **Clamp:** `to_id` is clamped to the head read when the run starts, so entries appended during the run are not checked. A range past the head checks nothing.
- **Batches:** a keyset walk on the primary key (`id > :after_id AND id <= :to_id ORDER BY id ASC LIMIT :limit`), 10 000 rows by default (ticket "Technical notes"), fetched as tuples in the trigger's field order. The `IS NULL OR` placeholder is gone because the upper bound is always known now.
- `_canonical_hash` (the page check) and the tuple path share one field order, `HASHED_FIELDS`, through `_canonical_digest`.
- **3b review NIT:** `query_page` builds its time budget before it takes a read slot, so nothing runs between the take and the `try` that gives the slot back. The new regression test leaks a slot on the old code (`(1, 1) != (0, 0)`).

**Review follow-up (`6cef3c4a`):** a test pins a deleted predecessor (row `from_id - 1` removed out of band) as a break at `from_id`; 4a-ii also pins its kind, `prev_hash_mismatch`.

Hashing still runs on the event loop here, as before this slice. 4a-ii (stacked on this PR) moves it off the loop and pipelines the fetches.

body:
## Pourquoi

Suite des lots 1 (#157) et 2 (#158) : dernier angle mort de la détection des données périmées signalé comme « limite connue ».

Le moteur de preuves (`src/evidence.js`) calculait l'âge d'une observation de station avec `Math.max(0, …)`. Une station datée du futur (horloge fautive, relais falsifié ou erroné : +3 h, an 2099) pesait donc comme une mesure faite « à l'instant », donc avec le poids maximal dans le verdict brouillard.

## Ce que change cette PR

- `src/evidence.js` : une observation datée de plus d'1 min dans le futur est **ignorée** ; une dérive d'horloge de 1 min ou moins reste tolérée. Deux lignes, aucune entrée/sortie nouvelle.
- `src/reliability.js` (commentaire seulement) : la tolérance de 90 min de la Tenue pour le bloc `current` est expliquée. Ce n'est pas un seuil de péremption : sans bloc `current` valable, le moteur date le repli au **début de l'heure en cours**, donc jusqu'à 59 min. La limiter à 20 min écarterait des valeurs horaires légitimes. Aucun changement de comportement.

## Précision sur la limite annoncée au lot 2

Je citais aussi `weather-watch.js`. Vérification faite : **il rejetait déjà** une observation du futur (au-delà de 60 s). Ce n'était pas un défaut. Un test verrouille désormais ce comportement.

## Tests

- `test_evidence.js` : scénario K (observations à +3 h, +2 min, an 2099 ignorées et sans effet sur le verdict ; +30 s et −10 min retenues) + une mutation rejetée (8 régressions rejetées au total). **Rouge avant le correctif**, vert après.
- `test_weather_watch.js` : comportement existant verrouillé (futur, +30 s, −10 min, date illisible).
- `e2e43-analyse.js` (**Chromium et WebKit en CI**) : frontière réelle de la politique 15 / 60 min dans l'onglet Analyse. À **59 min** : état `AGING`, aucun motif. À **61 min** : état `STALE`, motif « Météo ancienne (1 h) ». **Rouge** avec l'ancien seuil de 90 min (vérifié en le rétablissant), vert avec 60.
- Validation locale (Chromium) : 51 tests unitaires, `e2e38`, `e2e42`, `e2e43`, `e2e45`, `e2e47`, `e2e65`, `test_relay_clock`, `relay-smoke`, syntaxe de 230 scripts, `git diff --check`.

## À noter pour la revue

`src/evidence.js` est aussi chargé par le relais (`src/relay.js`, job privilégié, en VM sans accès réseau ni stockage). Ce n'est pas un chemin sensible listé dans `AGENTS.md`, mais le changement est volontairement minimal et pur (une garde avant le calcul de poids). Le relais exécutera le nouveau code après le prochain SHA validé par la CI.

## Ce qui n'est PAS touché

`tools/relay-trust.js`, les workflows, `src/session-vault.js`, `src/sw.js`, `src/backup.js`, `src/device-storage.js`, `tools/build.js` et `encrypted/`.

author: teemow
body:
Fixes https://github.com/giantswarm/substrate/issues/442

## Problem

A request to a crashed actor waited out atenet-router's whole 30 s park budget (37 refused `ResumeActor` calls in the lab) before the caller saw the refusal, and kagent's revert of the actor waited with it.

## Root cause

`ResumeActor` refuses an actor in `ACTOR_STATE_CRASHED` with `FailedPrecondition`, the code it also answers for an actor in transition, and the router parks `FailedPrecondition`. On the line the parking is done by the atenet-router's agentgateway sidecar (`substrateIngress`, `retryable_while_parked`), not only by the Go resumer. A crashed actor leaves `CRASHED` only through an explicit `RevertActor` or `DeleteActor` (a crash the control plane recovers by itself it recovers within the call, answering `Unavailable`), so no retry outlives the refusal.

## Solution

- The refusal of a `CRASHED` actor carries an AIP-193 `ErrorInfo`: domain `substrate.dev`, reason `ACTOR_CRASHED`, metadata `resumable: "false"`. Code and message are unchanged. `apierror.NotResumable` builds it, `apierror.FromError` keeps it on the wire, `apierror.IsNotResumable` reads it.
- The line's agentgateway (2.3.0 and later, the chart pins 2.4.0) already answers a refusal carrying this directive at once (agentgateway-upstream ledger `a-resume-refusal-marked-not-resumable-is-answered-at-once.md`); this is its producer for a crashed actor. The Go resumer honors the same directive, so both dataplanes share one contract.
- kagent (https://github.com/giantswarm/kagent-upstream/pull/585) keeps working: a2a-go maps a gRPC status whose ErrorInfo reason it does not know to `ErrInternalError`, which kagent's gateway reads as a send its runtime did not accept, and its `AwaitRuntime` reverts and resumes the actor; its own `ResumeActor` calls still see `FailedPrecondition`.
- Docs: `docs/request-parking.md`, the 1.11.2 to 1.11.3 entry of `docs/upgrade.md`; ledger `fork/ateapi-crashed-actor-refusal-not-resumable.md`. The first commit is a `git cherry-pick -x` of the upstream-ready commit on `upstream/ateapi-crashed-actor-not-resumable`. Rebase-merge.

Supersedes https://github.com/giantswarm/substrate/pull/443, which fixed only the Go resumer, not on the line's live path.

## Proof

- `TestEnsureWorkerAssigned_RejectsNonResumableStates`: only `CRASHED` is marked. `TestActorResumer_NotResumableRefusalIsNotParked`: a marked refusal fails after 1 call, an unmarked one parks for 30 s / 37 calls. `TestServerInterceptorsKeepNotResumable`, `TestNotResumable`, `TestIsNotResumable`.
- Without the fix the resumer case fails with `the resume took 30s` and `resume attempts = 37, want 1`, the controlapi case with `refusal marked not resumable = false, want true`.
- `go test` of `internal/apierror`, `internal/ateinterceptors`, `cmd/atenet/...` and the controlapi resume tests pass on this branch and on the upstream-ready branch; `golangci-lint` clean on the upstream-ready branch.
- Lab proof (kind agentlab, agent-platform 4.133.0, Substrate 1.11.2, ate-api-server swapped for this branch's build `dev-442-4ffa6956c`). A session remembers a code word and suspends. The next turn's gVisor sandbox is SIGKILLed 0.4 s after its `runsc restore` returns: the Actor is `CRASHED` and that turn fails in about 1 s. The turn after it is timed, and the session's `ResumeActor` calls are counted in ate-api-server's RPC log:

  | kagent | ate-api-server | next turn | `ResumeActor` by atenet-router |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1.11.5 | 1.11.2 | 30.4 s | 36 refused (+1 OK before the crash) |
  | 1.11.5 | this branch | 0.47 s | 1 refused (+1 OK before the crash) |
  | 1.11.6-rc.3 | this branch | 1.9 s, answers the code word | none refused |

## Summary

- When MindRoom creates a managed room, a non-empty `rooms.<key>.description` is now used as the Matrix topic, and the topic-generation LLM call is skipped.
- `ensure_room_has_topic` follows the same rule when it fills in a missing topic for an existing managed room.
- Rooms without a description keep the AI-generated topic. Rooms that already have a topic are never changed, so editing `description` later does not overwrite a topic.
- The `RoomConfig.description` field description, `docs/rooms.md`, the code map, the dashboard schema snapshot, and the regenerated `mindroom-docs` skill references are updated to match.

## Why

A config with 16 described rooms made 16 LLM calls (1-3 s each) before the rooms existed, and the topics they produced ignored the descriptions the operator had written.

## Testing

- New tests in `tests/test_topic_generator.py`:
  - `_ensure_room_exists` with a description creates the room with the trimmed description as its topic and makes no LLM call; with an empty description it uses the AI topic.
  - `ensure_room_has_topic` on a room without a topic writes the configured description and makes no LLM call.
- `uv run pytest tests/test_topic_generator.py tests/test_managed_room_alias_adoption.py tests/test_room_reconciliation_snapshot.py tests/test_team_room_updates.py tests/test_e2ee_phase2.py tests/test_managed_avatars.py tests/test_matrix_room_access.py tests/test_system_usage_callers.py tests/test_config_schema.py tests/test_config_reload.py --no-cov`: 263 passed, 3 skipped.
- `uv run pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

Use configured room descriptions as Matrix topics and fall back to AI generation only when no description is provided.

New Features:
- Use a room's configured, trimmed description as the Matrix topic for new managed rooms and existing rooms missing a topic.
- Retain AI topic generation for rooms without descriptions while preserving existing topics.

Enhancements:

- Start newly created dashboard rooms with an empty description rather than a placeholder value.

Documentation:
- Update room-management documentation, code maps, generated documentation references, and schema metadata for the new topic behavior.

Tests:

author: danemadsen
body:
## Summary
This PR improves the node rename editor (F2) by extracting rename cleanup logic into a dedicated method and fixing focus handling to prevent the editor from reopening immediately after pressing Enter or Escape.

## Key Changes
- **Extract `stop_renaming()` method**: Created a new private method that properly cleans up both `renaming` state and `rename_text`, replacing direct assignments throughout the codebase
- **Fix focus handling**: Modified the rename overlay to only request focus if the text field hasn't just lost focus (which happens when Enter or Escape is pressed), preventing the editor from immediately reopening
- **Add unique ID to TextEdit**: Assigned a stable ID to the rename text field based on the node ID to improve egui's focus tracking
- **Add comprehensive test**: Implemented `the_name_editor_takes_enter_and_escape()` test that verifies:
  - Enter key accepts the new name and closes the editor
  - Escape key closes the editor without applying changes
  - Clicking elsewhere closes the editor and clears the text buffer
  - Subsequent rename operations start fresh with the node's original name
  - `reset()` properly cleans up rename state

## Implementation Details
The key fix prevents focus thrashing by checking `response.lost_focus()` before calling `response.request_focus()`. This allows the editor to close cleanly when the user presses Enter or Escape, while still maintaining focus during normal typing.

author: pedronavhur
body:
## Summary

Stacked layers had turned into one commit each: `build_layers.sh` made one commit per layer, the policy aimed layers below 500 weighted, and every commit needed the full test gate. This PR makes commits the small unit and layers the reviewable one.

```diff
 commit   one step
+         ≤ 300 weighted / 600 raw, or a Size-Exception: <reason> trailer
+         gate: format, lint, typecheck on changed files
 layer    one reviewable purpose
-         target < 500 weighted, one commit
+         aim 400–1000 weighted, several commits; under 300 needs a reason
+         gate: format, lint, typecheck on each commit; tests deferred to the top
 stack    ≤ 5 layers
+         usually 2–4; work under the PR ceilings ships as one PR
+         gate: full pre-commit once, on the last layer's tip
```

```diff
 diff_budget.py BASE HEAD
+  --per-commit          each commit vs its parent, exit 2 over 300/600
 build_layers.sh
+  "# commit: SUBJECT"   manifest sections → several commits per layer (ignored-but-tracked files included)
 layer_gates.sh
+  typecheck, lint, format on every commit inside a layer (commits=OK|FAIL|none)
+  tests once on the top layer vs the stack base; --tests-each for per-layer runs
 refresh_stack.py
+  per-layer commit check (commit-over → exit 2), "small" under 300, commit count in PR size line
 split-stacked-prs/SKILL.md
+  cut layers at commit boundaries when the source's commits are already ordered and small
 lib.sh
~  layer_names without find -printf (BSD find on macOS lacked it)
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** a layer built from a manifest is always one commit, and on macOS `build_layers.sh` exits with `find: -printf: unknown primary or operator`.
  **After:** `test_build_layers` builds `01-domain` as two commits (`feat: add the types`, `feat: add the domain`) and the top tree equals the source; a section that changes nothing stops the build.
- `test_diff_budget` (per-commit): two 200-line commits pass though the range totals 400; a 301-line commit fails; a `Size-Exception` trailer exempts; merges are skipped.
- `test_refresh_stack`: a 500-line single-commit layer → `commit-over`, exit 2; the same layer as two commits passes; a 100-line layer shows `small` and passes.
- `test_build_layers`: a file the source force-added past `.gitignore` builds inside a commit section (the old script exits with "The following paths are ignored").
- `test_layer_gates` (needs bash 4): a 3-layer stack runs tests once, `s-03-c` against `main`, and lower layers report `tests=deferred`; `--tests-each` runs `01-a`←`main`, `02-b`←`01-a`, `03-c`←`02-b`. Typecheck runs on `01-a`'s middle commit and its tip; a broken middle commit, or a broken commit on a branch merged into a layer, fails the layer with `commits=FAIL` while its tip passes.
- Every suite in the README passes on macOS (36 tests in split-stacked-prs, with bash 5.3 on PATH) and split-stacked-prs passes on devbox at c94f33f. This branch measures itself: 11 commits, largest 89 weighted, 339 total.
- Review loop: 4 rounds (GPT-6.1 Sol high reviewing, Haiku 5.5 high fixing); the loop's comment below lists findings and outcomes.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Revert restores the old policy and scripts. Layer gates now run typecheck and lint once per commit inside a layer, so a layer of N commits costs N typechecks instead of one. `bin/sync` must run on each host to install the new instructions.

**Blast Radius:** stacks

Stacks open today whose layers are single commits over 300 weighted will fail `refresh_stack.py` with exit 2 on their next fix round, until those commits are split or carry a `Size-Exception` trailer. Retirement-only commits stay exempt.

author: postazure
body:
Hovering a recipe now shows Blizzard's normal recipe tooltip and, beside it, the real item it makes in `GameTooltip`. Our only additions are the reagent cost and profit lines (with Auctionator). The compare is always on. The probe reports every new API this uses.

## What players see

Left to right: **recipe list, recipe tooltip, item, equipped**. The tops line up, with the "Equipped" header above the compare. Nothing covers the recipe list.

- **Recipe tooltip** (our own tooltip, the "recipe box"): Blizzard's normal recipe tooltip, made by `SetTrainerService` on our tooltip. With Auctionator, it ends with:
  - **Reagents**: the cost of one craft, plus "(makes N)" when it makes more than one.
  - **Profit**: "Profit: +X after AH cut (5%)". That's auction price x number made x 0.95, minus reagents. Green "+" or red "-".
  - Gray text when a price is missing. No profit for items that bind on pickup.
- **Item** (`GameTooltip`): switched to the item with `SetHyperlink`. It's a normal item tooltip, so Blizzard's compare, its sell price, and Auctionator's and Disenchantry's item lines show by themselves.
- **Compare**: always on. No Shift needed, whatever "Always compare items" says. It sits right of the item, and only goes left of the recipe tooltip when the screen has no room.
  - If Blizzard starts its compare by itself, we only move it, and we move it back whenever Blizzard places it again.
  - After a modifier key changes, we check again a frame later, so a compare Blizzard hides on Shift release comes back.
  - The header reads "Equipped".
- Recipes with no item (enchants) keep Blizzard's tooltip untouched.
- Removed at the owner's request:
  - Our item level and stat lines. Blizzard's compare shows them.
  - Cost to learn. The trainer window shows it.
  - Our auction and vendor price lines. The item tooltip shows them.

## How reagents are found

- The recipe's spell id comes from `C_TooltipInfo.GetTrainerService(index)`. That function is confirmed present.
- The reagents come from `C_TradeSkillUI.GetRecipeSchematic(spellID, false)`, required slots only. Auctionator 341 calls it on Forever, so it likely exists. **Unknown:** whether it works for recipes not learned yet.
- Each reagent is priced like Auctionator's own crafting info: the merchant price if known, else the auction price.

## Code

- `src/compareTooltips.ts`: re-owns `GameTooltip` with `ANCHOR_NONE`, calls `SetHyperlink`, fills the recipe box with `SetTrainerService` plus our lines, places everything with tops aligned, and always shows the compare. If the box can't be made, our lines go under the item.
- `src/main.ts`: on `MODIFIER_STATE_CHANGED`, refresh the compare one frame later.
- `src/recipes.ts` (new), `src/prices.ts` (new): reagents, reagent cost, profit, money format.
- `src/tooltip.ts`: removed (our item level and stat lines).
- `src/trainerUI.ts`: post-hook on `TooltipComparisonManager.AnchorShoppingTooltips`, if present.
- `types/wow-forever.d.ts`: every new API is typed as possibly undefined, with its source noted. The Shift and CVar helpers are removed.
- `CLAUDE.md` product and taint rules are updated.
- Docs: README, CHANGELOG (Unreleased), HOW-IT-WORKS, DEVELOPMENT, CURSEFORGE, TEST-CHECKLIST, CurseForge description. None mention Auctionator yet: no compatibility claims until it's tested in game.
- `main` is merged in. The new CurseForge pitch from #3 is kept and updated for these tooltips.
- Not done yet: `compare.ts` still picks the "weaker" ring or weapon. That choice no longer shows anywhere. It can be trimmed once this layout is confirmed in game.

## Testing

- Tested here: `npm test` passes (main 111 checks, fallback 29).
  - There are fewer checks than before because our item level and stat lines are gone.
  - New checks cover: Blizzard's recipe tooltip in the box, the item in `GameTooltip`, `ANCHOR_NONE`, tops aligned, the compare showing without Shift, the compare coming back a frame after a key change, the compare to the right (and flipping when there's no room), moving Blizzard's compare back after it re-anchors, keeping a compare Blizzard started itself, lines under the item without a box, reagents, profit and loss.
  - Each new check was broken once to prove it can fail.
- Needs an in-game check:
  - Layout and alignment for gear, non-gear and an enchant.
  - Whether the "Equipped" header sits above the compare.
  - Whether the compare stays up while you press and release Shift.
  - Auctionator and Disenchantry lines on the item.
  - Reagents and Profit for recipes you haven't learned. If they're missing, paste `/tcprobe` then `/tcprobe show`.
  - Train still works.

author: ishiland
body:
## Summary

The Anthropic provider could only reach Anthropic's own API, so teams that buy Claude through a cloud platform or route it through a gateway couldn't use it. `ANTHROPIC_PLATFORM` now picks where requests go:

- `anthropic` (default): Anthropic's API, or a gateway or proxy that speaks the Messages API when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is set.
- `foundry`: Microsoft Foundry.
- `bedrock`: Amazon Bedrock.
- `vertex`: Google Vertex AI.

`get_anthropic_client()` in `llm_loop.py` is now the only place a Claude client gets built. The tool loop, streamed chat and structured output all go through it, and a test fails if another construction site shows up. The request fields are unchanged on every platform, prompt caching included. Bedrock and Vertex accept `cache_control`, and a test checks that it survives the SDK's Bedrock request translation.

Provider resolution (`LLM_PROVIDER`'s default and the metadata fallback), chat availability, admin AI status and the AI probe now ask `anthropic_configured()`. A cloud platform with its settings counts as configured without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. On Foundry, Bedrock and Vertex the light model falls back to `LLM_MODEL`, the same way `OPENAI_MODEL_LIGHT` falls back to `OPENAI_MODEL`. Those platforms use deployment names, inference-profile IDs or Vertex IDs, so the hardcoded Haiku name would 404. The new `LLM_MODEL_LIGHT` overrides it on any platform.

Like the API keys, these settings are environment-only. They aren't persistent settings, nothing in the admin UI can change where a Claude credential goes, and the OpenAPI schema doesn't change.

### Environment variables per platform

| Platform | Variables | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| all | `ANTHROPIC_PLATFORM`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_MODEL_LIGHT` | `LLM_MODEL` must be the platform's model ID |
| anthropic | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | base URL is optional, for gateways |
| foundry | `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_RESOURCE` | both required; the SDK's own names |
| bedrock | `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_AWS_REGION` (required), then `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_API_KEY`, or `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` + `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, or neither for the AWS default chain | see below |
| vertex | `CLOUD_ML_REGION`, `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | region and project required; the SDK's own names; credentials come from Application Default Credentials |

All of them are in both Compose `x-ai-env` anchors in the parse-safe `${VAR:-}` form, and they're documented in `.env.example`. `EGRESS.md` gets a row for the new destinations.

### Why Bedrock doesn't use the AWS_* names

The SDK's own names would break Bedrock in two ways:

- With `STORAGE_PROVIDER=s3`, the API and worker export the S3 storage keys and region as `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` for GDAL (`configure_gdal_s3_env`). Plain `AWS_*` names for Bedrock would collide with them in both directions: Bedrock could sign with the MinIO key, and a Bedrock `AWS_REGION` would change GDAL's S3 region.
- Compose passes an unset variable as a blank string, and the SDK treats a blank `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` as a key.

Bedrock's credentials and region are kept separate from the S3 storage ones and always passed to the client explicitly, so the region exported for storage never reaches it. The AWS default chain (instance, task or IRSA role) still works. It's refused while storage holds a static `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, because the chain reads the exported key before any role. In that case, and for a half-set key pair, the readiness checks report Claude as not configured and the client error names what to set. Readiness and the client share one credential-selection function, so they can't disagree.

For the same blank-string reason, the default platform now passes `https://api.anthropic.com` to the SDK when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is unset. Otherwise the SDK would read Compose's blank value as the URL. The API key is passed explicitly in both cases, so this doesn't change which credentials the SDK uses.

### Redirects

Every Claude client now gets the SDK's default httpx client with `follow_redirects=False`, on the default platform too. A Messages endpoint has no reason to answer with a 3xx, and following one could carry `x-api-key` or `api-key` to another origin. `make_safe_client()` isn't used here because it refuses private addresses, and an in-network gateway is the main reason to set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. A redirect now fails the request with an `APIStatusError`.

### Settings page key status (#3059)

`GET /settings/api-key-status/` now takes `anthropic_configured` from the same readiness check the AI routes use, and it adds `anthropic_platform`. On a cloud platform, the AI settings tab shows "Claude on Amazon Bedrock: configured" (or Microsoft Foundry, Google Vertex AI) where it used to show `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not set`. On Anthropic's API the line is unchanged. Older SDK clients ignore the extra field. The response carries no reason text, only the boolean and the platform name. The two new strings are in all five locales, and the platform names stay in English because they're product names.

### Default models (#3063)

The chat default moves from `claude-sonnet-5` to `claude-sonnet-5-5`, and the light default from `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` to `claude-haiku-5-5`. The change covers `ClaudeSettings.llm_model`, `llm_model_default()`, both Compose `LLM_MODEL` fallbacks, `.env.example`, the pinned tests, the `e2e/dataset-chat.spec.ts` stub, and the admin model example (API description and UI placeholder), which used to name the retired `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`. Foundry, Bedrock and Vertex still fall back to `LLM_MODEL` for the light model. Bedrock and Vertex have no default model, since neither serves Anthropic's model names. They need `LLM_MODEL` in the environment or a model set in the admin UI. Without either, chat availability, the chat route (503), admin AI status and the probe report Claude as not configured, and the light model follows whichever chat model is set. Foundry deployments can carry the model's own name, so Foundry keeps the default. To tell unset from default, `LLM_MODEL` is optional in the settings (blank or unset means `claude-sonnet-5-5` on Anthropic's API and Foundry), and Compose passes it as `${LLM_MODEL:-}` instead of hard-coding the default. The key-status response covers credentials only, and its description says so. The product docs on docs.getgeolens.com need the same change in that repository.

### Logging

The SDK logs request options, headers included, at DEBUG. Foundry sends its key in an `api-key` header, and `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` printed it through the real logging pipeline. `api-key` is now on the log redaction list. A test runs a mocked request on each platform through `setup_logging()` at DEBUG and checks that no credential appears.

## Related issue

Fixes #3055
Closes #3059
Closes #3063

## Area

- [x] Backend (API, services, models)
- [x] Frontend (UI, components, hooks)
- [x] Infrastructure (Docker, nginx)
- [ ] Tiles / Rendering
- [ ] Auth / Permissions
- [ ] Import / Ingestion
- [ ] OGC / Standards
- [x] Docs / Config

## Schema, API and config impact

- No migration. One additive API change: `ApiKeyStatusResponse` gains a required `anthropic_platform` enum, and `anthropic_configured` now follows the selected platform. `AIStatusResponse.model`'s example changes too. author: metaframework-dispatch-bot[bot]
body:
## TL;DR

- **Grades the node majors pinned *outside* the test matrix.** `lint`, `build` and `publish` each set `node-version:` to a bare literal that no gate could see — the condition #49 reports. Every pinned major must now equal `ARG NODE_IMAGE`'s, read off the Dockerfile.
- **#49's three open questions are settled in the code and argued in the comments**: strict equality (not `>=`), a closed partition (not a `length >= 1` floor), and `npmpublish.yaml` **in** scope.
- **One correction to the ticket, with evidence**: this is a *divergence* gate, not an end-of-life gate. No version of this assertion would have been red on the state #49's summary line describes.
- **Cut from `main`, not stacked on #47 as the briefing suggested** — measured clean against it, and the gate is green on the merged tree.
- 14 mutants: 11 killed by name, 3 that must stay green do. Full suite 197/197.

## The three things #49 deliberately left open

**1. Strict equality, not `>=`.** `>=` would permit `build` and `publish` to produce and ship the artifact on a newer interpreter than production runs, while catching strictly less than equality. Equality states one invariant — *every node major in CI outside the matrix is the runtime's* — and forces the Dockerfile and the workflows to move together, which is the forcing function #49 says was missing. Mutant **M2** (a pin moved *ahead* of the runtime) is the case `>=` passes and this catches.

The cost is real and is stated in the test: you cannot express "lint on a newer major than prod" without editing the test. That is deliberate — editing it is the only sanctioned exemption.

**2. The reachability control is a closed partition, not a floor.** `pinned.length >= 1`, which the ticket sketched, passes a **new** pin the reader cannot see — which is the regression this block exists to prevent. Instead `classify()` sorts every `node-version` / `node-version-file` line into four buckets and the test asserts the fourth is empty, per file, by name:

| bucket | examples | treatment |
|---|---|---|
| graded | `24`, `'24'`, `24.x`, `24.1.0`, with or without a trailing `#` comment | major extracted, compared |
| matrix-ref | `${{ matrix.node-version }}` | the matrix's job, graded above |
| matrix-list | `[24, 26]` | the matrix itself |
| **ungraded** | `node-version-file: .nvmrc`, `lts/*`, `latest`, `${{ env.NODE }}` | **asserted empty** |

Every ungraded form is a *working pin* that sets the interpreter and tells the gate nothing. A form nobody anticipated lands there and fails by name instead of going quietly uncounted.

**3. `npmpublish.yaml` is in scope.** The ticket wondered about leaving it out because `tsconfig.json` pins `target: es6` and `lib: ["es2015"]` — verified, both true. That makes the publish pin *lower risk*, not *unwatched*; excluding it would preserve exactly one third of the condition the ticket describes.

## Correction to the ticket's framing

**This is a divergence gate, not an end-of-life gate**, and the difference changes what to expect of it. Measured rather than reasoned:

- `git log -S'ARG NODE_IMAGE' -- Dockerfile` returns exactly **one** commit on `main` (`3cf9171`, `node:20-slim`).
- The CI literals have been `20` since `f819dd0`.
- The 20 → 24 move lives only on #47's branch.

So at the state #49's summary line describes — "lint/build/publish sat on EOL node 20 unwatched" — the literals and the runtime **agreed**, and both `>=` and `==` are green on it. No assertion comparing CI pins to the Dockerfile can know the Dockerfile is itself EOL. What this gate does catch is the **next** bump leaving a pin behind, which is the state #44 would have created in three jobs at once had it not been spotted by hand. That is still worth having; it just is not what the headline says.

## What review caught, and what changed

The first draft stayed green on four paths to exactly the condition this exists to catch. Each was reproduced, and each is now closed:

- **`node-version-file: .nvmrc` was invisible** to a `/node-version:/` scan — different key, never even counted. Both jobs could stop being graded with everything green.
- **`${{ env.NODE }}` was accepted as "the matrix's job".** The matrix-ref bucket is now anchored on `matrix.` specifically; any other interpolation is ungraded and red.
- **The workflow list was a hardcoded pair**, so a brand-new workflow pinning node 18 was unseen — #49's own scope bug, one level up, with an `expect(files.length).toBe(2)` beside it that checked a constant against itself. The directory is globbed now.
- **The vacuity guard sat in a sibling `it()`**, so `jest -t` on the equality test read green against zero pins. It is inside that test now.

Three *legitimate* forms the first draft rejected are now **graded** rather than refused: `'20'` (the quoted form `actions/setup-node`'s own README uses), `20.x`, and a correct pin carrying a trailing comment. Failures now name the file, the line and the offending text instead of printing `Expected: 4 / Received: 3`.

## Mutation round — 14 mutants, every one confirmed applied, control green, tree restored

**11 killed, each by its specifically named test:**

| mutant | killed by |
|---|---|
| M1 lint `20` → `19` (stale) | equality |
| M2 lint `20` → `24` (ahead — **`>=` would pass**) | equality |
| M3 `ARG` `20` → `24` (runtime moves alone) | equality |
| M5 quoted and wrong, `'19'` | equality |
| M8 `19.x` | equality |
| M9 `node-version-file: .nvmrc` | partition |
| M10 `${{ env.LINT_NODE }}` | partition |
| M11 `lts/*` | partition |
| M12 a NEW workflow pinning `18` | equality |
| M13 npmpublish `20` → `22` | equality (proves the 2nd file is read) |
| M14 every pin interpolated away | **vacuity guard, `0 >= 1`** |

**3 that must stay GREEN, and do** — the false positives review caught: M4 `'20'`, M6 `20 # keep in sync with the Dockerfile ARG`, M7 `20.x`.

**M14 is #49's second Done-when driven to failure by hand.** With no graded pin anywhere the equality loop iterates zero times and passes; the `>= 1` line — now inside that same test — is what turns it into a failure.

## Base choice: `main`, not stacked on #47

The briefing said to stack this on `claude/44-bump-node-image`. I cut from `main` instead, having measured rather than assumed:

- `git merge-tree` reports this branch **clean** against `claude/44-bump-node-image` and against #46, despite both branches editing this same spec file — the hunks are disjoint (#47's edit is a comment block at lines 142–153; this appends a new `describe`).
- I built the merged tree into a throwaway worktree and ran the gate on it: **12/12 green**, with `ARG NODE_IMAGE=node:24-slim`, all three pins at `24`, matrix `[24, 26]`. So the gate survives #47 in either merge order.
- It *does* report a conflict against **#45** on `CHANGELOG.md`, `__tests__/deploy-docs.spec.ts` and `deployment/README.md` — pre-existing, none of them touched here, and already on the board as the one resolve owed.

Stacking would therefore have bought an ordering constraint in a repo that already has four open PRs and nothing else.

## What Tom may want to overrule

1. **Strict equality has no escape hatch.** If you ever want a job deliberately on a newer major, it is a test edit. I think that is right — the natural workarounds (quoting, `.x`, `node-version-file`) are now respectively graded and red — but it is a real constraint.
2. **This block lives in `node-matrix-gate.spec.ts`**, whose name is about the matrix. #49 prescribed "one assertion in the existing file, reusing the helper it already has", and jest's `testRegex` matches every `.ts` under `__tests__/`, so a shared helper module cannot live there without being run as an empty suite. Splitting the file later is cheap; duplicating the Dockerfile reader would not be.
3. **`Closes #49`**, not `Refs` — both Done-when bullets are satisfied by this merge, unlike #48's.

author: andrescmg06-hue
body:
## Qué cambia

Cierra B-05. El panel canjeaba el refresh token **solo al cargar**: a los 15 minutos todas sus llamadas daban 401 y la campana mostraba «ninguna sin leer» aunque hubiera alertas (el sondeo tragaba el error).

- `AuthContext` renueva el access token un minuto antes de caducar y al volver a una pestaña dormida, con **una sola renovación en vuelo** (el refresh token rota y es de un solo uso).
- 401 al renovar → cierra la sesión local; fallo de red, 5xx o 429 → reintenta a los 30 s sin echar al tutor.
- Una renovación que termina tras cerrar sesión no la reabre y revoca su token nuevo.
- `parseJsonOrThrow` lanza `ApiError` (mismo mensaje) para distinguir 401 de un fallo de red.
- Sin cambios de backend, rutas ni paneles.

author: szewai
body:
#### ac49d112208f619fb92ce39b2f11fb2d2a5b5cbd 
_drawPagesToPDFSynchronouslyForTesting returns nil when nothing is registered to wait for
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=327617
rdar://190068101

Reviewed by NOBODY (OOPS!).

_drawPagesToPDFSynchronouslyForTesting blocks the main thread by calling PendingSnapshotDrawing::wait() with the reply
ID that WebPageProxy::drawPagesToPDF returns. wait() only blocks if a PendingSnapshotDrawing was registered for that
reply ID, and drawPagesToPDF only registered one PendingSnapshotDrawing on the remote snapshotting path, outside a DOM
print operation.

Everywhere else, wait() returned immediately and the SPI returned nil before the drawing came back:
- Without remote snapshotting, the web process draws the PDF and replies with it, but nothing was registered for the
reply.
- During a DOM print operation (window.print()), the remote snapshotting path returned before registering the drawing.

This patch makes the SPI work by registering the drawing in both cases. Without remote snapshotting it waits for
the web process's reply, as drawToPDFiOS and drawToImage already do on iOS. Waiting for a web process reply this way
needs DrawPagesToPDF and DrawPagesToPDFDuringDOMPrintOperation to be declared ReplyCanDispatchOutOfOrder, as
DrawRectToImage, DrawToPDFiOS and DrawToImage already are. Mac printing (WKPrintingView) does not wait on
PendingSnapshotDrawing, so it is not affected.

Tests: Printing.DrawPagesToPDFSynchronously
       Printing.DrawPagesToPDFSynchronouslyDuringDOMPrint
       SiteIsolation.DrawPagesToPDFSynchronouslyDuringDOMPrintIncludesCrossSiteFrames

* Tools/TestWebKitAPI/Tests/WebKit/WKWebView/SiteIsolation.mm:

author: dbaggott
body:
Resolves https://github.com/dbaggott/claude-plugins/issues/266

`coding-practices` is now a rule index: every rule has a stable ID and one or two sentences, grouped by when it applies (every change, security, naming, comments, agent-facing prose, logging, verification, work sizing). The long form lives in three references, each linked from its group with the trigger for opening it, and no reference links to another.

## Word counts (`wc -w`)

| File | Words |
| --- | --- |
| `SKILL.md` at `1239f78` (before) | 4,198 |
| `SKILL.md` (after, whole file) | 1,623 |
| `SKILL.md` (after, body below the frontmatter) | 1,518 |
| `references/comments.md` | 1,432 |
| `references/agent-prose.md` | 459 |
| `references/design.md` | 844 |

The body sits just over 1,500 after the review pass below put back the N3 naming example, a positive destination on E9, and an ID on the security fix-now rule. I stopped trimming there: the pass before it was already taking one-clause whys, and the next cuts come out of the rules themselves. Pushing back on the target by that margin, per chat.

## Every rule at `1239f78`, and where it went

| Was | Now |
| --- | --- |
| Design and clarity over expediency | E1 |
| Security: parameterize, quote shell args, trust boundary, secrets, safe API, fix now | S1–S6 |
| Keep code DRY; two abstraction vices; unification vs generalization-on-spec | E5, argued in `design.md` |
| Who owns this decision | E2 |
| Degenerate case: derive, don't fork | E4 |
| Rule of three | **Dropped** (pre-approved). Its "pressure-test the shape against every known instance" clause stays under E5 in `design.md` |
| Names do the work; what-it-is over how-it's-used; dominant-meaning collision | N1, N2, N3. The N3 collision example stays in the body in one line; the N2 example is not carried |
| Write the why, not a restatement | C1 |
| The comment bar | C preamble |
| What stays: current constraint, provenance markers | C2 |
| Enforceable > prose > nothing | C3 |
| History; another file's conclusions; transient state; identifier restatement; confirmation; implausible defence; warning about what breaks (with the test-pins-it litmus); rationale on the definition; specific value; count of a list (with the subset case) | C4–C13 |
| Executor/editor test; same argument twice; inverse of a condition; a read an earlier step could carry; branch for an impossible state | P1–P5 |
| Emphasis is a budget | **Dropped as a budget** (pre-approved); replaced by C15, a severity test |
| Never let a cross-reference name the glyph | C16 |
| One-time setup doesn't belong in the repo | E9 |
| Logging: framework not print; product carve-out; one event; no sensitive data; WARN actionable | L1–L5; L1 and L2 argued in `design.md` |
| WARN / ERROR / FATAL definitions | **Dropped** (pre-approved) |
| Smell: unverified API | V3 (stated once; the "Verify what you don't know" bullet and the Context7 section fold into it) |
| Smell: silencing an error | E8 |
| Smell: claiming a UI change works unopened | V4 |
| Smell: forwarding wrapper | E6 |
| Smell: poll loop without deadline | E7 |
| Smell: removal complete after a name-only grep | V6 |
| Smell: documenting a non-feature | C14 |
| Read before changing; say "I haven't verified" | V1, V2 |
| Use Context7 | **Dropped** (pre-approved); surviving clause is V3 |
| No human time estimates | W1 |

Added, both pre-approved in the issue: **E3** testability as a design signal, paired with E2; **V5** a changed test assertion needs a stated reason.

## Outside the issue's acceptance criteria

- The always-on "Verify before asserting" rule in `dnbg-workflow` also named Context7. It now says "fetch current docs", with its own fragment under `changelog.d/dnbg-workflow/`. Asked for in chat.
- The reference-reachability test in `tests/coupling.bats` enumerated only `dnbg-workflow` skills, so the new references were uncovered. Its list now carries the plugin. A first attempt at sweeping every skill with a `references/` directory failed on `issue-workflow`, whose references are reached from other skills, so the enumeration stays and says why.
- The README's skill row for `coding-practices` named "the smells to stop on", a section that no longer exists.

## Self-review

`/code-review` on the branch returned nine findings. Applied: the V3 wording had dropped the standard-library exemption the old text carried (restored); "cite the ID instead of restating the rule" would have left an author without the skill nothing to act on (a finding now cites the ID and says what to change); the pointer lines promised an example for every case when some have none (now "the long form"); the design reference labelled its logging half L2 when it carries L1 too; E9 kept only the prohibition and lost where repeatable setup does go; the security fix-now sentence had no ID (S6); the N3 example was gone with nowhere to land. The IDs the references cite were enforced by nothing, so `tests/coupling.bats` now checks that every ID cited in a reference is defined exactly once in the body, verified to fail on a citation of an undefined ID and on a duplicated definition.

Declined: dropping the contents list in `comments.md`, which is an acceptance criterion of the issue; and restoring the WARN/ERROR/FATAL ladder, a pre-approved drop. A third, splitting logging out of `design.md` into its own file, is the issue's stated layout and I left it.

## Acceptance checks run

- `grep -rn -i context7 dnbg-practices/` and the same over `dnbg-workflow/`: nothing.
- `grep -l 'references/' dnbg-practices/skills/coding-practices/references/*.md`: nothing.
- `grep -i verif` on the body: the frontmatter description and V3 only.
- `comments.md` is over 100 lines and opens with a contents list; the other two are under.
- `bats tests/`, shellcheck, the JSON checks, `claude plugin validate --strict` (root and `dnbg-practices`), actionlint, and `check-render.sh` all pass. The reachability test was also run against a scratch copy with one pointer removed, and it reported that one file.

## Follow-up, not runnable at merge

After the next day of orchestrated runs, read the usage report for the skill's share and for whether the references appear in author sessions that touched comments or agent-facing prose.

body:
Grants `statuses: write` to the repo-hygiene job so `rmartz/repo-hygiene-action` can post one `repo-hygiene / <check>` commit status per check. Without it, every run logs "Could not post per-check statuses (HTTP 403)" and only the overall result is reported.

The action has posted per-check statuses by default since v3.2.0. Its README documents granting `statuses: write` as the standard setup; the alternative, `statuses: false`, would only hide the warning. The change widens the workflow token's permissions by that single scope.

author: haliphax
body:
Closes #453

## Root cause

When a steering message is delivered to a session that has an active tool loop, it takes the steer-channel split path: `session_steer` (and inline subagent-result / OOB delivery) calls `pushSteer()`, and the tool loop drains the channel mid-loop via `model.pushSteerMessage()`. That path only pushed the message into the in-memory model conversation:

- **No transcript write** — the steer never reached `transcript_messages`, so it was absent from persisted history and from context assembly on subsequent turns.
- **No log entry** — the only trace was a `debug`-level line without the message content plus an audit row with outcome `injected`; the message itself never appeared in the daemon logs.

The fallback path (no active loop) was unaffected because `runSessionModelTurn` appends the user turn to the transcript as usual.

## Fix

In `runToolLoop`'s mid-loop steer-injection step (`packages/daemon/src/sessions/tool-loop.ts`), each drained steer now also:

1. emits an `info`-level log (`"steering message injected into active tool loop"`) with the session ID and full message content, and
2. is appended to the session transcript as a `user` message with `metadata: { steer: true }`, mirroring the existing structured-output-correction pattern, so it persists in history and flows into context assembly on later turns.

This covers every steer-channel producer uniformly (`session_steer` injected path, inline subagent result delivery, and inline OOB structured-response delivery).

## Tests

Extended `packages/daemon/test/sessions/tool-loop-steer.test.ts` with two new tests:

- steer messages are appended to the transcript as user messages with `steer: true` metadata
- the steer message content and session ID appear in daemon log output (via `setRootLogger` stub)

## Verification

- New tests + existing steer tests: 16/16 passed
- Full daemon suite: 226 files, 2343 tests — all passed
- `npm run typecheck` (lerna, 16 packages): green
- Pre-commit hooks (nano-staged oxfmt/oxlint + vitest --changed: 51 files / 569 tests): passed; pre-push typecheck: passed

body:
After the name dictionary (20261015010000), search_vehicles_fuzzy took
1.6 s as service_role but ran past 10 s as anon, and the REST RPC
returned 500 at anon's 15 s timeout. Under row security the planner
cannot use idx_vehicles_lower_make_model for anon: lower() is not
leakproof, so the index condition cannot run before the policy filter
and every vehicle is read. The old body behaved the same way.

The function returns only public rows and only columns anon already
reads (id, year, make, model, vin, primary_image_url, sale_price), and
the dictionary is granted to anon, so running it as its owner returns
the same rows to every caller. search_path is pinned to public, pg_temp.
The migration refuses any body but 20261015010000's.

Contract test_search_fuzzy_runs_as_owner.sql (db-contracts): vehicles
with row security and production's two read policies; anon, the owner
of private rows and the service role get the same rows; every row is
public and the matching private vehicles are never returned; definer
with the pinned path; idempotent. 4 of 4 pass on PG17 17.9.

## 요약

설계서 미결20(성 토요일 하루에 전례가 둘 — 낮 성 토요일 홍 · 밤 부활밤 백)을 사용자 결정으로 닫는다. 캘린더 탭 1단계(#348) 화면에서 성 토요일 칸이 「부활밤」(점은 적색)으로 보여 드러난 물음이다.

- **저녁 전례**(→ 설계서 R-6.1-evening): 부활밤(`t-부활밤` — 성 토요일 저녁)과 성탄 밤(`d1225-성탄-밤` — 12.25 로 정의돼 있지만 전날 12.24 저녁)은 **드리는 날의 후보 맨 끝**에 `evening: true` 로 실리고, 그날의 대표(`official`) · 색 · 재분류(`settle`)에 참여하지 않는다. 엔진 상수 `EVENING_LITURGIES` 가 정의 표의 id 와 「정의 날짜에서 드리는 날까지의 날 수」(부활밤 0 · 성탄 밤 −1)를 든다 — `resolveDateIn` 이 낮의 판정에서 빼고 끝에 붙인다.
- **성 토요일의 대표는 성 토요일 행**이다 — 등급 칸이 빈 temporal **평일** 행(실데이터에서 성 토요일 하나)은 유효 precedence 8(평일)이라 같은 날 격자 평일과 동률이고, 범주 사다리(temporal > 격자)로 그날의 대표가 된다. 주일 이름 줄(가정 · 평화통일 · 맥추감사 · 주의 변모 주일)은 그대로 최하위다(`effectivePrecedence`).
- 결과: 2026-04-04 대표 성 토요일 · 적색, 후보 「성 토요일 · 성주간 토요일 · 부활밤(저녁)」. 2026-12-24 대표 대림 평일 · 자색 + 성탄 밤(저녁). 2026-12-25 후보 성탄 낮 · 새벽.
- **이동 패스는 그대로다** — `computeTransfers` 는 이 상수를 보지 않는다. 성 토요일에 걸린 주요축일은 여전히 부활밤(prec 1)이 밀어낸다(R-6.3-holy-week-guard — 픽스처 T-2062-03-27 의 수태고지). 골든 덤프(1900~2100 이동) 무변경.
- **전례독서 화면**: 칩 꼬리말 「· 저녁」(`statusSuffix`). 성 토요일을 열면 성 토요일 독서(욥기 14 …)가 먼저이고 부활밤 칩을 고르면 백색 · 부활밤 독서(「고른 본문의 색」 — 기존 규칙). 성탄 밤의 독서 · 본기도는 12.24 에서도 정의 날짜(12.25) 키로 찾는다.
- 타입: `Candidate.evening?: true`(`js/types.d.ts`).

## 확정·근거

- **사용자 결정(2026-10-15)**: 「엔진은 "성 토요일"을 기본으로 보여줘야 해. 독서 화면에서 칩으로 부활밤을 보여줄 수 있게 하면 되. 부활밤은 저녁 전례로 보는 게 맞아. 성탄 밤도 12.24 저녁 전례가 되어야 맞겠지」 — 「네가 말한 "권장대로"인 셈이야」. 물은 셋: ① 부활밤을 저녁 전례로 따로 볼지 ② 그날 독서 화면을 열면 먼저 보일 본문(성 토요일 / 부활밤) — 권장대로 성 토요일 ③ 성탄 밤의 날짜(12.24 저녁 / 12.25) — 권장대로 12.24 저녁. coding-pitfalls §25(번호는 #348 의 §24 다음).
- **책자 근거**: 2024 · 2025 · 2026 「전례독서」 — 성 토요일 칸은 「성(주간) 토요일 [홍] · 감사성찬례 없음」, 부활밤은 「부활밤 예식 [백]」으로 따로(2025 · 2026 저녁 칸, 2024 한 줄). 12.24 칸에 「성탄밤 [백]」, 12.25 칸에는 성탄새벽 · 성탄낮만(2024 는 12.24 칸의 한 줄). **2027 검토용 초안만** 12.25 칸에 [성탄밤] · [성탄 새벽] · [성탄 낮] 셋을 실었다 — 확정판이 그대로면 `tools/booklet/` 재대조 때 다시 본다(초안의 차이로 데이터 · 엔진을 고치지 않는다 — §22).
- 이름: 책자는 그날을 「성 토요일」(2024 · 2027 초안) · 「성주간 토요일」(2025 · 2026)로 적었다 — 사용자 요청대로 데이터의 temporal 행 「성 토요일」.
- **사용자 아이디어(결정 전)**: 「시간대에 따라, 일몰 이후 또는 저녁 6시 이후가 되면 저녁 전례로 간주해 전례색을 변경하는 것도 하나의 방법」. 엔진은 날짜 단위로 두고, 뷰의 물음으로 ADR-038 「검토한 대안 — 저녁 전례」 C 에 보류로 적었다 — 같은 날짜 주소가 시각마다 다른 화면이 되는 문제(공유 · 뒤로 가기)와 일몰의 위치 권한이 걸린다. 「오늘」 화면에만, 고른 칩을 주소에 적는 꼴이면 가능하다.
- **기각한 갈래**(설계서 §9.2 미결20 · ADR-038 「검토한 대안」): 승자 부활밤 · 색 홍(이름과 색이 어긋나고 책자와 다르다) · `ResolvedDate` 가 색을 둘 낸다(소비자마다 낮 · 밤을 다시 가려야 한다) · 데이터 표에 저녁 표지 열(데이터 저장소 파서 변경 — 엔진 상수로 시작, 실데이터 테스트가 두 id 의 실재를 지킨다).

## 검증

- `npm run typecheck` 0.
- 유닛 `node --test tests/unit/*.test.js` — **1177**(1176 통과 · 실데이터 대기 1 skip). 새로 C-6.1-13(합성 — 저녁 후보의 자리 · 승자 밖 · 12.25 에 없음 · 상수 두 id) · C-6.1-13 실데이터(2025~2050 성 토요일 · 12.24 · 12.25, 2026 한 해 전수에서 저녁 후보는 두 날뿐, 상수 id 실재). 합성 표의 부활밤 · 성탄 밤 id 를 실제 id 로 바꿔(상수의 키) 공개 CI 에서도 저녁 규칙이 돈다. 갱신: C-4.3-3(후보 순서) · C-6.1-7(성 토요일의 승자 · 유효 precedence 8) · C-6.4-4 · C-6.4-2 · C-5.5-5 · 미결12 좁히기(성탄 밤은 12.24) · 성인력 행 전수 두 개(드리는 날로 조회 — `heldOn`) · A3 성 토요일 · 12.25/12.24 모델 · 픽스처 T-2062-03-27(대표 `t-성-토요일`, 이동은 그대로 `displacedBy: t-부활밤`).
- 이동 골든 덤프(`liturgical-engine.data.test.js` I-10) 무변경 — 패스가 그대로임을 보인다.
- CI — `Unit tests` · `Change ledger` 통과, 실데이터 워크플로를 PR 브랜치에서 돌림(`gh workflow run engine-data.yml --ref feat/liturgical-engine-evening` — run 38659029662: 153 중 152 통과 · skip 1).
- e2e — `test_lectionary_view.py` 43(새 1: 성 토요일 「부활밤 · 저녁」 칩 → 백색 · 마태 28, 12.24 「성탄 밤 · 저녁」, 12.25 에 없음) · `test_a11y_axe.py` 10 통과.

## 갱신한 문서

- `docs/design/liturgical-engine.md` — R-6.1-evening 신설 · §6.1 null 품계(평일 행 유효 8)와 성 토요일 행 · §6.4 E−1 · §4.10 표 · §5.5(`evening` 필드 · 출처 · 표시 순서 ④) · §9 미결20 을 §9.2 로 닫음 · 미결12 의 12.25 문장.
- `docs/design/liturgical-engine-review.md` — C-2-1 · C-6.1-7 · C-6.4-4 갱신, C-6.1-13 신설, §6 질문지에서 미결20 행 삭제.
- `docs/decisions/037-eucharist-lectionary-data-and-engine.md` — §6 `Candidate` 래퍼에 `evening`.
- `docs/decisions/038-calendar-lectionary-ui.md` — §3 「구현」(헤더 색 문장 · 칩 꼬리 「저녁」 · 12.25 칩 둘 · 저녁 전례 항목) · 「검토한 대안 — 저녁 전례」(A 채택 · B 기각 · C 보류).
- `docs/coding-pitfalls.md` — §25 신설, §21 의 12.25 · 성 토요일 문장.
- `docs/status.md` — 한 줄.
- `tests/fixtures/liturgical/transfers.cases.json` — T-2062-03-27 의 대표 · canon · checks · source.
- `CLAUDE.md` · `tests/README.md` — 유닛 1177 · e2e 288, 파일별 수.

## main 위로 옮김 (2026-10-15 — #348 머지 뒤)

#348(캘린더 탭 1단계)이 먼저 머지되어 이 브랜치를 main(`bf05e59`) 위로 rebase 했다. 코드(`liturgical-engine.js` · `lectionary.js` · `types.d.ts` · `test_lectionary_view.py`)는 저절로 합쳐졌고 문서 다섯 곳이 충돌했다 — 세 갈래(공통 조상 · main · 이 PR)를 견줘 양쪽 변경을 모두 살렸다.

- `CLAUDE.md` · `tests/README.md` 수치 — 두 PR 의 증분을 더했다: 유닛 1215 + 2 = **1217**, e2e 308 + 1 = **309**. 표의 행도 양쪽을 함께 — `test_lectionary_view.py` 는 「캘린더 탭 활성」(#348) + 「저녁 전례 칩」(이 PR) · 43건, `liturgical-engine.data.test.js` 는 이 PR 의 「저녁 전례」, `test_liturgical_render.py` 는 #348 의 라벨 정정.
- `docs/status.md` — 두 PR 이 맨 위에 각자 넣은 줄을 둘 다(이 PR 줄이 위). #348 줄의 「성 토요일 칸(지금 「부활밤」)은 … 엔진 PR 에서 「성 토요일」이 된다」는 결과(「성 토요일」)로 고쳤다.
- ADR-038 — §3 「구현」은 #348 의 「탭 분류」 줄과 이 PR 의 「12.25 칩 둘」 · 「저녁 전례는 칩」 줄을 함께, 「검토한 대안」은 #348 의 절들 뒤에 이 PR 의 「저녁 전례」.
- `docs/coding-pitfalls.md` — #348 의 §24 와 이 PR 의 §25 를 번호대로.
- 충돌 밖에서 #348 이 이 PR 을 예고하던 문장 둘을 결과로 — ADR-038 §2 「구현」(성 토요일 칸은 「성 토요일」) · `known-issues.md` §8(성주간 칸을 다시 봤다 — 월~수 칸 이름 그대로, 성 토요일 칸 「성 토요일」).

**합쳐서 생긴 문제(미해결 — 리뷰에서 다룬다)** — 12.24 평일의 캘린더 칸이 「성탄 밤」으로 보인다(점은 그날 색 자색, 링크 이름 「12월 24일 목요일, 성탄 밤 · 저녁, 자색」 — 2026 · 2027 재현). 칸 이름 규칙(`calendar.js cellCandidateOf`)은 대표가 격자 평일이면 이름 있는 후보를 찾는데, 이 PR 의 저녁 후보(`evening: true` · `status: "proper"`)를 거르지 않는다. 일요일인 12.24(2028)는 「대림4주」, 성 토요일은 「성 토요일」이라 어긋나고, 「저녁 전례는 그날의 대표가 아니라 칩」(ADR-038 §3)과도 맞지 않는다. 옮기기 전에 시작했다 멈춘 코드 리뷰의 에이전트 둘이 따로 짚었다.

**검증(옮긴 뒤)** — `npm run typecheck` 0 · 유닛 **1217건 — 1216 통과 · skip 1**(두 PR 합산과 같다) · e2e 전체 **309건 모두 통과**(29파일, 한 번에 — 8분) · 다시 쓴 커밋 넷 서명 정상.

author: devgunnin
body:
Part of #14, slice 2 of repository identity.

## Problem

Archon up to 1.2.1 creates agents with `scope.repository: "archon"`, so their memories are filed under that bare name. Direct sessions in the same checkout, and agents created with `repository_root` (#31), use the derived id `github.com/mengsig/archon`. These are two scopes for one repository, and neither side sees what the other learned.

## Change

An operator registers an alias once, which moves the memory:

```
aether memory alias archon --root ~/src/archon --dry-run   # what would move
aether memory alias archon --root ~/src/archon             # move it
aether memory aliases
```

- **Store (schema v20).** A new `repository_aliases` table.
  - Registering an alias inserts the row and rescopes every `repository` and `repository_role` memory under the alias, in any state. The JSON body, the scope key column and the FTS rows change together.
  - One `custom` event, `repository.aliased`, records the alias, the target, the moved counts and the operator.
  - All of this happens in one transaction. Text, ids, provenance, supersession, pins and forgotten state are untouched.
- **Refusals and re-registration.** Aliasing a name to a second target is refused, and so are chains. Re-registering the same pair is a no-op that also moves any memory filed under the alias since.
- **Resolution on use.** Agent rows are never rewritten. Aliases are resolved instead at:
  - memory retrieval
  - memory admission (`remember`, compaction, operator `create_memory`, seeding)
  - repository-note seeding
  - agent creation (a named id, a `repository_root`, an inherited one, a workspace-derived one)
  - child narrowing against a parent created before the alias
  - operator `memories` queries, `create_memory`'s `repository` field and `aether memory list --scope`

  An old agent still carrying `archon` therefore reads and writes the target from the next turn on, including a turn already in flight. Writes resolve under the same commit lock the move takes, so none can land under the alias after the move.
- **Protocol.**
  - `alias_repository {alias, root | repository, dry_run}` is host only, so paired devices are refused.
  - `list_repository_aliases` is observe.
  - Both are advertised as the `repository_aliases` feature. The Rust client and the CLI refuse an older daemon.
  - The Python and TypeScript clients are regenerated.

## Compatibility

- Opening an existing store migrates it to v20 and takes the usual backup first. The migration only adds a table, and nothing moves until an operator asks.
- The new event is a `custom` event, so older clients still decode the log.
- Older daemons do not have the commands, so clients check the feature first.

## Tests

- **Core:** alias normalization and validity, plus the event payload.
- **Store:**
  - a v19 store with a memory under the old name migrates to v20, and the memory can then be moved
  - a dry run counts exactly what the move then moves, with the body and the key column agreeing on every row
  - neighbours with lookalike ids (`archonite`, `archon2`) stay put
  - FTS finds a moved memory
  - duplicates are moved beside their twin, not merged
  - re-registering is idempotent, and a later registration sweeps stragglers
  - conflicts and both halves of a chain are refused
  - a trigger that fails the move partway leaves every memory, the alias table and the log untouched
- **Runtime:**
  - an old agent still naming `archon` sees memories filed before and after the alias, and its `remember` lands in the canonical scope
  - its row is not rewritten
  - a new agent naming `archon` stores the canonical id
  - children of an old parent (inheriting, naming the alias, naming the target) pass narrowing, and another repository is still refused
  - an operator query by `archon` finds the canonical memories
  - an agent in the canonical scope sees the moved memories
  - only an operator can alias
- **Daemon** (real socket): the feature is advertised; a dry run is followed by a real run with the same counts; a query by the alias works after the move; a paired device is forbidden and moves nothing. Device-gate and authz tables are updated.
- **Client and CLI:** an older daemon is refused before anything is sent; dry-run and real output; `--root` is sent as an absolute path; clap refuses neither or both of `--root`/`--repository`.
- **Results, locally all passing:**
  - core 234, store 140, memory 50, protocol 60, context 49, tools 273
  - client 128, TUI 1,332, runtime 883, daemon 288, CLI 341
  - fmt and clippy are clean, the generator reports no drift, Python 25/25, TypeScript 12/12 plus `tsc`

## Known limits

- **No unalias.** Moved memories do not move back. Removing an alias would also send old agents' new memories to the old name again, so an alias is permanent (stated in docs/protocol.md).
- **Prompt label.** An old agent's system prompt still shows the repository it was created with (`archon`); only memory follows the alias.
- **Late imports.** A run imported after the alias, carrying memories under the old name, keeps them there until the alias is registered again (which moves them).

## Review

A review by another model family asked for changes and reproduced three problems. Fixed in `6b1bbb15` on top of `a738565d`.

1. **Scope checks against an older parent.** A child created after the alias carries the new id, while its parent still says `archon`. The checks against an existing agent compared the two raw, so tightening the child, restarting it, or the parent scheduling to it was refused. Both sides are now resolved before comparing: `scope_widened_for_existing` (update, restart, recovery, integration), `scope_within_ancestor` (schedules, descendant checks) and the isolated-delegation precheck. A search for other raw comparisons found one more: the GitHub follow-up check compared `github.com/<repo>` raw with the agent's stored id, so a thread agent created after an alias of that repository never got its next mention. It now resolves both sides too.
   - Test `a_child_in_the_canonical_scope_stays_within_a_parent_naming_the_alias` tightens the child's network, cancels and restarts it, and has the parent schedule to it.
   - Test `automatic_followup_reaches_an_agent_created_after_an_alias` covers the GitHub check.
2. **Seeding racing an alias.** Seeding resolved the name before taking the write lock, so an alias landing in between hid a forgotten note, and the note was admitted again with a new id. Each note's scope is now resolved again under the lock the move also takes, before the presence check. The retraction sweep resolves the name again too.
   - Test `seeding_racing_the_alias_keeps_a_forgotten_note_forgotten` expects found 1, admitted 0, unchanged 1, and the original record still forgotten under the new id.
3. **Reads racing an alias.** Retrieval, the operator `memories` query and the sweep's read now go through `MemoryService::read_resolved`. It resolves, reads, then resolves again, and if the answer changed it reads once more against the target. One repeat is enough because aliases are permanent and never chain.
   - Tests `an_operator_query_racing_the_alias_reads_where_the_memories_went` and `a_turn_racing_the_alias_still_sees_the_repository_memories`.

The race tests use a new `RepositoryResolved` hook in the kernel store double. It commits the alias right after a resolution returns, and `arm_skipping` lets the hook pass over earlier resolutions.

All five tests fail on `a738565d` and pass on the fix. With only the existing-agent half of fix 1 applied, the scope test still fails at the schedule step, so each half is covered. The isolated-delegation precheck change is defensive: the delegate tool always copies the parent's repository, so no test can make that check fail on the old code.

`docs/protocol.md` now says that tightening, restarting and scheduling also treat the two ids as one repository. No protocol types changed, and the generator `--check` passes.

author: carstvaartjes
body:
## Problem
`vonk-forge/nemotron-3-5-lightning-30b-a3b-ashhart-tensorfold-single` failed smoke case `NEM_A391_OFF` with `path choices.0.message.reasoning_content is missing` (http 200). The case asserts no reasoning with thinking off; this engine omits the `reasoning_content` key entirely, which is exactly "no reasoning". False failure.

## Fix
`NEM_A391_OFF` already uses `path.empty` (the only `path.empty` use in `qualification/`); the evaluator just resolved the path strictly first. `path.empty` now reads an **absent final key** as empty, so absent / `null` / `""` all pass. A missing parent (e.g. no `choices.0.message`) is still a missing path and fails. No case JSON changed, no new kind, so the Controller fixture parser's fixed kind list is unaffected. `path.nonempty` (the `NEM_REASON` thinking-on case) stays strict.

Why change semantics instead of adding a kind: "empty" naturally includes "not emitted", there's exactly one user of the kind, and it avoids a coordinated kind-list change on the Controller side.

## Tests
`tests/test_sweep_vonkctl_smoke.py`: absent/null/empty pass for thinking off; non-empty reasoning and a missing parent fail; thinking on still fails for absent/null/empty and passes with reasoning. `tests/test_sweep_*.py` + `tests/test_qualification_*.py` (1270 passed), lint, format, types green locally.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
The Controller's own evaluator (`vonk-forge` `src/cluster_profiles/fleet_qualification.py`, `_service_path` + `path.empty` branch) has the same strict resolution and raises `QualificationObservationUnknown` on the absent key; it needs the same leaf-absent-is-empty rule.

author: nakucoder
body:
## What

Merge sort's Do it mode, on bars (no characters yet). #78 defined the "which goes next?" decision but kept Do it hidden; this turns it on and wires it into the Do it flow.

- **Explorer:** at each comparison in a merge, **Left one (L)** or **Right one (R)**. Both buttons look alike (the same "up" icon).
- **Engineer:** taps the front value itself **in the second row**. The value buttons lie over the second row and its tags (measured, so Watch's layout is unchanged), each named by its half (`left[0] = 2, comparing`). Empty places stay in the row but can't be picked.
- **Equal fronts:** the left one is right (stable).
- **No question** at a split, or when a half has run out (the rest moves up by itself), like "no question at the front" in insertion sort.
- Same feedback, help ladder, timing and hold rules as the other sorts (all generic; merge sort has no character, so no hold).

**Questions on the default input (5 2 8 1 9 3): 10** (16 moves).

### Choices to review

1. **Engineer has Help only in the bar.** The table's which-next row had "Take right (R)" as Engineer's one button, but both answers are taps on the stage, so one button would stand for only one of them. New optional table field `tapOnly`; with it, Engineer gets no answer button and no R key. On phones Help fills the bar (portrait) or sits beside Sound (landscape).
2. **"Moved up X of 16":** the first counter counts out of every move (new optional field `found: 'moves'`). It used to count out of trades, which would have shown "of 0" for merge sort.
3. **Explorer's line under the question** is now "Smaller one first. Same? Left one first." It was "The smaller one goes next. Same? The left one goes first.", which took two lines, so with help open the 1440×900 rail ran 33px past the screen.

## Tests

New `src/pages/WorkspaceMergeDoIt.test.tsx` (17 tests): every ask frame on the default input (question, pair, answer side), a full run answering everything right (both levels; 9 of 10 after one wrong), wrong answers (nudge, asks again), equal values (Left right, Right wrong; Show me; perfect run), a half running out (no question), L/R keys, Engineer taps (labels, empty places do nothing, R key does nothing, a value behind a front is wrong), the counters, phones.

**Existing test files changed: one**, `src/algorithms/sorting/mergeSort.test.ts`:
- `describe('merge sort: stability and Do it’s question (defined, hidden)'` → `'… Do it’s question'`: it isn't hidden any more.
- `it('Do it stays hidden for now: Watch only')` → `it('Do it is on, on bars only (no character yet)')`, and `expect(mergeSort.doIt).toBe(false)` → `toBe(true)`: this PR turns it on. The `character` check is unchanged.

## Proof

- `git diff main -- '*.snap'` is empty: every golden record (sounds, timing, Do it holds) untouched.
- `npm run check` passes (78 files, 9,513 tests); no runtime import cycles.
- Fit and pixel comparisons on the preview: results in a comment below.
