body:
dev / https://claude.ai/code/session_01Mx1YPvfrJUmfQZEfPX3dXP

정리 2단계 계획서 표의 PR 1 이다. 손으로 맞춰 두는 두 목록이 어긋나면 CI 를 빨갛게 하는 드리프트 검사를 돌리는 틀을 넣고, 첫 검사로 /features 의 id 와 기능 폴더를 맞춰 본다. 머지하면 웹 CI 의 스모크 단계가 이 검사까지 돌고, 2단계의 나머지 검사는 이름이 이미 package.json 에 있어서 파일만 넣으면 돈다.

좋아지는 것: 없음

## 할 일
- [x] 계획서(`docs/investigations/2026-10-cleanup-step2-plan.md`) 표의 PR 1 행과 `docs/rfc-cleanup.md` §2.4·§2.11 을 읽는다
- [x] PR 1 이 적은 네 파일만 고친다: `web/package.json`, `web/scripts/drift.ts`, `web/scripts/drift/_lib.ts`, `web/scripts/drift/features.ts`
- [x] `npm run check:ci` 전체, `typecheck`, `lint` 를 돌린다
- [x] 일부러 어긋나게 고친 판에서 검사가 빨개지는 것을 보이고 되돌린다
- [x] `npm run doc-map` 을 돌려 두 CSV 가 그대로인 것을 본다(커밋하지 않는다)
- [x] dev 를 merge 한다(dev 는 `daf5b4b` 에서 움직이지 않아 이미 들어 있다)

## 한 일
- `web/scripts/drift.ts`: 러너. 인자가 없으면 `scripts/drift/` 에서 이름이 `_` 로 시작하지 않는 `.ts` 를 모두, 이름을 주면 그것만 돌린다. 검사마다 따로 프로세스를 띄우고(`process.execArgv` 로 tsx 로더를 넘긴다), 끝에 검사마다 한 줄(passed·failed·skipped)을 찍는다. 하나라도 failed 면 exit 1. 파일이 아직 없는 이름은 `scripts/drift/<name>.ts is not written yet` 을 찍고 failed.
- `web/scripts/drift/_lib.ts`: 검사들이 가져다 쓰는 것. `ROOT`, `tracked(under?)`, `read(file)`, `compare(name, left, right)`(양쪽 목록과 한쪽에만 있는 것을 찍는다), `skip(name, why)`(D2), `done()`, 그리고 러너가 읽는 `SKIPPED`(=75).
- `web/scripts/drift/features.ts`: `features-data.ts` 의 `FEATURES` id 와 `firmware/patternflow/features/` 아래 폴더를 비교한다. 폴더가 아닌 id 는 `Feature.id` 의 주석이 따옴표로 적은 것(지금은 `"core"`)을 TypeScript 파서로 읽어 뺀다(D3, 베끼지 않고 읽는다).
- `web/package.json`: `check:drift`, `check:links-absolute`·`check:bom`·`check:bom-schematic`·`check:features`·`check:editions`·`check:presets`·`check:roadmap`·`check:changelog`(모두 `tsx scripts/drift.ts <name>`), `check:human-lock`(`tsx scripts/human-lock.ts`), `check:voice`(`tsx scripts/voice-lint.ts`). `check:ci` 끝에 `&& npm run check:drift`. 의존성은 더하지 않았다.

바뀐 줄: 4 파일, +154 −2.

## 증거

`npm run check:ci` (HEAD `e66669b`, web/): exit 0. vitest `Test Files 35 passed (35)`, `Tests 478 passed (478)`, 끝은:

```
> version2@0.1.0 check:drift
> tsx scripts/drift.ts

── features
ids that are not folders, by the comment on Feature.id: core
ids against folders: same
  web/src/app/features/features-data.ts (9): audio, audio_in, ble, clock, midi, mqtt, osc, show, weather
  firmware/patternflow/features/ (9): audio, audio_in, ble, clock, midi, mqtt, osc, show, weather

passed   features
check:ci exit 0
```

`npm run typecheck`: exit 0. `npm run lint`: exit 0, `✖ 12 problems (0 errors, 12 warnings)` — 경고 12개는 모두 원래 있던 `src/` 의 것이고 새 파일에는 하나도 없다.

일부러 어긋나게 고친 판 1 (`ble` 줄의 id 를 `bluetooth` 로, 커밋 전에 되돌림), `npm run check:drift`:

```
── features
ids that are not folders, by the comment on Feature.id: core
ids against folders: drift
  web/src/app/features/features-data.ts (9): audio, audio_in, bluetooth, clock, midi, mqtt, osc, show, weather
  firmware/patternflow/features/ (9): audio, audio_in, ble, clock, midi, mqtt, osc, show, weather
  only in web/src/app/features/features-data.ts: bluetooth
  only in firmware/patternflow/features/: ble

failed   features
exit 1
```

판 2 (`Feature.id` 주석에서 `or "core"` 를 지움, 되돌림), `npm run check:features`: `ids that are not folders, by the comment on Feature.id: (none)` … `only in web/src/app/features/features-data.ts: core`, `failed features`, exit 1. 예외는 주석에서 읽는다는 증거.

판 3 (버린 검사 파일 둘: `skip()` 만 부르는 것, `throw` 하는 것, 커밋 전에 지움):

```
passed   features
skipped  zz-skips
failed   zz-throws
exit 1
```

`skip()` 만 있을 때: 그냥은 `skipped zz-skips` / `passed features` exit 0, `PF_DRIFT_STRICT=1` 이면 `PF_DRIFT_STRICT=1, so a skip fails` 다음 `failed zz-skips` exit 1 (D2).

아직 파일이 없는 이름, `npm run check:bom`:

```
── bom
scripts/drift/bom.ts is not written yet

failed   bom
exit 1
```

`git fetch --tags` 뒤 `npm run doc-map`: `1066 links from 212 files → docs/investigations/2026-10-doc-map.csv`, `0 do not resolve`. 두 CSV 모두 바뀌지 않았고(`git status` 에 안 뜸) `git checkout` 으로 한 번 더 되돌렸다. `docs/voice-banned.txt` 의 말과 em dash 는 새 파일에 없다.

## 실행법
```
cd web
npm ci
npm run check:drift          # 모든 검사
npm run check:features       # 하나만
PF_DRIFT_STRICT=1 npm run check:drift   # skip 도 실패로
```

## 가정
- 러너가 skip 을 passed 와 가려 읽을 길을 계획서가 정하지 않아서, 검사가 exit 75(sysexits 의 EX_TEMPFAIL)로 알린다. `_lib.ts` 의 `SKIPPED` 상수다. `PF_DRIFT_STRICT=1` 에서는 `done()` 이 바로 1 로 끝낸다.
- 검사는 하나씩 차례로 돌고 출력은 그대로 흘려 보낸다. 실패한 검사의 양쪽 목록이 CI 로그에 그대로 남게 하려고.
- `compare()` 는 목록을 중복까지 센다(한쪽에 두 번, 다른 쪽에 한 번이면 한쪽에만 하나). 같은 id 가 두 줄이면 드리프트로 보인다.
- `features.ts` 는 `FEATURES` 를 import 해서 읽는다. `features-data.ts` 는 import 가 없는 데이터 파일이라 tsx 로 그대로 돈다.
- `check:human-lock`·`check:voice` 는 계획서대로 지금은 없는 파일(k8·k9 몫)을 가리킨다. 그 전까지는 tsx 의 module-not-found 로 실패하고, `check:ci` 에는 들어 있지 않다.
- `CHANGELOG.md` 는 고치지 않았다(머리말·계획서대로). 넣을 줄은 아래 「Changelog」.
- 라벨 `cleanup`·`step-2` 는 포크에 없어서 달지 않았다(D7 「도구가 되면」).
- `docs/rfc-cleanup-progress.md` 와 doc-map CSV 는 k13 몫이라 안 고쳤다.
- 웹 CI(`web-ci.yml`)가 `web/**` 에서만 도는 것은 계획서 소견 1 그대로 k10 몫이다.

### for another k
- k2: `links-absolute.ts` 는 k1 에서 아무것도 import 하지 않으므로, 러너에 skipped 로 보이려면 skip 일 때 exit 75 로, `PF_DRIFT_STRICT=1` 이면 exit 1 로 끝내야 한다. 0 으로 끝내면 passed 로 찍힌다.

## Changelog
### Web
- **`check:features` fails when /features and the feature folders disagree.** An id with no folder under `firmware/patternflow/features/`, or a folder with no id, turns `check:ci` red, and the run prints both lists and what is on one side only. `core` is the one id without a folder, because the comment on `Feature.id` says so. It is the first check `npm run check:drift` runs: every file in `web/scripts/drift/` is one, and the rest of the cleanup's step 2 lands there.

author: olydis
body:
## What

`eager-graph-nil-mmap-32-v2.hpp`, a copy of the eager evaluator made faster on forest's real build, is now what `-DRUNNER_EAGER` builds; the original stays as `-DRUNNER_EAGER_V1`, tested alongside and in the benchmark roster. `reduce_canonicalize.cpp` is rewritten around flat tables with the same algorithm and traversal order, so its output and `--stats-per-symbol` are byte-identical.

Measured by replaying the exact requests forest's compile phase and expect tests send the runner (outputs checked byte for byte, also under forced collections), then on forest's build itself (4 workers, cold cache; every `# = …` comment and generated file unchanged):

| forest phase | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| compile (all sources) | 2.79 s | 1.55 s |
| bundle reduce | 6.00 s | 0.60 s |
| arboretum bundle reduce | 1.36 s | 0.49 s |
| expect tests | 39.6 s | 31.6 s |

Single-process replays: compile 1.88x, expect subset 1.47x, the four heaviest tests 1.16x. The mini benchmark (log included) has v2 1.25–1.4x over the original.

## How

- The step loop keeps its state in registers: frames on an mmap'd stack, local step counter and arena pointer, the nursery fast path of `intern()` inlined, collection a cold call behind one byte. 184 instructions a step became 143.
- Rule (2)'s inner application is read off the function when its frame is pushed (`STEM`, `FORK_WITH`, `RETURN`, `FORK_RIGHT`): a quarter fewer steps. `apply(y, b)` is still reduced in every case.
- A collection marks into a side bitmap and re-inserts survivors as it sweeps: 267 → 109 ms at a 256 MB budget.
- Every reduction starts under a 16 MiB budget and only one that keeps collecting climbs to `RUNNER_RSS_THRESHOLD_MB`, now a ceiling: the arena, table and memo are read at random on every step, and the light workloads run ~1.5x faster while the three fit in cache, while the heavy tests need the big memo (3x the steps at a fixed 32 MiB).
- The hash-consing table's `EMPTY` is 0 (an untouched page is empty) and a group is scanned with one SSE2 movemask.
- `RUNNER_HUGEPAGES` (opt-in, runner and reducer): +13% on a machine that keeps its memory, −19% on a VM whose balloon hands freed 2 MiB blocks back to the host; nothing at startup can tell them apart.

What was measured and not taken is listed at the top of the v2 header (memo layouts and policies, kind-tagged nodes with switch dispatch, clang/-O2/PGO/hints, prefaulting, table growth variants, …), so nobody measures it twice; `runner.md` documents the budget's new meaning and the record-and-replay method.

## Follow-ups

- `Machine.lean` does not yet model the four result-only frames; the header's `Frame` comment states each as a transition, and `lean/Cpp/README.md` notes the gap.
- arboretum and forest pick this up by moving their submodule pins (PRs to follow).

author: chsami
body:
## Problem

Client error telemetry shows agent server requests crashing with an HTTP 500 and an error-level log from `AgentHandler.handle` ("Error handling {}"):

- **Group 977** (3 reports, 2.6.32): `com.google.gson.stream.MalformedJsonException: Invalid escape sequence at line 1 column 51`. The cause is unescaped Windows backslashes in a POST body, thrown out of `DynamicScriptDeployHandler.handleDeploy:90`.
- **Group 1532** (2 occurrences, 1 report, 2.6.31): `NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.util.Map.get(Object)" because "body" is null` at `BankHandler.handleDeposit:125`.
- **Group 667** (1 report, 2.6.30): the same NPE at `ScriptHandler.resolvePlugin:366`, reached via `handleStart:113`.

That is 6 occurrences in total. Each one is a bad client request, but it shows up as a server error and adds noise to telemetry.

## Root cause

`AgentHandler.readJsonBody` returns `gson.fromJson(body, LinkedHashMap.class)` as is:
- An empty body, or a literal `null`, parses to `null`. Handlers then call `body.get(...)` and hit an NPE.
- Malformed or non-object JSON throws `JsonSyntaxException`. Handlers without their own try/catch pass it up to the generic catch in `AgentHandler.handle`, which calls `log.error` and returns a 500.

## Change

The fix is in the shared helper `AgentHandler.java` only, so all 27 `readJsonBody` call sites across 17 handlers are covered:
- `readJsonBody` returns an empty `LinkedHashMap` when the parse gives `null`.
- A `JsonParseException` is rethrown as the new `AgentHandler.BadRequestException("Invalid JSON body")`. That class extends `IllegalArgumentException`, so handlers that already catch `Exception` still send their own 400.
- The two "Request body too large" throws now use `BadRequestException` as well. Before, they gave a 500 in handlers that don't catch.
- `AgentHandler.handle` maps `BadRequestException` to a 400 and logs it at debug, so it no longer produces `log.error` or error telemetry.
- The disconnect-safe error-response code is now a single private `sendErrorResponse` helper, used by both the 400 and 500 paths.

Handlers that check `body != null` (Login, Logout, Profile) behave the same with an empty map. This is client-only code, so no Hub version bump is needed.

## Validation

- New `AgentHandlerJsonBodyTest` covers an empty body, a `null` body, a valid body, a Windows-path invalid escape (400, never 500), non-object JSON (400) and an oversized Content-Length (400).
- `./gradlew :client:runUnitTests --tests 'net.runelite.client.plugins.microbot.agentserver.*'`: 110 passed, 0 failed.
- `./gradlew :client:checkstyleMain :client:checkstyleTest`: passed.

## Known gaps

- Not tested live against a running client. The change is limited to request parsing and error mapping, and the unit tests exercise it through `AgentHandler.handle`.
- Handlers that need specific fields still return their own 400 or 404 when a field is missing. This PR does not change those checks.

author: benvanik
body:
Make mixed-model serving behavior observable from the client request through host preparation, model admission, output publication, and final retirement. This gives model and scheduler authors a repeatable workload and measurements with explicit ownership boundaries, while leaving scheduling and residency policies unchanged. The resulting traces also expose an avoidable transport allocation cost: HTTP listeners now reuse registered receive storage across connections instead of registering new slabs for every request.

Running several agents alongside an image, speech, or embedding model makes aggregate tokens per second insufficient: an apparently busy model may be preparing inputs, waiting for parameter backing, or retaining work after a client disconnects. The new observations distinguish those cases without making inference wait for a log reader or introducing a thread per model.

## Latency and admission pressure

`/metrics` publishes cumulative request-duration histograms by model incarnation and terminal outcome, plus a first-meaningful-output histogram. Server totals retain observations after model removal and name reuse. Histograms remain available when the event ring wraps or periodic heartbeats are disabled.

First output means content, reasoning, tool-call output, or waveform bytes accepted by the HTTP carrier—not headers, an assistant-role announcement, an empty EOS response, or client receipt. Finite image, embedding, and decision requests record publication of their complete result. Streaming text and speech requests retain their first-output sample even if they later disconnect or fail. The matching `first_output` event correlates that observation with request begin/end records.

Parameter admission reports current wait state and age, cumulative wait episodes and duration, and accepted-consumer pins through `/v1/status` and `/metrics`. Retries do not manufacture additional episodes, cancellation preserves elapsed waiting, and the open interval is visible before admission succeeds. These are model-level parameter waits, not estimates of request queue time or device utilization. Successful uncontended admission gains no clock read, allocation, or observer synchronization.

```sh
curl --fail http://localhost:8080/v1/status
curl --fail http://localhost:8080/metrics
curl --no-buffer --fail http://localhost:8080/logz/stream \
  -H 'X-Loom-Model: coder'
```

The observation guide explains measurement boundaries and how to combine these views with existing KV, workspace, packing, and backpressure evidence. Prometheus formatting is separated from HTTP routing; the registry owns the shared readiness-gated service snapshot.

## Replay the same work, not just the same concurrency

The test-only replay tool takes frozen JSONL HTTP requests for streaming chat, images, embeddings, and decisions. A request can arrive at a fixed offset or after a named predecessor completes, making multi-turn agent work and sporadic auxiliary models reproducible without invoking live tools during a comparison.

```json
{"id":"turn-1","at_ms":0,"path":"/v1/chat/completions","headers":{"X-Loom-Session":"agent-a"},"body":{"model":"coder","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain this function."}],"stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true},"max_tokens":128}}
{"id":"search","at_ms":100,"path":"/v1/embeddings","body":{"model":"search","input":["find the tokenizer"]}}
```

The runner preserves request bodies and settings, validates the complete manifest before sending work, and bounds client concurrency. JSONL results include client launch lag, first meaningful output, answer-only first text, completion latency, server-reported token usage, and request/output fingerprints. A saturated client is visible as launch lag instead of being mistaken for server performance. Failed requests are not retried, and dependent requests cannot silently run after a failed predecessor. Python remains test-only; the server acquires no Python dependency.

## Host traces and earlier model diagnostics

Serving CPU work uses `IREE_TRACE_*` zones for source compilation, input preparation, scheduler turns, submission, completion handling, and output encoding. Model incarnation and request/cohort IDs connect those zones to telemetry. Public compiler operations and asynchronous compilation tasks have parent zones on the workers that execute them, making compiler allocations attributable rather than free-floating.

Proactor and HAL maintenance threads retain their thread names but no longer hold a zone across the entire thread lifetime or an idle maintenance wait. Proactor preparation and completion work is scoped separately from blocking waits. Asynchronous waits are not represented as occupied CPU threads or fake device timing.

The Tracy client moves to 0.14.1, with CPU zone emission delegated to its public C interface and message severity preserved alongside color. The observation workflow covers live profiler attachment, SSH forwarding, direct recording, and automatic discovery with `tracy-capture-daemon`. Build setup lives in the runtime tracing guide. Both guides make the buffered capture contract explicit: one collector per server process, capture memory separate from bounded operational telemetry, and saved files completed on graceful capture shutdown.

Model preparation also binds deferred control exports against their real host signatures before publishing a service. Public VM reflection checks argument/result counts, scalar widths, reference identities, and synchronous-call requirements without invoking model code. An incompatible model now fails registration with an export-specific diagnostic instead of waiting for its first inference request. No new per-invocation validation is added.

## Reuse registered HTTP receive storage

Each listener owns a demand-grown cache of exclusive registered receive pools. A connection leases one pool; its lease returns only after both asynchronous I/O and application ownership have retired. Simultaneous connections never share a live receive ring, and destroying a listener cannot reclaim storage still borrowed by a request.

The cache is bounded by existing connection admission and the listener's parked accept. Warm connections reuse registration and slab storage without allocating replacement receive storage. Growth and deregistration happen outside the cache lock. This removes connection-lifetime registration churn without changing HTTP backpressure, response ownership, or the underlying proactor backend.

## Startup correctness and test boundaries

AMDGPU host-memory selection no longer collects HSA enumeration results into fixed-size arrays. ROCr can expose enough valid CPU memory regions on a many-NUMA-node system to exceed the previous capacity. Selection now retains only the required handles as enumeration proceeds, with constant storage and unchanged native error propagation.

Stream-carrier retirement now serializes the final operation decrement and drain decision with deactivation. An active connection can reach zero operations before shutdown begins; that transition must not allow another thread to complete shutdown and free storage while the earlier completion still inspects it. The callback remains outside the mutex and may immediately release the carrier.

Native source-JIT fixtures cover text, image, speech, embedding, and decision HTTP paths; cancellation before and after output; registration retirement/name reuse; parameter-pressure retries and cancellation; and failed control preparation while a peer remains usable. Receive-pool tests exercise exclusive leases, ownership outliving listener teardown, and failed growth. Bounded catalog and pressure checks remain in ordinary CI; larger workload matrices use the existing explicit manual stress targets.

These checks establish ownership and measurement contracts. This change makes no learned-model throughput claim and selects no new scheduling policy.

body:
## Cut 4d-ii: the boot diagnostic bundle stops being mtcollins1's

`gunbc.machine_intake.mtcollins1_boot_diagnostic_bundle` (2573 lines) is host-generic now. It is
**deleted** and replaced by two modules, plus a neutral core. One boot procedure for every machine
(ruling `one_boot_procedure_for_every_machine`), so the split is by what is actually
controller-protocol-specific, not by machine.

### The three modules

| module | role | imports |
|---|---|---|
| `gunbc.host.boot_attempt` | the neutral core: what a boot attempt is | nothing MegaRAC |
| `gunbc.machine_intake.megarac_boot_diagnostic_bundle` | the MegaRAC/IPMI/Redfish adapter | core + BMC protocol modules |
| `gunbc.machine_intake.mtcollins1_boot_row` | mtcollins1's own measured facts | core + adapter |

Direction is one-way: adapter -> core, row -> (core, adapter). The core imports no MegaRAC type,
so srv3 (another BMC protocol) can inhabit a boot record without importing MegaRAC.

### What moved where

**Core `gunbc.host.boot_attempt`** — facts every controller has:
`HostPowerState`, `BootPresentation`, `StaleMediumPowerOff`, `MediaAttachRecord`,
`HandoffCallResult` (incl. `HandoffRefused` — refused by the controller and unreachable are two
findings), `HandoffMedia`, `EndMedia`, `PowerAfterAttempt` (incl. `PoweredOffAfterTerminal` /
`PoweredOffWithoutTerminal` / `PowerOffRefusedByController` / `PowerOffUnobserved`),
`BootOverrideConsumption` (incl. `OverrideConsumedByAttempt`), `BootFinding`, `TerminalObserved`,
`DiagnosticRef`, `BootRunRecord`, `ConsoleReading`. Plus the console decision (`console`,
`console_reading` — 6 row-named parameters: retained prefix, reference artifact path, the two
reference scopes, expected socket list, path) and shared text (`console_text`,
`checkpoint_relations`, `bracketed_int`, `firmware_report_text`, `grub_report_text`,
`console_path_retained`, `console_size_of_stat`, `attempt_identity_text`).
Ruling followed: no `Bool` field derivable from a record's own fields (the old
`MediaAttachAttempted.ready` became `media_attach_ready(...)`); no stringly `FindingDetail`
catch-all; `census_ended` and `PoweredOffAfterCensusEnd` are gone — terminal-neutral instead, and
the census mapping lives with the census consumer.

**Adapter `megarac_boot_diagnostic_bundle`** — the MegaRAC/IPMI/Redfish reads and the RAW records:
`MegaRacRunRecord` (what the bundle stores, once), `MegaRacMediaAttach`, `MegaRacStalePowerOff`,
`MegaRacHandoff`, `MegaRacHandoffCallResult`, `MegaRacEndMedia`, `MegaRacPowerAfter`,
`MegaRacOverride`, `MegaRacBootFindings`, `BootDiagnosticBundle`.
`MegaRacIpmiReadPolicy`, `MegaRacRedfishReadPolicy`, `MegaRacConsoleReference`,
`MegaRacAccountReceipt`, `MegaRacBootRow` are the row's shape, declared here because the adapter is
what consumes them.

**Row `mtcollins1_boot_row`** — the mtcollins1 receipts, and nothing else: artifact prefix,
diagnostics path, publish allowance, the IPMI and Redfish read bounds, the service-root path, the
census socket population, the planned IPMI read count (derived from that row's SMpro site), the two
census reference scopes, `mtcollins1_boot_console(path)`, `mtcollins1_boot_account_receipt(e)`, and
**`mtcollins1_boot_row(controller)`** which answers `BootRowFor { row }` only for the endpoint its
receipts were measured on and `BootRowEndpointMismatch { expected, observed }` for any other.

### The row is the only thing that names a machine

`MegaRacBootRow { controller, operator_host, label, ipmi, redfish, publish_allowance,
sensor_sockets, retained_artifact_prefix, diagnostics_path, console_reference }`.
Every read function takes `row: MegaRacBootRow` as its first parameter (≈45 of them), and the two
host-shaped strings in the text are row-derived: the title is `concat(row.label, " boot
diagnostics")` and the media-loss reason names `row.label`. There is no host name or board name
anywhere in the adapter except the vocabulary import of `mtcollins1_power_on_account` (which owns
`PowerOnAccount`/`PowerOnEvidence` — left to the untangle of that root), and no branch on one.
The account verdict arrives from the row as `MegaRacAccountReceipt`, so the adapter never opens a
power-on evidence record.

### Raw / neutral, stored once

Per review: the bundle stores the RAW records only (`bundle.run: MegaRacRunRecord`). No neutral
`BootRunRecord` beside them — that would be two representations of one fact that can disagree. A
neutral consumer asks for one:

```
megarac_boot_run_record(raw: MegaRacRunRecord, console: ConsoleReading,
                        identity: AttemptIdentityReading,
                        harness: List<HarnessFinding>) -> BootRunRecord
```
with per-record mappings `megarac_host_power`, `megarac_presentation`,
`megarac_stale_power_off_record`, `megarac_media_attach_record`, `megarac_handoff_call_result`,
`megarac_handoff_media_record`, `megarac_end_media_record`, `megarac_power_after_attempt`,
`megarac_override_consumption`, `megarac_harness_findings_neutral`,
`megarac_console_diagnostic_ref`. `test.claim.machine_intake.megarac_boot_record_mapping_witness`
pins every raw arm into the matching neutral arm (transport-only fields like the attach `attempt`
handle and the session `detail` are deliberately dropped; `CensusEnd` -> `Terminal`).

### Required REDs

`test.claim.machine_intake.megarac_boot_row_witness`:
- **a non-mtcollins1 row derives its own bundle** — an srv9 row (its own endpoint, operator host,
  artifact prefix, reference scopes and socket count) renders a bundle that carries srv9's own
  receipts and the string `mtcollins1` nowhere in it; a second claim pins that mtcollins1's own row
  still renders mtcollins1, so the first claim cannot pass by both rows forgetting who they are.
- **a mismatched binding refuses** — asking the mtcollins1 row for another board's endpoint answers
  `BootRowEndpointMismatch { expected, observed }`, and the refusal carries no row, so there is no
  half-built row to reach the reads with.
Plus: one boot procedure for every machine (two rows, one set of procedure fields, two different
bundles), and the row admits the endpoint its receipts were measured on.

### The boot_run re-point is IN this PR (manager ruling: delete-first means one PR)

`gunbc.machine_intake.mtcollins1_boot_run` is re-pointed here so the branch lands green and
self-contained. It is MECHANICAL: no logic change, no new shapes.

102 lines changed, all of them one of the four bullets below (HEAD vs `origin/main`; the file is
3006 lines, so ~97% is untouched):

`37, 107-122, 227, 557, 1600-1601, 1987-1993, 2002-2008, 2041-2047, 2069-2074, 2144-2173,
2310-2321, 2335-2343, 2357-2359, 2376, 2432-2435, 2460, 2476-2479, 2511-2513, 2536, 2631-2638,
2667, 2683-2690, 2727-2746, 2756-2777, 2787-2790, 2799-2804, 2813-2818, 2827, 2858-2869`

`1987-1993`…`2536` the read call sites gaining `row:`; `2631-2690` the renderers; `2727-2827` the
five assembly sites (types only — see the bullet below on why no field changed);
`2858-2869` the receipt lines.

- Its 66-name import of the deleted root is now four imports, one per owner.
- 80 body lines are renames only: `MtCollins1BootRunRecord -> MegaRacRunRecord`, the five raw
  record families -> `MegaRac*`, the ten read fns -> `megarac_boot_*`.
- 15 read call sites pass `row: mtcollins1_boot_row_value` — the same single row value the checked

- The **two bundle assembly sites** (the census-end arm and the `BmcAccessHeld` arm, ~2786 and

author: arpan404
body:
## What the owner saw

Thread "Respond to a Greeting" (nivra-rij) was created on Cursor Composer 2.5. `yo` failed because Cursor reported the account was out of usage. The person then picked Codex GPT-6.1 Sol in the composer. The daemon accepted the `thread.switch`, queued it, and failed it at once. It wrote "Cursor SDK runtime/account changes require a fresh portable fork or thread.create with handoffFrom; the source checkpoint is preserved" into the switch state and into a "Couldn't switch the model" notice. `hi` then went to Cursor again and failed the same way. The events are in `~/.ace-next/events.sqlite`, thread `8cd90eb0-…`, seq 22126–22157.

## Root cause

`apps/daemon/src/engine/transitions.ts:130-137` (on main) throws that internal message for any provider or account change out of a Cursor SDK thread. That refusal is correct. ADR 0043 pins an SDK checkpoint to its thread and account: the adapter keys its checkpoint and boundary journal by `(account home, threadId)` (`packages/adapter-cursor/src/checkpoints.ts:6`). Re-entering Cursor, or entering another account, in place would replay or drop journal frames. The bug was elsewhere:

1. No client followed the ADR. The web composer sent `thread.switch` anyway, and admission (`transition-handler.ts`) accepted it. The refusal only surfaced later, as raw text.
2. Portable forks refused any account change (`fork_account_mismatch_use_switch`). So even a correct client had no way to change a Cursor thread's account.
3. Transcript: a turn's "failure" was the last error notice in its stretch. A failed action notice that arrived after the run ended (the switch) replaced the run's own failure, so the real failure showed as a second row. `FailedTurn` also dropped the failure's words whenever a model was known, which is why the second failure read only "Turn failed · Composer 2.5". Details showed the summary again (as `provider: <same text>`).

## Fix

- **One rule** (`packages/core/src/switch-route.ts`, re-exported as `threadSwitchRoute` from `@ace/ui-core`): each change is `in_place`, `new_thread` (a Cursor SDK thread leaving Cursor or its account) or `unsupported` (an ACP agent in another provider's thread). The daemon and the web read the same rule.
- **Daemon**: `thread.switch` admission refuses `new_thread` changes up front with `switch_requires_new_thread`. Nothing is queued and no notice is written. The execution-time guard stays as a backstop with plain copy. Portable forks may now name another account (native forks still may not), which is how a Cursor account change continues.
- **Web composer**: a `new_thread` pick asks first ("Continue in a new thread?"), then waits in the chip ("Continues in a new thread with your next message"). The next message goes out as a single durable `thread.fork` from the newest finished turn, whatever its outcome, on the picked model and account. The UI then opens the new thread. The Cursor thread and its checkpoint are untouched. ACP models show "Starts new threads only" in the picker of other providers' threads.
- **Transcript**: failed actions (switch, Stop, answers) are never a turn's failure. A failed turn is one row, "Turn failed · <model> · <reason>". Details shows only text the summary doesn't already say.
- ADR 0043 amendment and the Cursor verification notes are updated.

## What works now

| From \ To | Codex | Claude | Cursor | OpenCode | Pi | ACP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Codex | model change in place | in place | in place | in place | in place | not offered (picker says so) |
| Claude | in place | model change in place | in place | in place | in place | not offered |
| OpenCode | in place | in place | in place | model change in place | in place | not offered |
| Pi | in place | in place | in place | in place | model change in place | not offered |
| ACP | in place | in place | in place | in place | in place | same agent only |
| Cursor (SDK) | new thread with context | new thread | model change in place; other account → new thread | new thread | new thread | not offered |

"In place" means the same thread with a portable handoff. Same-provider account changes on non-Cursor providers still go through account migration, as before.

## Tests

- `apps/daemon/src/engine/provider-switch-matrix.process.test.ts` (32 cases). Each case switches between fake adapters and checks that the next message reaches the right provider exactly once, with the prior context. The Cursor cases also check the source checkpoint still continues.
- `apps/web/src/features/thread/provider-continuation.test.tsx`: picking Codex on a Cursor thread sends the next message once, to a new Codex thread with lineage, and the Cursor thread gets no new message. ACP shows as unavailable before anything is sent.
- `apps/web/src/features/thread/failed-turn-rows.test.tsx`: one error row per failed turn; Details never repeats the summary.
- Existing Cursor and switch tests now expect the up-front refusal. `turn-structure` now expects no Details when Details would repeat the summary.

`bun run fmt`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `check:size` and `check:deps` pass. The scoped vitest runs pass. `check:ui` fails on `provider-account-icon.tsx` and `app-preview.tsx`, which this PR doesn't touch.

## Not in this PR

- The "Failed after" row order belongs to fix/model-option-params.
- Cursor's "You're out of usage" is classified as a generic provider failure, so it reads "Cursor couldn't finish the request. Try again." That wording is misleading. It is adapter-cursor error classification (fix/cursor-provider).
- A continuation carries text only (`thread.fork` input). A draft with attachments is kept, and the composer says so.
- iOS has no in-thread provider switch today, so there was nothing to route there.

author: pryce-turner
body:
## What and why

Two gaps found while testing on the devbox (ticket `devbox-small-gaps`).

**`apply_bqsr` didn't store its BAM index.** GATK writes `<name>.bai` beside the recalibrated BAM by default, but the task stored only the BAM. `mark_duplicates` and `sort_sam` store theirs, so fetching their BAMs brings the `.bai`, but fetching `apply_bqsr`'s didn't. It now stores the index as an `AlignmentIndex` (`alignment_cid` = the recalibrated BAM), as `mark_duplicates` does.

**`gatk_env` set no `resources=`**, which AGENTS.md requires of every TaskEnvironment. Its pods got the platform default: a 256 Mi request and a 512 Mi limit (measured on the devbox). It now requests 1 Gi with a 6 Gi limit, not `scrna_env`'s 2 Gi: the germline workflow holds three `gatk_env` pods at once (the workflow, `prepare_reference` or `preprocess_sample`, and the tool). The devbox node has 7,934 Mi allocatable with 2,094 Mi already requested by the cluster and the dashboard, so three 2 Gi requests (6,144 Mi) wouldn't fit beside them (inferred from those numbers). The reasoning is in a comment on `gatk_env` and in `.opencode/reference/devbox_workarounds.md`.

## Verification

Measured 2026-10-14.

- **`test_apply_bqsr_recalibrates_bam`** now also finds the stored index with `assemble(asset="alignment_index", alignment_cid=…)`. Before the fix it found none; after, one, named `NA12829_TP53_markdup_recalibrated.bai`. The task raises if GATK didn't write the file, and it didn't raise, so GATK does write it.
- **Tasks tier**: 37 passed (gatk and general), 15 passed (scrna).
- **Devbox**: `pytest -m devbox tests/devbox/test_germline.py` passes (2 tests, 2m36s). All 11 of the germline run's pods, from the workflow down to `joint_call_gvcfs`, ran with a 1Gi request and a 6Gi limit. The previous run's pods had 256Mi/512Mi.
- `apply_bqsr` isn't on the devbox germline path, which runs no BQSR without known sites, so the tasks-tier test is its evidence.

## Deferred

Nothing. Real-sized data on Union will need larger per-task limits than 6 Gi; that's for when it's run there.

author: taimoor-link-pricer
body:
## Merge order
Built on top of #13 (the search endpoint `search_sites` uses). **Merge #13 first**, then this one; the diff here then shrinks to the MCP work only. Merging this alone would also bring in everything in #13.

**Before merging:** add `MCP_OAUTH_SECRET` (random, at least 32 characters) to the Vercel production environment. Without it OAuth stays off and `/api/mcp` behaves exactly as it does today.

## What
AI apps (Claude.ai, ChatGPT) can connect to `/api/mcp` by signing the user in with their normal LinkPricer account, instead of pasting an API key.

- **OAuth 2.1 per the MCP auth spec:** `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, dynamic client registration (`/api/oauth/register`), PKCE S256, refresh tokens (`/api/oauth/token`).
- **Stateless:** client ids, codes and tokens are HMAC-signed with `MCP_OAUTH_SECRET`. No new tables, no migration.
- **Sign-in:** `/oauth/authorize` sends signed-out users through `/login` (and `/signup`, whose cross-links now keep `?redirect=`) and back, then shows an Allow screen naming the app's return address. The screen is styled like the login card, pending a proper design.
- **Billing:** calls are charged to the user's active API key, looked up on every call. Regenerating a key keeps apps connected; blocking it disconnects them all. Users without a key can connect and are told to create one.
- **`/api/mcp`:** returns 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=…` when there are no credentials, which is how apps know to start sign-in. API keys work as before (Bearer or `x-api-key`).
- **New `search_sites` tool** over the search endpoint: default 10 results, max 25 (charged per site returned).
- The pricing and search handlers accept an already-resolved key hash.

## Tested
- `lib/mcp/oauth.test.ts`: full flow plus forged, expired, wrong-client, wrong-verifier and wrong-audience cases. Whole suite: 370 passing; `tsc` clean.
- Locally, end to end, as an app would run it: 401 challenge → discovery → registration → authorize (signed out → `/login` redirect; signed in → Allow screen) → cross-site POST refused (403) → Cancel returns `access_denied` → Allow returns code + state → wrong PKCE refused → tokens → `initialize`, `tools/list`, `get_link_prices`, `search_sites` → tampered token 401 `invalid_token` → refresh. API-key access re-checked through both headers.

author: ahouprojectmaimai-beep
body:
This PR introduces a complete booking and scheduling system for TUMIKI, enabling customers to self-serve book appointments with automatic Google Calendar integration, email notifications, and admin management.

## Summary
Implements a full-stack appointment booking system built on Cloudflare Workers + D1 SQLite, with:
- Customer-facing booking interface with real-time availability checking
- Automatic Google Calendar event creation with Google Meet links
- Email confirmations via Resend or Gmail API
- Admin dashboard for managing bookings and settings
- Webhook-based calendar synchronization to detect external changes
- Rate limiting and CSRF protection

## Key Changes

**Core Booking Logic** (`src/lib/booking.ts`)
- Booking creation with input validation, availability checking, and conflict detection
- Support for three meeting modes: online (Google Meet), office, and customer location
- Booking state management (pending → confirmed → cancelled/failed)
- Rescheduling and cancellation with token-based access control
- Automatic cleanup of expired pending bookings

**Calendar Integration** (`src/lib/google.ts`, `src/lib/sync.ts`)
- Google OAuth 2.0 authentication for admin users
- Calendar API integration for event creation/updates with automatic Meet URL generation
- Free/busy checking across multiple calendars
- Webhook-based sync to detect external calendar changes (deletions, moves)
- Idempotent synchronization to handle concurrent updates safely

**Availability Engine** (`src/lib/availability.ts`, `src/lib/time.ts`)
- Timezone-aware date/time handling with DST support
- Slot availability calculation accounting for busy times, pending holds, and buffer periods
- Configurable working hours, duration, step size, and booking horizon
- Per-day and date-range availability queries

**Admin Interface** (`public/js/admin.js`, `src/worker/index.ts`)
- Booking list with filtering (upcoming/past/all)
- Booking detail view with edit/cancel/resend capabilities
- Settings management (hours, duration, location, calendar selection)
- Google account connection/disconnection
- Email send history with retry functionality

**Customer Interfaces**
- Booking form (`public/js/book.js`) with mode selection, calendar picker, and customer info
- Booking management (`public/js/manage.js`) for viewing, rescheduling, and canceling
- Token-based access (no login required)

**Email System** (`src/lib/mail.ts`)
- Dual provider support: Resend (default) and Gmail API
- HTML + plain text templates with booking details, meeting links, and management URLs
- Admin notification emails for new bookings

**Database** (`migrations/0001_init.sql`)
- Bookings table with status tracking, time blocks, and location details
- Google account credentials (encrypted)
- Rate limit tracking
- Sync state for calendar webhook handling

**Configuration** (`src/lib/settings.ts`)
- Comprehensive settings for availability rules, locations, and integrations
- Timezone support with sensible defaults

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Atomic booking**: Uses SQLite's transaction semantics to prevent double-booking
- **Token-based auth**: Customers access their bookings via secure tokens instead of login
- **Timezone handling**: All internal times are UTC seconds; display/input uses Intl API for proper DST handling
- **Conflict detection**: Post-creation check for external calendar conflicts with automatic cancellation
- **Rate limiting**: Fixed-window rate limiting on availability queries and booking management endpoints
- **CSRF protection**: Origin check on state-changing API calls
- **Idempotent webhooks**: Calendar sync handles duplicate notifications safely
- **No build step**: Frontend uses vanilla JS with no bundler requirement
- **Zero-cost hosting**: Designed to run entirely on Cloudflare's free tier

## Testing
Includes comprehensive test suite (`test/`) with:
- Booking creation, rescheduling, and cancellation flows
- Availability calculation with various busy/hold scenarios
- Time zone conversions and DST handling
- Mock Google Calendar and email implementations

author: rigerc
body:
Skills currently install from synced registry snapshots, so users cannot obtain current upstream content or update outdated installations. This switches installation to each skill’s upstream GitHub repository and adds `autoskills update` with interactive selection, `-y`, and `--dry-run`.

- Resolve the default branch to a commit, discover the skill and supporting files, verify downloaded bytes against Git blob hashes, and record source path, commit, content hashes, and agents in `skills-lock.json`. Reuse repository lookups within a batch and bound concurrent downloads.
- Compare skill file fingerprints rather than repository HEAD alone. Update changed skills, remove obsolete files, preserve existing agent drawers, migrate old `autoskills-registry` lock entries, and report individual failures with a nonzero exit code. Download and stage files before replacing an existing installation.
- Support Pi’s `.pi/skills` project drawer and discover `~/.pi/agent/skills` in the desk. Remove `claude.ts` and all `CLAUDE.md` cleanup; existing user instructions remain untouched.
- Update documentation and site copy. Historical registry reviews are not presented as reviews of current upstream content.

Validation: all 344 Node tests pass, including CLI and desk integration coverage; the 52 CLI tests also pass after the final output-label change. Changed files pass oxlint and oxfmt; repository-wide oxlint completes with existing warnings. Repository-wide formatting passes when excluding HTML (the formatter’s HTML workers require unavailable process-memory facilities in this sandbox). A live smoke test installed `anthropics/skills/frontend-design` into the Pi drawer and then reported it up to date.

The pinned TypeScript 7 compiler could not run here: its native executable fails during initialization because `/proc/self/exe` is unavailable. No dependency versions or lockfiles were changed.

body:
The flash message styling discussed on Oct 14, plus the Dispatches default you asked for in #6.

## Flash messages
- "You're logged in." (on Arrests) and "You're logged out." (on the home page) now look like confirmations: a soft green box with dark green text, a green edge, and a check mark. That matches the red error box and the amber out-of-date notice.
- New color tokens: `--colorSuccess`, `--colorSuccessText`, and `--colorSuccessSurface`. Contrast is 8.3:1 for the text on the green, 4.6:1 for the check mark, and 6.2:1 for the green box against the blue band.
- The check mark is a small inline SVG that screen readers skip, so they read only the message, as before (`role="status"`). Its size and stroke are set on the SVG itself, so it draws as a small check even if the stylesheet hasn't loaded.

## Dispatches: All time by default
As you asked in #6, the history now shows every day on record unless another range is chosen, like the home page.
- All time links to plain `/dispatches`, and Last 7 days gets a dated link.
- A bad range falls back to all dates, with the same message as the home page.
- **One thing to watch:** every visit to /dispatches now counts every call on record. That's fast with about 20 days of calls, but at 1,000+ calls a day it will grow. If the page gets slow in a few months, a short cache fixes it.
- An end date before the first call with no start date (only possible by typing a link) now gives an empty one-day range instead of a backwards one.

## Checked
- `npm test`: 135 pass, 1 of them new.
- A local server with made-up calls from Sep 25 and a throwaway login:
  - /dispatches defaults to "Sep 25, 2026 – Oct 14, 2026 (20 days)", with All time selected.
  - A bad date falls back to all dates.
  - Logging in and logging out each show their message once, in the new style.
  - Screenshots checked at desktop and phone width.

## How to check after it deploys
1. Log in: "You're logged in." shows in the green box on Arrests. Log out: "You're logged out." shows on the home page.
2. Open /dispatches: the history shows all time, with All time selected.

author: j3w1
body:
Implements PR-B of PES #63 (Pod 0.13.3). When a coordinator is lost with remote effects pending, a successor's claim now carries those Governor rows and settles them only by Pod's own readback. PR-A (#65, 0.13.0) delivered R1, R2, R4 and R5.

Requirements source: #63 R3 and the R6 parts it needs, from SEAL j3w1/dev-casaelida#133 (R4, AC4).

## What changes (R118, extending R110)

- **Carried rows.** R110's checks stay unchanged: loss, Run and generation, coordinator identity, a complete worker list and Dispatch settlement. On top of them, a claim carries the predecessor's pending or UNKNOWN rows of these kinds:
  - push and pr_update;
  - requested or publication-derived workflow_dispatch;
  - validation_rerun, remote_diagnostic and cancel_validation;
  - merge.
- **Still refused:**
  - release and deploy rows;
  - unresolved admissions, and reserved admissions that have a Dispatch;
  - live workers;
  - unreadable records or journals;
  - rows whose readback could never settle them.
- **Recording.** Carried rows are copied into the successor's own journal, marked with the predecessor and its record id. The predecessor's journal and files stay byte-identical apart from the existing `continued_by` link. The predecessor's status reads the carried rows' later settlement, following re-carried rows through later claims.
- **Settlement is readback only.** A carried row is never resubmitted, cancelled or settled by assertion:
  - Absence reads FAILED only after the recorded start time, plus the call's limit, plus a margin.
  - A pr_update settles only from its pull request.
  - A merge settles PASS only through R93's Git checks against its originally admitted candidate and base. It stays pending while its pull request is open.
  - A carried consent never authorizes a new effect.
- **Interrupted, chained and historical claims.** One incomplete-claim predicate covers every record shape that claims leave, across Pod 0.10.0–0.13.2 and the current writer:
  - A successor named by an incomplete claim refuses its own work and closure until the claim completes. Exact-decision replay, owner handoff and runtime rebind stay open.
  - An objective whose own claim is incomplete is never a predecessor.
  - Two claims naming one successor refuse as ambiguous.
  - A claim measures every record it would write, including capacity and continuity history, before it writes anything. A recorded closure still answers a repeated close as finished.
- **Documented limitations (liveness only).** Repeated losses after the link can exhaust the continuity history. An ambiguous double claim, or an already-linked oversized carry from an earlier candidate, has no supported completion route. While a Pod record is unreadable, it holds unstarted objectives' work. In every case effects stay visibly unsettled and nothing is falsely recorded or closed. A claim is a cooperative Pod record, not an operating-system fence against an already-running process.

## Compatibility

Existing claims, continued records, closures and retirements read unchanged. Tests run the genuine 0.12.0 and 0.13.x readers against carried journals and earlier-shaped `continued_by` links. Earlier Pods read a reserved successor as unsupported during a claim's crash window, as documented. Skill guidance is not lengthened. Suite-lane durations are recorded from main's run 38608288889.

## Verification on this exact head

- All 11 local milestone gates in `docs/validation.md` pass on the clean commit (unit suite 1331 tests).
- A fresh independent audit, then delta reviews after each correction round, and re-checks that PR-A's guarantees hold. Every SAFETY finding was corrected; the remaining findings are the liveness limitations above, recorded by owner decision. The reports are kept with the delivery evidence.
- Not run here: hosted CI (this pull request runs it), installation on the owner's host, and the controlled native trial (#63 PoD#7).

fixed `flush(60ms)` for mocked API data, then assert synchronously with `getBy*` or by reading
state an MSW handler sets. Under machine load the data hadn't arrived within that window, failing
tests that were actually correct (#166's cancel flow, #168's card amounts, the "Priya S." flake
in `pages.render.test.tsx`).

Each racy site now awaits the actual condition it depends on (`findBy*`, or `waitFor()` for
request bodies / callbacks / localStorage) instead of a fixed timer, following the precedent
already set by PR #175 for the `ReceiptsPage` #168 fix.

- **9 files changed, ~25 call sites rewritten:** `ReceiptsPage.test.tsx` (7), `ReceiptDetailPage.test.tsx` (2), `CheckoutPage.test.tsx` (3), `ItemDetailDrawer.test.tsx` (3), `EditCustomerPage.test.tsx` (1), `CouponsPage.test.tsx` (1), `ReportsPage.test.tsx` (4), `pages.render.test.tsx` (3), `PublicLayout.test.tsx` (1).
- **`flush()` itself is unchanged and still exported** — kept for the handful of sites where settling a debounce is genuinely the point (`ReportsPage.test.tsx`'s two `DEBOUNCE_SETTLE_MS` sites), with the assertions that follow now wrapped in `waitFor` rather than trusting the timer alone.
- **The other ~130 `flush()` call sites across the 20 files that use it were inspected and left as-is** — they're already safe: followed by `findBy*`/`waitFor`, driven only by local state (clicks, localStorage, modal open/close), or are legitimate "nothing happened" negative checks where elapsed time is the point.
- **Two assertions were strengthened, not just de-flaked:** `ItemDetailDrawer.test.tsx`'s delete-conflict test now also asserts the 409 error message text; `pages.render.test.tsx`'s gallery-401 test now asserts the "No images to show" empty state actually renders.
- **No production code changes.** Test-only, per the issue's scope.
- **No `.at(-1)` or other post-ES2020 APIs** — all array access uses `arr[arr.length - 1]`/`arr[0]` indexing (see "Review process" below for why this mattered specifically on this issue).

## Review process

This went through the full `/work-issue-auto` plan-review pipeline: a planning pass, then three
independent personas (devils-advocate, tech-lead, business-lead) reviewed the plan in parallel
against the issue's acceptance criteria, this repo's conventions, and the actual current file
contents (not assumed state).

### This issue was halted once before re-queueing

A prior run of this pipeline on #176 halted at the Triage stage on a Must-halt Blocker:
`devils-advocate` flagged that the original plan's test code used `requests.at(-1)`, and
`Array.prototype.at` is ES2022 while this repo's `frontend/tsconfig.json` targets
`lib: ["ES2020", ...]` — `pnpm type-check` genuinely rejects it (`TS2550`). The repo owner
independently confirmed the rejection and re-queued the issue with a binding planning constraint:
use `arr[arr.length - 1]` indexing instead. This run's plan and build honored that constraint
throughout, and `pnpm type-check` passes clean on this branch.

### This run's persona review: unanimous APPROVE, zero Blockers

All three personas independently re-verified the plan's line numbers and behavioral claims
against the live repo (the tree had moved since the prior halted run — PR #177 touched several
of the same files) and found no Must-halt issues. Only cosmetic/process **Suggestions** were
raised, all of which were applied during the build:

- Avoid double-querying `getAllByRole('button')` in `ReceiptsPage.test.tsx`'s pickup-date-headings
  test — capture the result once inside the `waitFor` callback.
- In `pages.render.test.tsx`, switch the `getByText` destructure to `findByText` cleanly (and drop
  the now-unused import) rather than leaving a stale reference that could trip `noUnusedLocals`.
- Don't over-justify `ReportsPage.test.tsx`'s retained `flush(DEBOUNCE_SETTLE_MS)` calls with an
  inaccurate "load-bearing against a superseding request" rationale in a comment — the debounce's
  initial state is already seeded from the URL param, so no comment was added.

A few other suggestions were about the plan document and the orchestrator's own test-execution
process (not about the test files themselves) and didn't require any code change.

### Triage

Not dispatched — the consolidated Blocker list from all three personas was empty, so there was
nothing to classify as Must-halt or Auto-absorb.

### Coverage stage

A follow-up review of the committed diff found no weakened assertions (every `waitFor`/`findBy*`
replacement either preserves or strengthens what the test verifies — no negative assertion was
converted to a `waitFor`, which could pass trivially before the real condition is met) and no
missing coverage — this is a wait-mechanics fix with no new behavior, so no new tests were needed
beyond the two strengthened assertions noted above.

## Test plan

- Backend: `./gradlew test` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL (unaffected by this change; confirmed green both
  before and after).
- Frontend: `pnpm test` — 352/352 passing, identical count to the pre-change baseline. No test was
  added, deleted, skipped, or weakened.
- `pnpm type-check` — clean (confirms the no-`.at()` constraint holds).
- `pnpm lint` — clean except the pre-existing `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` error in
  `AddItemPage.tsx`, which is explicitly out of scope for this issue and untouched.
- Pre-commit hook (frontend `type-check` + `vitest`) ran and passed on this commit.
- Not run in this sandbox (no multi-core load-generation harness / long-running loop available to
  this automated pipeline): the issue's own suggested 5×-consecutive-run-under-simulated-load
  check. The fix targets the documented root cause (fixed timers racing against async data
  delivery) with condition-based waits, which is deterministic by construction — but a human
  may want to run the 5× loaded-machine check from the issue's acceptance criteria before/after
  merge for extra confidence.

**Exact immutable parent:** E12 #2143 `47fb9fac2e4275df53c2cfa2f50564bf48895ae7`. The office pass takes the number as `--discussion <n>` and never searches titles. So the discussion should be titled "Read v2 feedback" for the card to point at it.

author: mberto79
body:
## Summary

`viscous_force` stops with a `MethodError` when the requested patch has a `Slip` (or `Symmetry`) velocity boundary condition. The same error stops the `forces=` history of `godunov!` (including with `LocalTimeStepping`) as soon as a Slip patch is listed, in serial runs too.

## Cause

`viscous_force` takes the wall velocity from the `value` of the velocity boundary condition and computes `U[cell] - value`. `Slip(:name)` and `Symmetry(:name)` store the placeholder `0` (an integer), so the subtraction `SVector{3} - 0` has no method. Even with a vector value, a `Symmetry` patch would report a spurious shear from the tangential velocity.

## Fix

A patch whose velocity boundary condition is `Slip` or `Symmetry` exerts no shear, so `viscous_force` now returns `[0, 0, 0]` for it before the kernel is launched. The check is on the host, so it is the same on CPU and GPU backends. `pressure_force` is unchanged. `Wall` and `Dirichlet` patches take the same path as before.

## Tests

`test/0_TEST_CASES/2d_godunov_supersonic_cylinder.jl` gains a test on the shipped supersonic cylinder mesh, for `Slip` and for `Symmetry` on the top and bottom patches: a `forces=` history over `[:cylinder, :top]` runs, the viscous force on `:top` is exactly zero, the pressure force is non-zero and finite, and direct calls of `viscous_force` and `pressure_force` agree. The test errors on current `main`. Full `Pkg.test()` was run single-threaded.

## Relation to other pull requests

#219 changes the last line of `viscous_force` and `pressure_force` (global sum over ranks). The two branches merge without source conflicts; only the adjacent `CHANGELOG.md` entries conflict, which is resolved by keeping both. The early return for a Slip or Symmetry patch is the same on every rank, so it adds no collective-communication mismatch.

body:
**What changes for a person:** nothing until a switch is turned on: both ship **off**, under `pointerGestures`, the one switch above every event tap, which ships off too; with any of that off no event tap of this feature is installed at all (board 3.4: on by a commit of its own once Q18 holds). With `titleBarDoubleClick` on, a double-click on a **docked** window's title bar frames that window, and again goes back, in place of macOS making it big. With `desktopDoubleClick` on, a double-click on the bare Desktop gives the Desktop the whole view, and again goes back. A tile still opens on one click; with a switch on, the second click of a habitual double-click on it goes nowhere instead of landing in the window just framed. Floating windows, windows Arbor does not arrange, window content, controls in a title bar, the gaps, and any double-click with ⌃ ⌥ ⇧ ⌘ held are left alone.

Stacked on the change that lets macOS's own zoom of a docked window be (board 1.22): the first commit of this branch is that change.

## Judged against the seven rules
| Rule | Verdict |
|---|---|
| 1 never fight macOS | **One double-click, one answer.** Where Arbor takes it, no app sees either half of the second click, so macOS's action cannot run as well; where it does not, Arbor runs nothing and lets macOS's frame be. `neverBothArborAndTheApp` walks every order of three events. **New, the product owner's decision:** framing replaces "make it big" and nothing else: with macOS set to *Minimize* or *Do Nothing* Arbor leaves title bars alone whatever its switch says (no zones, no taps), read afresh at every layout, at the first click of a pair, and when `doctor` or the settings window is asked, which say why in one line |
| 2 nothing moves until something is docked | No zones without a docked window; the Desktop's double-click is not Arbor's where nothing is wider than the Desktop |
| 3 no jolts | The command is an ordinary `zoom` / `back` / `out` / `desktop`: one move per window. The script measures it: one road, never past the gap, one `setFrame`, one layout (a second one is a window put back) |
| 4 front and into view | The first click reaches the app and focuses the window; `zoom` frames it |
| 5 sizes given back | Untouched |
| 6 input is never blocked | **What the Mac run is for, and why it ships off.** A click with an odd count costs a lock and a few rectangles. An even one *inside a title-bar zone* waits while the window server and the app are asked what is under the pointer, from inside the tap's callback, where everybody's input waits too. So (the product owner's numbers) the asking stops at the first answer that settles it (a control: one window list and two reads), **50 ms is the ceiling of the wait**, and when in doubt the click is not Arbor's. The script holds every other foreign click to 10 ms, that one kind to 50, and with a test window that hangs to 100, with nothing after it held up |
| 7 daily use | It is the third of the five moves |

## What was changed on the way here
The feature was written earlier and had never been compiled on this trunk. New in this round: the stand-aside for Minimize and Do Nothing; a press held back when the taps go away is given back while the button is down; the tap hears of an opened tile **before** the windows move, not after (the second click can be quicker than a layout); where a click is destroyed only the Dock's layer over the whole display is looked through, and a widget on the Desktop keeps its clicks (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: no rule made for taking a gesture decides that a click is destroyed); the tap no longer republishes its zones for every frame of a drag; the fakes play a whole double-click (first click, focus, second click, modifiers, macOS's own setting).

## How it is proven
| | |
|---|---|
| **Linux proves** | Every decision is a pure function or controller logic: `DoubleClickZonesTests`, `PointerCoverTests`, `DoubleClickRoleTests`, `DoubleClickGestureTests`, `DoubleClickTests`, `TileClickTests`, `OneDoubleClickOneAnswerTests`, `MacTitleBarActionTests`, scenario 06, and the random walks, which double-click title bars with every switch on and off. The macOS-only part type-checks against the stand-ins. `make gate` on the trunk of 9b4cd51, stacked on the first change: the gate is open, 5,962 tests pass and none fails. Two hunts of 800 walks of 300 steps, with every switch on and as Arbor ships: no failing script holds a double-click |
| **A Mac must run** | `scripts/mac-shell/run.sh scripts/mac-shell/check-F14.sh scripts/mac-shell/check-macos-double-click.sh`: one run, unattended, under ten minutes. Real double-clicks on the title bars of docked, framed and floating windows, in the gaps, in content, with ⌘, slowly, three times, turning into a drag, on an app that hangs, on a tile, on the Desktop, in Safari's toolbar; at both settings of macOS's tiling and wallpaper click; with macOS's own action at its default, Minimize and Do Nothing. Rehearsed on Linux: 158 of 158 and 78 of 78. The control: on a fake Mac where macOS acts as well as Arbor, 4 ✘ |
| **Judged afterwards** | `fought`, `jolt`: the frames per step (`frames-*.txt`) and a trace of every double-click (`traces/`). `input-held`: the witness at the far end of the taps (`witness.txt`): what is not Arbor's arrives, and how late, with the taps and without. The rubric's third move: the pictures. The script ends with one verdict per switch |

**Questions only a Mac can answer:** does a press that is held back and swallowed keep macOS's own action from running? Does one that is given back arrive whole, once? How long does the look under the pointer hold a click? Does a running Arbor see `AppleActionOnDoubleClick` change? What does a person see of macOS's sweep at a Desktop double-click, as macOS comes?

## Known, and said
- A press held back at the very moment the taps are taken away can be overtaken by its own mouse-up (a few milliseconds; the rectangle's tap has the same shape).
- The title bar is the top 28 points for every app (`titleBarHeight`); below that a unified toolbar's double-click is macOS's, and stays.
- Electron apps, Chrome, a hidden title bar, a panel over a title bar, a file on the Desktop: the spec lists how a script can check each; not written yet.

author: realxhabib
body:
In liveServer matches (Frontline today) every kill and the clock end were saved to Supabase from every player's browser, so concurrent writes conflicted. Now the match room on the Claude Arcade server holds the state: it orders writes (compare-and-set on its version) and broadcasts every copy, and nothing reaches Supabase during the match except heartbeats and the result submits at the end.

- live-room.ts: an optional RoomState on the transport. On every sign-in the host offers its cached copy, so a new or restarted room starts from the newest copy any player has; writes wait up to 5 s for the room's first copy.
- play-room.tsx: state.set goes to the room while it holds the state, behind the existing write gate (checked against the room's version too), and is refused once the match isn't active (the room isn't told). The room's copies reach the app as state.change.
- Fallback when the room is gone: hosts write to Supabase again. Its copy is still at the version from before the match, so the host first stores its newer copy with the new rebase_match_state (seated players, active match, forward only); the demo backend mirrors it as rebaseState.
- Accepted loss: if the room's server dies and every player reloads, that match's state is gone; the abandoned-match job ends it.

author: mahelbir
body:
## What

- New setting, Settings → Autofill → "Fill and save on HTTP pages". Default off.
- Off: no change. Fill, verification-code fill and save offers on plain-http pages keep refusing with the same "non-HTTPS" errors.
- On: those same gates open on http:// pages. https:// and local dev hosts (localhost, 127.0.0.1, *.test) behave exactly as before.

## Why

Routers, printers and internal tools often sit on plain http. PassBridge lists logins there but refuses to fill or save, which reads as broken to someone who knowingly wants it. The gate stays closed unless it is turned on, and the options row says plainly that it opens every HTTP page and the traffic is unencrypted.

## How

- The six copy-pasted https checks in the background become one `isFillUrlAllowed(url)` helper that reads the setting. No error strings change, no content-script changes.
- `drive-http-fill.mjs` serves the harness at `127.0.0.1.nip.io` (resolves to 127.0.0.1, not a local-dev hostname, so the page counts as plain http). The default run asserts the refusal, the setting is flipped in storage, and the same page then fills. Registered in run-all.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` / `npm test`: green
- The new driver's assertions were checked against a headed Chromium. Refused by default, fills when on. The Browser tests workflow (manual) runs it in CI too.

body:
Production deployments stop before migration because the workflow compares the new migration version with `/version` from the old API. Coolify's pre-deploy hook also runs the old image's migrator.

This change delegates the release to a restricted, durable VPS controller. It verifies current official main and CI, reads the real PostgreSQL history, checks applied migration hashes, builds the candidate, exports the deletion journal, encrypts and restores a backup, rehearses the upgrade twice and probes the candidate before live migration. It then derives EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION from that release, deploys the same revision through the official Coolify API and verifies public commit/schema/readiness. Releases are serialized and survive an Actions SSH disconnect. A failed or partial migration never triggers an automatic down/restore. Private terminal release copies expire after sixty days; the cumulative deletion journal and migration ledger are preserved.

Validation: 26 release safety tests; actionlint; actual isolated PostgreSQL16 backup/restore, synthetic0036 upgrade/idempotency/readiness and failed0037 rejection; no production schema changes. CI now runs the policy checks and real Docker/PostgreSQL rehearsal. Full verification passed on final head815d707: https://github.com/am-p/app-loyalty/actions/runs/38677930946.

Activation before merge: the reviewed controller and forced-command SSH public key are prepared on the VPS. A repository administrator must add secret `PUNTAZO_PRODUCTION_SSH_KEY` and variable `PUNTAZO_PRODUCTION_SSH_HOST`; the private key remains in the operator's protected credential directory and is not in this PR. The installed controller must match the merged main file. Details and recovery: docs/production-deployment.md.

Integration with open PR#34: its0036–0040 SQL files still need an operational compatibility review and `-- deploy: expand` declarations before integration; keep the new backend.yml checks when resolving that workflow's overlap. This PR adds no production migrations and does not approve/publish PR#34's product behavior. Contract/destructive migrations remain a reviewed maintenance operation.

author: nava308
body:
Follows #90 (merged).

## What changes

1. **Prototype tests run only when they matter** (`ci.yml`). They take about 68 s of the ~2 min Build and test job. A new first step reads the PR's diff and runs them only when it touches something the tests read: `brand/`, `docs/` (they check `data-model.md`), `tests/` and `.github/` (the personal-data guard scans them), `agent-sops/`, `scripts/ui-audit.mjs`, any root file (README, CLAUDE.md, `package.json`, the lockfile), or `packages/shared/src/profile.ts` / `documents.ts`. Pushes to `main` always run them. If the diff can't be read, they run.
2. **Design-only PRs skip the Integration deploy** (`integration.yml`). The existing Markdown-only skip now also covers `brand/`, `tests/prototype/`, `agent-sops/`, and `scripts/ui-audit.mjs`. No stack deploys any of those, and CI tests them. A PR like #90 waited about 25 minutes for two full AWS deploys.
3. **The prototype is published to GitHub Pages** (`pages.yml`). Every push to `main` that changes `brand/` publishes it to https://jobdeputy.github.io/jobdeputy/, and the site root opens sign-in. Sample data only. Permissions are least privilege: `contents: read` by default, and `pages: write` and `id-token: write` only on the publish job. Actions are pinned by SHA.

## Why it's done in the jobs, not with `paths:` filters

`Build and test` and `Integration` are required checks. A workflow skipped by a `paths:` filter never reports, so the required check stays "Expected" and the merge is blocked. Deciding inside the job, as Integration already does for Markdown, always reports a result.

## One-time setup (a maintainer)

Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: **GitHub Actions**. After this merges, the first push to `main` that touches `brand/` publishes the site, or run **Prototype site** by hand from the Actions tab.

## Docs

`docs/testing.md` (when the prototype tests run), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `docs/tasks/t11-pr-integration-tests.md` (the wider Integration skip), plus the hosted link in `brand/README.md`.

## Verification

- Prototype-test filter checked against sample diffs: `apps/api/...` → skip; `packages/shared/src/profile.ts`, `README.md`, `docs/...`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` → run. `pnpm -r --filter '!@jobdeputy/prototype-tests'` selects the other 8 packages.
- Integration rule checked in bash: `brand/` + `docs/*.md` → no deploy; `brand/` + `pnpm-lock.yaml` → deploys; `apps/api/...` → deploys.
- Pages build step run locally and served under `/jobdeputy/`: `/`, `login-preview.html`, `home-preview.html?skipLoader`, and assets all return 200 (the prototype uses relative paths only).
- Markdown lint (71 files, 0 issues), `pnpm check`, prototype tests (2785 passed).

body:
## Summary

`update_reminder` and `complete_reminder` take an optional `expected` object (`title`, `due`, `completed`): the reminder state the caller read before deciding the write. The Mac compares it with a fresh lookup and refuses the write, saving nothing, when any listed field differs. Owletto side: lobu-ai/owletto#1262, merged; the pointer is its squash commit. The pointer also carries unrelated owletto main commits under `deploy/` (db backups, image updates).

The manifest moves to `apple.reminders@0.4.0` with a new pinned hash; 0.3.0 stays pinned.

## Why

The personal-agent task Automation (#4109) decides reminder changes from a live read, but the write runs later on the Mac, after the queue, any approval, and other concurrent jobs. A person's edit in between was silently overwritten, and the reaction had grown ~600 lines of ledger-based ordering trying to prevent that from the middle tier. The check now lives where the current state is, and #4109's reaction shrinks to plain dispatch.

Contract change (confirmed with Emre): one optional, additive input field on two actions. No DB, API, SDK, or bridge changes. Without `expected` the actions behave as before.

## Test plan

- `bun test packages/device-connectors`: 9 pass (new 0.4.0 assertion + pinned hash + server validator accepts the manifest)
- Swift: `EventKitActionServiceTests` pass, including stale title/due/completion refusals with no save, same-instant different-format due, malformed `expected`; disabling the check fails `stale title: expected an error`
- `make pre-pr` clean
- Swift standalone suite (as CI runs it): 35 passed, 0 failed
- Live on the Mac mini (signed build of this branch, connection advertises 0.4.0 with `expected`), against a throwaway reminder:
  - update with matching `expected`: completed
  - update with a stale title: refused, "Reminder changed since it was read (title); nothing was written"
  - a plain edit, then an update decided before it: refused (due)
  - complete expecting `completed: true` on an open reminder: refused
  - complete with the due date written in another offset: completed
  - same flow through #4109's reaction code: create, update, stale update refused, complete; a reworded re-proposal of the create was skipped
  - test reminders deleted afterwards

author: bigintersmind
body:
Closes #32. ## What **R2: focus no longer drops to ``.** Dismiss, Back and Load Puzzle each unmounted the button holding focus, so a keyboard or screen-reader user had to start again from the top of the page. Focus now goes to the More button, the issue's default: - **From the notice:** `moveFocusOffNotice()` runs before the notice unmounts, and only when focus is actually inside it, because Safari doesn't focus a clicked button. More sits just before the notice, so the next Tab reaches the board, as it would have from the notice. - **From the manual screen:** an effect on `screen` fires when it comes back from `"manual"`. It never runs on mount, so the first Tab still lands on Today (#10). **Beyond the issue: a Retry that lands.** Testing found a fourth case on the same notice: - Retry was `disabled` while its fetch ran, and Chrome takes focus away from a control the moment it becomes disabled. Focus was on `` before the board even arrived, and stayed there after a slow failure. - Retry is now `aria-disabled` while its fetch runs, with the click guarded. This is the same pattern tiles in locked rows already use. - `landed()` moves focus off the notice. It looks and behaves the same: faded to 50%, does nothing while a load runs. **R3: a swap is announced.** A tap or drag swap now announces "Swapped CHEESE with MAGIC WAND." through the hint's existing live region: - The text is screen-reader-only and comes before the resting instruction the hint flips back to. - The hint now has `aria-atomic`, so both sentences are read as one. - **I didn't use the status `

` the issue suggested.** That element holds a failed-load message for as long as the notice shows, so a swap message there would either wait behind it or make it repeat once the note clears. - The note is tied to the board it happened on. A tap swap whose 200ms commit lands after a day switch never speaks on the new board, or on the old one when you switch back. - It's cleared on the next pick-up, a shuffle, or a board landing. **R4: sheet rows are named by their label.** `aria-describedby` on its own doesn't take a hint out of a button's name, because a button's name is built from all the text inside it. So Share and Reset are also `aria-labelledby` their label span. CLAUDE.md's accessibility section records all three, since they're easy to undo by accident. ## Verified `npm run lint`, `npm test` (325) and `npm run build` are clean; `impeccable detect` reports only the known `cream-palette` false positive. I scripted a headless Chrome walk-through over CDP at 390 × 844, using real `Input.dispatchKeyEvent` / `dispatchMouseEvent` input. All 23 checks pass: | | | |---|---| | First Tab on a fresh load | lands on Today | | Enter, Tab, Enter on two tiles | words swap; hint reads `Swapped A with B. Tap a tile to select, then another to swap`; the day-switch status stays empty | | Next pick-up | note cleared | | Mouse drag swap | same note | | Tap swap, then switch day within 200 ms | no note on the new board, nor on the old one after switching back | | Share / Reset in the AX tree | name `Share this site` / `Reset board`; hints are the descriptions | | Back (keyboard), Back (mouse), Load Puzzle | focus on More; focus ring shown for the keyboard, not for the mouse | | Dismiss (keyboard) | focus on More, focus ring shown | | Failed Retry | focus stays on Retry | | Retry with the request held 1.5 s | focus holds on Retry, `aria-disabled`, opacity 0.5 | | Retry that lands | focus on More | Not verified: what VoiceOver or NVDA actually *speak*. The checks read the DOM and the accessibility tree, not speech output, so the announcement of the swap note is worth one pass by ear. Safari's click-focus behaviour is from its documented behaviour, not tested here.

Closes #684

## What

Adds a **policy tier** to `scripts/action_space.py`: mint / split / supersede / park / rewire / replan were mechanisms fired by detectors, never CHOSEN actions. They are now registered actions carrying propensity, settleable and revocable against their producing step.

- **Registry** — new `POLICY` level with six entries (`mint_arm`, `split_claim`, `supersede`, `park`, `rewire_deps`, `replan`; `replan` moves up from orchestration where it sat unused), each with `settleable=True` and the same unimplemented ΔV-estimator stub every other action carries. `ActionSpec.settleable` flag added (default `False`). `plan_segment` demoted to a worker-domain verb (plan-first contract). Registry assert 18 → 23. Every entry REUSES its mechanism by reference — nothing rebuilt.
- **`scripts/planning_actions.py`** (new, 202 lines) — the guardrail: `record()` appends `planning-action/1` rows (action, step_ref, claim_ref, propensity ∈ [0,1]) to `runs/planning-actions.jsonl`; `revoke()` appends `planning-revoke/1` with the producing `step_ref` **resolved from the ledger** (the caller never points the revoke target), one revoke per action.
