author: buildsmarterai
body:
## What
Wave 0 item 4 of the SEO audit remediation plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-seo-audit-remediation.md`, added here). The plan was approved 2026-10-14.

- **Apply layer fails loudly.** `cms.snapshot()` and `cms.approvedRows()` now throw on a Supabase `{ error }`.
  - supabase-js returns errors instead of throwing.
  - Before this change, a failed snapshot still let the live WordPress write go ahead with no rollback copy.
  - A failed query reported a broken run as "applied 0".
- **New content guards.** `scaffold-label`, `ai-summary-heading` and `social-sharing-heading` cover the drafting labels the 2026-10-14 audit found live. `[Insert Table` was already covered by `insert-placeholder`.
  - They run at the apply boundary and in the CI/hook content checks.
  - They catch all 5 live leak pages and do not flag a clean full page.
- **`applyRow` regression test.** When the snapshot rejects, the outcome is `failed`, there are zero adapter writes, and the status is `failed`.
- **`npm test` is hermetic.** It preloads `scripts/lib/hermetic-guard.mjs`.
- **Docs.** The durable plan document, and an `AGENTS.md` test-entry-point note.

## Real-client access: investigation
- Every test file seeds credentials with `process.env.X ||= "dummy"`. `||=` **keeps a real value already in the environment**, for example under `node --env-file=.env --test` or in a shell that exported production credentials.
- supabase-js and the CMS packs look up the global `fetch` on every call, so such a run would talk to the real services.
- The slow calls seen earlier (about 7 s) came from `approvedRows` ignoring an injected client before this fix. They tried to reach the dummy host `x.supabase.co`; no real service was involved, but nothing prevented it.
- CI (`test.yml`) passes no secrets, so CI was not exposed. The exposure was local.

**What the guard does now:**
- forces dummy Supabase, WordPress, Webflow and Google credentials;
- rejects non-loopback `fetch` and `node:http`/`https` requests (googleapis uses gaxios → node-fetch → https);
- exports itself through `NODE_OPTIONS`, so `spawnSync` CLI tests are guarded too.

`test/hermetic.test.mjs` pins all of this, and fails if someone runs a bare `node --test`.

## Evidence
- **Hermetic tests went RED first.** With real-looking credentials exported, before the guard, all 3 initial tests failed; the Supabase-client check made a real 7.6 s network attempt. The 3 http/https, Google-credential and subprocess tests also failed before their guard code; the subprocess check attempted network.
- **The snapshot test is regression coverage, not a historical RED.** It passes on this branch's code. Under a temporary mutation that swallows the snapshot error (`await store.snapshot(...).catch(() => {})`), it fails with `actual: 'applied'`. The mutation was reverted with `git checkout`, and the file is byte-identical.
- **The new guard rules** went RED before implementation (2 tests).

## Gates (this commit)
| Gate | Command | Exit | Units |
|---|---|---|---|

author: spaciouskarter78
body:
## Summary

Fixes three simulator problems found in the code review for publication (`docs/CODE_REVIEW_FOR_PUBLICATION.md`) and two random-stream problems found in QA (`docs/QA_PR5_REPORT.md`). Also picks a new headline training scenario, because the old one is no longer congested under the fixed simulator.

**Dynamics change: results from 0.3.0 are not comparable.**

### Simulator fixes (version 0.4.0)

| | Problem in 0.3.0 | Fix | Measured effect (3x3 grid, same seeds) |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Dijkstra always resolved equal-cost paths the same way, and nodes were served in id order. Symmetric grid corners delivered 72% to 96% of their traffic | Random choice among equal-cost next hops (per-packet ECMP); random service order each step | Spread across source nodes 0.05-0.30 (0.16-0.30 for the hop-count heuristics) → at most 0.028 |
| F2 | One FIFO per node: a packet stuck on one link blocked packets for every other link | One FIFO per outgoing link, sharing the node buffer | Allocated bandwidth unused while traffic waited: 14-20% → 3-4% |
| F3 | The random topology was drawn from the episode seed, so the graph and action space changed with the seed (9 to 16 edges) | Separate `topology_seed`, default 0 | 15 edges for every seed |

The 0.3.0-style behaviour stays available through options (`queueing`, `tie_break`, `service_order`, `topology_seed`). It reproduces 0.3.0 exactly where shortest paths are unique (the ring). Where paths tie, its lowest-id rule differs from networkx's, and delivered traffic can differ by up to 5.8 points (3x3 grid, equal split). Routing distances now use vectorised Floyd-Warshall.

### Random streams (QA findings)
- **Q1:** the network's generator was seeded exactly like the traffic generator and replayed its random numbers. It now uses its own stream, derived from the seed.
- **R2-2** (older than this PR): the `random` baseline in the benchmark scripts had the same problem. It now uses `carla_gym.baselines.policy_rng`.

### Results regenerated
- Baseline scenario matrix rerun (37 scenarios); README tables regenerated by `scripts/update_readme_results.py`, and prose figures checked against the new tables.
- The RL results in `results/grid_b08/` were trained on 0.3.0. They are kept as a record and marked as such in the README.

### Headline scenario (`docs/HEADLINE_SCENARIO.md`)
Under 0.4.0 every baseline delivers about 95% in the old headline (grid, load x1, budget 0.8). The new headline is **grid 3x3, load x1.25, budget 0.6**:
- chosen on validation seeds only, against criteria fixed before each sweep;
- reopened after the Q1 fix, when it failed the stability criterion on 10 seeds;
- **confirmed on 30 validation seeds**, narrowly ahead of load x1 / budget 0.5.

A second-topology sweep found no scenario that meets the criteria. That is reported as it came out, along with the defects found in the criteria.

### Not in this PR
- The training queue for these scenarios is on `feat/rl-scenarios`.
- Speed at larger sizes (F4), traffic model (F5), ECMP/LP baselines.

## Test plan
- [x] 163 tests pass (29 new in `tests/test_model_options.py`)
- [x] QA round 1 on a fresh clone: invariant fuzzing, determinism, identical traffic across policies, single/multi-agent equivalence, API checks, exact benchmark reproduction
- [x] QA round 2 on the Q1 fix (local tree)
- [ ] QA round 3 on the pushed branch
- [ ] Not run on Python 3.10-3.13 or Linux (no CI yet)

body:
Closes #856 (ISSUE-144). The driver conformance harness: all 29 cases of `15` §6 (C-01…C-29, with C-25b under `[C-25]`). `SimulatedDriver` passes all 29. This is new code, so there is no candidate to keep or adapt.

## Built

All under `src/host/modules/suppliers/testing/`:
- **`driverConformance.ts`**, the harness. `runCase` returns a verdict, so the negative tests can show a broken driver failing. There is one test per case, titled with its `C-nn`.
- **`expected.ts`** checks the `15` §1.4 ordering rules first. It then finds each expected event, in order, by its key: `sourceKey`, `turnKey` or request id.
- **`fixtureSet.ts`** loads a fixture folder. It refuses one with a missing or unscrubbed `meta.json`, a person as `capturedBy`, or no `-with-extra` or CRLF variant.
- **`fixtureTransport.ts`** replays recorded output as recorded, split or coalesced. It can inject an early EOF (CH-04) or a hang (CH-05).
- **`recordingSpawn.ts`**, a spawn double composed over the kernel `FakeProcessControl`. The kernel fake itself is untouched.
- **`driverConformance.simulated.ts`** holds the reference options.
- **`driverConformance.lineDriver.ts`** is a JSONL test driver with one fault switch per broken case. It exists because `SimulatedDriver` never spawns and never opens asks.

Also:
- `SimulatedDriver.conformance.test.ts`.
- `fixtures/simulated/simulated/1/**`: 8 hand-written cases (C-01, 05, 08, 13, 20, 25, 28).

## Lead decision (2026-10-14): inapplicable cases on the reference run

The run declares these in `options.cases`, with a comment citing this decision:
- **Spawn cases: C-02, C-03, C-23, C-24 and C-04.** `SimulatedDriver` never spawns, and no simulated process can exit before readiness. Each spawn case is still proven by a broken driver over `recordingSpawn`, next to its conformant twin.
- **No asks: C-06, 07, 09, 10, 11, 14, 15.**
- **One missing capability each:** C-12, 16, 17, 21, 22, 26, 27.

Five cases can never be declared inapplicable: C-18, 19, 25, 28 and 29. `[C-25]` (TC-144-04) shows three ways a declaration is caught:
- a false declaration fails the run;
- an undeclared case with no fixture fails;
- a spawn declaration on a driver that does spawn fails.

## RED evidence

- **`[C-05] a driver that emits turn.ended twice…`** failed with `expected true to be false` against a stub harness. A deliberately wrong expected file then made the conformant reference fail with `expected event #6 (turn.ended …) not found in order`. That file was corrected in its own step.
- **`[ADR-009]` fixture refusal:** `expected 'accepted' to match /… has no …-with-extra\.jsonl/`.
- **The CH and spawn cases** failed with `expected { ok: false … } to deeply equal { ok: true, failures: [] }`.

## Break proofs

- Remove the at-most-once rule per `turnKey`: C-05 fails.
- Turn the CH-05 hang off: C-15 fails.
- Let the hand-over finish at 29 000 ms: C-15 fails.
- Turn the C-23 env check off: C-23 fails.
- Drop `--yolo` from the forbidden list: C-24 fails.

## Gaps

These are left for the driver issues:
- **C-02:** the `detect()` half needs the install resolver.
- **C-22:** only the policy argv is checked, not the question-tool removal.
- **C-23:** the harness cannot see "present only in the credential file".
- **C-24:** the Codex rule of exactly two pre-approved tools waits for the Codex driver.
- **TC-144-02** "exactly one case": only C-29 checks whole runs.
- **ADR-008 static check (ISSUE-149):** it has to exempt `driverConformance.ts` and `driverConformance.lineDriver.ts`, because both name the forbidden flags in order to assert their absence.

## Verification

- Focused tests: 78 passed; the reference run passes 29/29
- `node scripts/checks/fixtures-layout.mjs fixtures`: ok
- fixtures privacy test: 2 passed
- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0, depcruise clean

- `pnpm test:canaries`: 24/24

author: aadamowski
body:
Long songs that need on-the-fly transcoding no longer get killed with
"Reason: failed to start" while FFmpeg is still producing; the verdict now
tracks real transcode progress instead of a blind deadline.

- playback_controller: the fixed wait for the client's start confirmation
  becomes a progress-aware watchdog that only fails a start when FFmpeg stops
  producing (15 s) or 45 s pass without a confirmed start.
- stream_manager: new transcode_progress() reports growth in whichever form
  the transcode writes - HLS .m4s segments, or the single progressive-MP4
  .mp4 - so both streaming formats are watched, not just HLS.
- socket_events: a client can no longer force "failed to start"; that verdict
  is the server's alone.
- splash.js: the client-side playbackStartTimeout timer and its
  end_song("failed to start") are removed; start-failure detection lives
  server-side.
- tests: coverage for the watchdog (slow-but-healthy, stalled, gone client,
  playback-id mismatch), the format-aware progress probe (HLS and MP4), and the
  socket guard.

Test plan

- Pi: enqueued a long, transcode-bound song (~107 MB, several minutes). It
  started ("Stream is playing") and was still transcoding and playing well
  past the old fixed deadline (pre-fix such a song died at ~16-31 s with
  "failed to start"); the start survived a slow transcode.
- The server guard fired correctly: a client-forced "failed to start" was
  logged as ignored ("start failures are decided server-side") and dropped,
  with zero real errors.
- Note: the end path on this branch can still fall to the pre-existing "no
  end reported" backstop when a stale kiosk tab holds the master seat; that is
  the master-election fix (a separate PR), out of scope here.

Closes #985

author: ryanjkendrick
body:
Work item 2.15 of the phase 2 plan: the Index window, the status bar indexing indicator and the Indexing options page, behind the new flag `features.indexWindow`. It builds against contract 1.3 and the fake host; the real host side is work item 2.9.

## What landed

**Flag.** `features.indexWindow` (default on, like every flag) in `FeatureSettings.cs`, the README flag table and both flag-list tests. With it off: the View > Other Windows entry and `Tools > Pillion: Open Index` are hidden (`DynamicVisibility`, set when the menu opens), the status bar shows no indicator, an open window says "The Index window is disabled by settings or policy", and the Indexing options page says it is disabled. The extension reads the flag the way it reads `chat` (`ChatAvailability.IsIndexWindowEnabled`).

**Pillion Index window** (`ToolWindows/IndexToolWindow*`, view model `IndexWindowViewModel` in `Pillion.VisualStudio.Core/Indexing`):
- Status header: phase, progress bar with "files done of total, chunks", estimate, pause reason, last error, totals, Pause / Resume / Refresh.
- Roots tab: one card per root (path, role writer or reader, files indexed of total, chunks, disk use, embedding model, last full sweep, exclusion counts) with Rebuild and Delete (Delete confirms, default No).
- Excluded files tab: root picker, "secret-bearing only" filter, paged list (200 a page, Previous / Next) with the secret-bearing files grouped first and marked by a drawn shield plus the words "Secret-bearing file", Copy path (button, Ctrl+C, context menu) and Open .pillionignore (creates the file with a one-line comment only when it does not exist).
- Indexes tab: every index folder from `ListIndexesAsync` with disk use, root exists / gone (stale) / unknown, open here / in use by another host / not in use, and Delete.
- Updates come from `IHostConnection.IndexStatusChanged`: the handler only stores the latest status and schedules one UI-thread visit (100 ms gather), which updates the rows in place. One read of the status, the index folders and the first root's exclusions when the window opens (and again when the host becomes ready, and after a user action); no polling. The exclusions are read again only when the chosen root's exclusion counts change. A notification that arrives while the opening read is in flight wins over it. Every RPC runs on the thread pool through one helper; every timed stretch on the UI thread goes through `UiThreadTimings` (`index.window.apply`, `package.statusbar.index`, `package.querystatus.openindex`).

**Status bar.** `IndexStatusIndicator` (Core) turns the status into "↻ Indexing 42%", "‖ Index paused: build", "⚠ Index error", or nothing when idle (folded to at most twice a second). The package shows it as a small clickable button inserted into the status bar's panel, which opens the window; if the panel cannot be found it falls back to adding the text after the host state in the existing `IVsStatusbar.SetText` text (no click). See open questions.

**Indexing options page** (Tools > Options > Pillion Programmer > Indexing): exclude patterns (multi-line, one per line), max memory MB (256-65,536), pause on battery saver, retention days (0-3,650; 0 turns the age rule off), and a read-only line naming the active embedding model (the one the open index was built with). It saves **only the keys that changed, each under its own dotted key** (`indexing.exclude`, `indexing.maxMemoryMb`, ...), never the `indexing` object and never another section, so it cannot overwrite what another page or an editor changed meanwhile (the #57 mistake). A test covers the two-writers case.

**Accessibility pass (section 15).** Every control has an automation name (a unit-testable check is in the integration test); tabs, buttons and the lists have access keys (no clashes in the window); cards and the phase line are keyboard-focusable and carry a full sentence as their name; live regions announce the phase, pause reason, errors and action results but not every progress tick; the shield is never the only sign (the Kind column says "Secret-bearing file", a stale index says "Root is gone (stale)"); all colours are `VsBrushes` keys (window) or system colours the Options dialog themes (options page). All strings are in `Indexing/IndexStrings.resx` (191 strings, one test resolves every one).

## Tests

- `Pillion.VisualStudio.Tests`: 34 `IndexWindowTests` (status updates, phase walk, burst folding, pause / resume and every pause reason, rebuild, delete with and without confirmation, root reconciliation, excluded paging / grouping / secret-only / copy path / reload only on count change, index folders and delete, host not ready, failures, the flag), 39 `IndexFormatTests` (text, status bar indicator, `ChatAvailability` flag), 22 `IndexingOptionsTests` (load, validation, changed-keys-only save, two-writers case, reload on `settingsChanged`) and 4 `IndexWindowRealHostTests` against the fake host over the real pipe (`PILLION_FAKEHOST_INDEX=ready`: the canned root, secret-bearing files first, the orphan index, pause / resume, a rebuild walking the phases, deleting the orphan).
- Integration test `IndexWindow_ShowsTheRootRow_AndPauseAndResumeGoThroughTheHost` (VS 2026 only) written and built; **not run** (another agent holds the IDE-test slot).

## Counts and checks

- 35 files, +6,709 / -14 lines against `feature/phase2-wave1`; 99 new tests in `Pillion.VisualStudio.Tests` (813 in the project, all green) and one written integration test.
- `dotnet build PillionProgrammer.NoVsix.slnf -c Release`: 0 warnings, 0 errors. `src/Pillion.VisualStudio` built with the Visual Studio 2026 MSBuild (VSCT and XAML compile, pkgdef registers the Indexing page). Both integration test projects (VS 2026 and VS 2022 variants) build.
- `dotnet test PillionProgrammer.NoVsix.slnf --filter "Category!=Live&Category!=Benchmark"`: everything green except five timing tests that failed only while the whole solution ran in parallel on a busy machine (`ChunkerPerformanceTests` x3, `SymbolPerformanceTests`, `HandshakeCompatibilityTests.AContractOnePointOneClient...`); all pass when run alone (11 and 5 tests), and none touches this change.

## Manual look (Visual Studio 2026, private hive `PillionIdx`)

Installed this VSIX into a private root suffix (`/rootsuffix PillionIdx`, VSIXInstaller `/rootSuffix:PillionIdx`) with the fake host behind it (`PILLION_TEST_HOST_PATH`, `PILLION_FAKEHOST_INDEX=ready`) and drove it with UI Automation; uninstalled afterwards (no other hive touched). What I saw and fixed:

- The window loads and follows the fake host: roots card, Excluded files tab (shield column, secret-bearing group first), Indexes tab (the orphan marked "Root is gone (stale)"), Pause / Resume, Rebuild walking the phases with the progress bar, the Delete confirmation (default No).
- First run showed three real bugs, all fixed here: `{StaticResource {x:Type ListViewItem}}` threw while the window was created (the themed styles do not define it; replaced by an item `ToString` for the screen-reader name and a list-level context menu); the default TabControl chrome ignored the VS theme (white content area; now drawn with theme keys, with `PART_SelectedContentHost` kept because without it UI Automation could not reach the tab content); the "no repository root" line showed beside a root.
- The status bar item is inserted into the `StatusBarPanel` in VS 2026: "↻ Indexing 50%" while rebuilding, "‖ Index paused: you" when paused, hidden when idle, and a click on it (invoked through UI Automation) reopens a closed window. Not checked on VS 2022.
- Not checked: high-contrast themes (only the theme keys were reviewed), a screen reader, the Indexing options page rendering, Ctrl+C in the list.

## Open questions

1. **Clickable status bar item.** `IVsStatusbar` cannot take a click, so the click works through an element inserted into the status bar's WPF panel (`StatusBarPanel` in the main window's visual tree), which is not a public extension point. I

body:
Every figure built from several climbers' input now says how many people it comes from, and over what time window where one applies.

**Difficulty breakdown:** the header says "the average of N climbers' own reads". Each axis legend says "3.4/5 · N rated". "✓ counted" now always shows the count, or "the first read" if you are the only rater.

**Route page**
- Header ★ cell: "★ N rated".
- Community Consensus:
  - "avg of N ratings". It shows "—" instead of "0.0" when nobody has rated.
  - Top conditions show the report total.
  - The heatmap is labelled as reports per month, and its colour no longer counts unrated reports as zero stars.
  - Best months show "(avg 4★+)" plus a rated count on each month.
- Overview:
  - Hazard flags show report counts.
  - "Reported cleared" shows how many climbers said the hazard was gone.
  - The confidence pill reads "N reports".
  - The 45-day line shows its report count, and the hazards box states its 45-day window.
  - "What to expect" states its window and report count.
  - The social chips read "N climbers logged it" plus "N in the last 45 days". The old "N ascents logged" counted attempts and conditions-only reports.
- Trip Reports opens with "N reports from M climbers · K in the last 45 days".

**Elsewhere**
- The sun verdict reads "X of N climbers…".
- Ranks shows "★ —" rather than "★ 0.0" for a climb nobody has rated.
- `avgStars()` and the seed Ranks average no longer divide by unrated reports.

- **Bug fix.** Before, when three climbers agreed a rack, rope length or descent correction through the database, the value was written to the route. An accepted rack or gear correction also goes into required gear, the same as a local one.

- The edit form shows "✓ N climbers agreed" next to an agreed field (new `_contribAgreed`).

- The guard notes record the database-path gap (`docs/guards/contributions-and-logbook.md`).

author: gabeklein
body:
Splits the 1,277-line `render/render.ts` into seven modules. Every function and declaration moves unchanged: the statement, branch and function counts under coverage are identical, and `dist/index.js` stays the same size (32.16 kB).

| module | holds |
| --- | --- |
| `fiber.ts` | `Fiber`, `Boundary`, `Renderable`, `Appearance`, `Style` types; `range`, `makeScope`, `move`, `park`, range removal |
| `render.ts` | `render()` root, `pass`, `attempt`, focus queue, `passiveRender` / `depth` |
| `mount.ts` | `mount*` per node kind, `run*`, `complete`, `unmountFiber` |
| `reconcile.ts` | `reconcile*`, `patch`, `compatible`, keying |
| `suspense.ts` | boundary waiting, `settle` / `hide` / `reveal`, `suspend`, `recover` |
| `element.ts` | host prop patching, events, controlled-input restore, refs |
| `style.ts` | `style` prop observation, doors and tickets, class / declaration claims |

The modules import each other in a cycle (`mount` → `reconcile` → `mount`). That's safe because nothing runs at module scope beyond creating constants. Each mutable `let` stays in the only module that assigns it (`passiveRender` and `depth` in `render`, `holding` and `settling` in `suspense`, `rendering` and `touched` in `style`), so other modules read them through live ES bindings.

`suspense.test.tsx` now sits beside `suspense.ts`. `render.test.tsx` stays as the integration suite for the rest; splitting it per module can come later.

No changeset (internal only). Verified: dom typecheck and coverage at 100%, workspace build, `cascade-probe`, `hot-probe`, examples e2e (109 passed).

author: 0ssol1620-byte
body:
## Release 2 (2026-10-15) — head `8b0e5b2`

The four Release 2 lanes were merged with ordinary merges: hero `a0fc3b2`, film `ea08d7c`, layout `e65b82c`, example `8cd2211`. The only conflict was the HANDOFF.md add/add. Every lane handoff is applied, and the HANDOFF file is removed in `109fd0e`. `8b0e5b2` is the single fix round. **Do not merge without founder review**: merging deploys production.

### What changed, by critic item

- **Blocker 1, consent card.** The card is no longer in the server HTML or the first paint. It appears after the first scroll past 200px or 8 s after mount, whichever comes first. The footer's "Analytics preferences" opens it at once. Below 900px it is two rows: the sentence with its Privacy link, then two equal 44px buttons. From 900px up it is a bottom-left card at most 360px wide. GA still loads only after consent, and the Escape, refusal-persistence and GA-0 guards are unchanged. The EN sentence is shorter ("…on public pages, never workspace content."). The KO sentence is too (fix round, "…측정하며, 워크스페이스 내용은 제외합니다."), because the real build measured 110.8px at 360. Both keep the same four facts: vendor, cookies, what is measured, what is excluded.
- **Blocker 3, empty blocks.** s3's right column (notes, method, rights) is printed, not folded behind "Read the record". s2's "The context this passage needs" opens by default, and s2's bottom padding went from 120px to 72px (48px on phones).
- **Blocker 4, WebKit weight.** The cause is engine-side, not our CSS. Playwright WebKit on Windows applies Wanted Sans Variable's wght axis to advances but draws outlines at 400. `FontOutlineProbe`, mounted first in `<body>`, measures ink at 400 and at 1000 and sets `html[data-static-wght="1"]` only where the axis is not drawn. The WEIGHT-HOOK CSS then adds the font's measured stem difference as `-webkit-text-stroke`. There is no inline script and no CSP change. Real Safari on Apple hardware was not tested.
- **Hero copy.** H1 is "Knowledge your AI can trust." / "AI가 믿고 사용하는 지식.". The support line says what TAVONEL does.
- **Header CTA.** `HeaderCta` renders nothing on `/explore` and `/ko/explore`.
- **390 footer.** The footer is a true two-column grid, so headings in a row share a top edge, and separators are `aria-hidden` spans between items.
- **Phone menu.** The menu control is a borderless 44×44 icon whose three lines cross to an X. Its accessible name is still "Menu"/"메뉴", and the focus ring is 2px #244ac8.
- **Film reading line (move 2).** Each stage's line now quotes a string that is on screen in at least 80% of the sampled frames (`compile-stage-player.frame-strings.json`, unit-tested): WORKING COPY.md / # Payment terms / CHANGED / nodes lit. The 1440 tab row is a compact left-aligned group with 36px gaps. The pane strip uses Wanted Sans 13px instead of mono.
- **Evidence Line (move 5).** On hover or focus of a region button or the passage card, a 1px cobalt line runs to that region's box on the page. Its label is derived from the record: "SOURCE · 10-Q · p.4 · [64,476 → 932,538]", plus "page 4 · region A" the first time. It animates in 240ms and does not animate under reduced motion. It is a pointer-transparent overlay, so CLS is 0. Below the side-by-side workbench (960px) no line is drawn, and the label sits on the card instead.
- **Example (move 8).** The "What you receive" rule now also skips boilerplate and fragments under 12 words, and the FAQ states the whole rule. The region crop gets a 16-raster-px display margin. `data-bbox1000` is still the record bbox, and the window shown is `data-crop1000`.
- **Material (move 4).** One 8px card radius everywhere. Mono is kept only for filenames, coordinates, digests and dates. The extra ink rules are gone, and "Read what TAVONEL does" is a two-column list of four proofs with quiet "Read →" links.

### QA

Local production builds use the fixture env. Build 1 is `izLTPqCZ3IoWkqgphOKmB`. Build 2, after the fix round, is `YhHVpZIxpB20H26_TNaw9`; captures and phone shots were taken on it.

- `pnpm check`: green. Full vitest: **404 files / 5,955 tests passed**.
- e2e, **whole suite** on the chromium projects (seven widths, reduced-motion, audit, audit-768, audit-1280, launch-chromium; system Chrome channel): **1,844 passed / 4 failed / 2 flaky / 590 skipped**. The fix round re-ran the failed specs plus the consent spec on build 2: **90 passed / 0 failed**. The four failures:
  - Evidence Line, reduced motion: the project's `use.reducedMotion` does not reach `matchMedia` in this runner (measured `false`). The spec now emulates the media itself.
  - Footer height ×2 (390/360): the budget was re-derived from a measurement. See below.
  - `site-nav` "webkit answers the same questions": `Unsupported webkit channel "chrome"` comes from the local wrapper config. Re-run with the repo config, it hit the 600 s test timeout on Windows WebKit, the known Windows WebKit hang. The CI Browser QA (webkit) job covers it.
- WebKit, reduced motion, explicit timeouts (`launch-qa-mobile-nav` at 390 and 1440, plus the whole `marketing-consent` spec at 390): **18/18**.
- Hosted QA (EN/KO × 1440/390/360), local build 2: **117/119**. Both failures are `stages.walkLoadsEachCut`. The check takes a full-page screenshot just before walking the stages, and that sometimes leaves the player's `inView` false, so it shows posters. A probe reproduces it in one run out of two and never without the full-page shot. Preview: **95/119**. All 24 failures are the vercel.live toolbar script (console/CSP), with 0 from the app origin, and the stage walk passes there.
- `find-overflow` at 390 on `/`, `/ko`, `/pricing`: 0 wide elements. The phone overflow is 0px at 360/390/412/430 × EN/KO.
- **Blocker 4:** h1 computes to 600 in both engines. Chromium: flag `null`, stroke 0. WebKit: flag `1`, stroke 1.52px at 390 and 3.04px at 1440. H1 is 1 line at 1440 and 2 lines at 390, in EN and KO.
- **Blocker 1:** the card is absent at scroll 0 after 1.5 s and present after a 300px scroll on `/`, `/ko` and `/pricing` at 360, 390 and 1440. On phones it is 95.2px tall with an 8px bottom gap (360/390/412/430 × EN/KO). At 1440 it is 360px wide at x=16: 122.4px tall on Home, 140.6px on `/pricing`.
- **Blocker 3:** s3's right column holds 6 items and 719 visible chars (EN) / 380 (KO), with no `<summary>`. The s2 trailing gap is 73px at 1440 and 49px at 390.
- 1440 tab gaps are 36/36/36px, and the first tab is at x=120 (the container edge). The header CTA href is `/explore` on `/pricing`, `/` and `/ko`.
- Films and posters: all 14 tracked files are byte-identical to `main` (sha256), and nothing under `public/` changed.

### Spec changes and reasons (no security, consent-gating, a11y or evidence guard relaxed)

- `marketing-consent`: the server HTML no longer has the panel. There is no card at scroll 0 for 1.5 s, then `revealConsent` scrolls 300px. The card sits at the bottom: on phones it is ≤96px tall; from 900px it is ≤360px wide and sits left. The `/pricing` intersection check is gone because the card is delayed (orchestrator decision). GA-0, Escape, persistence and footer reopen are unchanged.
- Specs that expected the card at once now reveal it by scroll. Explore specs that are not about consent start with a stored refusal.
- `evidence-first` and `landing-v2` follow the new H1. `hero-home-responsive` pins the 32–40px tab gaps and the ≥15px reading line, with and without reduced motion.
- `public-layout-balance` footer budget: **re-derived from a measurement, not raised to go green**. The two-column phone footer measures 896px at 390×844 and 360×844, so the budget went from 0.9× to 1.1× viewport (928px). One more row of links still fails.
- New `home-evidence-line.spec.ts` covers keyboard A→B→C with coordinates, CLS 0, no animation under reduced motion, no line on phones (label on the card), the padded crop window, and the header CTA href.

### PR CI

All 13 checks on `8b0e5b2` passed (see the CI line at the end).

### Preview

author: rithybondeth
body:
Water depth alone makes it difficult to understand canal flow, compare terrain, or see whether reservoirs are filling or draining. Add planning tools to the map toolbar and Water management panel:

- Flow (F) draws each tile’s strongest expected outgoing transfer next tick. Arrow width reflects volume. The preview shares the solver’s pressure, donor-budget, and floodgate calculations; it works while paused and excludes rain and evaporation.
- Elevation (E) shades ground from low blue to high gold and fades structures so terrain remains visible. Water planning overlays provide tap/hover readouts for ground height, water depth, surface level, and strongest outgoing flow.
- Reservoir inspectors show up to 60 daily observed readings as a storage chart and accessible table. Completed reservoirs receive an initial reading, pauses and speed changes cannot duplicate samples, and demolished reservoirs are pruned. Overflow above nominal storage remains visible. History persists in saves/exports; older saves begin collecting at their current day.

Preserve expanded history tables and focused controls during live updates, keep the map legend clear of the building dock, and document the new tools.

Validation:
- All 151 tests pass. Coverage includes exact flow-preview agreement with the solver, conservation/donor budgets, closed/ruined/unfinished gates, daily sampling and retention, construction/demolition, save compatibility and invalid history rejection, and single-point/overflow chart rendering.
- Production build with strict TypeScript, formatting check, and diff check pass.
- Browser checks: paused flow arrows, elevation shading, tile readouts, live chart/table, expansion persistence, and save/continue restoring 15 readings. Chart and controls verified at 320px; no horizontal overflow at 768/1024/1440px and no browser console errors.

body:
Closes #426

Nahrazuje #449 (obnova jen části PID) a #498 (PR datové linky s týmž grafem, ke kterému chyběl přepočet zastávek škol).

## Co se změnilo
- `data/transit_graph.json` je z úlohy datové linky **MUCR9** (#497, schválená vlastníkem 15. 10. 2026): celostátní GTFS ze spojenka.cz, vydání 15. 10. 2026, referenční pondělí 19. 10. 2026. Soubor je bytově shodný s grafem v #498. Má 32 391 zastávek a 69 393 hran (dosud 30 810 a 65 279). Zaniklá linka XB v grafu není; od Divadla Gong jezdí 10, 12, 31 a 9.
- **Spojenka.cz změnila ID zastávek** z `CISJR:…|CRZ:…` na `S…`. Nový skript `scripts/prepocet_zastavek_skol.py` ke stávajícím souřadnicím škol v `data/school_locations.json` najde nejbližší zastávku v novém grafu, stejně jako `geocode_schools.py`; nic znovu negeokóduje. Mění se každý ze 1 088 záznamů (proto 3 442 změněných řádků), u 172 škol se změnil i název zastávky.
- Test `tests/dostupnost-cache-odpovedi.test.mjs` hledá plzeňské hlavní nádraží v grafu podle názvu místo natvrdo zapsaného ID (v #498 kvůli tomu padalo 7 testů).
- `public/pid_stops_compact.json` (zastávky PID pro výběr zastávky na pražské Dostupnosti) ze `stops.json` PID z 9. 10. 2026, převzato z #449. Generátor `scripts/build_pid_stops_compact.py` vznikl z části skriptu z #449; na grafu nezávisí.
- Registr: sada `doprava-gtfs` přepnuta skriptem `stav-datovych-sad.py prepni` na 2026-10-15, další období 2026-12 (odhad). Doklad: MUCR9 (#497) a rozhodnutí vlastníka v #426 z 12. 10. 2026.
- Dokumentace: `docs/zdroje-dat.md` 2.9 (ID zastávek, `school_locations.json`, obnova zastávek PID), `docs/gotchas.md` (předání úlohy `doprava-gtfs` jen v den přípravy; přepočet zastávek po obnově grafu), `docs/changes.md`.

## Pro vlastníka
Dostupnost počítá s jízdními řády platnými od 19. 10. 2026 a už nenabízí linku XB, která nejezdí. Od Divadla Gong proto za 30 minut najdeš 75 škol místo 95; těch 20 bylo dosažitelných jen přes XB. U stejnojmenných zastávek v nápovědě uvidíš místo kraje souřadnice. Ověříš na https://www.prijimackynaskolu.cz/dostupnost, zastávka Divadlo Gong, 30 minut.

## Jak ověřit
1. `<náhled>/dostupnost`, zastávka „Praha, Divadlo Gong“, 30 minut: 75 škol, mezi linkami není XB.
2. Lokálně ověřeno přes `next start` a `POST /api/dostupnost`: Gong 75 škol (produkce 95, chybějící školy používaly XB), linky 9, 12, 31, 133, 136, 177, 195, A, B, C; Plzeň, Hlavní nádraží 23 škol (produkce 22).

- [x] `npm test` (472 testů, OK), `npm run test:js` (896, 0 selhání), `npm run test:mesto`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, ESLint nad změněnými soubory, `npm run build`: vše prošlo lokálně.

- [ ] `npm run test:integrace` jsem nespouštěl.

## Mimo rozsah / poznámky

author: adtzlr
body:
Adds `SolidBodyContactNitsche`, a frictionless contact between the surfaces of solid bodies, enforced by Nitsche's method. In contrast to `SolidBodyContact` (penalty), the contact pressure contains the normal stress of the solid bodies, i.e. the penetration doesn't grow with the contact pressure.

```python
contact = SolidBodyContactNitsche(solid)                 # all faces on the outline of a mesh
contact = SolidBodyContactNitsche(rubber, metal)         # two solid bodies, weighted two-pass (default)
contact = SolidBodyContactNitsche(rubber, metal, two_pass=False)
contact.results.gap, contact.results.pressure, contact.results.traction  # traction = λ_N of the body
```

## Formulation
- **Contact pressure:** `p_N = [λ_N − γ g]_+` with `λ_N = (P N) · n`, the normal stress of the solid body at the integration points of its contact surface (Chouly & Hild 2013). Non-symmetric variant (θ = 0), i.e. only the elasticity tensor of the material model is required.
- **Consistent:** at the exact solution `p_N = λ_N` and `g = 0`, independent of γ. At the discrete solution, `g = (λ_N − p_N) / γ`, i.e. the gap is the discretization error of the surface stress divided by γ.
- **Integration:** at the integration points of the secondary surface with a closest-point projection (GPTS), like `SolidBodyContact`. This is **not** a segment-based mortar integration, see *Limits*.
- **Solid bodies:** `SolidBody` and `SolidBodyNearlyIncompressible` (with the cell-wise constant pressure `K (v/V − 1)`, which is the pressure of FElupe at a converged increment). Mixed-field containers are rejected. Material models with state variables are evaluated with own state variables at the integration points of the contact surfaces; these are updated after converged increments and are part of `checkpoint()`/`restore()`.
- **Tangent:** consistent and non-symmetric. It contains the change of the stress w.r.t. *all* points of the cell of a face (incl. Δp of the nearly incompressible solid and the circumferential stretch for axisymmetric fields) and the change of the normal of the primary surface (`ContactSurfacePair.variations_projection()`, shared with the friction).
- **Activation:** the contact search also considers small positive gaps (`max_gap`, default half a face), because a Nitsche contact is active as long as `g < λ_N / γ`.
- **Regularization:** w.r.t. the effective penetration `s = λ_N / γ − g`. It is exact for `s ≥ δ`. Within the transition zone the penetration is at most `4 δ / 27` (≈ 0.15 % of a face for the default δ), independent of the contact pressure.

## Decision: weighted two-pass (please check)
The unbiased two-pass formulation of Mlika, Renard & Chouly (2017) uses ½/½ weights. That **failed for a rubber block on a 1000× stiffer base**: the pass with the stress of the stiff body needs γ ≳ E_stiff/h, but γ is estimated from the softer body.

The fix weights the tractions of an integration point of body `b` that is projected on body `b̄` by `w = k_b̄ / (k_b + k_b̄)`, like the weighted average of the robust Nitsche formulation for interfaces (Annavarapu, Hautefeuille & Dolbow 2012). `k_b` is the existing penalty estimate, evaluated **per connected body** instead of per surface.
- Both weights of a contact zone sum up to one, so the formulation stays consistent.
- Equal bodies → ½/½. Rubber on metal → the stress of the rubber is used.
- It also works when all faces on the outline of *one* mesh are used, e.g. a single solid with cell-wise materials, because the bodies are identified by their connectivity.
- γ = scale · min_b k_b.
- `items` that don't contain all bodies of the contact surfaces raise a `ValueError`, because the estimated stiffness would be zero.

Rubber block on a base (two solid bodies, `SolidBodyNearlyIncompressible`, 3 increments). The table shows Newton iterations and the max. penetration:

| stiffness ratio | penalty | Nitsche, unweighted ½/½ | Nitsche, `two_pass=False` | **Nitsche, weighted (default)** |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 14 · 2.7e-3 | 15 · 2.1e-3 | 14 · 1.4e-3 | 16 · 2.6e-3 |
| 10 | 13 · 1.4e-3 | 15 · 6.4e-4 | 14 · 2.6e-4 | 14 · 3.4e-4 |
| 1000 | 11 · 1.4e-3 | **fails** | 14 · 2.4e-4 | 14 · 2.4e-4 |

## Verification
- **Tangent vs. central differences** (error < 1e-6 · max|K|): all 6 boundary regions × (3d, plane strain, axisymmetric) × (`SolidBody`, `SolidBodyNearlyIncompressible`), a viscoelastic material with state variables, and two bodies with a stiffness ratio of 1000 (weights ≠ ½).
- **Patch test on matching meshes** (uniaxial compression, `smoothing=0`): gap < 1e-10 and `p_N = σ` to machine precision for γ-scales 0.5 and 10, in 2d and 3d. The same holds for two bodies with a stiffness ratio of 1000 (laterally constrained, both passes). The penalty contact penetrates.
- **Force balance:** the contact forces on both bodies are equal and opposite, and the reaction forces at the top and bottom faces match.
- **Non-matching meshes** (lower 3×3 vs. upper 4×4 cells, and 4 vs. 7): neither formulation passes the patch test exactly. The scatter of the pressure (3–100 %) is the same for penalty and Nitsche, because both use GPTS integration. Nitsche transmits the full stress (p/σ ≈ 1.00–1.07); its max. gap is 2–27× smaller (default regularization).

## Accuracy and robustness, honestly
- **Where Nitsche helps:** wherever the surface stress is accurate. Examples: the patch tests; the interior of the contact zone with `SolidBodyNearlyIncompressible` (3× smaller gap than penalty on a coarse mesh, 11× on a finer one); rubber on a stiff base (Ex. 8: max. penetration 2.1e-4 vs. 1.9e-3).
- **Where it doesn't:** at the sharp edges of a punch (stress singularity) the max. penetration is about the same as with penalty. With a fully integrated `SolidBody` and a nearly incompressible material (volumetric locking), the surface stress oscillates and Nitsche inherits it, so there is no gain. Both cases are documented as hints.
- **Robustness sweep:** block punch, compressed by 50 %, n ∈ {4…8} cells, {2, 3, 6} increments, scale ∈ {1, 10}, `SolidBody` and `SolidBodyNearlyIncompressible`, no cutback. Penalty fails in **20/60** cases, Nitsche in **13/60**. On the cases where both converge, Nitsche needs ≈ 5 % more iterations. Both fail mostly on the fine nearly incompressible meshes.
- **Small γ is not recommended:** with scale 0.1 the θ = 0 variant loses stability / amplifies stress errors. The docstring says γ should scale like the estimate.

## Limits
- **Frictionless only.** The friction of `SolidBodyContact` is not wired in yet.
- **No segment-based (mortar) integration.** For non-matching meshes the patch test is passed only approximately, like the penalty contact. Segment-to-segment integration would be a follow-up of its own.
- The surface stress needs a reasonably accurate stress field: `SolidBodyNearlyIncompressible` for rubber, and a finer mesh or quadratic cells at the contact surface.

## Shared code (penalty contact unchanged)
- `_assemble_vector()`, `_assemble_matrix()` and `_diagonal()` are factored out of `SolidBodyContact`.
- `copy_statevars()` is generic.
- `ContactSurfacePair.kinematics(max_gap=0.0)` and `ContactSurfacePair.variations_projection()` are added.
- `SolidBodyContact` results are **bit-identical** to `main` (frictionless and with friction, two-pass), and the penalty column of the sweep is unchanged.

## Docs and tests
- **Docs:** the docstring of `SolidBodyContactNitsche` (formulation, weights, stiffness estimate, regularization bound, hints, example: rubber on metal with two solid bodies), API reference, landing page (highlights and the comparison table), README, changelog and **Ex. 8** (Nitsche vs. penalty, two solid bodies).
- **Tests:** `tests/test_nitsche.py` (FD tangents, patch tests for one and two materials, weights, stiffness estimate with a given γ, invalid items/solid bodies, surface pairs, no contact for stress-free touching surfaces, regularization, cutback with state variables, a job for each material type).
- **Fixed

## Summary
Refactored the cos-setup.sh script to improve robustness, logging, and user experience. The main changes include wrapping the entire script in a `main()` function to support `curl | bash` execution, adding comprehensive logging, improving Claude account detection and display, and handling plugin marketplace migrations.

## Key Changes

- **Script structure**: Wrapped all executable code in a `main()` function called at the end, ensuring the entire script is read before execution. This prevents stdin from being consumed by child commands when run via `curl | bash`.

- **Logging system**: Added persistent logging to `~/.local/state/cos-setup/install.log` with a new `quiet()` helper function that captures command output. Error messages now reference the log file location for debugging.

- **Claude account handling**: 
  - Implemented `signed_in()` function to reliably detect authentication status using both JSON parsing and exit codes
  - Added `auth_field()` and `account_desc()` helpers to extract and display account details (email, organization, plan)
  - Added account verification step to ensure the correct Claude organization is selected before proceeding
  - Improved sign-in prompts to show which account/organization is active

- **Plugin marketplace management**:
  - Implemented `cv_marketplace()` function to detect existing Carbon Voice plugin sources
  - Added logic to handle three scenarios: adding new marketplace, updating existing one, or replacing an older source
  - Validates that the Chief of Staff plugin is available before installation

- **Error handling**: Enhanced error messages with actionable guidance and log file references. Added `brew_install()` helper to standardize Homebrew installation with consistent error handling.

- **Environment variables**: Added Homebrew configuration flags to suppress auto-update and cleanup messages.

- **Input handling**: Redirected stdin appropriately (`</dev/null` for background operations, `</dev/tty` for interactive prompts) to prevent conflicts in piped execution.

## Notable Implementation Details

- The `label()` and `where()` functions were moved earlier in the script to support the new status display logic
- Added `LOG_SHOWN` variable to display user-friendly log paths (with `~` instead of full home directory)
- Plugin installation now validates the marketplace contains the required plugins before attempting installation
- Account selection happens early in the setup flow to catch misconfigurations before installing dependencies

author: stabrea
body:
The Branch app's main process held about 95% CPU and grew memory about 5 MB a minute after a few hours open.

**Root cause.** `desktop/src/mac-computer-driver.ts` kept `host.waitForExit(generation)` pending for the life of the Mac computer driver. The SDK's `wait_for_exit` sleeps 50 ms and returns pending, so uniffi re-polls about 20 times a second. The pinned Node binding (`@ubjs/node` 0.31.0-3, pinned by every `@trycua/cua-driver` release through 0.35.4) leaks one N-API threadsafe function per poll ([trycua/cua#4339](https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/4339)). Each one is a libuv async handle, and libuv walks the whole handle queue on every wakeup, so the main loop got slower the longer the app ran.

Evidence from a 3 s `sample` of the running app: about 2,000 of about 2,150 main-thread samples sat inside `uv__async_io`, with the one busy Rust thread in uniffi `waker_wake` → `napi_call_threadsafe_function`. Two `footprint` readings five minutes apart showed memory still growing.

**Fix.** The driver's exit is noticed with the SDK's synchronous `state()` every two seconds on an unref'd timer, and no native call is left pending. Once the state leaves Ready, the endpoint clears and the same log line as before is written. `stop()` clears the timer.

**Tests.** `desktop/scripts/mac-computer-driver.test.mjs`:
- The fakes' `waitForExit` now throws, so the old code fails these tests.
- A new test checks that an exit is noticed through `state()`, that the checks stop once the exit is seen, and that `stop()` ends them.

7/7 pass after `node scripts/build.mjs`.

No visible change: the computer pane behaves the same; only how the app notices the driver exiting changed.

author: johnamcruz
body:
## What

Curated training lists (owner-approved): a seeded, year-balanced set of setup moments that a practice replay runs window by window, so the local model trains without weeks of full-day replays.

- `scripts/lib/learning/curated-moments.js` scans setup moments. It follows the history library's own scan; with the library's 700-bar window, a test shows it gives the library's records exactly. The default window is the live runner's history, so the 1h and 4h trend facts are the ones live reads.
  - Use `practice` scans practice-train only; use `validate` scans practice-validate only. Test, final and any other use are refused (`assertUse`).
  - **Trend at the reaction bar**, from briefing facts:
    - Clear trend: 1h and 4h trend agree, the latest 1h break is with them, no 15m CHoCH against, and the regime is not range.
    - trend-end: a CHoCH against a 4h trend.
    - chop: a range regime, or a 1h or 4h range.
  - **Lists:**
    - trend-up and trend-down: a rejection or a breakout with a clear trend (an FVG failure through its far edge counts as a breakout).
    - counter-trend: a reaction against a clear trend.
    - trend-end and chop: either side.
  - **What each moment records:**
    - Every read true at its bar, checked with `checkReads` and mapped to a skill through the trade-lifecycle crosswalk (a test holds each mapping to its step's row).
    - The library's standard outcome.
    - The gate's view: the trend rule, and D2 through the gate's own `reversalAllowed` and `D2_TIERS`.
    - The expected decision (take or pass), the year and regime, and a replay window.
- `scripts/lib/learning/curated-lists.js` does the selection, coverage, fingerprint and replay integration. Each list is chosen in this order:
  1. Skills under their minimum, the scarcest first.
  2. The list's pass share.
  3. Year balance: fewest picks first, and no year above 1.5 times its even share.
  4. Winners and losers kept level.
  5. Skills that line up.
  6. A seeded tie-break.
- List sizes add up exactly to `total`. The default mix is 35/35/10/10/10.
- The mix is in time order: a replay's clock only moves forward and the experience index is walk-forward by day. The selection balances it across years.
- Coverage is reported per list and per reaction kind: each skill's count, what the data had, its combinations and an UNDER flag, plus the outcome, expected and year mixes.
- A validation document is built from practice-validate moments only, never runs on practice-train, and never feeds the index.
- **Replay integration:** a new replay config field, `curatedList: { file, list }`.
  - It requires `practice`, every bar, the list's market (root, bar and setup timeframes), and no `prop`. Every window must hold a decision time.
  - The list's fingerprint and name are in `setupHash` and `configHash`.
  - The pin stores only the windows, so no outcomes sit in the run home, and it must match the fingerprint the config resolved.
  - Inside a window, setup-focused practice decides which bars run. Every other time after the first window is a management time: the driver checks the broker (any listed position or working order) and steps the bar only while something is open. It checks again at each day's first time, so a position carried past its window or past an end of day is managed bar by bar, as practice does.
- CLI `scripts/curated-lists.js`: `scan` (with `--jobs N`, which scans whole session dates in parallel processes with identical output), `build` and `show`. It is 165 lines.

Not changed: setup-moments.js, setup-library.js, experience.js and composed-reads.js (their functions are reused as they are), and no skills. No lists were generated over the real data store.

## Owner decisions applied
1. With-trend breakouts go in trend-up and trend-down; coverage is split by reaction kind.
2. Management continues until flat, including on later days and through end of day.
3. Scan speed is measured below.
4. The library's `mtf-bias-filter` label counts as `multi-timeframe-analysis`.
5. Windows are replayed in time order.
6. `pullback-vs-reversal` is counted only when the reads show it exactly:
   - Reversal: a true CHoCH the trade's way.
   - Pullback: a trend read, the 15m alignment read `read <side> pullback`, and a rejection, all the trade's way.

## Scan speed
- With the full live window: about 197 ms per briefing and about 45 s per trading day in one process, so about 14 hours for practice-train (about 1,130 days).
- `--jobs 4` ran five days in 48 s with 3.25 cores busy. With about 10 jobs on a 12-core machine I estimate 1.5 to 2 hours; that figure is not measured.
- No prefilter: I found no cheap test that can't miss a moment, because candle relations depend on levels built from the whole window (swings, gaps), and about 44% of 15m closes are moments anyway.
- No caching of higher-timeframe state: it would mean changing briefing.js, which live also uses. Profiling puts about half of each briefing in time-zone and session-key work plus level computation.

## Fixture coverage
Drifted copies of the parity MNQ bars placed in 2020 to 2024; 192 moments; `build --total 40 --seed 1 --min-skill 2`. Short: trend-up 14, trend-down 8, counter-trend 2.

| List | Picked | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| trend-up | 0 | no candidates: the fixture rarely forms a clear 4h uptrend |
| trend-down | 6 of 6 | 4 breakouts, 2 rejections; all losses |
| trend-end | 4 of 40 | 2 D2 reversals allowed |
| chop | 4 of 144 | 50% pass |
| counter-trend | 2 of 2 | both pass |
| mix | 16 | 38% pass; 2020: 1, 2021: 6, 2022: 1, 2023: 6, 2024: 2 |

- In the mix, every skill reached its minimum except absorption, which the data never showed.
- Chop held 50% passes, not its 70% share, because rare skills rank above the pass share in the selection order.

## What was run
- `npm run verify` alone, with its own TMPDIR, on head 5fa68167: exit 0. 2674 tests, 2654 passed, 0 failed (the other 20 skipped); lint, generated-files check, strategy validation and the secrets check all passed.
- Mutation testing on the key behaviours: causality, the split guards, year balance and cap, skill minimums, seeded selection, the fingerprint in both hashes, window-only stepping, management until flat (including the day reset and the carried position), the pin's checks, the market checks, and the list rules. Every mutation is killed, with one gap: replacing the driver's real broker check inline survives, because the tests stub the broker. That check calls `accountOpen`, which is tested directly, including `size: null`.

## Review
- **Round 1** (independent reviewer), three findings, all fixed:
  - Positions went unmanaged after a window's tail.
  - Nothing tied a list to the run's symbol and timeframes.
  - The pinned copy could differ from the list the config resolved.
  - Three of its minor notes were also taken: outcomes kept out of the run home, a no-entry-window moment read and judged on one bar, and the CLI's `--pass-share`.
- **Round 2** (independent reviewer), four findings, all fixed:
  - An unreadable position size was counted as flat.
  - A position not flat after the end-of-day retries went unmanaged on later days.
  - `manageTailMin` did nothing useful; it is removed.
  - A pinned window's end revealed the standard trade's exit. Windows now end at max(reaction close + 15m, decision close), capped at end of day.
  - Its minor notes were also addressed:
    - tests for a broker check that throws and for resuming during management;
    - `prop` refused with a curated list;
    - list sizes that add up exactly;
    - an integer `--minutes`;
    - part files cleaned up and a clear error when a child scan is killed;
    - `replay.js points` counts curated windows and says management times are not counted.

author: jeronimorepetto
body:
Closes #906 (ISSUE-194). Adds the Jev half of `SettingsMirrorBridge`. It mirrors five preferences to the Host: the routing profile, the default provider, the default model, the default effort and the delegation toggle.

## How it works

- It reads the values from the legacy store through today's A-47 handler (`getJevSettings`).
- Around each A-51 save it reads the store before and after the save, and reports each key that changed. The bridge core then sends one `preferences.set` per changed key, each with a new `requestId`.
- It never calls A-51 itself.
- It sends nothing for a refused save, or for a save whose values were already stored.
- When a read fails, it treats every key as changed. Re-sending an unchanged value publishes nothing on the Host.
- It is registered only from cut-3a to cut-3e, which is the bridge's lifetime (`21` §3). `ROUTES_RELEASE` is still `cut-2`, so the half is built but not active yet.

## Package gap: composition

The issue says to register the half in `settingsMirrorBridge.ts`, but the halves are composed in `src/ui-main/index.ts`, which is a hot spot. This PR adds `settingsMirrorHalves(release, route)` and `reportSettingsMirrorWrites(release, route, hub)`. The issue that holds `index.ts` (the step-3a route switch) has to replace two calls:
- `reportNotificationsWrites(createLegacyRuntimeRoute(...), legacySettingsWrites)` → `reportSettingsMirrorWrites(ROUTES_RELEASE, createLegacyRuntimeRoute(...), legacySettingsWrites)`
- `halves: [createNotificationsMirrorHalf(legacyRuntime)]` → `halves: settingsMirrorHalves(ROUTES_RELEASE, legacyRuntime)`

## Tests

`jevMirror.test.ts` has 6 tests at L2. The TC-194 cases:
- **TC-194-01:** a legacy write is mirrored once, with a new requestId.
- **TC-194-02:** at start, one `preferences.set` is sent for each key that differs.
- **TC-194-03 (`[ADR-016, C-21]`):** no secret and no integration gate is ever mirrored.
- **Detached Host:** the pending keys are retried at the next attach, and the legacy store is never written.

Plus registration from 3a to 3e only, and A-51 reported once per changed key.

## RED evidence

Against a well-typed stub, all 6 tests failed. Examples:
- `expected [] to deeply equal [ …(4) ]`
- `expected { release: 'cut-3a', sent: false } to deeply equal { … sent: true }`

## Break proofs

- A secret key added to the mirrored list: C-21 fails.
- Every key reported on each save: 3 tests fail.
- The 3e upper bound removed: the registration test fails.

## Verification

- Focused tests: 16 passed
- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0
- `pnpm format:check`: clean
- `pnpm test`, shuffled: 14360 passed
- census: +6, no losses
- `pnpm trace:check --from <package>`: ok

author: woopstar
body:
## Summary

The self-learning pass crashed with `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'float' and 'NoneType'` whenever the slot's weather snapshot had a NULL `temperature` (or `wind_speed`). Those NULLs are written at Home Assistant startup, before the temperature sensor has loaded.

`HistoryStorage.find_weather_for_timestamp()` returns every column, with NULL ones as `None`. So `actual_weather.get("temperature", fc_temp)` returned `None` instead of the fallback, and the broad `except` in `learn_from_actual_price()` swallowed the error. The matched predictions were never removed, and the lead-time accuracy and evaluation records for the slot were skipped.

**Branch:** `fix/216-null-weather-snapshot`

## What changed

- `ml/learning.py`: new `forecast_errors()` helper. Temperature and wind forecast errors are now scored **separately**, each only when both the stored forecast and the measured value exist. A NULL value or a missing forecast adds no error, rather than a fake `0` that would make the forecast look perfectly accurate and lift the learned confidence.
  - Before this change, wind was scored only when the temperature forecast existed, and a missing wind forecast added a `0` wind error. Now each quantity is scored on its own.
  - The cap of 50 samples per slot and the debug log are unchanged. The block now writes through the `metrics` dict the method already holds.
- `docs/ml_documentation.md`: the self-learning loop step 5 now describes the separate scoring and the NULL handling.

I left out the issue's optional suggestions: skipping snapshots or picking the nearest non-NULL one. A snapshot row also stores solar power and the other columns, so dropping it would lose data, and with this fix a NULL value is harmless.

## Tests

- `tests/test_history_lookups.py::test_learning_survives_a_snapshot_without_weather`, run for NULL temperature, NULL wind and both NULL: learning returns `True`, the price error is counted, only the known quantity is scored and the matched predictions are removed. All three cases fail on `main` with the `TypeError`.
- `tests/test_history_lookups.py::test_forecast_errors_skip_unknown_values`: unit test for the helper.

## Results

`./scripts/quality.sh all` exits 0 in a venv with the pinned requirements (Home Assistant 2026.10.1): lint, mypy, pyright and vulture are clean, 1442 tests pass and the translations are unchanged. The devcontainer still has Home Assistant 2026.9.3. Against that version, mypy reports the known `arg-type` errors in `services.py`, which this PR does not touch.

No configuration, storage schema or user-facing strings changed.

Fixes #216

author: chcodex
body:
Closes #3155.

E2B offers persistent volumes that exist independently of sandbox lifecycles. This PR wires attach-at-create through the E2B backend so users no longer need TAR persist/hydrate on every turn for cross-sandbox persistence.

## What is included

- New `E2bVolumeMount` POJO (existing volume name + absolute in-sandbox path, validation + normalization)
- `E2bSandboxClientOptions.volumeMounts` (fluent adders, distinct-path check) and `E2bFilesystemSpec.volumeMount/volumeMounts`
- `POST /sandboxes` serializes `volumeMounts: [{name, path}]` (omitted when empty); platform 400s propagate with the response body
- Mounts threaded through `E2bSandboxClient.create` into `E2bSandboxState` and across all three creation paths (new, connect-fallback recreate, native-snapshot restore)
- `workspaceOnVolume` detection (`root.equals(mount) || root.startsWith(mount + "/")`): TAR persist/hydrate become no-ops, destroy skips `rm -rf`; nested mounts get TAR `--exclude` args
- Hardening found via live testing: fail fast on non-absolute `workspaceRoot`, shell-quote TAR excludes, run workspace `mkdir` from `/`
- `E2bSandboxState` JSON stays backward compatible; empty `E2bCloudBucketMountStrategy` placeholder removed
- Docs: E2B volumes section in `filesystem.md` (EN/ZH)

## Tests

- Unit: request-body assertions (MockWebServer), validation/normalization, merge, serde round-trip incl. legacy compat, recovery with mounts
- Live (`E2bVolumeMountLiveTest`, opt-in via `E2B_API_KEY`, skipped in CI): mount visibility, unknown-volume 400, cross-sandbox persistence, `workspaceOnVolume` end-to-end, native-snapshot restore, nested-mount independence from snapshots — all passing against the real API
- Verified live: platform snapshots do **not** capture volume bytes, so nested mounts are unaffected by snapshot restore

author: bor4brn
body:
## Summary

Adds a third agent system tool next to `web_search` and `browser_use`. Picking a crawler in the agent's tool selector (new **Web Fetch** card, same single-`Select` layout as Web Search) binds a stateless `web_fetch({ url })` tool. It runs the crawler's own plan (engine, headers/cookies/auth, markdown options) for exactly one URL and returns the page as markdown. Nothing is persisted (no crawl job) and links are not followed.

Binding shape: `{ source: 'system', sourceKey: 'crawler', config: { crawlerKey } }`. Policy name: `agent.crawler.web_fetch`.

## Which URLs the agent may fetch

The model picks the URL, so it is confined to the crawler's configuration:

- Allowed hosts = crawler `allowList` plus seed hosts (seed subdomains only with `includeSubdomains`). `blockList` always wins.
- A crawler with neither seeds nor allowList is open-web, and is only usable **without credentials**. Binding a credentialed one is rejected at save time (agent config validation) and refused again at call time, since the crawler can be edited after binding.
- Only `http(s)` URLs. The engine's existing SSRF guard (`allowPrivateNetwork`, off by default) still applies.
- Returned content is capped at 50,000 characters unless the crawler sets `maxBodyChars`.

## Changes

- `crawler/singlePage.ts` (new): `fetchPageWithCrawler`, host policy (`refuseCrawlerUrl`), credential detection. Reuses the engine's `crawl()` with `maxDepth 0 / maxPages 1 / autoCrawl false`.
- `crawler/agentTools.ts` (new): the `web_fetch` tool factory, wired to the turn's abort signal.
- `crawlerService.ts` / `crawlerJobService.ts`: export `loadCrawler`, `withTenantDb`, `snapshotToPlan` (no behaviour change).
- `agentService.ts`: bind the `crawler` system tool; guard it under `agent.crawler.*`.
- `agentConfigValidation.ts`: require `crawlerKey`, and check the crawler exists, is active and, if credentialed, is pinned to hosts.
- `agentHumanInTheLoop.ts`: `web_fetch` listed as read-only.
- `ToolSelectorModal.tsx`: Web Fetch card, options from `/api/crawler/crawlers?status=active`.
- `resources/*` + i18n: `agent.crawler` reference edge.

## Known limits

- The SSRF guard inspects the host literal only (no DNS resolution), so a public name that resolves to a private address is not caught. This is the engine's existing limit; it is more exposed here because the model chooses the URL, most of all in open-web mode.
- `web_fetch` is on the HITL read-only list, so agents with approval enabled will not be asked before a fetch. A fetched URL can carry data out, so you may want it gated.
- When a crawler sets `maxBodyChars`, it replaces the 50,000-character default instead of lowering it, so a large value can put a very large page into the model's context.
- Out of scope: multi-page crawl from the agent, job/RAG persistence, mapping Claude-import `web_fetch` to this tool, docs under `docs/guide`.

## Enterprise overlay

No seam change. `console-ee` needs nothing, but its `communityRef` pin only picks this up once it is released in a community tag.

## Testing

- New `crawler-single-page.test.ts` (12 tests: host policy matrix, credential detection, one-page plan, truncation, error pages, tenant/inactive crawler) and 4 cases in `agent-config-validation.test.ts`.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, lint 0 errors, full unit suite green (469 files, 8406 tests).
- Ran locally on the community server and confirmed the tool works with an open-web crawler (manual check by the author).
- Not tested: the seed-host restriction and the credentialed-crawler refusal against a running server; both are covered by unit tests only.

body:
Video recipe imports never logged what they cost. Now every Gemini call that gets an answer writes one numbers-only line, in the same style as the pantry-vision scan line:

`recipe-import: extract ok kind=video source=youtube ms=8422 tokensIn=41250 tokensOut=812 thinking=1500 model=gemini-2.5-flash`

- `ok` = usable recipe. `rejected` = answered but failed the schema check. `failed` = answered (and billed) but empty or unreadable.
- kind: video, link, text, photo, screenshot. source: youtube, tiktok, instagram, facebook, reddit, web, photo, upload.
- No URLs, user ids or recipe text. Label values are stripped down to plain letters and numbers as a safety net.
- No length cap added (owner decision pending). Video duration is not logged: Gemini's usage data does not include it.
- Otherwise nothing changes: same calls, same retries, same results.

## Jira
- [GROMO-2288](https://romance.atlassian.net/browse/GROMO-2288)

## 변경 유형
CHORE

## Summary
운영 승격은 반드시 **main → release**로 진행한다. 오래된 release의 squash 이력 때문에 현재 main → release PR에 충돌이 발생하므로, 기존 release 이력을 main에 먼저 연결한다.

```text
작업 브랜치 → main (이 PR: 이력 동기화·문서·회귀 검사)
main → release (별도 운영 승격 PR)
```

이 PR은 처음에 작업 브랜치 → release로 잘못 생성했다. 그 경로로는 머지되지 않았으며 base를 main으로 바로잡았다.

## 커밋 목록
- 75335fbd — main 55b16da3의 파일을 유지하며 release 33caa690의 이력을 병합 부모로 연결한다.
- 8800d4f6 — SSM 접수 불명 시 자동 재전송 금지 회귀 검사와 복구·이력 보존 절차를 추가한다.

## Changes
- main 대비 파일 변경은 `.github/scripts/test_catus_version_badges.py`와 `docs/prd/fishcat/server-separation/deployment.md` 두 개다. 앱·서버·배포 실행 코드는 변경하지 않는다.
- 75335fbd의 tree는 main 55b16da3와 동일하며, 부모는 main 55b16da3와 release 33caa690 두 개다. release의 과거 1.x 파일로 main의 파일을 덮어쓰지 않는다.
- main에 이력을 연결한 뒤에는 별도 main → release PR에서 동일한 과거 squash 충돌을 반복하지 않는다.
- SSM 전송 의도만 남은 중단은 접수 여부를 확정할 수 없으므로 재전송하지 않는다. 이 정책을 회귀 검사와 운영 절차로 명시한다.

## 주의사항
- **이 이력 동기화 PR은 Create a merge commit 방식으로 병합해야 한다.** squash/rebase로 병합하면 release 부모 이력이 main에 연결되지 않아 목적을 달성하지 못한다.
- 이 PR을 release로 직접 머지하지 않는다. 실제 운영 승격 PR의 head는 반드시 main이다.
- 로컬 회귀 검사 43개 통과, 기존 head 8800d4f6의 전체 ARM64 CI 및 Codex 주요 문제 없음 판정 확인. base 변경 후 상태는 다시 확인한다.
- main 머지는 기존 dev CI·배포를 실행할 수 있다. 운영 발행은 별도 main → release 승격 후이며 운영 CD는 수동 승인 절차를 따른다.
- Gromo 1.x의 기존 소스·워크플로는 `chore/GROMO-2288-gromo-1x-release`(33caa690)에 보존했다.

body:
## 概要

`PATCH /api/notes/{id}` の `NoteUpdate` が `status` を `str` で受けていたため、`active` / `archived` 以外を送ると DB の CHECK 制約違反（`asyncpg.CheckViolationError`）が捕まらず 500 になっていた。`topic` / `content` / `summary` / `category` にも長さの上限が無く、巨大な本文がそのまま復習のプロンプトと埋め込みの入力に入っていた。

## 関連 Issue

Closes #590

## 変更内容

- `schemas/note.py`
  - `status` を `Literal["active", "archived"]`（`NoteStatus`）にする
  - `topic` は聞き取りの上限 `MAX_TOPIC_ANSWER_LENGTH`（60）と同じ。前後の空白を取り、空は拒否（セッション中のトピック訂正 `TopicEdit` と同じ制約）
  - `summary` 1000・`content` 20000・`category` 100 を `MAX_NOTE_*_LENGTH` として定義。`content` と `category` は空を拒否、`summary` は空を許す（今の編集フォームが空で送る）
  - 上限の根拠：ローカル DB のノートは topic 最大 32・summary 最大 102・content 最大 965（p95 848）。生成のプロンプトは topic を「簡潔に」、summary を 1〜2 文と指示している。埋め込みの入力は別に `MAX_EMBEDDING_INPUT_CHARS`（6000）で切られる
- `note-edit-form.tsx`・`note-category-editor.tsx`：入力欄に同じ値の `maxLength` を付ける
- `.claude/rules/server/notes.md`：上限はサーバーの定数とクライアントの `maxLength` をそろえる旨を追記
- 回帰テスト `tests/unit/test_note_routes.py::TestNoteUpdateValidation`：不正な `status` の `ValidationError`、各フィールドの上限ちょうど / 超過、空の扱い、`TestClient` で `{"status": "foo"}` を PATCH すると 422 でリポジトリを呼ばないこと

## テスト

- [x] ユニットテスト追加（上の 9 件）
- [x] ローカルで動作確認済み: `ruff` / `mypy` / `pytest`（1642 件）、`npm run lint` / `tsc --noEmit` / `vitest`（1551 件）

## レビューポイント

- 上限の値（60 / 1000 / 20000 / 100）は上の根拠で決めた暫定値。本番に topic が 60 字を超えるノートがあれば、編集フォームは topic も一緒に送るので保存が 422 になる（入力欄の `maxLength` は既に入っている値を切らない）。心配なら本番の `max(length(topic))` を確かめる
- `NoteResponse.status` は `str` のまま（レスポンス側は変えていない）

author: ayanbhardwaj1
body:
A custom mailbox's IMAP and SMTP hosts were connected to exactly as typed. That let a mailbox point YouBank's server at loopback, a private network, cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`) or internal services on any port. This closes the follow-up noted in `AyanBhardwaj1/YouBank#18`.

## What changed
- **`mailEndpoint` in `src/lib/crm/imap.ts`:**
  - Only mail ports are allowed: IMAP 993 and 143; SMTP 465, 587, 25 and 2525.
  - The name is resolved with the same rule as pasted links, and refused if any answer is private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, metadata, `.local`, `.internal` or `localhost`.
  - Refusals are a plain 400 (`UNSAFE_URL`) that says what to fix.
- **Pinned connections:** `imapClient` and `smtpTransport` connect to the checked IP and keep the typed name for TLS SNI and certificate verification, so DNS rebinding can't swap in a private address. Both are now async.
- **Where it applies:**
  - when a mailbox is saved (`verifyMailbox` checks both servers before contacting either);
  - before every connection: sync, send, and the Newsroom's email to yourself.
- **`resolvePublicHost`:** split out of `assertPublicUrl` in `src/lib/calendar/net.ts` and re-exported from `src/lib/net.ts`. It prefers an IPv4 answer, because serverless hosts often have no IPv6 route out. `assertPublicUrl` behaves the same as before.
- **Docs:** `docs/production.md` and the README mailbox section.

## Note
An existing custom mailbox on a non-standard port, or on a private host, will now fail to sync with that 400 message. The presets (Gmail, iCloud, Yahoo, Zoho, Fastmail) all use standard ports.

## Verification
- `tsc`: clean.
- `lint`: 0 errors. The one existing warning is in `scripts/load/run.mjs`, which this PR doesn't touch.
- All 24 `scripts/test-*.ts` exit 0. `test-prod` adds 11 mail checks covering:
  - 14 private hosts and literals refused;
  - non-mail ports refused, and IMAP and SMTP keeping to their own ports;
  - a public IP literal and a bracketed IPv6 literal;
  - a name pinned to its checked address with SNI kept;
  - a rebinding name refused;
  - the IMAP client never built for a private host.
- `pnpm build`: succeeds.
- Against a local TLS server, connecting to `127.0.0.1` with the server name set to the certificate's name succeeds, and a different name is refused with `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID`. So pinning to the IP keeps certificate checks intact.
- **Not tested:** a live connection to a real mail server, because the sandbox has no outside DNS.

author: iamtharunsai
body:
Preparing the Rainlight office view exposed two missing evidence fields: specialist entries could only be matched by display name, and a session's newest event could be mistaken for activity at every desk. This adds optional stable specialist IDs, per-specialist event receipt/stage, and an explicit alias map for challenge participants. A later session stage does not invent per-specialist final-vote activity.

Four new reducer contracts cover stage/freshness independence, all fourteen canonical names and unknown/prototype names, complete-transcript attribution and bounded concurrent histories. Existing event/auth/session behavior and limits remain unchanged. Complete-transcript times mean receipt of that transcript, not reconstructed historical timestamps.

This is an evidence prerequisite only: no city screen, avatars, microphone, financial controls or backend event topology are added. The separate Rainlight composition remains under review.

Validation at publication: source/whitespace review passed. Local test execution is blocked because Windows has about 53 MB free memory and WSL reports insufficient system resources (0x800705aa); no host test fallback was used. This PR remains draft until the existing installed frontend build and all fourteen source contracts, plus the other exact-head CI gates, pass. No local passing-test claim is made for this patch.


Release verification: all six exact-head checks succeeded on 96a0300c9e03bf81f15cbc6cb903bbc5472f1778, including the installed frontend build and all fourteen source contracts. Local test execution remained unavailable because WSL could not start; no local pass is claimed. No city UI or voice runtime is implemented by this patch.

author: kaguya-19
body:
## Summary

Project file endpoints trusted request-derived project names as filesystem roots, allowing an authenticated request to read, write or delete files outside registered workspaces. Validate the project registration in the existing file middleware and reuse its authorized root throughout the file endpoints, including workspace uploads.

- Reject unregistered absolute paths and dash-encoded names without trusting the project presentation cache; retain registered IDs, registered absolute paths and backed legacy IDs.
- Reject file operations for roots overlapping PILOT_HOME, including its parents and descendants, closing the report's parent-directory bypass.
- Remove the file-tree path-decoding fallback.

This change is limited to the reported file API vulnerability. Shared project/session resolution, Git/Memory/Taskmaster behavior, symlink policy and General attachment storage remain unchanged. File routes remain in the existing server entrypoint.

## Validation

- 4 focused test files, 33 tests passed: project filesystem middleware and reported HTTP handlers, project registration, existing workspace uploads, and existing project/session management.
- Coverage includes unauthenticated rejection; unregistered absolute/dash roots; binary download, read, write, delete and upload rejection; PILOT_HOME parent/child roots; removed registrations; and legitimate project operations.
- Server entrypoint syntax check and git diff --check passed.
- Tests use temporary files and simulated authentication. No report scripts, production systems or real secrets were accessed; full gateway and deployment acceptance were not run.

author: mattiavolpe
body:
💡 **What**: Replaced static component imports in `src/router.js` with dynamic imports (`() => import(...)`).

🎯 **Why**: Previously, all Vue components were statically imported, forcing Vite to bundle the entire application into a single, large JavaScript file loaded upfront. Using dynamic imports enables route-level code splitting, meaning a component's code is only downloaded when the user actually navigates to that route.

📊 **Impact**: Reduces the initial JavaScript bundle size, leading to a faster initial page load time. The `index.js` file is significantly smaller, as view components (like Projects, Contact, etc.) are now separated into their own lazy-loaded chunks.

🔬 **Measurement**: To verify, run `pnpm run build` and observe the output. Vite will list multiple `.js` chunk files (e.g., `AppHome-*.js`, `ProjectsView-*.js`) instead of bundling everything into `index-*.js`. Additionally, navigating between routes in the browser's Network tab will show smaller JavaScript files being requested on-demand.
