author: lucas-blip-png
body:
Related to #40.

The game binary uses BMI1 (about 700 `andn`, 2900 `bextr`, `blsi`, `blsr`, `tzcnt`), `lzcnt` and `movbe` (about 280), because the PS4's Jaguar CPU has them. On older CPUs (Intel Sandy/Ivy Bridge, early AMD) this ends in `0xc000001d` / "Failed to patch address ... andn" and the window closes. `tzcnt`/`lzcnt` do not even fault there: they decode as `bsf`/`bsr`, which return different values for a zero input, so the guest would compute wrong results silently.

This adds one CPUID check in `main` before the guest is loaded. If a feature is missing, it shows a message box (Windows) and exits with the same text on stderr, e.g. `This CPU is not supported: it lacks BMI1 LZCNT MOVBE (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer is required).`

Emulating the missing instructions would mean patching several thousand sites, so I did not try that; it can be a separate discussion.

Tested: MSYS2 CLANG64 build links and the game starts as before on a CPU that has all three features. The failure path was not exercised on real hardware (no pre-Haswell CPU here).

author: juliuslov
body:
## What this is

The 1.x plugin (`installer.nvim`) is now **kaeru.nvim 2.0**: same plugin-installer core, plus a real music player, casting from the YouTube / YouTube Music apps, autocomplete that covers *everything*, and integration with the Neovim plugins you already run.

`python3 tests/run.py tests/run.lua` → **60 passed, 0 failed** (was 10 failing before this work).

---

## 1. Rename: installer.nvim → kaeru.nvim

| 1.x | 2.x |
| --- | --- |
| `require("installer")`, `lua/installer/**` | `require("kaeru")`, `lua/kaeru/**` |
| `:Installer` | `:Kaeru` |
| `:MusicPlayer`, `require("installer.music")` | `:Kikru`, `require("kaeru.kikru")` |
| `doc/installer.txt`, `plugin/installer.lua` | `doc/kaeru.txt`, `plugin/kaeru.lua` |
| `music:` in `kaeru.yaml` | `kikru:` (both accepted) |
| `nvim-installer-music.sock`, `stdpath("data")/installer/…` | `nvim-kaeru-kikru.sock`, `stdpath("data")/kaeru/…` |

The GitHub slug stays `getwizardo/installer.nvim`, so lazy.nvim specs keep working unchanged. `:MusicPlayer` remains as an alias of `:Kikru`, `require("kaeru").music` as an alias of `.kikru`.

## 2. `:Kikru` — a Winamp-style player in Lua

Feature set researched from [cliamp](https://github.com/bjarneo/cliamp) (layout, EQ, radio, providers) and [NodeLink](https://github.com/PerformanC/NodeLink) / [lavalink-client](https://github.com/tomato6966/lavalink-client) (filter vocabulary, source prefixes, worker-per-player):

* LCD marquee, FFT spectrum / bars / wave / VU / matrix / starfield analyzers (cava-compatible config)
* 10-band EQ (31 Hz … 16 kHz), per-band editing (`:Kikru band 3 -2`) and presets (`flat`, `lofi-coding`, `synthwave`, `bass-boost`, `vocal`, `night`, …)
* LavaLink-style filter chain: timescale, tremolo, vibrato, 8D rotation, karaoke, lowpass, echo, reverb, chorus, phaser, compressor, distortion, channel mix
* internet radio (curated + Radio Browser search), synced lyrics (tags → `.lrc` → [LRCLIB](https://lrclib.net)), M3U/PLS/TOML/JSON playlists, file-library indexing, MPRIS/MPD control
* multi-engine backends: mpv (IPC + equalizer + lavfi), ffplay, VLC, mpc, playerctl — `:Kikru engine` reports capabilities; state persisted to `stdpath("data")/kaeru/kikru.json`

Robustness fixes forced by tests: `backend.load` now fails fast with *"no audio backend found — install mpv, ffplay or VLC (see :Kikru engine)"* instead of restarting the engine in a loop, and `auto_advance()` / `playback_error()` are re-entrancy- and streak-capped so a dead track can no longer recurse into a stack overflow.

## 3. Casting YouTube & YouTube Music

```vim
:Kikru cast https://music.youtube.com/watch?v=…    " play
:Kikru cast https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL…  " expand into the queue
:Kikru cast lofi hip hop radio                     " not a URL ⇒ YT Music search
:Kikru youtube|ytmusic <terms> [--queue|--next]
:Kikru appcast        " continue what the YouTube Music app / a tab / Spotify plays (MPRIS)
:Kikru cast server    " HTTP cast server on 127.0.0.1:8722 (+ browser page, JSON API)
:Kikru cast scheme    " install the kikru:// URL handler ("Open with Kikru")
```

The classifier handles `watch`, `youtu.be`, `shorts/`, `live/`, `playlist?list=`, `channel/`, `@handle`, `m.youtube.com`, `&t=1m30s`, SoundCloud sets/tracks, Spotify, Bandcamp, Mixcloud, Bilibili, Twitch, Vimeo, archive.org, Icecast/SHOUTcast streams, and rejects `mailto:`/`magnet:`/`ftp:` with HTTP 415. Endpoints: `/cast`, `/ytm`, `/youtube`, `/appcast`, `/status`, `/queue`, `/eq`, `/volume`, `/play|pause|toggle|next|prev|stop`, CORS-enabled, optional `?token=`.

## 4. Autocomplete everything

* fuzzy `:` completion for `:Kaeru` / `:Kikru` / `:Clina` — every subcommand, every argument position (repositories with **live GitHub search**, Mason packages, SFTP profiles, cache entries, AI presets, EQ presets, filters, visualizers, themes, engines, radio stations, queue actions, cast targets, playlists, paths), with descriptions in the popup, live popup while typing, `<Tab>`/`<S-Tab>` cycling
* `complete.any = true` extends completion to **every** `:` command line (files, buffers, options, events, filetypes, colorschemes, help tags, mappings, env vars, shell commands, augroups, tags)
* ready-made **nvim-cmp** and **blink.cmp** command-line/`:` sources
* `:Kaeru complete <partial>` — pick from every candidate for a partial line and run it

## 5. Integrations (`:Kaeru integrations`)

telescope.nvim extension (`:Telescope kaeru plugins|mason|sftp|cache|radio|queue|cast`), fzf-lua, snacks.nvim picker, mini.pick, `vim.ui.select` fallback; lualine component + plain statusline; nvim-notify/fidget; plenary jobs; colorscheme-aware Kikru themes; binary report (`yt-dlp`, `mpv`, `ffplay`, `ffmpeg`, `vlc`, `mpc`, `playerctl`, `gh`, `fzf`, `node`/`deno`/`bun`, …). Everything degrades gracefully when a plugin or binary is missing.

## 6. Docs

`README.md` and `doc/kaeru.txt` gained chapters for autocomplete, the Kikru player, casting, integrations, a requirements table of optional binaries, and a 1.x → 2.x migration table.

---

### Scope note

The `starsky/` Next.js webclient is deliberately untouched apart from a cosmetic string fix — this PR is the Neovim plugin.

author: gucardona
body:
## O que é
Um consultor financeiro dentro do app. Cada usuário coloca a própria chave da API da Anthropic em **Ajustes > Assistente**, escolhe o modelo (Haiku, Sonnet padrão, Opus), liga o chat e define por quantos dias as conversas ficam guardadas (1 a 30, padrão 7). Aparece uma aba **Chat** que responde por texto, em streaming, sobre os gastos (somente leitura), com gráficos simples (barras, linha, pizza). Há um seletor de carteiras (padrão: a atual; "Selecionar todas").

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-assistente-consulta-design.md` · Plano: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-15-assistente-consulta.md` · Guia: `docs/assistente.md`

## Segurança
- Chave da Anthropic criptografada (AES-GCM) com `GASTOS_SECRET_KEY`; nunca volta ao navegador, nem entra em log ou erro (só os 4 últimos caracteres).
- Cada rota nova confere sessão e associação a cada carteira; as ferramentas só leem as carteiras já autorizadas pelo servidor; SQL parametrizado.
- Erros internos das ferramentas não chegam ao modelo.

## ⚠️ Atenção: este merge faz deploy em produção
O schema virou um só (`schema.sql`, versão 3) e as migrations foram removidas. **O banco de produção precisa ser recriado** (os dados atuais são descartados, decisão do Gustavo). Siga os passos 1 a 4 de `docs/assistente.md` **antes** de mesclar (backup fora do servidor, parar o serviço, mover o banco antigo, definir `GASTOS_SECRET_KEY`). Se mesclar antes, a nova versão se recusa a abrir o banco antigo, o `/healthz` falha e o deploy volta sozinho; nada se perde.

## Testes
Go (`-race`), 462 testes no Vitest, e2e (desktop e celular) contra uma Anthropic falsa. Fora desta parte: ferramentas de escrita com confirmação (parte 2) e voz (parte 3).

author: jeong-byeong-hun
body:
## 요약

장비·장신구 풀세트 풀강 기준으로 **실측 딜량**(게임 안에서 측정)과 **추정 딜량**(코드 계산)을 비교한 문서 `docs/DAMAGE.md`를 추가합니다. 측정하다 찾은 버그(스킬 부채꼴 투사체가 바로 앞의 적에게 여러 발 맞던 문제)도 고쳤습니다. 버전 0.5.30.

| 직업 | 추정 DPS | 실측 DPS | 실측 / 추정 (무기 평균) | 무기별 범위 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 전사 | 152.7 | 152.8 | **100%** | 92% ~ 116% |
| 도적 | 219.9 | 213.8 | **97%** | 81% ~ 123% |
| 법사 | 242.7 | 270.7 | **112%** | 89% ~ 150% |
| 궁수 | 196 | 197.3 | **101%** | 85% ~ 119% |
| 해적 | 176 | 185.5 | **106%** | 96% ~ 112% |
| 사신 | 209.5 | 206.4 | **98%** | 76% ~ 130% |
| 헌터 | 224.2 | 226.9 | **101%** | 90% ~ 118% |

- **7 / 7개 직업**이 95~120% 안에 들어왔습니다. 무기 하나씩 보면 63개 중 39개이고, 나머지 24개는 문서의 "95~120% 밖의 무기" 표에 이유와 함께 있습니다.
- 측정 조건: Lv 100, 4차 무기 +15 ✦5, 그 레벨 최고 방어구 세트 +15 ✦5, 에테릭스 장신구 5부위 +10(추가 옵션·각인 없음), 특성은 1마리 피해 최대 분배, 훈련용 허수아비 상대로 60초.

## 변경 내용

### 게임플레이: 스킬 부채꼴 투사체는 적마다 1발 (`Actions`, `CombatHooks`)
- 부채꼴로 퍼지는 스킬 투사체(49개 스킬)가 한 번 시전할 때 적 하나에 1발만 맞습니다. 기본 사격의 `BasicAttacks.Fan`과 같은 규칙입니다.
- 이전에는 바로 앞의 적이나 큰 보스가 옆으로 퍼진 투사체까지 다 맞아서 툴팁·문서보다 2~5배 피해가 들어갔습니다(아론다이트 "호수 베기", 카미쉬의 분노 "용아 투척" 등). 이 무기들이 실측에서 추정의 140~180%로 나와서 찾았습니다.
- 바닐라 화살로 쏘는 스킬도 `trackSkillArrow(..., fan)`로 같은 fan을 씁니다. 나란히 쏘는 스킬(`parallel`)과 한 방향 연사는 이전과 같습니다.

### 추정 계산 (`ClassComparison`)
- `build(job, level, Loadout, Scenario)`: 같은 추정을 어떤 강화·각성·장신구 조합과 대상(문서용 `Scenario.DOCS`, 허수아비용 `Scenario.dummy`)에도 쓸 수 있게 했습니다.
- `CombatHooks.outgoing`과 같은 순서로 계산합니다. 주는 피해·보스 피해·선제 일격은 모든 타격의 같은 보너스 칸에 더하고, 최종 피해는 맨 마지막에 곱합니다. 연쇄 번개는 맞은 대상에게도 떨어지고 보너스가 한 번 더 붙습니다. 활은 당기는 시간 + 1틱마다 1발입니다.
- 스킬의 지원 효과를 넣었습니다. 새 `SkillSupport`와 `SkillAction.supports()`로 버프, 표식, 강화 타격·은신, 취약, 재사용 단축을 보고하고, 실제 사용 빈도에서 유지되는 시간만큼 셉니다. CLASSES.md 표는 이전처럼 지원 효과를 빼고 계산합니다.

### 측정 테스트 (`DamageClientGameTest`, 수동 실행)
- 실행: `./gradlew runClientGameTest -Ptests=damage`. 약 1시간 걸리고, `TestSelection.MANUAL`에 넣어 전체 스위트에서는 빠집니다.
- 테스트 내용:
  - 스킬마다 1회 피해를 따로 잽니다(치명타 운은 타격마다 뺍니다).
  - 플레이어처럼 1분 동안 싸웁니다. 게이지가 차면 휘두르고, 활은 끝까지 당기고, 스킬은 준비되면 버프부터 씁니다. 닿지 않는 스킬은 앞으로 나가서 쓰고, 이동 스킬 뒤에는 제자리로 돌아옵니다.
  - 결과를 `damage-report.md`/`.tsv`로 씁니다.
- `TickRateCap` + `MinecraftTickRateMixin`(gametest 소스셋 전용): 클라이언트가 `/tick rate`를 따라가게 해서 측정이 약 1.7배 빨라집니다.
- 옵션: `-Dminecraft_mode.damage.classes/weapons`로 일부만 측정하고, `.reuse`로 이전 TSV를 합칩니다.

### 문서
- `docs/DAMAGE.md`(새 문서), `docs/CLASSES.md`(다시 생성), `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md`를 바꿨습니다.
- CLASSES.md "직업 비교" Lv 100(평균 대비): 전사 91% → 90%, 도적 95% → 94%, 궁수 109% → 105%, 해적 91% → 99%, 사신 105% → 104%. 모든 차수가 90~110% 안입니다.

## 테스트
- `runClientGameTestParallel`(전체 스위트) 통과했습니다(28분 37초).
- `JobClientGameTest`에 확인을 하나 추가했습니다. 2블록 앞에서 쓴 "호수 베기"가 검기 1.75발보다 적게 들어가야 하고, 측정은 43.2 대 검기 1발 43.9로 통과했습니다.
- `-Ptests=damage`로 7개 직업 63개 무기를 측정했고, 결과는 `docs/DAMAGE.md`에 있습니다.

## 참고
- 실측값은 직업을 나눠 돌린 여러 번의 실행을 `.reuse`로 합친 것입니다. 마지막 문서는 추정만 다시 계산했습니다.
- 허수아비 한계: 체력이 줄지 않아 선제 일격은 항상 붙고 처형은 붙지 않습니다. 갑옷 거치대라 취약 같은 상태 효과도 받지 않습니다. 추정도 같은 조건으로 계산했습니다.

author: isseis
body:
## Summary

Step 2-4 of task 0011 (`docs/tasks/0011_localhost_server/03_implementation_plan.md`, PR-6).

- **`cmd/yt2column-server`.** `main` runs `run` under `signalrun.Run`. `run` starts the server in the order architecture §3.1 sets:
  1. `config.LoadServer`
  2. The shared token: loaded, or created and shown once on stdout, before listening.
  3. The components: LLM clients, the writer with the CLI's default steps, `SlackWebhookPublisher`, `SlackFailureNotifier`, and `internal/server` with the API keys, the Webhook URL and the token as redacted secrets.
  4. `Listen` on 127.0.0.1 and ::1.
  5. `Serve` until the first signal, then wait for in-flight jobs. A second signal exits at once.

  Exit codes: 2 before listening, 1 for a listen or serve failure, 0 after a signal.
- **`make build`** builds both binaries. `allowedEnvRefs` lists `cmd/yt2column-server/main.go`. `package_reference.md` has the new row.
- **`internal/server`:**
  - `ArticlesPath` is exported, so the listening URLs are logged from the one definition.
  - `Serve` logs the shutdown with the pending job count (architecture §3.10). PR-5 did not log this.
- **Writer defaults.** The two `package main`s cannot import each other. So `writertestutil.DefaultOptions` holds the default writer options, and both the CLI test (`TestRunDefaultWriterOptions`) and the server test (`TestWriterOptionsMatchCLIDefaults`) compare against it. Architecture §3.1 and §7.1 now describe this mechanism.
- **Logging race.** `run` serializes stderr. Its own logger and the server's write from different goroutines; `-race` found this.

## Review points (plan PR-6)

- Startup order and exit codes 2/1/0 follow architecture §3.1. The architecture's exit-code set "2・3・4・5" in the plan's review point reads as a typo for the §3.1 codes: 0, 1 and 2.
- `server.Options.Secrets` holds the API keys, the Webhook URL and the shared token. `TestOutputsOmitSecrets` leaks both keys, the URL and the token through an LLM error and checks they are redacted on stderr.
- The integration test (`TestServerEndToEnd`) swaps the LLM client in `deps` for a fake, and uses the real publisher and notifier pointed at a loopback webhook. It passes an `https` `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL`; it does not pass the `httptest` `http://` URL.
- Child processes register kill and reap in `t.Cleanup` as soon as they start.
- The request ID the server generates passes the real `SlackFailureNotifier` check. The notice reaches the loopback webhook with the response's `requestId`.

## Test results

- `make test` and `make lint` pass. Each new test was confirmed to fail with its target broken; the commit messages list each break.
- **Real socket, AC-12.** On the macOS loopback, a body of 4 MiB + 1 bytes with a wrong token received `401 unauthorized`.

## Manual checks still to record (plan §2, completion conditions)

- [ ] AC-01: a connection to the machine's external interface address is refused.
- [ ] The failure notice in Mattermost: the `video:` line's `<URL>` is rendered as a link, and the three lines keep their line breaks.

## Known gaps (recorded, not fixed)

- When a listener fails while serving, `Serve` waits for jobs with no guidance in the log. The stop notice is tied to the signal and is also logged when nothing is in flight.
- The serve-failure exit path is checked only by reading `run`, plus `internal/server`'s `TestServeListenerFailureStops`.
- The test helper that waits for the server to start probes only the IPv4 address. If another process takes the port in between, the test can fail with a misleading message. This is unlikely.
- `splitJoined` and `stderrWriter` and a few test helpers are copied from `cmd/yt2column`.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s `make build` text is updated in step 2-5 (PR-7).
- `TestCommandExecutorDrainsStderr` in `internal/transcript` failed once in the pre-commit hook under load. It passed 5/5 on its own; this PR does not touch that package.

author: garthvh
body:
## Summary
The device models were built from the flasher's front-view illustrations alone, so backs, sides, depths, ports, stands and antennas were guessed or missing, and a few illustrations weren't front views at all. This rebuilds all 35 from measurements of the vendors' CAD, mechanical drawings and photos, and adds the generator features that needed.

## What changed
- Generator:
  - A spec can set `drawing = "drawings/<name>.svg"` to use our own front drawing instead of the flasher's illustration.
  - `[[solid]]` places a block in mm on any face, with a size, rotation and corner radius, for ports, buttons, screws, stands, boxes and connectors.
  - `render.swift` renders the back (`back`, `back-three-quarter`).
- Every spec records where its figures come from:
  - Elecrow's and Seeed's CAD for the CrowPanels, ThinkNode M1/M2, the SenseCAP Indicator, the XIAO kits and the Wio Tracker L1 case
  - RAK's mechanical drawings for the WisBlock boards and the WisMesh hub
  - calibrated vendor photos for the rest, marked as estimated
- 18 devices whose illustration wasn't a clean front view (perspective, several views at once, cables over the face, or a bare board where the device ships in a case) now use our own drawing in `scripts/device-models/drawings/`.
- Size corrections include:
  - the RAK 4631 case, which is the WisMesh Pocket V2
  - the WM1110 dev board
  - the Indicator, the CrowPanels (which follow Elecrow's current case revision), and the ThinkNode M2, M7 and M9
- All 35 models in `Meshtastic/Resources/DeviceModels` rebuilt, including the linear color fix from #2618.

Vendor CAD and photos are used for measurement only and aren't in the repo or the models. The geometry is ours.

## Known limits
- Openings, seams, lanyard holes and recesses are painted as dark areas rather than cut, because the generator can't cut into the body yet. That's the most common gap across the devices and the next generator change.
- The WisMesh Pocket V3's back, bottom and depth are unconfirmed (RAK publishes no V3 drawings). The ThinkNode M6's back and the Wio Tracker L1 Pro 1W's case are photo or inference based. Photos of devices we own (Tag, Pocket, T1000-E, L1, M9, Solar Node) would firm these up.

## Testing
- `build.sh` builds all 35 and `usdchecker --arkit` passes for each.
- Each device was compared front and back against its CAD views or reference photos, then checked again by a second pass that re-measured the key figures and fixed what was off.
- The flasher's USDZ and GLB copies will follow in one flasher PR after this merges.

Closes #33 (PQ-13). Design source: docs/spec.md#10-test-and-verification-strategy; gates: ADR-0002, ADR-0003.

## What

- **quicx diagnostics** (the PQ-11 acceptance leftover): the QUIC handshake emits the decision line the TCP ladder emits — negotiated (offered/negotiated/group_class/alpn/dial_ms/handshake_ms) and classified answers (refused/blocked + udp_blocked, warn/error levels). Watched-RED→GREEN pair.

Diagnostics must cover both planes; provenance must be verifiable by the operators the governance page targets.

author: malu-m2
body:
… push

## What

- **Typed client over the Weclapp v2 API** — `WeclappClient` plus 156 generated endpoint classes, one per documented resource, with a lazy response proxy, a queued `WeclappApiCallJob`, `WeclappApiCallCompleted` events and a logging listener. Per-call base URL and token come from config, with rate limiting, retries and timeouts configurable.
- **Mirror tables and sync** — nine mirror models (`Party`, `Article`, `ArticleCategory`, `ArticlePrice`, `User`, `Quotation`, `SalesOrder`, `SalesInvoice`, `Project`) with publishable migrations, a declarative `SyncRegistry`, `weclapp:sync` (full, with reconciliation that archives rows Weclapp no longer returns) and `weclapp:update --since` (delta). Article rows flatten the main image, both text fields, `primarySupplySourceId`, the `supplySources` count and a configurable article tag (`MINDTWO_WECLAPP_VISIBLE_TAG`) as the `visible` boolean — empty means every article; price rows flatten the price-relevant `reductionAdditions` entry. A field a user clears in Weclapp is written through as `null` — Weclapp omits empty fields rather than sending them.
- **Write safety and tooling** — `writes_enabled` suppresses `POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE` (logged, neutral response) and defaults off in `local`/`testing` only; the client can dry-run a `PUT` and upload a binary. `weclapp:make-mirror` scaffolds a mirror from the vendored OpenAPI spec (`docs/specifications/`), which the endpoint and registry tests are validated against.

## Why

Consuming applications need Weclapp as the source of truth for articles, prices, customers and quotations, and they need it through one tested, typed layer instead of ad-hoc HTTP calls per app — with local mirror tables so pages and resolvers read from the database, and with writes that can be switched off outside production. The history is 84 commits of iterative development squashed to one; the `Squashed commits:` list in the commit body preserves every original subject.

## How to test

- [ ] `composer install` and `vendor/bin/pest` — 145 tests, 5 465 assertions; covers every endpoint path, every spec resource through the mirror generator, the sync and reconcile behaviour, write suppression, the visible-tag derivation and the `MINDTWO_WECLAPP_*` config/env pinning.
- [ ] `composer lint` (pint) and `composer analyse` (phpstan, 512M) pass.
- [ ] CI matrix: `L12.*/testbench 10.*` and `L13.*/testbench 11.*`, `prefer-lowest` and `prefer-stable`, on Ubuntu and Windows — all green. `orchestra/canvas` and `orchestra/canvas-core` (pulled in by testbench 10) are pinned to `preferred-install: source` in `composer.json`, because GitHub's by-commit archives for them 404 intermittently and Composer no longer falls back from dist to source; everything else installs from dist.
- [ ] In a consuming app: `php artisan vendor:publish --tag=weclapp-api-migrations`, migrate, set `MINDTWO_WECLAPP_URL`, `MINDTWO_WECLAPP_API_KEY` and (if you filter by tag) `MINDTWO_WECLAPP_VISIBLE_TAG`, run `weclapp:sync articles` and `weclapp:sync article-prices`, and check the mirror tables fill; a second run must leave `updated_at` untouched on unchanged rows.

## Migrations

Publishable, tagged — consumers opt in:

- `create_weclapp_parties_table` — customers and suppliers (one table, `customer_number` / `supplier_number`)
- `create_weclapp_article_categories_table`
- `create_weclapp_articles_table` — incl. `visible` (configured tag), `supply_source_count`, `primary_supply_source_id`, main image columns, `long_text`
- `create_weclapp_users_table`
- `create_weclapp_quotations_table`
- `create_weclapp_sales_orders_table`
- `create_weclapp_projects_table`
- `create_weclapp_article_prices_table` — incl. `reduction_type` / `reduction_value`, validity window, soft deletes for reconciliation
- `create_weclapp_sales_invoices_table`

## Notes

**Breaking changes** (the commit carries `!` and a `BREAKING CHANGE` footer):

- The `Amount` and `Report` models, their factories and migrations are removed, as is `Quotation::report()`. Consumers that published those migrations should drop `weclapp_amounts` and `weclapp_reports`.
- Every environment variable is now `MINDTWO_WECLAPP_*`-prefixed; `WECLAPP_TOKEN` becomes `MINDTWO_WECLAPP_API_KEY`. A published `config/weclapp-api.php` keeps working until re-published, so rename the keys there too — the README's "Upgrading" section has the full table.
- Migrations are published rather than auto-loaded; the skeleton files (`configure.php`, `Skeleton*`) are gone and the generator is scoped to development.

**For consumers with a published config:** add `visible_tag` to it (or set `MINDTWO_WECLAPP_VISIBLE_TAG`); with neither, every mirrored article reads as visible.

**Scope of the mirror set:** the nine entities and their column selections are a documented default, not a complete model of Weclapp — an entity gets a mirror when something reads it (see CONTRIBUTING). Further mirrors are added with `weclapp:make-mirror` and a `SyncRegistry` entry.

**Dependencies:** dev stack stays on Pest 4 / PHPUnit 12 with `orchestra/testbench ^10.12 || ^11.1`, because the package supports `illuminate/contracts ^12 || ^13` and Pest 5 cannot resolve for the Laravel 12 line. Node tooling on commitlint 21 / semantic-release plugins at current majors; `pnpm-lock.yaml` is dropped in favour of npm.

**Not in this PR:** nothing writes consumer-side price tables; the mirror's `PriceResolver` only fills gaps. Consumer-specific sync notes live with the consuming applications, not here.

author: kkollu99-ux
body:
## 1. Landing page hamburger (phones)
The menu button now opens a panel with Markets / Platforms / Why FXCM / Contact and Login / Open Account (icon turns into ✕; closes on link tap or when the screen widens). Login and Open Account in the menu use the same flows as the desktop buttons.

## 2. Automatic stop-out (margin protection)
A sweep every 3 s computes each account's equity (free balance + margin held + floating P&L, the dashboard's figure). When margin level (equity ÷ margin held) falls to **20 %** or below (`STOP_OUT_LEVEL_PCT`, `STOP_OUT_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`), the position with the biggest floating loss is closed, repeating until the account is back above the level, so losses can't exceed the account's own money. The user sees "Stop-out (margin protection) triggered on …". Per-position **Stop Loss** and **Take Profit** (profit or loss targets set in the order ticket) already existed and are unchanged.

## 3. Password change signs out other devices
Changing the password inside the account now revokes every other session and returns a fresh token so the current device stays signed in (the client stores it). The revocation cut-off uses the app server's clock (also for Forgot Password) so a token issued right after is never judged older.

## 4. Email addresses
Contact email on the landing page → `support@fxcaptialmarket.online`; demo placeholder → `demo@fxcaptialmarket.online`; README updated. The default admin created on an **empty** database is now `admin@fxcaptialmarket.online`, and it is only created when **no admin exists at all** (previously it was re-created whenever the old default email was missing, which would have put a known default password on the live site). Existing accounts are untouched, including the current `admin@fxcc.capital` login.

## Verified (local, 12/12)
Default admin uses the new email; change-password returns a token, the changing device stays signed in, other devices and the old token get 401, new password logs in; a healthy account keeps its position at the 20 % level, an account under the level is stopped out (tested with a raised level); hamburger opens, shows the menu and Login opens the sign-in screen (screenshot checked).

author: justine-george
body:
A live tab, group or window dragged out of Open now and let go on a saved session saves a copy there. The live tab is not touched. This is the second half of KAN-280 Part F (spec O12c); PR 1 (#520) made the carry record where its item came from.

## What a user can do

- Drag a tab or a group's title row out of Open now, to either side, and drop it on a session row: it becomes that session's first window. "Copied to “…”." with Show.
- Drop it straight into the session on screen at an exact spot, or on a New window target, with no detour through the list. No toast, as for a move.
- Rest on a session row to open it first (spring-open), as for a saved carry.
- Pick up a window by its row (glyph and title) and drop it between the shown session's windows. Its place and state are read from Chrome when the carry starts.
- Drop on the save row to make a new session named by the tab.
- One ⌘Z takes any copy back. Copies sync like any edit.

## Rules

- **Duplicates (D6 A):** tabs whose address the target session already holds are skipped. "Copied to “…”. N tabs were already there." when some were; "Already in “…”." when all were, which saves nothing, records no undo step and does not take ⌘Z from a Reopen offer. An empty address matches nothing.
- **Incognito (Q2 A):** a live incognito tab lands only in an incognito saved window or a new window, which keeps the mark; a normal one never lands in an incognito window.
- **Open now's search (O14c amended B):** a tab row is carried out at once and copies; group and window rows don't pick up.
- **Saved search (D5 A):** a row drop works under it; resting opens nothing.
- **Folded tab view (N3 A):** resting on the selected session's row opens it as a peek.
- **Narrow drawer (N2 A):** once the pointer leaves the drawer, it slides away so every drop works as wide, and comes back after the drop or Esc with its scroll kept. Esc during a carry cancels the carry; the drawer stays open.
- **Over Open now (N4 A):** a live carry let go over Open now is cancelled, including after the shown session adopted it.
- **The live tab closing mid-carry (Q1 A):** the drop saves what was picked up.
- **Skip toast:** wraps to a second line so the count survives a long session name (Justine's pick A), and a name with no spaces breaks inside it.

## How it is built

- `CarriedItem` gains its `live` arm: a snapshot of the live window, converted at pick-up with Save window's converter (`toSavedWindow`, now exported).
- `copyToSessionInternal` and `copyToNewSessionInternal` reuse the move's landing, extracted into `landTabsIn` and `landWindowIn` (the move is unchanged; its tests pin its new-window shape). `liveCopy.ts` decides what lands after D6.
- The copy thunks go through `dropOnTop` like every drop, behind PR 1's router.
- The drag engine gains three opt-in props: `cardOnPickUp`, `handsOffBesidePane`, `carryOnly`. Defaults keep every existing list as it was.
- Open now passes them, with `carryOut` for tabs and groups and a new windows area. It also registers a carry receiver that answers only a live carry and takes nothing (N4 A); saved drags and carries over Open now are as KAN-352 left them.
- Three new toast keys (four with plurals) in 13 locales, each ending with a full stop, reviewed for fluency per locale; Justine picked six changes.

## Decisions made in the plan (P1–P12)

P1 hand off beside Open now's pane, not only at the list · P2 window and searched tab rows are carries from the first move · P3 a cancelled live carry re-selects nothing · P4 no spring-open under the saved search · P5 "on screen" means selected and not folded · P6 a window's place is read from Chrome at carry start · P7 an empty address matches nothing · P8 Esc in the drawer during a carry is the carry's · P9 a copy lands under the snapshot's ids · P10 "Already in" is not a saved change · P11 a skip at an exact spot is silent · P12 a new session from a window is named by its first tab.

## Found while testing, fixed with a test that failed first

- A live carry adopted by the shown session and let go over Open now was saved as a new window (N4 A).
- Wrapping Open now's window block for the new windows area turned two comment lines into text drawn above every window. Three existing e2e tests caught it; all three pass on main's build.
- The copy badge's size and weight broke the shared scale (KAN-205).
- In a narrow window the saved detail adopted a carry under the drawer and handed it straight back, every move.

## Evidence

- Unit, full suite: 478 files, 5529 passed + 7 expected fail, exit 0, no `Errors` line, on Node 22 and Node 26. `tsc` 0. Lint: 0 errors in changed files.
- New e2e `copy-from-open-now.spec.ts`: 15 cases, 30/30 over two runs on bundle fb087c1a. `copy-from-open-now-two-devices.spec.ts` against the dev cloud: device B receives the copy, then the undo.
- e2e mutation controls, each built with its own hash and each failing its case: no hand-off beside the pane → case 2; D6 address set emptied → case 6; drawer never comes back → case 10; no Open now receiver → case 7b.
- Unit mutation controls for every task are in the ledger.
- Full e2e, local, on fb087c1a: 1683 passed, 1 failed: `new-session-drop.spec.ts` N6, which pinned KAN-394's "an Open now tab on the save row changes nothing". N1 A replaces that rule, so the test now asserts a new session holding the copy, with Chrome untouched (d55b0c7c); that spec is 29/29. KAN-605's `first-run-full` passed in this run.
- Toast fit, 13 locales, 41-character name: every count kept and inside the toast after the change (cut in all 13 before).

KAN-280

body:
## 문제
메뉴바 아이콘의 빨간 점과 workspace의 attention 표시는 "무언가 문제가 있다"는 것만 알려 줬습니다. 어느 메뉴, 화면, 탭에서 해결해야 하는지는 알 수 없었습니다.

## 변경
- **판정 규칙 단일화(`src/shared/attention.cjs`):** `attentionAreas()`가 이슈를 해결하는 위치별로 나누고, `attentionNotices()`가 원인 문구를 만듭니다. 트레이와 workspace가 같은 결과를 씁니다.
- **맥 메뉴바 메뉴:** 해당 메뉴 항목에 빨간 점 아이콘을 붙이고, 이름 아래(`sublabel`)에 원인을 표시합니다.

  | 이슈 | 메뉴 항목 |
  | --- | --- |
  | 리소스·코딩 계정 attention | **Dashboard** |
  | 읽기 연결 실패 | **Settings…** (Connections로 이동) |
  | 통합 수리·업데이트, 로컬 전송 설정 오류, 클라우드 전송 확인 실패 | **Integrations…** |
  | 앱 업데이트 | **About VibeMon** |

  아이콘 툴팁은 원인과 열 메뉴를 함께 나열합니다. 메뉴는 원인 문구가 바뀔 때만 다시 만듭니다. macOS에서 클릭 중에 메뉴를 다시 만들면 클릭이 유실되기 때문입니다.
- **앱 화면:** 사이드바의 Resources·Coding agents·Settings와 설정 탭(Connections·Integrations·About)에 빨간 점을 표시합니다. 점의 접근성 이름과 툴팁이 원인입니다. Overview의 Need attention 타일은 "2 resources · 1 account"처럼 위치를 보여 줍니다.
- 문서 `docs/features.md`에 이슈별 표시 위치 표를 추가했습니다.

## 검증
- `pnpm test`: 886 tests 통과. `attention.test.js`를 새로 추가했고, 트레이의 점·sublabel·Settings 경로·재생성 조건을 테스트합니다.
- `pnpm test:workspace`: 통과. 실제 Electron `Menu`에서 Integrations 항목의 sublabel을 확인하고, 설정 탭 점의 접근성 이름도 확인합니다.
- 스크린샷으로 사이드바와 About 탭의 점, Need attention 타일 문구를 확인했습니다.
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm check:distribution`: 통과

## 메뉴 정리 (추가)
트레이 preference를 workspace로 옮길 때 메뉴의 버전 표시가 사라졌습니다. 메뉴를 다음과 같이 정리합니다.
```
VibeMon 3.8.5            (비활성 머리글)
──
Dashboard                ● 원인
Show companion
──
Settings…        ⌘,      ● 원인
Integrations…            ● 원인
──
About VibeMon            ● 원인
Quit VibeMon     ⌘Q
```
실제 Electron `Menu`로 메뉴를 만들어 항목, 단축키, sublabel, 아이콘을 확인했습니다.

author: wzj003243-dotcom
body:
## Product milestone — evidence-first public reading
Replaces the old `/analyze` form and heuristic fate percentages with a simple three-step, mobile-friendly experience: (1) birth date & optional time, (2) past milestones (optional), (3) one area of future interest. Offers fictional one-click example for zero-friction preview.

The report explicitly divides:
1. **Past facts** — user's own dated milestones, never called predictions.
2. **Possible futures** — three actionable scenarios without synthetic or uncalibrated likelihoods.
3. **Traditional interpretation** — optional, labeled symbolic calendar readings; no invented birth hour, no DaYun from unchecked local time, no causal "fortune" claims.
4. **Scientific evidence** — frozen R6 age-only research biography event-density benchmark with units, sample exposure and heavy generalization warnings. Does NOT apply R6 rates to a person's life, or equate user milestones with source-canonical events.

Scientific model contract:
- `lib/public-reading.ts` validates dates/ages, strips future events, records a read cutoff, never generates a personal prediction probability, prevents using nonexistent birth hour, prevents trained-range extrapolation, and preserves source provenance.
- Cohort research counts are shown only as **documented historical events per 1,000 research person-years**, NOT as probabilities of real-world events.
- Current R7B negative traditional prediction result remains; no BaZi signal granted positive predictive weight.
- All browser-side during preview; no automatic storage/submission.
- Test coverage in `tests/public-reading.test.ts`.

The legacy `lib/model.ts` heuristic utilities are **not called by this new public flow**; no retroactive accuracy claim.

**Draft PR** pending typecheck, full tests, build, and user experience review. Old R4/R5 test individuals remain untouched. No production release planned.

author: betorzdev
body:
Each task in Progress's Tasks tab now carries the lists' round pin to the Map (design round 78, Albert's picks: A in all four).

**Where the pin goes** (`taskPin()` in `js/app-progress.js`):
- Before the task is taken: whoever gives it, its Wishwall (`board:`) or whoever asks (`giver:`), through the existing `wishFrom` (the Pre's board first).
- Once taken: what's still to do of it on the Map (what it asks for and where it's done, `js/spots.js` TASKS by its quest or a stage before it that no other task names). When nothing is left, back to whoever gives it.
- A main objective: the game's own pin for it. The melodies and the Old Hearts go to their pieces. After the Fall takes the game pin whose check stands for it.
- Without a save: whoever gives it, or else its marks.
- One mark opens `App.mapShow`; several open `App.mapFocus` (only those marks, ‹ i of n ›, nearest to the bench first). The rows reuse the road's `FOCUS` map and the `pgFocus` action.
- A task with no mark keeps the empty slot, and a task done has no pin, as in the 100% lists.

`row()` changes in one place: a row can carry a `focus` key in place of a single `mark`. Tasks set no `mark`, so Free mode's mark boxes don't appear on them.

**Test:** `test/spots.test.js` checks that every wish and main objective (all 74) has a place on the Map, either who gives it or what it asks for. It reads `TASK_QUEST` from the source, so the two can't drift apart.

**Checked:**
- `npm test`: 189 pass.
- Coverage over all 73 saves in Albert's folder plus Free mode (headless, `tools/drive.js`): 2,898 open task rows, every one with a pin, 0 console errors.
- Clicks land on the right mark:
  - Beast in the Bells (Save 2): the Map focus on its 13 marks.
  - Silver Bells (Save 2, at 390): Bellhart's Wishwall, picked.
  - Songclave Supplies, taken (Save 1): its delivery spot.
  - Heart of Might (Free mode): the Encrusted Heart.

Docs: `docs/guide.md` (the Tasks paragraph) and `design/03-redesign.md` (step 5, the round and its decision). The variants page isn't committed.

author: commdata2338
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

For the fixed PR #2021 P112 two-column completion with ports `(0,1)` and coefficient `+1`, the sharp separate COPY-power minimum remains

`7*8^q + 7^q + 1`, for every `0<q<=1`,

when **any finite number of complex rank-one terms is allowed and both factors stay in the completion's minimal nine-dimensional column and row spaces**. COPY has sharp minimum 64. For `q<1`, the minimum is still strictly above `8*8^q`.

This extends Hanhong Zhao's [PR #2321](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2321), which covers exactly nine terms. Its support catalogue and rational attainer are credited and reconstructed independently. The new proof replaces termwise nine-dimensional duality with an eight-dimensional projection argument when exactly eight terms are mixed, and a rank-three bound on the aggregate cost-seven contribution when more terms are mixed. A compensation argument allows arbitrary numbers of pure terms, including nonzero zero-COPY terms.

The new package is `research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces/`. It contains the proof, exact certificate, verifier, source pins and registered replay. An eleven-term in-space fixture attains the bound with two nonzero zero-COPY terms. A ten-term boundary fixture in the one-dimensional right-space extension `col(R)+Ce_0` has profile `(8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,0,0)`, demonstrating that the factor-space restriction is essential for the power bound.

This is a **scoped proof supported by finite certificates**, not an unrestricted masked-decoder barrier, physical supplier, completed moment, or κ improvement. Native frames, arbitrary-dirty realization, shared COPY work, precision, reserve, hosting and all-size transfer remain unchecked. The written universal argument is not formally verified or independently human-reviewed.

## Task and overlap

- **Task ID / scope key:** `complex-new-helper-inventory` / `f3b0895a4f9f1cc62e75`, refined to `P112/fixed-completion-01/lambda1/overcomplete-both-minimal-factor-spaces/COPY-floor`. Full machine-readable card: `TASK.json` in the package.
- **Chooser:** original nonce `b839c7d51965d70bcac5d0fde27becf6`, track `complex-mechanisms`, priority revision 4; no reroll. The first suggestion was used with a scoped override to the explicit more-terms handoff in [discussion #2006](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2006#discussioncomment-18940755). Other suggestions were `p104-side-correction` and `complex-rank-shape-decoder`; active overlap ruled out those scopes.
- **Base:** `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. Final `git fetch origin main` checkpoint at 2026-10-15 07:11 UTC found this same commit, revision 4, and no changed guidance, selected record or input.
- **Predecessors / exact dependency heads:** PR #2021 `9943467c4b24d2050275a202e3866cfc522afbe7`; PR #2321 `0665be26c2db1bd7f393d829e786698b34b626e4`, anonymously refetched and unchanged at the final checkpoint. Only the main-branch root prototype is a runtime scientific input. Pending predecessor code is not imported or required; its proof provenance is pinned in `SOURCES.json`.
- **Concrete object / question:** for `K=LR^T`, `L=[X,e_0]`, `R=[(I-e_0e_0^T)X,4e_0+e_1]`, determine the separate actual-support COPY-power minimum over every finite identity decomposition `sum_i m_i n_i^T=I_9`.
- **Scope status / changed restriction:** changed from the original positive physical-inventory card to a bounded algebraic obstruction. Drop the exactly-nine-term / invertible-dual-basis premise, retaining both minimal factor spaces, original labels and separate billing. Nonzero zero-COPY terms remain admissible.
- **Method / parameter domain:** all finite complex term counts, ordinary transpose, fixed ports and coefficient; exact rational kernels for 511 nonzero binary characters per side, complete class-pair table, written rank/compensation proof and rational fixtures.
- **Bottleneck / optimistic budget:** asks whether extra terms alone can lower the fixed decoder's COPY64 or concave power bill. The result rules this out inside both spaces. It does not meet the original physical-inventory acceptance gate or supply a complete local invoice.
- **Success evidence / stop rule / budget:** one fixed completion; stop after the all-length proof, all-entry witnesses, finite premises and failure controls. One approximately 60-minute session; no search over coefficients, port pairs, physical sharing or other suppliers.
- **Nearest overlap:** PR #2321 has exactly nine terms; PR #2021 proves completion rank and displays COPY65. The [parallel coefficient-family claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2006#discussioncomment-18942817) varies the coefficient with exactly nine terms. PR #2308's shared-plane correction and the two-call cross-form problem are different matrices/interfaces. The other active helper-inventory scope concerns PR #2339's T74 native compensation.
- **Coordination:** [canonical claim in discussion #2006](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2006#discussioncomment-18942846). Final offline overlap queries used all terms `2321` + `terms`, and path `research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces/*`. Snapshot coverage: 587 open PRs including drafts at `2026-10-15T07:07:38.026722Z`, 1,116 Discussion records at `07:09:50.407275Z`, and changed-file records for 590 PRs at `07:11:20.395325Z`, all with complete pagination. No open PR touched this new package path. Cached metadata does not establish novelty.
- **Artifact / reproduction:** `research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces/`; registered command below. Contribution commit `8051d99dfd91a788d25bfc92c3863a33c658a5a9`; main was rechecked unchanged at 07:26 UTC before submission.

## Validation

Python 3.12.3, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces --check-only
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces
```

Both pass. The mathematical finite-premise replay reports:

```text
PASS_P112_OVERCOMPLETE_FACTOR_SPACES kernels=1022 class_pairs=132 entries=12544 COPY=64 controls=7
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces outcome=negative-result
```

Coverage includes SHA256 and Gram/binary source binding; exact rational kernels and intersections; both direct-support and span-based binary rank elimination; 12,544-entry comparisons for each factorization fixture; and exact integer partial-sum comparisons, without sampling `q`.

Seven rejection controls cover altered factors, omitted compensation, V/V undercharge, changed source bytes, a changed character premise, substitution of Hermitian transpose, and an undercharged certificate. A nonreal Gaussian-integer phase fixture passes with ordinary transpose.

A minimal relocated source export also passed `python3 -I -OO -B <export>/research/p112-overcomplete-factor-spaces/verify.py` from a different working directory, preserving every input/package hash. Mutating the actual exported source or certificate was rejected. The combined portability/mutation check took 4.36 seconds. The normal verifier is read-only; evidence regeneration uses exclusive creation and refuses to overwrite.

The selected-result binding check and the card's local-word ceiling positive control passed during orientation. The selected full cold replay was not run because the selected construction is unchanged. No Lean build, external-agent proof review or hosted-CI success is claimed. `git diff --check` and reverse patch applicability passed.

The registered replay was run again on the final package bytes before submission, under an 8 GiB memory cap: it passed in about two seconds and left the worktree unchanged. The optimum matches the exactly-nine-term value (COPY 64 at q = 1); this account's PR #2385 covers the complementary question of other nonzero coefficients at exactly nine terms.

## What does this PR do?

Background-process completion notifications no longer retry forever when the gateway cannot admit their synthetic event. The process watcher now makes at most three admission attempts and doubles the retry delay up to 60 seconds. Successful admissions and the existing completion delivery path are unchanged.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138940

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

- `gateway/run_notifications.py` — bounds refused completion admissions and adds capped exponential retry delays for exited background processes.
- `tests/gateway/test_background_process_notifications.py` — proves that failed admissions stop after the third attempt instead of polling an exited process indefinitely.

body:
## What this changes
- Adds a Supabase migration for atomic order creation, stock reservation/release, payment/COD actions, coupons, product reviews, newsletter subscriptions, and tighter product/order write policies.
- Adds an optional Supabase `pg_cron` setup script to release stock from unpaid orders that expire; documents that it must be enabled and scheduled.
- Fixes wishlist queries to match the existing `products.stock` schema.
- Adds a visible View Cart action after adding a product.
- Removes account-menu links to routes that do not exist and points Returns to `/returns`.
- Preserves existing product gallery images when editing the main image.
- Corrects the UPI checkout amount label to show the server-calculated payable total after order creation.
- Adds a selectable product image gallery with accessible thumbnail controls.
- Fixes homepage desktop/mobile search so it submits to the full catalogue instead of searching only the featured products.
- Adds wishlist load-error messaging and a retry action, avoiding a false empty-wishlist state when Supabase fails.
- Adds `docs/WEBSITE_AUDIT.md` with a prioritized backlog and `docs/REPAIR_DEPLOYMENT.md` with deployment instructions.

## Important deployment blocker
The migration has been added to the repository but has **not** been run against the live Supabase project or validated on a test database from this environment. Apply and test `supabase/migrations/202610150001_timora_repairs.sql` in Supabase first, then enable `pg_cron` and run `supabase/schedule_expired_orders.sql`. Do not deploy the app changes to production before the database changes are verified.

## Validation
- No local build or live checkout/auth/payment tests have been run from this environment.
- Vercel status has been pending on recent commits; no successful build has been confirmed yet.
- Before production, test login/email confirmation, password reset, order totals, stock release on cancel/expiry/rejection, payment verification, COD lifecycle, reviews, coupons, newsletter, and gallery/search/wishlist behavior as documented in `docs/WEBSITE_AUDIT.md`.

body:
## 원인
PR #121에서는 카카오의 광역버스 후보 추가까지만 처리했습니다. 하지만 등록 가능한 첫차·막차 후보가 되려면 `TransitScheduleService`가 서울 버스 정류장별 운행시간 조회를 통과해야 했고, 경기 소속 광역버스는 서울 버스 노선/정류장 매핑에서 실패해 후보가 계속 누락될 수 있었습니다. 또한 카카오 `좌석` 버스 유형은 OTHER로 매핑됐습니다.

## 개선
- 서울 버스 정류장 조회 실패 시, 카카오 광역/직행좌석/좌석 버스에 대해서만 ODsay `pointSearch`로 실제 승·하차 정류장의 좌표와 이름을 대조합니다.
- 양쪽의 `busStationInfo`에서 **같은 busID + 같은 노선번호 + 출발정류장 순번 < 도착정류장 순번**을 검증한 후, 출발 정류장에서 제공되는 `busFirstTime`·`busLastTime`을 사용합니다.
- 중복·모호한 노선 또는 동명이역·반대 방향·시간 누락은 기존처럼 거절합니다. 임의의 시각을 생성하거나 등록 제한을 우회하지 않습니다.
- 카카오 `좌석`/`직행좌석` 등 광역 버스 후보 분류를 보완합니다.
- 서울 API가 정상인 기존 경로는 변경하지 않으며, 프론트·API 계약 변경이 없습니다.

## 검증
- 경기 광역버스 시간표 매핑 성공과 반대방향 정류장 매핑 거절 회귀 테스트 추가.
- ODsay 연동은 mock 응답 기준입니다. 운영 API의 실제 응답과 특정 경기 노선의 등록 성공 여부는 배포 후 검증해야 합니다. 누락이 계속되는 노선은 실제 start/end 정류장과 운수 정보에서 조회 실패 단계를 확인해야 합니다.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **새 기능**
  * 서울 버스 시간표를 확인할 수 없는 경우, 일부 광역버스 노선은 ODsay 시간표를 사용해 첫차·막차와 운행 시간을 확인합니다.
  * 출발·도착 정류장의 노선과 순서가 일치하는 경우에만 대체 시간표를 적용합니다.
  * ‘광역급행’, ‘좌석’, ‘직행좌석’ 버스 유형을 광역버스로 구분합니다.

author: pablobernabeu
body:
This is stage 2, chunk 3 of the September 2026 audit improvements: data handling and argument validation. It has two change sets, one commit each, on top of #16, which is merged. Both have companions in depictr-py's PR. Each commit message says what was wrong and how the fix was verified. NEWS.md lists the changes. The version stays at 0.3.0.

Changes that alter results or output:

- **`conf_level` (CS47).**
  - Every function that takes a `conf_level` now refuses a value outside (0, 1). That covers `roc_curve_plot()` and `random_effects_plot()` too, beyond the plan's list. `acf_plot()`'s own check moves onto the shared helper.
  - An `NA` `conf_level` is refused, except in `survival_plot()` and `calibration_plot()`, where it means "no interval".
- **Arguments that were misread (CS47).** Several other arguments that were silently misread are now checked. The commit lists them.
- **Dates (CS46).**
  - `summary_table()` gives a date column a single Range row. Before, it listed every date as a level.
  - `explore_bivariate()` draws dates on a continuous axis.
  - A difftime is drawn as a number, with its unit in the axis title, because ggplot2 has no difftime scale.
  - `correlation_heatmap()` refuses non-numeric columns instead of coercing them.

Verified locally:
- **Tests:** `devtools::test()` gives PASS 3201, FAIL 0, WARN 0, SKIP 1. At the declared floor (ggplot2 3.5.2, with patchwork 1.3.0 and 1.3.2) there are 0 failures.
- **Examples:** the strict examples run passes on all 63 pages, on each of three stacks.
- **R CMD check `--as-cran`:** the only warning is "Insufficient package version".
- **Parity:** a new parity harness compared date summaries across the twins on 60 random frames (1,589 cells), with 0 differences. All goldens are byte-identical to the last verification.
- **Docs:** `pkgdown::check_pkgdown()` finds no problems.

For review:
- **Changes you can veto.** These defaults were decided on your behalf; DECISIONS.md, depictr Q1 to Q10, records them:
  - A `conf_level` outside (0, 1) is an error.
  - `NA` is refused outside `survival_plot()` and `calibration_plot()`.
  - Dates get a Range row and a continuous axis.
  - `correlation_heatmap()` refuses non-numeric columns.
- **Left as they were:**
  - `qq_plot()` and the other `level = 0.95` function in `diagnostics_extra.R` still accept any `level`.
  - `depictr_palette(n = NaN)` fails with base R's message, not depictr's own.
- **No separate reviewer.** These P2/P3 change sets had an implementer and an integrator, but no adversarial reviewer.

author: danielhanchen
body:
Fixes https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/7139

Studio could not train on a dataset that is already tokenized (rows holding `input_ids`, `attention_mask` and custom `labels`). The dataset check reported an unknown format and asked for a column mapping, and the mapping only offers system / user / assistant roles, so there was no way to start the run. Unsloth itself already trains these rows correctly (TRL and Unsloth's SFT preparation detect `input_ids` and keep the user's `labels`); Studio just never routed them there.

## What changes

* Auto detection recognises a pre-tokenized dataset (non-empty integer `input_ids` on every sampled row, `labels` of the same length when present) and reports it as `pretokenized` with no manual mapping. It only claims datasets that every other detector (Alpaca, ShareGPT, ChatML, the column heuristic) already gave up on, so any dataset that trained before keeps exactly its current route. The same holds when the format dropdown is set explicitly (a choice kept from an earlier run would otherwise strand a dataset the check calls ready); Raw is never overridden.
* The rows go to the trainer untouched: no chat template, and when the dataset brings `labels` no `Train on responses only` masking (the labels are the objective; without a `labels` column the toggle still masks prompts from `input_ids`), and sequence packing is turned off (on TRL < 1.7, which Studio installs, packing keeps only `input_ids` and silently replaces the custom labels).
* Before training, token ids are checked against the model's embedding size and every token column is truncated to `max_seq_length`, both in Arrow (52M tokens over 20k rows: 0.02 s to check, 0.6 s to truncate, against 26.9 s for a Python-level slice). Unsloth's preparation passes tokenized rows through as-is, so without this a dataset tokenized for another model hit a CUDA device-side assert mid-run, and an over-long row reached the model whole. Both steps are idempotent.
* Mac (MLX): unsloth-zoo's MLX trainer already consumes pre-tokenized rows. Its response masker works from text, so a label-less pre-tokenized dataset with `Train on responses only` on trains full sequences there and the run shows a warning saying so (add a `labels` column to pick the trained tokens).

No UI change: the Train page already proceeds when the check returns `requires_manual_mapping: false`, and the preview reads "Detected pretokenized format".

## Verification

* Routing differential, merge base vs this branch, through Studio's own check and format functions on the first 50 rows of 12 real datasets (alpaca-cleaned, FineTome-100k, ultrachat_200k, guanaco-sharegpt-style, gsm8k, TinyStories, Capybara, OpenOrca, dolly-15k, OpenMathReasoning-mini, tldr, smoltalk) plus 4 token-id sets: 96 cells, 72 identical, 24 moved. Every real dataset is identical on all 6 checks (auto, Alpaca and ChatML formatting included); the 24 moved cells are the 4 token-id sets, which base refused in every mode with `Could not auto-detect format mapping`.
* Unsloth `SFTTrainer` on `unsloth/Qwen3-0.6B` with prepared rows: the user's labels arrive unchanged in the collated batch, 5 finite losses, an over-long row cut to `max_seq_length`, an out-of-vocabulary id refused with a clear message.
* `studio/backend/tests/test_pretokenized_dataset.py` (20 tests): detection, normal datasets keeping their route, malformed rows still asking for a mapping, truncation idempotence, vocabulary and label-length checks.
* Existing dataset / format / training-config suites (48 files): identical results on base and head.

## Before / after

The same 16-row JSONL (`input_ids`, `attention_mask`, `labels`) opened in the Train page's dataset preview, merge base on the left, this PR on the right. Before, the check reports `unknown` and asks for a role mapping the columns cannot satisfy; after, it reports `pretokenized` and the dataset is ready to train.

![Dataset preview for a pre-tokenized upload, before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/danielhanchen/unsloth-staging-2/pr-media/pr/13816/pr13816_preview-57c754826083.png)

author: tranphuocloc070699
body:
Four fixes for the admin Words list (TASK-57, TASK-58, TASK-59, TASK-60). After merge it deploys by itself. Flyway V9 runs on the server at that deploy.

## Test it
**Goal:** On https://admin.loffy.me the check button clears "Needs review" at once, no word is listed twice, every chip filters on the server, and you can filter by media.

**Steps:**
1. Hard-reload https://admin.loffy.me/words (Cmd+Shift+R). Press the **Needs review** chip. Each flagged row now has a small badge after the "Needs review" badge: "2 problems", "1 problem" or "0 problems". Hover it: the reasons show as a tooltip.
2. Open **working** and **apple** (search for them). For each word:
   - If it has problems, press the pencil, change the hard words in the text, save, then press the check button.
   - If it says "0 problems" (or "No problems found now"), press the check button.
   - Expected: the badge disappears from the row at once. Reload the page: it stays gone. The count line goes down by one.
3. Search "run". Expected: **one** row, "Bundled" (before this PR: two rows).
4. Press the **From backend** chip. Expected: one request, the count line shows the filtered total (for example "40 of 40"), the list does not keep loading, and "Nothing found" does not flash. Press **Bundled**: it replaces "From backend" (one source at a time). Press **A1-A2** and **B1-B2** together: both stay on and the levels are OR-ed. Press a chip again to turn it off.
5. Press **No media**, then **Has media**. Expected: only one of the two stays on. "No media" shows the bundled words the Pixabay pass has not reached yet. The count line shows the total for the filter. Combine it with **Bundled**: it still works.
6. Failure case: while logged in, open `https://api.loffy.me/api/admin/words?media=some` in the browser. Expected: 400 "media must be one of: with, without."

**Expected:** as written in each step. Step 2 is the fix for "Two words still need review".

**Automated:** `cd backend && ./mvnw -B test` (178 pass), `cd admin && npm test && npm run build` (41 pass, build ok), `python3 scripts/check_docs.py` (17 docs, 0 problems).

## What I found for "apple" and "working" (TASK-57)
- The backend was **not** the problem. `POST /api/admin/words/w-ID/reviewed` does clear `word_lookup.needs_review`. A new test marks a flagged backend word reviewed (same request the admin sends, body `{}`) and reads it back from the API, the "Needs review" list and the table.
- The real bug was in the admin web app, shipped with infinite scroll (PR #52). After the check button, a save or a delete, the app asked Refine to refresh its `list` queries. An infinite list is kept under the key `infinite`, so the **old rows (and the badge) stayed on screen until a reload**. It now refreshes with `all`. The same bug hid a new picture after "Pick another" (MediaRow); fixed the same way. A Vitest test checks that the list is loaded again without the badge.
- So "apple" and "working" may already be reviewed in the database. After you reload, the Needs review chip shows what is really flagged.
- What to do for the two words: see step 2. Fix the hard words with the pencil, or press the check button if you are happy with the text. Nothing is cleared automatically.

## Duplicates: what Flyway V9 deletes in production (TASK-58)
V9 deletes every `word_lookup` row whose word is a bundled lemma, with its `word_lookup_media` links. The media rows and files stay on disk (known gap, doc-15).
- **"run" is a bundled lemma**, so its backend row is deleted. This is the one I am sure about.
- **"working" is not a lemma.** In the bundled dictionary it is a *form* of "work" (`forms` table: working -> work), so it is not in `dictionary_word` and it **stays**. The match is by lemma only, as asked.
- **"apple" is not bundled** (it is not in the 2,750 words), so it stays.
- I cannot read the production database. To see the exact list before you merge, run on the server:
  `SELECT id, word, needs_review FROM word_lookup WHERE lower(word) IN (SELECT lower(lemma) FROM dictionary_word);`
  Those are the rows V9 deletes.

## What changed
- **TASK-58 (backend):** `WordService.lookUp` first looks for the word in `dictionary_word` (by lemma). If found, it returns the bundled entry with its media (`imageUrl`), the bundled IPA and `cached: true`. No Claude call, no `word_lookup` row. Same response shape. The iOS app looks bundled words up on the device first, so this protects the admin and other clients. New `BundledEntryReader` (shared with the admin), `DictionaryWordRepository.findWithSensesByLemma`, Flyway `V9__remove_backend_words_that_are_bundled.sql`.
- **TASK-57:** list refresh fix (`invalidates: ["all"]`), reason count and tooltip badge in the list row, mark-reviewed round-trip test.
- **TASK-59 (admin):** a chip is now `{field, value, combine}` and always a query parameter. Source chips work one at a time, level chips are OR-ed into one `cefr` list. The client-side matching is gone. Note: the level now means the level of the **first sense** (the backend column), not "any sense" as the old client match did.
- **TASK-60:** `media=with|without` on `GET /api/admin/words` (SQL `exists` on `dictionary_sense.media_id` and `word_lookup_media.media_id`, no view change, bad value is 400). Chips "Has media" and "No media" on the words page.
- Docs: doc-5, doc-13, doc-14, doc-15, doc-7 (two decision rows), CLAUDE.md overview.

## Follow-up ideas
- A form like "working" (a form of "work") is still a backend word if another client asks for it. Resolving forms through `dictionary_form` would fix that. Not in scope here.
- Clean up media rows and files of deleted words (known gap).

author: jbearak
body:
**The bug**

A line break (`<w:br/>`) inside a Word Title paragraph lost the text after it. Import wrote the break as `\` and a line end inside the title:

```yaml
title: one\
two
```

The frontmatter reads a title entry as one line, so the next export wrote a Title paragraph of `one\`, and `two` was gone. A break at the title's start or end left `title: \` or a trailing `\` the same way.

**The fix**

In converter.ts, `extractTitleLines` splits a title paragraph at its line breaks, and each line becomes a `title` entry of its own. Export already writes several `title` entries as Title paragraphs, one for each, so both lines reach Word and the Markdown is stable from the first import on.

- A break at the start or end of the paragraph, or next to another break, adds no empty title line.
- The spaces on either side of a break are dropped, since export trims a title line.
- The paragraph's XML is added to the title paragraphs once for each line it gives, so `title-font-style` and the other per-paragraph fields still line up with the titles.

A page break in the title is unchanged. #630 drops it, and the title still comes back as `onetwo`.

The specification's section on multi-paragraph titles now says how import writes a line break in a title.

**Tests**

In converter.test.ts, a new describe next to #630's page break rows. For each row, the title paragraph from an export is edited as Word would have it, imported, and checked over two more trips:

- A line break between the words comes back as `title: one` / `title: two`, Word gets two Title paragraphs, and the Markdown stays the same over two trips. The same holds with spaces on either side of the break.
- A break at the title's start or end comes back as `title: one two`, which is stable.
- Guard: a title of two `title` entries comes back as two, with two Title paragraphs.
- Guard: a page break between the words still gives `title: onetwo`, as #630 has it.

Of these 6 tests, 4 fail on main and the 2 guards pass.

I also checked that two breaks in a row, three lines, a text-wrapping break, `<w:cr/>`, a break in the first of two title paragraphs, and a title with `title-font-style` set for each paragraph all round-trip stably.

**Not fixed here**

- A page or column break between words in a title still joins them, as #630 left it: `one`, a page break, `two` comes back as `title: onetwo`. With this change it could become a title line like a line break, which is a small follow-up.

author: chevalier12
body:
Fixes #237

## Root cause

`ItemContainerGenerator.GetOrCreate(index)` added an item that is its own container (a `ListBoxItem` in a `ListBox`) under `index` while that container was still realized under an old key that no longer holds it. Only `Realize` moved such containers, through `MoveShiftedItemContainers`. The next `GetOrCreate` for the old key saw the container there for a data item, rejected it, and recycled it: `ClearItemContainer` set its `ItemIndex` to -1 and its `Item` to `null`, while `RealizedContainers[index]` still held it.

## Fix

- `GetOrCreate` now removes such a container from its old key, realizes it at `index`, and prepares it there, without clearing or detaching it. A container is never realized under two keys.
- `MoveShiftedItemContainers` and `GetOrCreate` share one lookup, `GetMovedOwnContainerKey`, so `Realize` keeps its results.
- The `ItemContainerGenerator` docs page says `GetOrCreate` moves such a container like `Realize`, with an example.

## Decisions made without the user

- **Move the container in `GetOrCreate` (chosen)**, versus documenting `Realize` as the only move path, or recycling the container from its old key first. The canonical page already says a moved container keeps its recorded index "until the next `Realize` or `GetOrCreate` prepares it for the new index", and that such a container "belongs to that item rather than to an index". WPF has no equivalent public `GetOrCreate` contract.
- A `UIElement` item that appears twice in `Items` is outside this fix and keeps its existing behavior.

## Tests

Both reproductions from the issue are regression tests in `ItemContainerGeneratorTests`:
- `ListBoxReplacedListBoxItemInsertedBackAtItsIndexIsRealizedOnlyThereByDirectGetOrCreate`
- `UnnotifiedGeneratorMovesListBoxItemToItsNewIndexByDirectGetOrCreate` (`a` keeps its visual parent and is not cleared)

Verification, all on `tests/Cerneala.Tests/Cerneala.Tests.csproj -c Release`:

| Filter | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `FullyQualifiedName~ByDirectGetOrCreate` before the fix | 2 failed of 2 (RED: `ItemIndex` -1) |
| `FullyQualifiedName~ByDirectGetOrCreate` after the fix | 2 passed |
| `ItemContainerGeneratorTests\|SelectorTests\|ListBoxTests\|ComboBoxTests\|MenuItemTests\|TabControlTests\|ItemsControlTests\|ItemsPresenterTests` | 265 passed, 0 failed |
| `FullyQualifiedName~Cerneala.Tests.Controls` | 1536 passed, 0 failed |

The complete repository suite was not run, by the user's choice.

author: lidge-jun
body:
## Summary

Carry #7117 by @luvs01 so requests cannot accumulate unlimited consumers of a shared OAuth refresh after disconnecting. Pending refresh resolution now has an independent process-local ceiling of 256 consumers alongside the existing 32-flight ceiling. Fresh cached credentials bypass admission; capacity refusal returns HTTP 503 with `Retry-After: 1` without quarantining accounts, and cancellation wins with 499. Already-committed runTurn SSE reports a server error.

The original contribution is preserved by cherry-picking `b722d746f10dafb7eeea2aabcf8b94aec6a6a5db` as `0cb3868b03`. Follow-ups keep stale owners registered through definitive-result cleanup and durable retirement even with spare capacity, recheck single-flight ownership when concurrent replacements resume, and observe both request and option cancellation signals during initial auth refusal and runTurn recovery. Deferred durable retirement logs once per flight without account or credential identity. Owning runtime/failover contracts and public troubleshooting guidance are updated. No GUI or dependency changes.

Verified against `origin/dev` at `7640a942b35044c974e534b84d5a8049f4a8ae9a`: the consumer gate and capacity mapping were absent. The source PR had no submitted reviews or inline review comments when inspected; CodeRabbit skipped the draft. It links a fork PR, with no closing issue references. The original PR is left for the coordinator to manage.

Authentication/OAuth changes require explicit maintainer security review under MAINTAINERS.md; that review remains pending. This PR is implementation and test evidence, not security approval. The limit bounds unresolved consumer count, not retained bytes, provider duration, or multiple processes. An abort-ignoring refresh retains finite capacity until it settles.

Co-authored-by: Epinephrine <luvs01@hanmail.net>

## Verification

All runtime checks used temporary HOME, OPENCODEX_HOME, CODEX_HOME, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and XDG directories, plus the repository's test preload; synthetic credentials only. `isolate` below denotes that environment wrapper. The test runner was a scratch-local Bun 1.4.3 matching package.json; no global runtime or real account configuration was changed.

- `bun install` — passed before implementation; no tracked lockfile changes.
- `isolate bun test --isolate --timeout 30000 tests/oauth/oauth-refresh-stale-capacity.test.ts tests/oauth/oauth-refresh.test.ts tests/oauth/oauth-refresh-generic-lock.test.ts tests/oauth/oauth-refresh-lock-multiprocess.test.ts tests/responses/responses-oauth-refresh-capacity.test.ts tests/responses/responses-devin-401-replay.test.ts tests/oauth/adapter-event-oauth-failover.test.ts tests/oauth/generic-oauth-failover.test.ts tests/providers/kiro/kiro-leased-responses.test.ts tests/codex-integration/active-turn-disconnect.test.ts tests/codex-integration/active-registry-admission.test.ts tests/test-layout.test.ts tests/test-layout-tooling.test.ts tests/ci-workflows/file-size-ratchet.test.ts` — **322 pass / 0 fail / 3,051 assertions**, 14 files.
- `isolate bun run typecheck` — passed.
- `isolate bun run structure:check` — passed.
- `isolate bun run privacy:scan` — passed.
- `(cd docs-site && bun install --frozen-lockfile && isolate bun run build)` — passed; 577 pages and 81,203 internal links checked.
- `git diff --check origin/dev` — passed.

Red controls on the carried contributor tree: the independent-signal cancellation cases yielded **1 pass / 1 fail** (expected 499, received 503); the unsaturated late-rejection/retirement-IO cases yielded **0 pass / 2 fail**. The final run above covers the corrections. Hosted Codex identified a runTurn request-only cancellation gap: three new cases failed before the correction (including committed SSE), then passed with both client signals linked and cleaned up. CodeRabbit identified silent retirement failure; a once-per-flight identity-free diagnostic and bounded-log regression address it. The diagnostic red control yielded 1 pass / 1 fail before the log existed. An initial run on the shell's Bun 1.4.0 had 316 passes and one tooling failure because that guard requires Bun 1.4.3; using the repository-pinned runtime resolved it without changing the guard. Counts from overlapping runs are not added.

The maintainer prohibits heavy/full local suites on this shared host. The full suite, prepush, and whole tests directory were therefore **NOT RUN locally**. Current implementation head: `6fba175cac2ff1a55e5c2d92ea85d9e5f2a5c291`. Broad Ubuntu and cross-platform validation belongs to hosted CI; exact-head PR checks and a subsequent `workflow_dispatch` with `lane=all` will be inspected separately. Live-provider refresh, an end-to-end resource-exhaustion benchmark, and operational sizing of the 256-consumer limit were not established.

## Checklist

- [x] Scope stays focused and avoids unrelated cleanup.
- [x] Docs or release notes were updated when needed.
- [ ] Security-sensitive changes were reviewed for secrets, auth, and unsafe defaults. Privacy scan passes; explicit maintainer security review is pending.

## Phase 6 (Focus & Pomodoro) Complete Implementation

### Summary

This pull request delivers the complete implementation of **Phase 6: Focus & Pomodoro** for Orbit, providing a resilient, distraction-free focus workspace, offline-first Web Audio ambient noise synthesis, atomic local session tracking, and weekly analytics.

---

### Deliverables & Key Changes

#### 1. P6-POM-001: Pomodoro Domain, Atomic Local Storage & Resilient Timer Engine
- **Domain Contracts (`packages/shared-types`):**
  - Added `FocusSessionEntity`, `FocusSessionMode` (`WORK`, `SHORT_BREAK`, `LONG_BREAK`), `FocusSessionStatus` (`ACTIVE`, `PAUSED`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED`), and `PomodoroSettings`.
  - Added `'FOCUS_SESSION'` to `EntityType` and `MutationPayload`.
- **Atomic Local Storage (`packages/sync-engine` & `apps/web`):**
  - Defined `AtomicFocusStore` port with `saveFocusSessionWithMutation`, `getFocusSession`, and `listFocusSessions`.
  - Upgraded IndexedDB to version 4 with `focusSessions` object store and `by-taskId` index.
  - Implemented atomic mutation recording with LWW conflict resolution in `IndexedDbLocalStore` and `MemoryLocalStore`.
- **Resilient Calculation Engine & Chime (`apps/web`):**
  - Pure calculation engine in `pomodoro-timer.ts` immune to background browser throttling and tab sleep using wall-clock delta calculation (`startedAtTimestamp`, `pausedAtTimestamp`, `accumulatedPausedMs`).
  - Zero-dependency completion chime generator using standard Web Audio API (`playPomodoroChime`).
  - Lifecycle management in `pomodoro-service.ts` (`startFocusSession`, `pauseFocusSession`, `resumeFocusSession`, `completeFocusSession`, `cancelFocusSession`, `getTodayFocusSummary`).

#### 2. P6-FOC-001: Distraction-Free Focus Page & UI Integration
- **Focus Page Component (`FocusPage.tsx` & `FocusPage.module.css`):**
  - Full-screen distraction-free mode toggle.
  - Circular SVG countdown ring with smooth dynamic progress calculation.
  - Mode switcher (Work, Short Break, Long Break) with automatic cycle progression (`🍅 🍅 ⚪ ⚪`).
  - Timer action controls (Start, Pause, Complete Early, Skip, Reset).
  - Quick Pomodoro settings drawer.
  - Direct task attachment via `🍅` shortcut in `TaskItem.tsx` and URL query parameter `/focus?taskId=...`.
  - Registered route `/focus` and navigation item with ⏱️ icon in `AppShell.tsx`.

#### 3. P6-SND-001: Offline Ambient Sound & White Noise Synthesis (Web Audio API)
- **Native Web Audio Synthesis (`ambient-sound.ts`):**
  - `WhiteNoise`: Uniform random distribution buffer in `[-1, 1]`.
  - `PinkNoise`: Multi-pole filter (Paul Kellet's algorithm) providing balanced 1/f spectral density.
  - `BrownNoise`: Leaky integrator filter providing warm, deep relaxation sound.
  - `RainSimulation`: Filtered brown noise layered with randomized high-frequency impulse drops.
  - `AmbientSoundEngine` & singleton `ambientSoundManager` with smooth volume ramp-in/ramp-out (`linearRampToValueAtTime`) and volume controls ($0.0$ to $1.0$).
  - Integrated into settings drawer in `FocusPage.tsx` with auto-sync (plays during work sessions, pauses on break/reset).

#### 4. P6-STA-001: Weekly Focus Analytics & Pure CSS/SVG Bar Chart
- **Focus Analytics Service:**
  - `getWeeklyFocusStats` calculates total hours, daily average, streak days, completion rate, top tasks, and tag distribution for the last 7 days.
  - Compatible with both Persian Jalali and Gregorian weekday calendars.
- **Analytics Widget (`FocusAnalyticsCard.tsx` & `FocusAnalyticsCard.module.css`):**
  - 4 KPI summary cards (Total Focus, Daily Average, Streak, Completion Rate).
  - Pure CSS/SVG 7-day bar chart with dynamic height scaling and weekday labels.
  - Breakdown of top tasks and tag distribution pills (`#tag`).
  - Interactive toggle button in `FocusPage.tsx`.

---

### Validation & Quality Gate

- [x] **Scoped Tests:** 30 unit & component tests passing cleanly:
  - `apps/web/src/features/pomodoro/services/pomodoro-timer.test.ts` (6 tests)
  - `apps/web/src/features/pomodoro/services/ambient-sound.test.ts` (8 tests)

  - `apps/web/src/features/pomodoro/pages/FocusPage.test.tsx` (4 tests)
- [x] **Monorepo Typecheck:** `npm run typecheck` passed with 0 errors across all workspaces (`@orbit/shared-types`, `@orbit/sync-engine`, `@orbit/web`, `@orbit/server`).
- [x] **Documentation:** Updated `PROGRESS.md` marking Phase 6 as 100% complete.

### Exit Gate Requirements Met

- [x] Timer maintains millisecond accuracy across tab sleep, laptop lid close, and background throttling.
- [x] Ambient sound generation is 100% offline with zero external audio assets or network requests.
- [x] Atomic mutations follow LWW synchronization protocol with offline IndexedDB storage.

body:
Thorough currently hides most final-synthesis models and caps several reasoning controls below what their native clients support. The picker now offers seven OpenAI models, Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1, with each model's full supported effort range and its maximum selected by default. Quick/Balanced recommendations remain unchanged.

Final model/effort settings are frozen separately from proposer/reviewer settings and applied only during Layer 3. This prevents a shared route's final effort from overwriting an earlier stage. Gemini now runs through the recorded synthesis path, and lane cards, retry controls and duration samples honor the saved final settings. Existing jobs retain their configuration.

Validation: 423 offline, recovery, evidence, browser and Slack checks passed; native maximum-effort structured-output probes passed for all seven OpenAI models, Argon and Opus. Fable's probe received an upstream safeguard refusal and was not retried; its dispatch/settings/artifact contracts pass offline. Browser coverage exercises every final model and supported effort, maximum defaults, preset changes and upstream/final setting independence. Documentation includes the exact model/effort table.

Review fixes add independent final-stage deadlines, accurate final identity in early manifests, strict Luna/CLI validation, preserved custom Codex effort settings and model-authoritative AGY depth. The exact failure cases have regression coverage.

Independent Claude Opus 5.5 review approved the final revision with no remaining findings after the fixes.
