## What's in it

Ten chapters: first run (cold-start window, RAM tiers) · querying (text/file/deep links, disagreement tools, 50k-row CSV mode switch) · reading results (verdict semantics, "0 = no evidence, not innocence", the four fusion-algorithm badges σP/▮share/★r/◇fixed, full per-type evidence field walkthrough) · exports (CSV's 28 columns, STIX 2.1) · the admin console's three tabs (Sources with the r/θ dual track, API keys with the one-time token reveal and scoping, the task feed and its failure semantics) · the source lifecycle loop (four add paths, the eval CLI, human-gated tuning, sunset retirement) · a full-endpoint API reference (four rate-limit buckets, error envelope, 503-warming semantics, SSE, cookie sessions, curl examples with real response excerpts) · troubleshooting · ops runbooks (upgrade/self-update, backup/restore, alerts) · pointers to the desktop companion and the three integrations.

author: ellypeachi
body:
…border

On retina screens (every iPhone, most Macs) the 256px basemap.at tiles were stretched to 512 or 768 device pixels, which is the blur. basemap.at publishes the same map as 512px tiles, but as opaque JPEGs that are white outside Austria, so they cannot simply replace the PNG layer.

AustriaTiles uses a tile as it is when it lies wholly inside Austria, and otherwise draws it on a canvas cut with the standard transparent PNG, which follows the real border (and keeps what basemap.at draws just past it, such as Liechtenstein). austriaOutline.json only decides which tiles are safely inside. Screens that are not high-DPI keep the plain PNG layer.

author: kgwinnup
body:
## Problem

`org--fontify` decides whether a `#+BEGIN_…` line opens a src/example block with

```scheme
(string-match "_[sS][rR][cC]\\|_[eE][xX]" line)
```

Rust's regex crate reads `\|` as a literal pipe, so this never matched. Src block bodies were never marked as code: they got no `org-block` face and were parsed for emphasis. A path like `~/repos/x.scm` inside a block showed `/repos/` in italic.

## Fix

Use a plain `|` alternation. The other `\\|` patterns in `org.scm` (table rows, tag `a|b` matching) are meant to match a literal `|` and are unchanged.

## Testing

- New test `src_block_body_is_painted_as_a_block`: the body gets `org-block` and no `org-italic`. It fails on the old regex and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test --bin macros`: 994 passed.
- Hot-loaded into a running editor: a `#+BEGIN_SRC` body now gets `org-block` on every line.

author: brackcarmony
body:
Before: the only way to get monsters into DM Screen from an AI was pasting JSON into Import, and nothing outside the app could read a campaign.

After: an AI app such as Claude can connect to a DM's campaign over the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), look things up and add monsters and encounters. For example: "make a random encounter table for my level 5 party in the woods" searches the bestiary, adds monsters only where nothing fits, prices each entry and saves the table as an encounter group.

- **Tools:** `search_monsters`, `get_monster`, `get_battle`, `encounter_xp` (the Battle page's XP formula, from `rules.js`), `roll_dice`, `list_encounters`, `add_monsters` (tagged AI with the request, normalized like Import) and `add_encounters` (all or nothing; "Dire Wolf" finds `dire-wolf` and is saved as the bestiary spells it). Nothing edits or deletes.
- **Resources:** `dm://party`, `dm://monster/{name}`. **Prompts:** `plan_encounter`, `random_encounter_table`.
- **Remote, at `$APP_URL/mcp`:** a DM adds the address in their AI app (Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector), signs in to DM Screen and allows it on a new `/connect` page. The Account page lists connected apps with Disconnect. Changing the password disconnects them all.
- **Local:** `server/mcp-stdio.js`, registered for Claude Code in `.mcp.json`, on local data.

How: DM Screen is its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server. The MCP SDK's `mcpAuthRouter` serves `/authorize`, `/token`, `/register`, `/revoke` and the `/.well-known` metadata, and `server/oauth.js` implements its provider: dynamic client registration (stored, capped at 1000 with unused ones dropped first), consent through `/connect`, one-time five-minute codes checked with PKCE, one-hour HMAC-signed access tokens issued only for `/mcp` and checked against their grant on every request, and refresh tokens stored hashed and replaced on every use, in `$DATA_DIR/oauth.json`. Google stays just a way to log in: no Google token reaches the app, and Google sign-in from `/connect` now returns there (a same-site path only). `/mcp` is stateless Streamable HTTP with JSON replies: a new server per request, so restarts lose nothing and nginx needs no streaming settings.

Three writers now share a DM's file, so: the DM store reloads a file whose modification time changed, and the app reloads the campaign when its tab regains focus, unless a save is pending. A tab left open and edited without switching away can still overwrite an AI app's additions; per-item saves would close that.

nginx: `deploy/nginx.conf` now forwards `X-Forwarded-For`. Without it every visitor looks like 127.0.0.1, so the login limiter and the SDK's per-IP OAuth limits are shared by everyone.

Testing: `npm test` (38 passing). `test/mcp.test.js` runs the tools against a running app on the same data: writes survive the app saving, all-or-nothing encounters, loose name matching, and the prompt. These tests fail with the old store cache. `test/remote-mcp.test.js` drives the SDK's own OAuth client end to end: the 401 and metadata discovery, registration, consent, PKCE, tools over HTTP reaching the DM's data, single-use refresh tokens, cut-off on password change and on disconnect, deny, and a forged token. Also run against a copy of the real data over stdio (which found the `dire-wolf` naming issue) and on a local server. The `/connect` and Account pages were built but not checked in a browser.

author: 0xmanhnv
body:
## What

Follow-up to the CLA check that was merged here. A security review found a bypass in its "Decide who must sign" step, fixed here.

**The hole:** in a pull request opened by an outside account, a commit linked to an allowlisted account (the maintainer or a bot) was accepted when its signature was verified. A signature proves only the *committer*, and the author e-mail is free text, so a contributor could set the maintainer's e-mail as author, sign with their own key, and skip the CLA.

**The fix:** the step judges each commit by the account the CLA action uses (author, else committer). If that is an allowlisted account, the commit counts only when the author AND the committer are both allowlisted AND the signature is verified; otherwise the check fails and names the commit. Steps now select pull request events by payload (`github.event.pull_request`), not by event name.

**Tests:** `.github/scripts/cla-scope.test.sh` extracts the step from `cla.yml` and runs it against 10 recorded commit lists (maintainer, bot and outside pull requests; forged author, forged committer, contributor-signed). The previous logic fails 2 of them. `cla-test.yml` runs the test on pull requests and pushes that change the workflow or the test (read-only token, `persist-credentials: false`).

Also documented in the workflow header: keep `cla` required on pull requests; in the merge queue it passes at once. The archived upstream action's replacement is planned in openctemio/openctem#2299.

Security: same model as before. The check runs in the base context and never checks out or runs pull request code; the test workflow runs the pull request's own copy on `pull_request` with `contents: read` only. Secret still needed: org secret `CLA_SIGNATURES_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT, resource owner `openctemio`, repository access only `openctemio/cla-signatures`, Contents read/write).

author: rustlanglatam
body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The OS reports its locale with a region (`LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8`), but the catalogues are per language (`en`, `fr`, `ja`, `es`, `zh-CN`). `normalize_locale` produced `fr-FR`, which matches no built-in arm and no `<ftl dir>/fr-FR/` directory, so French, Spanish and Japanese users got English everywhere. Only `zh_CN` worked, because that catalogue carries the region in its name.
  - `zeroclaw-runtime`: `normalize_locale` now maps the normalized tag to the `available_locales()` code it matches, ignoring case (`zh_cn` → `zh-CN`). If nothing matches, it uses the language when that is a registry code (`fr_FR` → `fr`, `es_AR` → `es`). Otherwise the tag stays as before (`de_DE` → `de-DE`, `zh_TW` → `zh-TW`), which still means English. It also drops a POSIX `@modifier` (`fr_FR@euro`) the way it already dropped the encoding. Config `locale`, OS detection and `i18n::init` all go through `normalize_locale`, so all three get the fallback.
  - `zeroclaw-tools` cannot see the runtime registry (the dependency runs runtime → tools). Its `load_ftl_from_disk` now tries `<ftl dir>/<tag>/tools.ftl` and then `<ftl dir>/<language>/tools.ftl`. Its `normalize_locale` drops `@modifier` too.
- **Scope boundary:** no catalogue, registry or config schema change. No new locales. `zh-TW` and other languages without a catalogue keep falling back to English.
- **Blast radius:** processes whose locale comes from a regional tag of `fr`, `es` or `ja` now show those translations instead of English. That covers CLI strings, channel notices and tool descriptions.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11773

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw ships French, Spanish and Japanese translations, but a computer set to "French (France)" reports `fr_FR`, and ZeroClaw only looked for a catalogue named exactly `fr-FR`. It found none and used English. Now it falls back from the region to the language, so those users get their language without having to set `locale` in the config.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional:

```bash
LANGUAGE= LC_ALL= LC_MESSAGES= LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8 \
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --lib voice_drop_notices
```

On `master` this passes, because the notice is still English. On this head it fails on the English-only assertion that #11769 / #11770 fix, which shows the French catalogue is now selected.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `Test` job runs the new unit tests below. They call `normalize_locale` and `catalogue_candidates` directly and do not depend on the environment.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI runs in English, so it does not exercise detection from a regional OS locale end to end. The manual run below does.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings \
    -A clippy::needless_borrows_for_generic_args -A deprecated
(clean)

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib i18n::
test result: ok. 45 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib i18n::
test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `normalize_locale_falls_back_from_region_to_language_catalogue`: `fr_FR.UTF-8`, `es_AR.UTF-8`, `ja_JP.eucJP`, `fr_FR@euro` and `es-MX` map to their language. `zh_cn.utf8` maps to `zh-CN`. `zh_TW` and `de_DE` are left as they are.
  - `catalogue_candidates_fall_back_from_region_to_language` (tools).
  - With `LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8`, the Telegram voice-drop notice comes out in French on this head. On `master` it stays English (see above).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** clippy with `needless_borrows_for_generic_args` and `deprecated` allowed: my local stable 1.99 flags untouched code that CI's pinned 1.98.0 does not. The pre-push hook was skipped with `--no-verify`; I ran the touched crates' suites above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (the tools crate may read one more catalogue path, inside the same FTL directory)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. An explicit `locale = "fr"` behaves as before. Only regional tags change, from English to their language.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the squash commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** set `locale = "en"` in config to keep English.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** strings in an unexpected language for users with a regional OS locale.

author: flyboutiqueperu
body:
## Problema
Alberto instaló «Fly Staff» y, al abrirla, salía la tienda en vez del acceso del staff.

Causa: el celular (sobre todo el iPhone) toma la dirección de inicio del manifiesto que encuentra **al cargar la página**. Si se entró al staff desde la tienda sin recargar, el manifiesto cargado era el de la tienda (`start_url: "/"`), aunque el nombre ya dijera «Fly Staff».

## Qué cambió
- `index.html`: el manifiesto, el ícono y el nombre se eligen con un script pequeño mientras se lee la página (`/staff` → Fly Staff, `/caja` → Fly Caja, resto → tienda). Así el celular siempre ve el correcto.
- **Arreglo para las apps ya instaladas:**
  - Al usarse como app instalada, recuerda si es la de staff o la de caja (`localStorage fly:homeApp`).
  - Si el celular la abre en «/», vuelve sola al acceso del staff o a la caja.
  - Se olvida al tocar «Volver a la tienda».
- Si se toca «Instalar» en una página que se cargó como tienda, primero recarga en `/staff` o `/caja` y avisa «Toca otra vez «Instalar»».
- Las instrucciones para iPhone y Android ahora dicen la dirección exacta (`flyboutique.vercel.app/staff` o `/caja`).

## Qué probé
- `npm run build` OK y lint sin errores.
- `pruebas/ui/apps.cjs`: todo OK. Incluye:
  - Un solo manifiesto por página.
  - Instalar desde la tienda → recarga en /staff con el manifiesto staff y muestra el aviso.
  - App instalada simulada (display-mode standalone) abierta en «/» → vuelve al acceso del staff, con su manifiesto y sin botón de instalar.
  - «Volver a la tienda» → la próxima vez abre la tienda.
- La tienda normal sigue con su manifiesto de siempre.
- `api/p.js` (vista previa de productos) no depende de las líneas cambiadas.

## Riesgos
- Bajos. La tienda, para quien compra, no cambia.
- Una persona del staff que use la app de la tienda instalada y entre al staff verá el staff al reabrirla, hasta que toque «Volver a la tienda».

author: menghuan1918
body:
## 这个版本修什么

社区反馈的「**0.24 没问题，之后就会卡**」：侧栏在前台开久了卡、多轮对话后 DSH 卡、重装重启又暂时好。产物级 A/B 把分界线定在 **v0.25.0** —— v0.26.0 的 git 轮询收敛只覆盖了其中一族，下面四条机制一直原样留着。

### 根因（三者相乘）

1. **v0.25 打开了 `keepMounted`**（0.24.1 里 0 处）：访问过的每个 tab body 都不再卸载，于是它持有的计时器 / socket / 观察者 / 缓存全部活到整页结束。
2. **同一版给每个 body 配的周期任务都没问「我看得见吗」**：每 tab 一条 5s 会话根轮询（不看可见性）、每棵树一条 `/sidebar/ws/fs-watch`（宿主按连接给 ≤64 个 `fs.watch` 句柄）、两条 500ms 表（右侧栏展开态每条消费者各一条；空白会话兜底入口的 interval 注册在 early return **之前**，渲染 `null` 也照跑）、`settings-nav-icon` 的 body 观察者带 `characterData`（主对话每吐一个 token 触发一次全文档查询）。
3. **同一版把宿主每次轮询的代价抬高约一个数量级**：`active-worktree.ts`（0.25 新文件）插进了 12 条 `/sidebar/*` 路由共用的 `cwdOf()` —— 每次未命中 = 一次真实 `git rev-parse` 子进程 + 回扫 4 000 条会话事件（实测 9.6–44.7 ms），而它的 TTL 是 3 s、比新增的 5 s 客户端轮询还短 ⇒ **每次轮询必然未命中**。

### 真机 A/B（4 个访问过的页签、15s 空闲窗）

| 指标 | before (0.26.0) | after |
|---|---|---|
| 活着的 500ms 表 | 3 | **1** |
| 活着的 5s 表 | 5 | **0** |
| 空闲窗 `session.cwd` 请求 | 15 | **0** |
| 命中测试 `elementsFromPoint` | 1 620 | **0** |
| 强制布局 rect / style | 5 190 / 586 | **30 / 30** |

单 tick CPU（Chromium 微基准）：0.02–0.32 ms → **0.001 ms**（最拥挤形态此前可达 9.7 ms）。

### 修法

- **可见性门控**：两个 500ms 表按「真的渲染 / 页面可见」起停（展开态改全模块一条共享表），观察者合帧，兜底表按需起停；`use-center-column` 的兜底表只在无缓存列时 armed；`session-phase` 隐藏不请求、值未变不重渲。
- **「每 tab」→「每会话」**：`use-session-root` 改为按会话引用计数的共享 store（一条表、只在 ≥1 个可见订阅者时存在，恢复即补刷）；文件树目录 watch 与侧聊推送同样门控；native body 传真实 `visible`。
- **`keepMounted` 保留语义、加上界**：`git-status` 槽位参与淘汰（256）、`ops-stream` LRU 32 且保留游标（parked 回来仍折到错过的写操作）、`bySession` LRU 32 且不再每次整份复制、`previewScrollMemory` / `commitDrafts` / `pendingAnchors` 有界；每秒重建整份列表的三处收敛。
- **宿主侧**：cwd 解析加在飞去重 + TTL 3s→15s + 三个缓存 LRU；`git.ts` 两条 `--numstat` 加 pathspec（未忽略大目录下零条 diff）+ 8MiB 输出上限 + **行数封顶后不再累加输出**；单层 `fs.tree` 补 gate、折叠探测封顶 32；冷线程日志 memo；agent-opens 队列封顶；teardown 关闭已接受的 WS 连接。
- **#935 遗留项**同批修完（numstat 无 pathspec / runGit 无字节上限 / compact 探测无总量上限 / 每秒重渲染 / 模块级 Map 无上限）。

### 门禁

- 新增跨模块门禁 `tests/steady-state.spec.tsx`（不可见时不得有周期表 / 不得读布局 / 不得发请求；同一会话至多一个轮询器）+ **客户端 `setInterval` 站点清单**（新增未登记的周期任务即红）。
- perf lane 新增 `steady-state` 指标与两条硬断言；真机上 **before 侧就是红的**（命中测试 1620 > 40），after 侧通过 —— 判别力被真机证明。
- 全量：210 文件 / 2524 用例、`pnpm test:mount`、`ci` 与 `ci-windows` 全绿。
- 15 份既有 spec 扩展 + 5 份新 spec；判别性由逐条「临时回退 → 变红 → 还原」实测。

### 明确未做 / 已知代价

关闭 `keepMounted`、文件树虚拟化、CSS `:has` 回潮、任何宿主侧改动、perf lane 的耗时阈值；跟随 linked worktree 的延迟 3s→15s；`runGit` 超 8MiB 的答案改为失败而不是累积；两个 socket hook 的 `document.hidden` 门控留作后续（隐藏标签页仍持有 socket）。**无公开接入 API 变化。**

设计与全部实测数字：`docs/plans/2026-10-15-perf-steady-state.md`。

> 说明：本 PR 同时带上 dev 上已合入的 README 中英分文件整理（纯文档；main 的 README 修订此前已并入 dev，两边无冲突）。

body:
Fixes for the review of #2643 (https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#pullrequestreview-5535346016). Merge into `development`; the next sync PR carries them to beta. Nothing here is merged by the reviewer.

## Findings → commits
| Finding | Commit | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| iq-f1 [🔴 StUF-ZDS envelope with plaintext WS-Security password is persisted on an open schema](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673529) | `eef8fb3bf`, `c51999b8f`, `2db6d092f`, `7c32d6200` | The stored envelope carries no Security header; `transmit()` adds the UsernameToken at send time on every attempt. New `99-stuf-message-lockdown.json` (admin-only on every verb), `_rbac:false` on every internal `stuf_message` read/write, retrying rows expire after 24 h and only `retrying` rows are swept. REQ-020 updated in the new change `stuf-message-admin-only`, since the bridge no longer needs a right on `stuf_message`. |
| iq-f2 [🔴 Call-log retention sweep deletes nothing after the admin-only lockdown](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673550) | `ac08b6584` | `cleanupSchema` reads and deletes with `_rbac:false, _multitenancy:false`; the swallowed exceptions are logged. |
| iq-f3 [🟡 Document fetch ignores connectionKey and takes any handle](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673565) | `8719ab35e`, `84a68e916`, `2773001cf` | `DocumentConnectionGuard` resolves (sourceApp, connectionKey) through app_connection and requires a linked, existing source, failing closed; `itemPath` refuses `.`/`..` segments. A source-type check was tried and dropped again (the Microsoft 365 adapter has no source row). |
| iq-f4 [🟡 Replay of a record whose bodies are gone sends a body-less request](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673573) | `088b2d226`, `66dd18284` | `replay()` refuses a record whose request is gone; the stored url is accepted as the endpoint only under the source `location`, with no `REDACTED` part and no dot segments. |
| iq-f6 [🟡 Call bodies still reach execution_trace outside an investigation window](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673597) | `d400653c5` | The trace step loses its bodies unless the investigation window is open or the caller passed `logBody` (`BodyCapturePolicy::captures()`). |
| iq-f7 [🟡 tasks.md ticks a StUFXMLBuilder::buildBv01 that does not exist](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673608) | `0f987f354` | `buildBv01` removed from tasks.md; the proposal and spec now say Bv03/Fo03 to match the writes delta. |
| iq-f8 [🟡 Provider queries without any criterion are put to the owning app](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673619) | `136c3775e` | A zakLv01 without a non-empty criterion and an npsLv01 without a 9-digit BSN get a 400 Fo02 and no event; at most 100 cases are rendered. |
| iq-f9 [🟡 Public confirmation endpoint has no body ceiling before parsing](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673631) | `2ad4ed38a`, `62af91713` | `StufZknRequestBody` reads at most 2 MiB + 1 byte; both receivers answer 413 before any parse or lookup. |
| aud-f3 [🟡 Public StUF endpoints: one static shared secret, no replay protection, no success audit](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673664) | `1c011d98d`, `422139e89`, `03f44c7a9`, `366268554` | `StufWsseInboundVerifier`: a token with `Nonce` + `Created` must be fresh (±5 min) and unseen (per source and user, atomic with an IMemcache); `requireNonce` opts a source into refusing tokens without them. Documented as transitional (PasswordDigest is the follow-up). Each accepted provider request writes a `[StUF audit]` warning line with no BSN or criteria. |

## Left to the author (threads stay open)
- iq-f5 [🟡 BRP relation read has no caller authorization and no asking app in its record](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673580) — not done: a caller check on `BrpRelationReader::read()` changes the by-name contract dossiq calls, so it has to land together with a dossiq change. Recommendation: a `relationApps` allowlist on the source, `sourceApp` in `$config`, `reason: not-permitted` otherwise, and `firedBy` on the withheld record. Whether doelbinding/verwerking headers are mandatory is a question for the municipality's RvIG authorisation.
- aud-f3 [🟡 Public StUF endpoints: one static shared secret, no replay protection, no success audit](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673664) — remaining: separate inbound and outbound secrets per source (needs a new source field and a migration; recommendation `authentication.inboundWsse` plus a repair step that copies the current pair), a per-source throttle, a persisted audit row instead of a log line (needs a retention decision), and making `requireNonce` the default once case systems send a Nonce.
- iq-f3 [🟡 Document fetch ignores connectionKey and takes any handle](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673565) — partly closed: any app with a connection linked to an existing integriq source can search and fetch through the organisation-wide Microsoft 365 credential, because the adapter has no source row. Binding it needs a Microsoft 365 source template or a declaration on the connection row.
- iq-f6 [🟡 Call bodies still reach execution_trace outside an investigation window](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673597) — residue: `logBody: true` keeps bodies with no expiry, and `replayRequest` keeps the request body for the error retention outside a window, while the spec says no request body is stored there; which of the two gives way is a design call.
- Heads-up for iq-f1: `WebhookProfiles::stufZkn()` now has `requiredActions: []` (the preflight only checked rights on `stuf_message`, which is admin-only now); zaak and document upserts still run as the connection account. The legacy HMAC bridge `StufZknController::inbound` still reads its body unbounded (it needs the exact bytes for the signature).

## Tracked elsewhere
- iq-f1 [🔴 StUF-ZDS envelope with plaintext WS-Security password is persisted on an open schema](https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/pull/2643#discussion_r4284673529) → https://github.com/ConductionNL/integriq/issues/2684 (a credential exposure that outlives the sync PR's threads)

## Checks run on this branch
- `bash hydra/scripts/run-hydra-gates.sh --scope-to-diff --base e391fac5f` → exit 0, COVERAGE 55 of 55 applicable gates ran (42 not applicable)
- `vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit-unit.xml` on `tests/Unit/Service/StufZkn`, Settings, BackgroundJob, Outbound, EventListener, Service/Adapter, Controller and `StufZknSyncServiceTest` → OK (1483 tests); `--filter "CallService|Trace|Webhook|Stuf"` → OK (488 tests). The new tests for iq-f2 and iq-f6 were confirmed to fail without their fix.
- `vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml` on every changed `lib/` file → no new findings (the remaining ones are identical on the base commit)

author: mikelward
body:
## What

A bug report from St Pancras showed Thameslink and Southeastern trains there being dropped as "unchecked" (`destination matches no route`). That left the trip's **Direct** section without them, and gave a trip's Thameslink leg no live trains to time it.

**Cause:** TfL's own route data gives one station's platforms a different id in each direction:

| Line | Northbound / inbound | Southbound / outbound |
|---|---|---|
| Thameslink (low level) | `910GSTPXBOX` | `910GSTPX` |
| Southeastern (HS1) | one route ends at `910GSTPX` | the rest leave `910GSTPADOM` |

A train is matched to its route by the id its board lists it under. So every southbound Thameslink at the low level (Brighton, Horsham, Sutton…) found only the northbound routes, and every northbound one under the main id found only the southbound routes. `LineSequence.callingAt` already merged a station's sibling ids, but only when *no* route called at the boarding id. Here each direction calls at a different id, so that merge never fired.

**Fix:**
- `RouteStops.candidatePaths` now gets one retry when a train that names where it's going has no way there from its own id. The retry uses `LineSequence.throughStation`, which puts the boarding id in place of the station's other ids on the routes that don't call at it.
- "The same station" means TfL's own station code (`icsId`), which is now parsed from the route sequence and kept in the route cache.
- `resolve`, `reaches` and everything built on them (Direct rows, trip legs, route pages, journeys) get the retry.
- A stop list found through the other id is read on that same route when the route page places an alert's stretch before the boarding stop (`wholeRouteOf`, Codex on #879). Without that, the alert's location beside the line pill was lost for these trains.

**When the retry doesn't happen.** The retry is taken only when the train's own id has no way to a named destination; every other empty answer stands (Codex on #879, three findings on this guard, so it's now stated as one rule). Each case is pinned by a test:
- **When the train's own id already gives a path.** A station code also covers platforms that really are separate. Liverpool Street's terminus and the Elizabeth line's through platforms beneath it share one code, but run to Shenfield by different routes, and Paddington is the same. Merging up front would turn a path the train's own id already gives into an ambiguous one.
- **For a bus.** A bus stop shares its code with the pole across the road, which goes the other way. So a stop served by road alone (bus or coach) gets no code, and a bus never takes the retry. A railway station TfL also lists buses at (Redhill, Merstham, Elstree & Borehamwood) keeps its code.
- **When the train names no destination** ("Check Front of Train"). If its own id only ends its routes, it's arriving here, not leaving from another platform.
- **When only the board's via rules the train's own path out.** If the train's own id reaches its terminus but not by the via its board names, it stays `ViaMatchesNoRoute`: the station's other platforms running by that via aren't where it leaves from.
- Its own id saying it ends here (`endsAt`) reads the same through the other ids, and a branch, platform compass or direction never empties the ways, so neither needs a rule.

**Not in this PR:**
- **The other end.** A trip *to* St Pancras main (`910GSTPX`) on a northbound Thameslink, whose route calls there as `910GSTPXBOX`, is still judged as missing it: `callingAt` aliases an end's siblings only when no route calls at it. That predates this PR and is recorded in `TODO.md` (Codex on #879). You chose the shape for the follow-up after this PR:
  - one logical station for boarding and ends alike;
  - the hub for routing;
  - platform > stop > station for where the rider is.
- **Routes TfL doesn't model:** Thameslink to Orpington, and Great Northern to Kings Lynn (TfL splits that route at Cambridge), still unchecked.

## Surfaces

Nothing renders from anything new. The Direct section, trip legs and route pages read the same arrivals and route sequences as before, on the same refresh. Only the route matching changed, and it still runs off the main thread.

## Cost and reliability

£0. `icsId` is already in the route sequence responses we fetch. The route cache goes to version 3 (Codex on #879), so no sequence an earlier build cached without codes is reused. Each one is fetched again the first time a screen needs it after the update, as already happens after the cache's daily expiry. Those first lookups are slow the way a cold cache is (a National Rail line's sequence takes TfL a few seconds), once. Apart from that one refetch there are no new requests.

## Testing

- `RouteStopsTest`:
  - St Pancras in both directions.
  - The station's own id still wins.
  - No station codes means no retry.
  - Liverpool Street-style separate platforms stay apart.
  - A bus is never matched through the pole across the road.
  - A "Check Front of Train" departure under an id that only ends its routes is never routed from the other platforms (HS1-shaped), while a named one there still is.
  - A via that the train's own path misses isn't read through the other platforms; a via on a path through the other id still is.
  - Removing the retry, the bus guard, the via guard or the unknown-destination guard each makes one test fail.
  - A southbound list from the low level reads its whole route through the main id's route, so an alert's stretch before the boarding stop is placed; a northbound one reads its own route. It fails without the fix.
- `RouteSequenceThameslinkTest`: against recorded TfL data, using the existing inbound fixture (now with `icsId`) and a new trimmed outbound fixture.
  - Resolving southbound from `910GSTPXBOX` and northbound from `910GSTPX`.
  - A `DirectTrips.judge` verdict.
  - The DTO keeps station codes, a railway station's that TfL also lists buses at included (Redhill in the recorded data, both ways), but never a bus or coach stop's.
- `FileRouteStopsStoreTest`: the codes round-trip through the cache, and a version-2 file (cached before codes) loads as empty.
- `./gradlew test lint`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL on the head rebased onto `main` (every unit test, screenshot tests included, plus lint).
- Not checked on a device.

author: disk83
body:
Build step 3 from `gym-log-spec.md`. History browsing, the report and backup are not part of this PR.

## What's in it
- **Home**: shows the suggested next routine, worked out from history and never stored. You can pick another routine or "No routine (free session)", then press "Start session". Below that is a summary of the last finished session. If no cycle is active, Home says so and a free session can still be started. If a session is open, Home shows **Resume** and **Discard** instead; Discard asks first, then deletes the session and its logs.
- **Session**: the routine's exercises in order, a ✓ on each logged one and a **Next** marker on the first one not logged yet. Exercises can be opened in any order. "＋ Add exercise" adds one from the list (archived ones are hidden) or creates a new one on the spot. **Finish** stays pinned above the tab bar.
- **Exercise log**: sets, reps (seconds for timed exercises), weight (optional for bodyweight) and remarks. The fields are prefilled from the most recent log of that exercise in any session, or from the exercise defaults if there is none. "Last time" always shows, or "No previous log". Saving writes to Dexie straight away. Opening it again in the same session edits that log.
- **Finish**: sets `finishedAt` and shows either "Routine complete, next: X" or "Session finished, next suggested: X".
- **Archive rules**: the data layer already archived items with history instead of deleting them. On top of that, an archived routine can't be started and an archived exercise can't be added to a session. Archived routines are skipped when suggesting the next one. A routine exercise that was archived is hidden in a new session and doesn't count against "Routine complete".

## Choices worth checking
- The prefill copies the last log's **remarks** as well as sets, reps and weight. When it falls back to the exercise defaults, remarks start empty.
- A session started from a routine shared with a newly active cycle counts toward that cycle's suggestion. The spec says "whose routine belongs to the active cycle", not "started in that cycle".
- Weight is required for exercises that aren't bodyweight.
- Finish asks for confirmation, and says how many routine exercises are still not logged.
- `Session` gains an optional `extraExerciseIds` field, so exercises added during a session survive closing the app. It is not indexed, so there's no schema version bump.

## Tests
`npm test` runs 41 tests. The new `src/session.test.ts` covers:
- the next-routine suggestion: first session ever, wrap-around, free sessions ignored, routine not in the active cycle, cycle changed, archived routines skipped
- prefill: last log versus defaults, and the most recent log across sessions
- the finish message
- one open session at a time, one log per exercise per session, discard

I also ran the whole flow in headless Chromium against `vite preview`, including going offline and reloading in the middle of a session.

## What to click to test
1. **Manage**: create 2–3 exercises (include a timed bodyweight one, e.g. Plank), routines **Push** and **Pull**, and a cycle with Push then Pull.
2. **Home**: it suggests **Push**. Press **Start session**.
3. Tap **Bench**: "Last time" says "No previous log" and the fields show the defaults. Change the weight and **Save**. Bench gets a ✓ and **Next** moves on.
4. Close the app (or turn on airplane mode and reload). Home shows **Resume** / **Discard**. Press **Resume**.
5. **＋ Add exercise** → pick one, or **Create a new exercise**. It opens straight on its log screen.
6. Tap Bench again: it shows your saved values and "Save changes".
7. Press **Finish** with an exercise not logged: you get "Session finished, next suggested: Pull".
8. Start **Pull**, log everything, then **Finish**: you get "Routine complete, next: Push", which shows the wrap-around.
9. Start a free session ("No routine") and finish it: the suggestion doesn't change.
10. Log an exercise you logged before: it is prefilled from that log, and "Last time" shows its date.
11. **Discard**: start a session, log something, go back to Home and press **Discard** → confirm. The session and its log are gone.
12. **Manage**: delete an exercise that has a log. It is archived, and it no longer shows up in "＋ Add exercise".

author: tadmstr
body:
## Summary

When a turn has ended but the session still has background work running (a backgrounded command, agent or workflow), sending a message starts a new turn, which stops that work. Today the composer guards this with `window.confirm`. That has two problems:

1. **There is no way to wait.** The choices are OK (send now and stop the work) or Cancel. The composer only queues while a turn is in flight (`isLoading`), so in this post-turn state you can't reply without killing the work you are waiting on.
2. **OK is the browser default.** A second Enter pressed right after sending (a double press, a key repeat) confirms the send and stops the work.

This PR replaces the confirm with a dialog that offers **Send anyway**, **Queue** and **Cancel**.

## Behaviour

- **Queue** writes the same server-side queued message that the composer already uses while a turn is in flight (`writeQueuedMessage`, shown as the "Will send when this finishes" card). The attachments uploaded before the prompt are reused rather than uploaded again. **No server change is needed.** `isSessionBusy` in the scheduled-message dispatcher already counts `hasBackgroundWork`, so the message is held until the background work finishes.
- **Cancel** is the default. Enter, Escape and a click outside all cancel and keep the draft in the composer. Sending anyway takes a deliberate click or Tab.
- **Send anyway** behaves exactly as OK does today.

## Implementation notes

- `useChatComposerState` now awaits a promise-returning prompt (`backgroundSendPrompt` / `resolveBackgroundSendPrompt`) instead of calling `window.confirm`. The composer renders it as `BackgroundSendDialog`, using the shared `Dialog`.
- **Default focus:** `DialogContent` focuses the first focusable element on open, so the dialog puts Cancel first in the DOM rather than adding an `initialFocus` prop to `Dialog`. That keeps the shared component unchanged. Happy to switch to a prop if you'd prefer the visual order to differ.
- The queued-message write and composer reset are extracted into a `queueMessage` helper, shared by the in-flight path and the new Queue choice, so there is still one queue entry point.
- The existing per-scope submit guard (`submittingScopesRef`) already blocks a second submit while the prompt is awaited. A test now covers that.
- i18n: there are new keys under `claudeStatus.backgroundTask.prompt.*` with English values and `defaultValue` fallbacks. The old `claudeStatus.backgroundTask.sendAnyway` string is no longer used, so it is removed from `en`, `cs`, `he` and `pt-BR`. The new strings are left for translators.

## Relation to open PRs

- #1449 (send modes while a turn runs) uses similar vocabulary, but it covers the in-flight state. This PR covers only the post-turn background-work state and reuses the existing queue.
- #1534 and #1526 reshape the queued-draft path. This change calls the existing queue entry point and adds no new one, so it should rebase onto either.

## Tests

- `composerSendOverBackgroundWork.test.ts`: the prompt lists the session's own tasks; cancel sends nothing and keeps the draft; queue persists the message with the uploaded attachments (one upload), sends nothing and clears the composer; send anyway sends; a second submit while the prompt is open opens no second prompt and sends nothing; no background work → no prompt.
- `backgroundSendDialog.test.tsx`: Cancel has focus on open; each button maps to its choice; Escape and an overlay click cancel.
- Each test was checked against a mutation that breaks the behaviour it covers (e.g. routing Queue to send, putting Send anyway first in the DOM), and each mutation turns at least one test red.
- `npm run lint`: no errors, and the warning count is unchanged from `main`. `npm run test:client`: 755/755.

author: 0xmanhnv
body:
## What

Follow-up to the CLA check that was merged here. A security review found a bypass in its "Decide who must sign" step, fixed here.

**The hole:** in a pull request opened by an outside account, a commit linked to an allowlisted account (the maintainer or a bot) was accepted when its signature was verified. A signature proves only the *committer*, and the author e-mail is free text, so a contributor could set the maintainer's e-mail as author, sign with their own key, and skip the CLA.

**The fix:** the step judges each commit by the account the CLA action uses (author, else committer). If that is an allowlisted account, the commit counts only when the author AND the committer are both allowlisted AND the signature is verified; otherwise the check fails and names the commit. Steps now select pull request events by payload (`github.event.pull_request`), not by event name.

**Tests:** `.github/scripts/cla-scope.test.sh` extracts the step from `cla.yml` and runs it against 10 recorded commit lists (maintainer, bot and outside pull requests; forged author, forged committer, contributor-signed). The previous logic fails 2 of them. `cla-test.yml` runs the test on pull requests and pushes that change the workflow or the test (read-only token, `persist-credentials: false`).

Also documented in the workflow header: keep `cla` required on pull requests; in the merge queue it passes at once. The archived upstream action's replacement is planned in openctemio/openctem#2299.

Security: same model as before. The check runs in the base context and never checks out or runs pull request code; the test workflow runs the pull request's own copy on `pull_request` with `contents: read` only. Secret still needed: org secret `CLA_SIGNATURES_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT, resource owner `openctemio`, repository access only `openctemio/cla-signatures`, Contents read/write).

author: massivemarmot
body:
## Summary
Upgrade `maplibre-gl` 4.7.1 → **6.14.0** (latest 6.x; the advisory is fixed in ≥6.4.1, so the newest patch level gives a durable clean audit). **Licence: BSD-3-Clause, unchanged** (verified: `npm view maplibre-gl@6.14.0 license` → BSD-3-Clause; the built bundle carries the 3-Clause BSD header). No new dependency (same package); one transitive spec bump (`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-style-spec` 20.4 → 26.4, BSD-3-Clause per its npm metadata).

### Breaking-change review (official v5.0.0 and v6.0.0 release notes, read in full)
Affecting our files:
1. **6.0: ESM-only distribution** — no default export. `useMap.ts` used `import maplibregl` (only for `new maplibregl.Map`); `Map.tsx` used it only as a type namespace. Fixed with named imports (`Map as MapLibreMap`) and pure type imports. These were the **only two compile errors** the upgrade produced.
2. **6.0: real event classes** — the `error` listener now receives `ErrorEvent & Object`, not a bare `Error`; the two inline-typed handlers in `useMap.ts` no longer compiled. Merged into one handler reading `event.error` for the message and `event.sourceId` for the tile notice (same behaviour as before: 404 tiles fire no error; suppression re-verified present in the 6.14 dist).

Reviewed and **not** affecting us (checked against the code): `on()` returning Subscription (we use callback form); `setData` second-parameter removal (unused); `styleimagemissing` notify-only (unused); `Map` no longer extends `Camera`/`transform` removed (unused); style-spec 25 throwing on legacy expressions (our style uses current expressions; build+validate pass); `geometry-type` "Multi-" change (unused); WebGL2 required (maplibre handles the missing-WebGL2 error via the `error` event, which we already surface); `zoomLevelsToOverscale` default change (only affects dense label rendering/query results marginally; our labels are sparse airport names); icon-offset scaling change (we use `icon-rotate`/`icon-size`, no offset); `#${pragma mapbox}` (no custom shaders); Hash/URLSearchParams (hash option unused). None of `NoiseOverlay.tsx`, `airportLayer.ts`, `aircraftIcons.ts` import maplibre at all (checked); the layers are plain style objects that validate against the new style-spec at runtime (build passes, layer-config tests pass).

**CSP: unchanged.** No new origins; `worker-src 'self' blob:` stays exactly as-is (the 6.0 notes say `blob:` is no longer *required* because the ESM build loads its worker as a real URL — but our built bundle still creates `blob:` worker URLs, verified by grep of `dist/assets/Map-*.js`, so `blob:` must stay).

### Verification
```
$ pnpm install                                  # exit 0
$ pnpm audit --prod
No known vulnerabilities found                  # was: 1 critical (GHSA-jrc7-96c5-q579)
$ pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test      # all exit 0
core test:       Test Files  8 passed (8)        Tests  143 passed (143)
data-build test: Test Files  12 passed (12)      Tests  129 passed (129)
web test:        Test Files  25 passed (25)      Tests  229 passed (229)
$ pnpm --filter @vliegvuil/web build            # exit 0
```
Advisory verified via `gh api /advisories/GHSA-jrc7-96c5-q579`: "XSS Sanitizer Bypass in DOM.sanitize() via Live NamedNodeMap Removal Skip", vulnerable ≤6.4.0. The app does not use `Popup`/`setHTML` (the app's AirportPopup is a plain React component; no maplibre Popup/Marker usage anywhere — grep-verified), so 4.7.1 was not exploitable, as the task notes; this closes it anyway.

### Not verified
- **Visual map behaviour was NOT verified in a browser.** No browser exists in the sandbox. What was verified: compile (tsc), the full unit suite (including the layer/style-readiness and mock-map tests), a production build, and static checks of the built bundle (license header, blob-worker usage, no default-export usage). Rendering (tiles drawing, icon rotation, labels, popups positioning) needs a real browser — recommend a quick visual pass on the live map after merge, especially icon rotation (`icon-rotate` with the 6.0 "disable icon scaling with offset" change is adjacent but should not affect us) and the 404-tile fallback behaviour the self-hosted tiles rely on.

author: charan-manjunath
body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds opt-in remote packet capture support to the node Private Action Runner. The runner gets access to a system-probe socket that serves only the `packet_capture` module; the full system-probe socket (`/var/run/sysprobe/sysprobe.sock`) is not mounted into the runner. The cluster-agent runner is unchanged.

### Configuration

```yaml
agent.datadoghq.com/private-action-runner-enabled: "true"
agent.datadoghq.com/private-action-runner-packet-capture-enabled: "true"
```

The annotation accepts only `"true"` or `"false"`; invalid values are rejected before the node pod template is modified. It has no effect unless node PAR is enabled. When enabled, the `system-probe` container is added to the node agent pod.

### Mounts and env

| Item | `system-probe` | `private-action-runner` |
|---|---|---|
| emptyDir `sysprobe-capture-socket-dir` at `/var/run/sysprobe-capture` | Read-write | Read-only |
| `DD_PACKET_CAPTURE_SOCKET=/var/run/sysprobe-capture/capture.sock` | Yes | Yes |
| `DD_PACKET_CAPTURE_ENABLED=true` | Yes | No |
| emptyDir `sysprobe-socket-dir` at `/var/run/sysprobe` (main socket) | Read-write | Not mounted |
| Capabilities `SYS_ADMIN`, `SYS_RESOURCE`, `NET_ADMIN`, `NET_RAW`, `IPC_LOCK` | Added | Unchanged |

The main socket dir and capabilities are added so system-probe can start when packet capture is its only consumer.

### Motivation

The PAR action `com.datadoghq.remoteaction.pcap.runCapture` calls system-probe's `packet_capture` module. Under the Operator the runner container has no path to system-probe, so the call fails with `dial unix ...: no such file or directory`.

### Additional Notes

Depends on a datadog-agent change that adds `packet_capture.socket` (`DD_PACKET_CAPTURE_SOCKET`), a second system-probe socket serving only packet capture. Companion datadog-agent PR: https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/58221.

Follows the structure of #3319 (systemd host mounts): separate `packet_capture.go`, strict bool annotation parsing, validation before pod template mutation.

### Minimum Agent Versions

* Agent: TBD (release containing the companion datadog-agent change)
* Cluster Agent: N/A

### Describe your test plan

- Unit tests in `packet_capture_test.go` (annotation parsing, required components, mounts/env, invalid value rejection).
- Reconcile test asserting the DaemonSet has the `system-probe` container, the capture socket volume and mounts, and no main system-probe socket mount in the runner.
- `go test ./internal/controller/datadogagent/...`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` pass.

### Checklist

- [ ] PR has at least one valid label: `bug`, `enhancement`, `refactoring`, `documentation`, `tooling`, and/or `dependencies`
- [ ] PR has a milestone or the `qa/skip-qa` label
- [x] All commits are signed (see: [signing commits][1])

[1]: https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/signing-commits

author: qutibah
body:
## Summary

Adds a Claude-powered chatbot on top of the RAG stores, in two forms:

- **`rag/chatbot.py`** - terminal chatbot. Retrieves the top 3 chunks per readable store (hybrid vector + keyword search), adds the live facts from `Knowledge_Base/facts.yaml`, and makes **one** LLM call per question through **OpenRouter** (OpenAI-compatible API, `openai` package). Customer view by default (`rag_public_reader`); `--internal` for the staff view.
- **`rag/chat_web.py`** - the customer chatbot as a single-page website (FastAPI + inline HTML, same pattern as `rag/webui.py`), themed after www.dhakakacchi.com (its colours, Cormorant Garamond + DM Sans, the real logo in `rag/static/logo.webp`).

### Key design points
- **Facts are never embedded.** Prices, fees and deadlines come from `facts.yaml`, re-read on every question. `[CONFIRM]` values are sent as *(unconfirmed)* and quoted as "subject to change"; `null` becomes `unknown` (including inside YAML flow maps).
- **Small prompts.** Context rides only on the current message; history keeps the last 3 bare Q/A pairs. ~2,000 input / ~250 output tokens per question.
- **Website safety.** Always the public reader (no internal switch), rate limits (15 questions / 10 min per visitor, 300 / day total; `CF-Connecting-IP` aware), 500-char input cap, FastAPI docs disabled, replies HTML-escaped before formatting.
- **Config.** `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (required, fail-fast) and optional `CHAT_MODEL` (default `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`; we run `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`). Documented in `.env.example`. No secrets in the diff.

### New make targets

body:
## Purpose
Add a governed **Decision Safeguard Gate** so an owner can see whether important safeguards are actually defined before exposure grows, without turning Thebe into a blocker, approver, or execution authority.

## What changes
- adds a separate V336 Safeguard Gate layer after Decision Pre-Mortem
- owner-only surface
- derives only from the canonical Owner Focus snapshot
- runs only on items already classified into the canonical **Needs your decision** lane
- reuses V335 `premortemSpec(item)` for bounded current decision context
- performs no fetch/API call and no persistence
- does not create a second decision queue, shadow business record, or risk ledger

## Safeguard review contract
For each verified current owner decision, Thebe must classify each category only as **Defined, Partial, Missing, or Unknown** from verified context:
1. measurable success / failure signal
2. early warning signal
3. reversible first step or bounded test
4. explicit exit trigger / stop condition
5. exposure limit / maximum downside where a verified limit exists
6. accountable human owner / reviewer
7. irreversible commitment requiring extra scrutiny

Thebe must cite or describe the verified evidence behind each classification. A safeguard cannot be marked Defined merely because it would be sensible to have one.

## Exposure presentation
The layer uses deterministic canonical signals such as high/urgent priority, overdue status, approval sensitivity, and material money/compliance/people/property domains only to order and label cards for review.

These are explicitly **presentation heuristics, not an authoritative risk score**.

## Reasoning / authority boundary
- canonical current business evidence stays primary
- Thebe must not invent thresholds, limits, probabilities, approvals, or evidence
- `Unknown` stays unknown until a measurement or owner decision defines it
- if canonical decision data is not `ready`, the gate fails closed and does not classify readiness
- V336 itself performs no `apiJson`, `fetch`, XHR, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, or direct `/api/` request
- this is an advisory readiness check, **not a blocker, approval, or execution gate**
- no approval, payment, filing, sending, execution, or domain-record mutation is introduced
- specs are explicitly `authoritative:false` and `authority: context_only_no_execution`

author: edwardfward
body:
## Why
Main's ruleset requires branches to be up to date. With squash merges, every merge made every other open pull request update and rerun its whole CI (about 5 minutes) before it could merge. A merge queue keeps the guarantee, since each pull request is tested as it would merge, without that rerun chain. The queue needs the required checks to run on its temporary branches.

## What
- `ci.yml` runs on `merge_group`. Its cache restores read main's caches for `merge_group` runs as for pull requests; only a push to `main` saves.
- `AGENTS.md`: the cache paragraph and the Git section describe the queue.

After this merges, the ruleset "Protect main" gains the merge queue rule (squash, and the required checks `lint` and `test`). That is a repository setting, changed separately.

## Tests
`go test ./scripts/... ./internal/version/...`, which read `ci.yml` and `AGENTS.md`, pass.

## Gate
Not run in full: workflow and docs only.

AGENTS.md.

author: ashdamle
body:
## What

A transiently-down $0 subscription lane (codex auth-event/logout blip, cold daemon, 429, timeout) was
misread as a **dead** lane, so lane-eligible work for hook/panel calls fell over to the **metered API**
almost immediately — measured **$6.34/mo** of lane-tried-then-down metered (codex $2.23), and worse while a
plan is capped. Same failure class as #66's `budget_usd`: *a control the caller believed was in force — "I'm
on a $0 lane" — was silently not.*

## The reliability ladder (on the real `adapters._call_once` path; reuses existing infra)

1. **Classify** (`lane_recovery.lane_failure_shape`) by **fixed transport shapes only** — 429/5xx, reset/
   timeout, logout/auth-event/cold-daemon — unknown prose → `"ambiguous"`, never a keyword judgement.
2. **Retry** (`retry_free_lane`) — bounded, configured retry+backoff to **confirm down** before declaring it.
   One error no longer marks a lane dead.
3. **Shed** to a ready $0 substitute (existing shed/fallback).
4. **Queue** (`lane_queue.hold_free_recovery`) — hold-and-retry while all $0 lanes are transiently down,
   bounded by a configured deadline.
5. **Metered = last resort, gated.** `LaneRecoveryProof.authorize_metered_recovery` requires retry+shed+queue
   exhausted **and** an explicit `gate._rt_precheck` pass; a metered transition without that proof raises the
   typed `LaneRecoveryViolation` and is recorded. **In-flight is never cancelled.**

All thresholds are named config (`lane_recovery.*` / `SPENDGUARD_LANE_*`) — nothing hardcoded.

## The process change — a fault-injection CHAOS tier (`tests/chaos/`)

The reason this (and the budget gap) survived two months: the suite was hermetic **unit** tests mocking a
**static** up/down lane — no test injected the **transient-under-concurrency** window, so a bypassed ladder
never turned a test red. This adds the missing tier:

- **`lane_faults.py`** — zero-spend, **6-way-concurrent** injection of a transient-then-recover lane through
  the **real** recovery path; asserts retry/shed/queue serve on $0 and the paid door is reached **only** when
  every free rung is exhausted, gated.
- **`mutation_proof.py`** — disables each production rung and asserts the contract goes **RED** (intact
  GREEN). *A P0 test that cannot be shown to fail on a broken ladder is not accepted.* Verified matrix:
  `intact GREEN · disable_retry RED · disable_shed RED · disable_queue RED · allow_ungated_metered RED`.
- **`live_fidelity.py`** — opt-in real-lane check behind an explicit budget
  (`SPENDGUARD_CHAOS_LIVE_BUDGET_USD`); default run is $0 simulation.

## Axis-4 absence gate (`tests/test_lane_recovery_axis4.py`)

Scans **every** paid-routing edge / SDK sink across the repo and **fails closed** on an unknown edge — the
"no lane-eligible intent reaches metered without retry→shed→queue" invariant that no per-file reviewer can
see. **22/22 edges + 15/15 sinks, UNREVIEWED=0, INSUFFICIENT=0.**

## Verification (reviewer's own runs, not the author's word)

- Offline suite: **545 passed, 0 failed**.
- Mutation matrix re-run independently: **intact GREEN, every broken rung RED**.
- Axis-4: green, fail-closed on unknown.
- Diff reviewed: ladder on the production `_call_once` path, classification fixed-shape-only, config-driven,
  metered gated+proof-required, new symbols unique (`grep -c` == 1), name-uniqueness + ruff green.

author: coma-toast
body:
## Summary

Implements JD-271: mcp-local now surfaces stuck/degraded/orphaned services and provides a `doctor` command to diagnose and auto-fix issues.

## Changes

### Config
- **New `extra_ports` field** on services — additional TCP ports that mcp-local owns and monitors
- **New `StateKind` type** with states: `running`, `degraded`, `orphaned`, `port conflict`, `stopped`
- **`OwnedPorts()`** method on ServiceConfig — collects port, dashboard_url port, health_url port, mcp_url port, extra_ports

### Port utilities (internal/portutil)
- **`GetCommandForPID(pid)`** — returns the executable path of a process
- **`IsSameBinary(pid, expectedCommand)`** — checks if running process matches expected binary
- **`FetchHealth(healthURL)`** — GET health endpoint, parses JSON for status/embed_error/startup_message

### Runtime status (internal/mgr/runtime)
- **Enhanced `CheckStatus()`** — now returns `State` (StateKind) and `Detail` string
- Classifies services as: running, degraded (health check failed), orphaned (same binary on port), port conflict (different program), stopped

### Lifecycle (cmd/mcp-local/lifecycle.go)
- **start/stop/restart** now check all owned ports for orphans and conflicts
- Same-binary orphan: stop the orphaned process (PID file preserved for mcp-local)
- Port conflict: refuse to start, print error with PID of conflicting program
- On start failure: print last 10 lines of service log

### Status UI (internal/statusui)
- **New DETAIL column** showing the reason for the current state
- **New state colors**: degraded=yellow, orphaned=orange, port conflict=red
- Plain output also includes DETAIL column

### Doctor command (cmd/mcp-local/doctor.go)
New subcommand `mcp-local doctor [service] [--fix]`:

**Diagnoses:**
1. PID file status (alive, stale, missing)
2. Owned ports (orphaned same-binary, port conflict with different program)
3. Health check via health_url (if configured)
4. Missing dependencies (deps check)
5. Stale PID files (dead process, PID file still present)
6. Agent registration status (OpenCode, Cursor, Claude Desktop)
7. Disk space on log volume

**`--fix` applies safe auto-fixes:**
- Stops same-binary orphans
- Removes stale PID files
- Restarts degraded services
- **Does not kill** programs owned by different binaries (port conflict)

## Files Changed
- `internal/mgr/config/config.go` — ExtraPorts, StateKind, OwnedPorts()
- `internal/portutil/port.go` — GetCommandForPID, IsSameBinary, FetchHealth
- `internal/mgr/runtime/status.go` — Enhanced CheckStatus with State/Detail
- `cmd/mcp-local/lifecycle.go` — Orphan/conflict handling in start/stop/restart
- `cmd/mcp-local/doctor.go` — NEW doctor command
- `internal/statusui/statusui.go` — DETAIL column, new state colors
- `internal/mgr/runtime/status_test.go` — TestCheckStatus_States
- `README.md` — Doctor command docs, new status states, extra_ports field
- `AGENTS.md` — Diagnostics section with doctor command reference

## Validation
- `make check` passes (test + vet + fmt)
- Branch: `jd-271-doctor-command`
- Target: `coma-toast/mcp-local:main`

## Change

Competition directors can now publish structured event dates, regular and late application fees, a competition bio, AV guidelines, a venue address, public payment instructions, and a downloadable PDF application packet. Teams see these details on competition pages and fee summaries while applying.

Existing free-text dates, descriptions, and lighting guidelines are preserved. Packet uploads, replacement, and removal require the competition's active approved admin; hidden listings keep their packets private. Files are limited to 3 MiB and checked for PDF structure.

## Evidence

- [ ] CI Release gate is green on this commit
- [x] Regression covers the changed permission/state boundary
- [ ] Relevant staging role checks completed (evidence below)
- [x] Documentation and changelog updated

Completed locally on the exact published Git tree:
- `npm run check`: lint, TypeScript, and 78 unit tests passed.
- All 30 integration tests passed against isolated local PostgreSQL.
- Production build passed.
- 16 targeted browser tests passed across Chromium and WebKit, covering competition details, visibility, applications, and exports.
- New coverage includes date validation, fee precision and unknown/zero values, legacy field preservation, authorization, hidden packet downloads, forged target IDs, PDF upload/replacement/removal, and reset behavior.
- Manual local browser inspection completed. Hosted preview and production smoke checks remain pending.

## Release impact

Migration: `20261015120000_competition_details` adds optional profile fields and a separate packet blob table. No backfill, new environment variables, dependencies, or external services are required. The production owner reported applying the migration through Supabase SQL Editor and confirming both `applied = true` and `checksum_matches = true`; production was not independently queried here. No repeat application is needed.

Rollout: require a green Release gate, review the preview, merge, then confirm the Vercel deployment and production profile save/public details/PDF upload-download flow.

Rollback: revert the application deployment while retaining the additive schema and migration history. Existing fields remain compatible with the previous application. Do not drop the new table or columns during an application rollback.

Remaining risks: hosted preview and production smoke verification belong to the release owner. PDF validation checks format and size; it is not malware scanning.

author: mayteio
body:
## Problem

Email recipients who open the message preferences page, the one-click unsubscribe page, or the expired-link error page get unstyled browser-default HTML.

- The templates link `{% static 'message-preferences.css' %}`, which production manifest storage turns into `message-preferences.<hash>.css`.
- The CDN that serves `/static/` holds only the unhashed files from `frontend/public`, so the hashed URL returns 404.
- `error.html` was a bare fragment with no `<head>` and no stylesheet. Every link older than the token lifetime lands there.

Raised in [this Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C06GG249PR6/p1792076858397389). Replaces the closed [#117946](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/117946), which inlined the CSS through the view.

## Changes

- All three pages load their styles again. A shared `_head.html` links `/static/message-preferences.css`, without the static tag.
- This follows the [hosted survey page](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/a2ffe7b17/posthog/templates/surveys/public_survey.html#L7-L31), which hit the same 404.
- No cache-busting param is needed. The CDN serves the file with `max-age=60, must-revalidate` and an ETag, so a rebuild goes live within a minute.
- The expired or invalid link page is now a full HTML page with the same head.
- Mechanical: the Tailwind `@source` and the style test now point at `products/messaging/backend/templates/`, where #113926 moved the templates. A rebuild with the fixed path gives byte-identical CSS.

## Linked issue

Fixes #29

## Problem

Token Plan video metadata does not connect to Hermes's normal `video_generate` tool. A native backend also needs model-specific setup hints and safe handling when a paid task outlives the local tool call.

## Solution

Add an opt-in `VideoGenProvider` with canonical region/tier hosts and credentials, exact HappyHorse mode IDs and unsuffixed `wan3.0-video`. Submit once, poll with a bounded deadline and cache through Hermes's safe downloader. Preserve existing chat profiles, aliases, endpoints, credential precedence and defaults.

The follow-up implements model-specific picker strengths, duration/resolution metadata and a setup tag naming the selected profile. Hermes `/stop` is checked before submission, during polling/backoff and before caching. After submission, cancellation and failure retain the task ID and `resubmit_safe: false`. Local stopping does not cancel vendor billing. Transient GET errors retry at most three consecutive failed reads within the same deadline; POST is never retried. Optional `poll_timeout` accepts 1 to 600 seconds, retaining the existing 600-second default.

## Scope

Video only, on this same feature branch. Hermes v0.22.0 minimum for native video; the existing chat compatibility lanes remain unchanged. The installer copies and verifies the independent backend, preserves backups and rolls back failed upgrades. It never enables the backend, selects defaults or accesses keys. Active installation/configuration and sibling branches were not changed.

Implemented subset: five seconds, HappyHorse t2v/i2v/r2v at 720p; Wan t2v at 480p or 720p with adaptive ratio. Wan image/reference modes, broader duration/resolution ranges, audio controls, editing and driving remain gated. No live generation or measured Token Plan deductions are claimed. Integrate video before rebasing the additive installer changes in TTS #28 and ASR #27.

author: soup9x
body:
The last group of the IT Glue parity pass. Three of its four parts were assembly, as the plan said. The fourth was not — and two things it depended on turned out not to work at all.

**Read the first two sections before the feature work.** One of them is a control this product traded two-person approval for.

---

## The audit fan-out had never run

`fanOutNotifications` enumerated its tenants with a raw query on the bare worker pool:

```sql
SELECT ... FROM tenant t WHERE t.status = 'active' AND ...
```

`tenant` is behind RLS — `tenant_rls_select: id = helm.current_tenant_id()` — and a worker connection sets no tenant context. **Zero rows, every tick.** The audit fan-out never queued anything from the job, so 0400 removed two-person approval from credential exports on the understanding that these notifications replace it, and the replacement was not running.

Three things about why it survived:

- **Every test called the function, not the job.** `helm.fan_out_notifications()` inside `withTenant()` is the right way to test what the function does, and it skips the enumeration completely. The job's tenant discovery had no test at all.
- **The other half was always correct.** `deliverNotifications` uses `helm.notification_backlog()`, a `SECURITY DEFINER` function — the pattern `alert_backlog`, `email_backlog` and `external_check_backlog` all follow. 0420's own comment two functions below the defect states the rule: *"the worker holds no tenant context of its own, so it asks which tenants to iterate and then enters each one."* The one raw query among them was the one that silently did nothing.
- **A read fails differently from a write.** This is the project's third zero-rows-under-RLS defect, and the first in a **read**: an empty list is indistinguishable from "there was nothing to do", so the job logged `idle: true` once a minute, correctly, forever. H's refresh worker at least reported success while writing nothing.

Fixed with `helm.notification_fanout_backlog()`, and the guard asserts `prosecdef` rather than mere existence — a non-definer function of the same name would have the identical defect.

## And raising a reminder required a mail relay

Both of 0690's reminder-raising functions carried `JOIN smtp_setting m ON ... AND m.enabled`, so an install with no mail created **no `task_reminder` rows at all** — and the trigger that lights the new bell never fired. An air-gapped MSP would have had a bell that could not show the one thing it is most for.

Correct when email was the only output. Safe to remove because 0690 already separated raising from sending: `helm.email_backlog()` still requires an enabled relay, so a reminder raised without one sits `pending` until somebody configures mail — which is exactly what 0690's own comment describes. Three of K's tests asserted the old rule and were **rewritten rather than deleted**, to the stronger pair: the rows *are* created, and nothing is sent.

---

## The inbox

`user_notification` is the first notification table in this schema pointing **inwards**. 0110, 0420 and 0690 built three outbound queues: a `webhook_delivery` row belongs to a destination, a `task_reminder` row is a message about to be sent. None can express *"this person has not seen this"*, which is the whole of what a bell is — hence `read_at`, and hence the plan's line that *a bell that cannot be distinguished from an empty inbox is worse than no bell* could not be honoured until now.

Two sources, mirroring the outbound queue's two:

- **The audit fan-out**, driven by the `candidate` rows and **deliberately not joined to `webhook_endpoint`** — a tenant with no destination and no relay still has a working bell, which is the air-gapped install the rest of this system is built for.
- **A trigger on `task_reminder`**, so both of 0690's writers are covered by one place and a third added later cannot forget. Only a `pending` row lights it: lighting the bell for a `suppressed` lead would undo 0690's one-message rule.

Addressed by `helm.notification_audience()` — a tenant-wide seat (`org_scope_all`) holding `audit:read` that has opted into the kind. The `org_scope_all` half is **decision 31 written set-based**: `client_admin` holds `audit:read` and is not tenant-wide, which is the leak 0690 had to correct on `task_reminder`.

**Custody.** `helm_app` holds `SELECT`, `DELETE` and `UPDATE` on **`read_at` alone** — a column grant, because RLS cannot restrict a column and rewriting the subject of a notification about an export would be putting words in Helm's mouth. There is **no `audit:read` carve-out on the SELECT policy at all**: what somebody has and has not read is a record of their attention, and the oversight material is in the audit log.

Four oversight kinds added (`export_activity`, `credential_access`, `expiring_soon`, `operations`), defaulting **off** — one preference set governs both channels, so defaulting them on would have emailed every administrator about every export the moment 0700 applied. Decision 37.

## The header

Four of its five icons went somewhere unrelated: Documentation and Help both opened `/settings`, Assistant opened `/search`, Recently viewed opened `/dashboard`.

- **Recently viewed** is the real popover now — and that component already existed, fully built and unwired. The third such thing in this codebase after 0110's webhook tables and 0690's `transport` column. The rule this pass keeps earning: before building a control, grep for it.
- **Documentation and Assistant are gone.** Neither exists to wire, and an icon promising a feature nobody is building is the same problem with an extra step.
- **Help is gone too**, which narrows what was asked for, so the reasoning is in decision 38: it was a second copy of the floating Support badge — same `LifeBuoy` icon, same destination — and a panel in its place would have had to invent keyboard shortcuts (there are none beyond Escape) or surface a version that `api/health/route.ts` says in as many words is reconnaissance. The Support badge stays, so no route to help was lost.

## Personal and Global

Real landing pages rather than aliases for one of their own sub-pages, which is why both read as parity on the summary table and were not. Personal collects My Tasks, the recent bell and the account signposts; Global carries a count per card — **counts, never a score**, decision 20 applied to a menu.

Global does **not** invent the cross-client asset list the plan's wording mentioned. There is no such page, and a filterable table over every asset in the tenant is a group of its own with its own scope surface. Decision 39.

## Important Contacts, with no migration

The plan said "a flag on `contact`". `contact` already carries `is_primary`, `is_technical`, `is_billing`, `is_emergency` and `is_authorised`, and `organization.primary_contact_id` is a sixth way to say it — so an `is_important` column would have had nothing to say about what distinguishes it from `is_primary`, and two people would have filled them in differently within a month. The widget ranks the flags that exist, near the top of the client page where somebody on a call can reach a phone number. Decision 35.

---

## Verification

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm verify` | **1976 tests across 99 files, no drift** |
| `pnpm test:sql` | **625 assertions**, including §51 at 19 |
| New this PR | 16 integration (the inbox end to end), 7 unit (contact ranking), 4 page value tests, §51, 2 `helm_test` helpers |
| Rewritten | 3 of K's reminder tests, to the new raise-without-a-relay rule |
| Sabotages | 9 run, **8 caught** — 5 by migration guards, 3 by tests — and 1 survived |

**The sabotage that survived:** removing the lead day from the reminder's dedupe key broke nothing. The assertion meant to hold it inserted one `due` row and checked the count went up by one — which passes with the lead removed entirely, because the row it compared against was a `task_assigned` row and the *kind* already distinguished them. author: roed-math
body:
This PR proves Hadamard's `ℓ¹` determinant bound and applies it to the regulator of a number field. It advances [HeightsAndUnits/README.md, Layer 3 §3.3, "The regulator and the heights of a fundamental system"](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/HeightsAndUnits/README.md#layer-3-heights-of-units-and-the-regulator). The route for *Hadamard's bound, for every fundamental system* names `Matrix.abs_det_le_prod_sum_abs`, which bounds `|det M|` by the product of the `ℓ¹` norms of the rows, as its matrix input. This PR supplies that lemma and the regulator bound it gives. After this PR, Hadamard's bound in heights, `regulator K ≤ (2d)^r · ∏ i, h(ε i)`, needs only §3.1's comparison `∑_{w ≠ w₀} |logEmbedding u w| ≤ 2 · logHeight₁ u`, or the `S = ∅` identity in open #16890. The reduced-fundamental-system half of §3.3 still needs §2.1's basis from the minima.

`TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/AbsoluteValue.lean` (new, 75 lines) is the companion of Mathlib's `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/AbsoluteValue.lean`. It proves:
- `Matrix.abv_det_le_prod_sum_abv'`: for any absolute value, `abv A.det ≤ ∏ j, ∑ i, abv (A i j)`, the column form.
- `Matrix.abv_det_le_prod_sum_abv`: the row form, `abv A.det ≤ ∏ i, ∑ j, abv (A i j)`.
- `Matrix.abs_det_le_prod_sum_abs` (the roadmap's name) and `Matrix.abs_det_le_prod_sum_abs'`: the same bounds for `|·|` over a linearly ordered commutative ring.

The proof follows Mathlib's `Matrix.det_le` through the Leibniz expansion. The last step replaces the sum over permutations with the sum over all maps (`Finset.sum_le_sum_of_injOn`), and `Fintype.prod_sum` turns that sum into the product of the column sums.

`TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/Regulator.lean` (extended, with an updated module docstring) adds:
- `regOfFamily_eq_regulator_iff`: `regOfFamily u = regulator K ↔ closure (range u) ⊔ torsion K = ⊤`. This is Mathlib's `regOfFamily_div_regulator` at index one.
- `regOfFamily_le_prod_sum_abs_logEmbedding` and `regulator_le_prod_sum_abs_logEmbedding` (for every fundamental system): the regulator is at most `∏ i, ∑ w, |logEmbedding (ε i) w|`, from Mathlib's `regOfFamily_eq_det'`.
- `sum_abs_logEmbedding_le_sum_mult_mul_abs_log`, together with `regOfFamily_le_prod_sum_mult_mul_abs_log` and `regulator_le_prod_sum_mult_mul_abs_log`: the same bounds with the full sums `∑ w, mult w * |log (w u)|` over all infinite places. This form does not depend on the choice of `w₀`. It is exactly `2 · logHeight₁` of each unit, which is the `S = ∅` case of the identity in open #16890.

I searched pinned Mathlib and Tau Ceti for an existing `ℓ¹` Hadamard bound. Mathlib has only `Matrix.det_le`, `det_sum_le` and `det_sum_smul_le`, all from a uniform entrywise bound. I also searched for a regulator-equals-`regOfFamily` criterion and found none. No open PR touches §3.3 or the Hadamard bound. The related open HeightsAndUnits PRs #16672, #16681, #16688 and #16806, and DAT's #16890, cover other milestones, and this PR depends on none of them. No Mathlib infrastructure is vendored. The informal source is Bugeaud–Győry 1996, §3, Lemma 1, cited in the module docstring.

Roadmap: HeightsAndUnits

## Rebalancing proposal (Rolf: by asset class, not fund by fund; include the guarantee resets)
For each account with fund detail and a profile, the engine works out the switch **by asset class**, **inside the account**, to bring it to its profile's iA model mix (e.g. 40% income for Balanced), and lists the death benefit reset with it. Nothing is executed. Amounts are computed in code from the latest account value.

Summary ("$X into income funds and $Y into equity funds"), then a row per account: income now, the model's income, the switch (amount and direction), a badge **Outside range** (a move is needed) or **Optional** (inside the range, but off the model mix), a **Taxable** badge on non-registered accounts with the year's change as an indicator (per-fund cost is not stored, so no gain is calculated), and the **Reset** amount. **Copy worksheet** copies it as plain text to work through on the iA advisor site.
