body:
**What:** on SharePoint Server, a read-by-path that fails now says either "File not found: '<path>'" or "Ambiguous path: '<path>' matches N files", and lists each match by its full path.
**Why:** both outcomes raised the same "File path is missing or ambiguous" message, so the agent couldn't tell whether to fix the path or choose a library.

No linked issue. Seen in the same live chat as [bagofwords1/bagofwords#1398](https://github.com/bagofwords1/bagofwords/pull/1398).

## Executive summary

When an agent reads a SharePoint document by name and the read fails, it now learns why. If the file doesn't exist, it's told so plainly. If the same name exists in several document libraries, it gets the exact paths and can read the right one on the next step instead of guessing or re-listing. This is a small quality fix: in the reported chat the agent recovered after one wasted step, and this removes the guesswork.

## Product visual

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Path doesn't exist | `File path is missing or ambiguous. Use the id returned by list_files/search_files.` | `File not found: 'contract.pdf' does not exist in the connected document libraries. Use the id returned by list_files/search_files (the full path starting with '/').` |
| Same name in two libraries | Same message as above | `Ambiguous path: 'shared.txt' matches 2 files in different document libraries: /sites/research/Policies/shared.txt; /sites/research/Shared Documents/shared.txt. Read one of them by that full path; it is the file id.` |

## Technical visual

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[read_file 'name.pdf'] --> T[try path in every visible library]
  T -->|0 matches| N[File not found + hint]
  T -->|1 match| R[read]
  T -->|2+ matches| A[Ambiguous + full paths]
  A --> R2[read by listed full path]
  style N fill:#dcfce7
  style A fill:#dcfce7
```

## Reviewer decision box

| | |
|---|---|
| **Risk** | Low. Only the error text changes, plus one shared helper. Resolution logic is untouched. |
| **Blast radius** | SharePoint Server connections, both 2010 SOAP and modern REST, on read-by-path failures. |
| **Behavior change (intended)** | The error message text. Callers still get a `ValueError`. |
| **Verified ✅** | The reproduction fails on `main` (8 failed) and passes here (10 passed), for both clients, through the real clients and the in-memory SharePoint providers. The test reads each listed path to prove the suggestion works. All 202 SharePoint unit tests pass. Full unit suite has the same failing set with and without the change. |
| **NOT verified ⚠️** | Not run against a real SharePoint Server, since none is available in the sandbox. Not run live with a model. Documentum has the same combined message and is left as is. |
| **Look first** | `unresolved_path_error` in `backend/app/data_sources/clients/sharepoint_onprem_client.py`. |

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Reproduction on `main` | 8 failed, 2 passed |
| Reproduction with fix | 10 passed |
| SharePoint unit tests | 202 passed |
| Full unit suite, failures caused by this PR | 0 (40 on both sides, identical sets, with the sandbox CA override unset) |

## Context map

- `backend/app/data_sources/clients/sharepoint_onprem_client.py`: `unresolved_path_error`.
- `backend/app/data_sources/clients/_sharepoint_rest.py` and `_sharepoint_2010.py`: the two call sites.
- `backend/tests/unit/test_sharepoint_read_path_errors.py`: both clients, parametrized.
- `docs/feedback-loops/2026-10-15-sharepoint-read-path-errors.md`: commands and output.

**Convention.** A path-resolution error names the outcome, and when it offers alternatives, they must be directly usable as ids.

author: blairham
body:
Closes #51

This follows #78. That PR added SCRAM-SHA-256, SASL/PLAIN, OAUTHBEARER and opt-in SASL without TLS to the CLI, the TUI and config contexts. It left out `cmd/k4a-index`'s own flags while #77 was editing the same lines. #77 and #80 have since merged, so this wires the daemon.

- **Flags:** `--no-tls` plus `--oauth-token`, `--oauth-token-file`, `--oauth-token-url`, `--oauth-client-id`, `--oauth-client-secret` and `--oauth-scopes`. The OAuth flags also read `KAFKA_OAUTH_*`, the same names as the CLI.
  - They go through the daemon's `overlayAuth` from #80 one field at a time, so a context's OAuth settings can be overridden individually.
  - `--no-tls` can only turn TLS off, the same way `--insecure` can only turn verification off.
- **Warning:** the daemon logs `kafka.CleartextWarning` at warn before it connects.
- **Chart:**
  - `kafka.noTLS` is rendered as the `--no-tls` argument, since the flag has no env form.
  - `kafka.oauth.{tokenUrl,clientId,scopes}` are rendered as env.
  - The client secret or a static token comes from `kafka.oauth.existingSecret` (`clientSecretKey` / `tokenKey`), so the chart never holds the secret.
  - The SASL credentials comments now cover `scram-sha-256` and `plain`.
- **Docs:** `docs/guides/deploy.md`, `docs/design/auth.md` and `SECURITY.md` are updated to match.

The direct-`--brokers` default of `scram` when `--auth` is absent is unchanged.

## Tests

- Direct `--brokers` with the OAuth flags and the env secret parses, resolves and builds client options.
- Over a context, a single OAuth flag overrides only its own field and `--no-tls` turns TLS off; with no flags the context is untouched. Removing the `--no-tls` overlay fails this test.
- `make helm-lint` passes. `helm template` with the new values renders `--insecure`/`--no-tls` args and `KAFKA_OAUTH_*` env with a `secretKeyRef`. With default values it renders neither.

author: vprusso
body:
Adds [[254,86,18]], a weight-28 cyclic generalized-bicycle code on x^127 - 1 built from a designed divisor ideal of degree 43. No tracked issue covers this.

At row weight 28 or lighter, the best distance on the board with n <= 254 and k >= 86 is 10, at [[228,86,10]] and row weight 12, against 18 here; allowing any row weight the board reaches 18 at row weight 30. Score kd^2/n reads 109.7 against 125.0 for the best of the 13 other entries at this blocklength, [[254,98,18]], so this is a corner rather than a better score. Nothing on the board dominates it, checked against origin/main at the time of filing.

Here m = 127 is prime, so the quotient fold has no proper divisor to act on and is vacuous; only the single-block ceiling binds, and degree 43 sits below where it bites. The single-block cyclic code has dimension 43, leaving 84 residues as its zeros with a longest consecutive run of 28, so the Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem bound puts the lightest single-block logical at 29 or above; a direct search confined to one circulant block at 12 seeds of 600,000 trials found nothing below 21. The orbit fold over every equal-orbit partition returns nothing lighter. The leak between the single-block kernels and k is 0.

Distance is a witness-backed upper bound, not certified. A 24-seed gate at 2,000,000 information-set trials per seed settled at 18. A single uninterrupted run of 8,000,000 trials, the depth the verifier itself reaches, reads 18. Every seed read 18. Both witnesses are in the JSON and were rechecked against H_X and H_Z (X at 18, Z at 18).

notes/254-86-18.md records the rest of the front this came from and how it compares.

author: team-litigation-lab
body:
Follow-up to [team-litigation-lab/Foundational-Training#208](https://github.com/team-litigation-lab/Foundational-Training/pull/208), which is merged. Two things: embed the resource links we hand the trainees, and close the `MONITOR_TOPICS` gap that PR left open.

## 1. Resource links open on the platform, not in a new tab

Everything the Training Guide hands the trainees — the activity instructions, the videos and the resource sheets — now opens in the **pop-out viewer** (the draggable pane with ⛶ Full screen and *Open in a new tab ↗*), so nobody loses the page they were on. Drive files and folders already did; this adds the rest of what we provide.

**`lvEmbedUrl`** (`js/ft-updates.js`) learned four more addresses:

| Link | Embedded as |
|---|---|
| Google Doc / Sheet | `/preview` |
| Google Slides | `/embed` |
| Canva design | `/view?embed` |
| Loom recording | `loom.com/embed/<id>` |

**`link_html`** (`build/curriculum/convert.py`) routes them through the viewer on import, so re-importing the Word guide keeps this. Its `EMBEDDABLE` list and `lvEmbedUrl` are the two halves of one rule and the comments say to keep them in step.

A Doc, Sheet, Slides deck or Canva deck is `data-kind="doc"` — it is read, not watched, so the viewer opens it at document proportions and without the *"do you want to watch this video?"* prompt. Loom is `video`.

**Migrated in place**, since the Word source is deliberately not in the repo: **57 links** — 31 in `trainer/curriculum.json`, 11 in `trainer/notes.json`, 15 in the reference `build/days/*.js`. Links that were **already** viewer links are untouched, so the diff is only the ones that changed. Each new one is titled from the guide's own words (the link's own text, else the nearest heading above it) rather than a raw URL.

Result in `trainer/curriculum.json` — 191 embedded, 17 left as plain links on purpose:

| | Embedded |
|---|---|
| drive.google.com | 160 (pre-existing, untouched) |
| canva.com | 15 |
| docs.google.com | 14 |
| loom.com | 2 |

## 2. What deliberately stays an ordinary new-tab link

- **Third-party tools the trainee has to go and use** — the typing and spelling tests (TypingClub, SpellQuiz, TypingTest, Spelling-Test), iLovePDF, the WinRAR download, the NPI registries (npidb.org, npino.com), the free HIPAA course and the Smart Advocate knowledge base. They are not resources of ours and most of them refuse to be framed.
- **The credentials document.** Never embedded, so log-in details never render inside the platform.

## 3. Credentials: nothing to remove

I scanned `trainer/curriculum.json`, `trainer/notes.json`, `trainer/cues.json`, `build/days/*.js` and `build/lessons/**` for credential values — `Password:`/`Username:`/`PW:` style lines, and high-entropy tokens near any of those words. **No credentials are in the tree.** Every place that wants them already carries the padlock note and a plain link out:

> 🔒 Log-in credentials aren't stored on the platform. Get them from the credentials document.

That is `convert.py`'s existing redaction (`CRED` / `CRED_HTML`), and the import still **fails** rather than write one. The 13 regex hits were all the hostname sitting next to the word "password" in the SOP text ("VAs are not permitted to alter this password. SMART ADVOCATE: https://app.smartadvocate.com/..."), not secrets. This PR adds one guard: the credentials document is excluded from embedding, so it can only ever open in a new tab.

## 4. `MONITOR_TOPICS` now covers all 18 days

`js/ft-tracker-rules.js` listed **16** classroom discussions (Days 1–16); the Lien Negotiator days had no monitoring entry. Now **18** — they close the programme and are monitored like the rest. `worker.js` imports the same file, so the page and the Worker grade against one list.

A trainer who already saved their own list in Admin → 📒 Monitoring Sheets → *Discussions and key points* (`settings:monitor`) **keeps it**: the 18 are the default, not an overwrite.

## Checks

Green: `check-site`, `batch-id`, `sso`, `gemini-keys`, `r2-docs`, `drive`, and the Worker `wrangler deploy --dry-run`; `requests`, `graded-calls`, `blueprint` and `practice-sessions` each on a freshly started server (that harness keeps its store in memory, so a second run on the same process fails on its own leftovers, not on the diff). Also verified in a browser that clicking a Canva viewer link opens the pane with `src=…/view?embed` and no fallback, and that `lvEmbedUrl` resolves Docs, Sheets, Slides, Canva, Loom and Drive while leaving TypingClub to a new tab — no page errors.

author: 0xmanhnv
body:
## What

Follow-up to the CLA check that was merged here. A security review found a bypass in its "Decide who must sign" step, fixed here.

**The hole:** in a pull request opened by an outside account, a commit linked to an allowlisted account (the maintainer or a bot) was accepted when its signature was verified. A signature proves only the *committer*, and the author e-mail is free text, so a contributor could set the maintainer's e-mail as author, sign with their own key, and skip the CLA.

**The fix:** the step judges each commit by the account the CLA action uses (author, else committer). If that is an allowlisted account, the commit counts only when the author AND the committer are both allowlisted AND the signature is verified; otherwise the check fails and names the commit. Steps now select pull request events by payload (`github.event.pull_request`), not by event name.

**Tests:** `.github/scripts/cla-scope.test.sh` extracts the step from `cla.yml` and runs it against 10 recorded commit lists (maintainer, bot and outside pull requests; forged author, forged committer, contributor-signed). The previous logic fails 2 of them. `cla-test.yml` runs the test on pull requests and pushes that change the workflow or the test (read-only token, `persist-credentials: false`).

Also documented in the workflow header: keep `cla` required on pull requests; in the merge queue it passes at once. The archived upstream action's replacement is planned in openctemio/openctem#2299.

Security: same model as before. The check runs in the base context and never checks out or runs pull request code; the test workflow runs the pull request's own copy on `pull_request` with `contents: read` only. Secret still needed: org secret `CLA_SIGNATURES_TOKEN` (fine-grained PAT, resource owner `openctemio`, repository access only `openctemio/cla-signatures`, Contents read/write).

body:
Core rules p.84 gives two options for lighting more than one source; this goes with option 2: "Extinguish all old light sources. Start a new timer with the fresh light source."

- **Per player:** when a player lights something new (panel or token right-click), their current light is **paused**: it keeps its remaining time and is shown as "Paused". Their list keeps two, the current light and the one last paused. This replaces the 3-per-player cap.
- **Per token:** lights remember the token they were lit on. Right-clicking a token that already has a light burning (the GM's or a player's) pauses it and starts the new one. Before this fix, the GM's right-click lit a second light and left the first running.
- These paused lights aren't out: no burn-out alert, and **Resume all skips them**. The GM can still relight one with its play button.
- GM gets "Bo paused Bo's torch". The old light dropped by a swap doesn't produce a false "removed".
- Code calls this state `setAside` to keep it distinct from an ordinary GM pause; the UI only ever says "Paused".

Commit 3 of the platform-neutral MCP plan; follows smith6jt-cop/KINTSUGI#67, which merged commits 1–2.

## Problem
Project state was written to `<project>/.claude_workflow/`. Every `ParameterLearningEngine` construction created that directory, `~/.kintsugi/` and both SQLite schemas, so read-only MCP tools (`get_learned_parameters`, `suggest_with_learning`, `get_learning_statistics`, the `kintsugi://learning/stats` resource) left files behind.

## Changes
- **`kintsugi.assist.state_dir.project_state_dir(project, create=False)`**
  - Reads use `.kintsugi/`, otherwise an existing legacy `.claude_workflow/`, and create nothing.
  - The first write renames `.claude_workflow/` to `.kintsugi/`. A rename already done by another process counts as success. Any other rename failure logs a warning and keeps writing to the legacy directory. If both directories exist, `.kintsugi/` is used and a warning is logged once.
- **`ParameterLearningEngine`**
  - `__init__` creates nothing; both databases and their schema are created on the first recorded parameters.
  - `project_db_path` is computed on each access, so cached engines follow a migration.
  - A legacy database without the `algorithm_version` column is upgraded when it is first read.
- **`WorkflowState`** uses the same state directory.
- **Project setup:** `kintsugi init` adds `.kintsugi/` to the project `.gitignore` once. Project scans skip `.kintsugi` and `.claude_workflow`.

**Breaking:** state moved from `.claude_workflow/` to `.kintsugi/`. Existing directories are read as is and moved on the first write.

## Code submission

- Parameters: [[n, k, d]] = [[216,112,4]]
- Tracks: unrestricted / weight-9plus (computed by the verifier from H and the layout)
- Distance confidence: X: upper_bound, Z: upper_bound

Family tag: other (a self-declared filter, never used for ranking).

### Checklist
- [x] One JSON file under `codes/`, conforming to `schema/code.schema.json`
- [x] Distance witness(es) included for each reported side
- [x] `python verify/qldpc_verify.py codes/216-112-4.json` passes locally
- [x] Construction and references filled in under `provenance`
- [x] Checked against the current board by exact fingerprint and WL signature, local-Hadamard images included: no equivalent entry

### What frontier does this advance?
- **unrestricted / any weight**: on the Pareto frontier — dominates [[225,104,3]], [[232,104,3]]
Score kd^2/n = 8.296, max check weight 12, locality class unrestricted.

Construction: Cornucopia code (Lu, Li & Deng, arXiv:2608.02773; block-convolutional CSS construction with the check matrices given in the Methods of arXiv:2610.19073): q=6, n=36q=216 data qubits in twelve 3x6 tiles L0..L5,R0..R5 plus nine 3x6 X-check and nine 3x6 Z-check tiles; HX=[A_(j-i)|B_(j-i)], HZ=[B^-1_(i-j)|A^-1_(i-j)] with the coordinate permutations A_p,B_p:(r,c)|->(rho(p,r),c+s[p]) on Z_3 x Z_6, row maps rho_A(0)=r+1, rho_A(1)=2r+2, rho_B(2)=r+1, rho_B(3)=2r+2 (identity otherwise), and column shifts sA=[4, 4, 3, 3, 0, 3], sB=[2, 0, 3, 1, 4, 3]. These shifts were found by a random shift search; the paper publishes instances only at q=7,16,25,29,49,64,79. Weight-12 checks, k=18q+4=112.

author: addieflips
body:
The first real run of the invoice dry run found two bugs, both in the harness. That is the dry run doing its job — before a send rather than after one — but it means the version currently on `main` reports nonsense and must not be relied on until this lands.

## 1. Every bill died on `invoiceEmailPlaceServer is not defined`

The lift list was typed by hand, copied from `nightly-invoice.test.js`, and `main` had since split **four** helpers out of the invoice body. The run reported *"0 bills would send"* — which reads as a fact about the book and was a fact about my list.

That is the extraction-list trap for the **thirteenth** time in this repo, and twelve hand-kept lists is enough: a list that must be edited whenever somebody else refactors will be wrong again.

**The closure is computed now** — start at `runInvoiceBatch`, add every name it calls that `functions/index.js` defines, repeat until nothing new appears. 26 functions, nothing unresolved.

`ensureToken` is held back by name and is the one that must never be lifted: the real one **writes** a portal token, and a dry run that edits the book by being looked at is not a dry run ([[RS-65]]).

## 2. Every bill fell back to the built-in wording

The script matched template names with a flattener of its own, which disagreed with the server's `tplNameKey` — so her templates sat on file and were never found. A second opinion answering about itself, which is the mistake this repo has been bitten by over the bins count and the put-into wording.

The closure brings in the real `findTemplateSnapByName` and `tplNameKey`, and `emailTemplates` is seeded into the fake database for them to read, so **the matching under test is the matching that ships**. The recorder only watches: it notes the name asked for and hands straight to the real function.

## Gate changes

Two checks **repointed, not weakened**. They asserted the script had its own matcher and its own dash-flattener — which it did, and which *was* the bug. The claim worth holding was never *"does it flatten dashes"* but *"is the matching under test the matching that ships"*.

New checks: the lookup is never stubbed here, the templates are seeded, the lift list is computed rather than typed, and `ensureToken` stays out of the closure.

## Checks

- **8 of 8 sabotages caught**, including handing the run the real database and letting `ensureToken` into the closure; `invoice-dry-run.js` byte-for-byte after each
- 28 checks in `invoice-dry-run.test.js`
- `npm test`: **9044 passed, 0 failed**

author: kevinch3
body:
## What

NicotinD now answers the [OpenSubsonic](https://opensubsonic.netlify.app/) API at `/rest/*`, so **Music Assistant** (via its OpenSubsonic provider) and any Subsonic app can use the library as a music server.

- **Settings → Subsonic apps**: create, copy and revoke per-app API keys, and see the connection details (server URL, username, where the key goes).
- **~45 methods**: browse (`getArtists`, `getArtist`, `getAlbum`, `getSong`, `getMusicDirectory`, `getIndexes`, `getGenres`), lists (`getAlbumList2`, `getRandomSongs`, `getSongsByGenre`, `getStarred2`), `search3` (including the empty-query full-library sync Music Assistant uses), `stream`/`download` with Range, `getCoverArt`, `star`/`unstar`, playlists CRUD, `scrobble` → listening history, `getSimilarSongs(2)`, `getTopSongs`, `getLyricsBySongId`. Podcasts, radio, bookmarks and shares answer empty.
- **XML and JSON**, form POST, `.view` suffixes, and Subsonic error codes (an unknown method is error 70, not a 404 page).

## Design

`/rest` is a **translator over `/api`, not a second library**. Each call runs in-process against the real routes as the key's owner (`internalUpstream` mints a short-lived JWT and calls `app.fetch`). Roles, hidden/in-flight suppression, feed eligibility, multi-artist credits and the transcode-cached stream therefore behave exactly as in the web app. Text search uses `LibrarySearchProvider` directly, so it never triggers a network (Soulseek) search.

**Auth**: revocable, hash-only API keys (`subsonic_api_keys`). The key goes in `apiKey=` or as the password in legacy `u=&p=`. md5 token auth is refused with error 41 because it needs a stored plaintext password.

**Stars**: a song star is a like, so it shows up in Liked Songs. Album and artist stars live in `user_starred_items`.

## Supporting changes

- `/api/library/albums`: `classification=any` returns every release type, and there are new `alphabeticalByArtist` and `byYear` orders.
- `songOrderBy` now ends every order on `s.id`, so paged walks are stable across ties.
- `check:route-auth`: a mount **outside `/api`** used to be counted but never audited. Each such mount must now be named in `NON_API_MOUNTS` with how it authenticates.

## Testing

- Unit tests for keys, the envelope (JSON and XML), the mapping and the upstream session cache. A route suite runs `/rest` over the real `/api` routes and a real file on disk. There are web component specs and a new e2e spec that creates a key in the UI and syncs and streams with it.
- `bun run verify` is green and the full `bun run e2e` passed (265 tests).
- **Real-client smoke test**: I booted a throwaway server and drove it with `py-opensonic` 10.4.1, the library inside Music Assistant's provider, over both GET and POST. Every method passed. This caught one bug that JSON assertions had missed: search returned albums without the required `created` field. It is fixed, and there is a regression test.

Docs: `docs/opensubsonic.md`, an index line in `docs/index/users-auth.md`, and `docs/api-routes.md`.

body:
Closes #616

Migration **0051** (the number was stated on the issue before building): origin/dev's highest is 0050 (sieges), 0049 is #545's, no open PR adds a migration, and #419 adds no 0051.

## What
The decayed coup average (flag `HARIMU_FAVOR_DECAY_ENABLED`, off) reads one citizen's settlements and spends for every settling citizen, and neither table had an index on `clerk_user_id`, so it was quadratic (QA2: 12 s at 3,000 citizens, 95 ms with an index). Two covering indexes:

- `idx_aurelle_settlements_user_settled ON aurelle_settlements(clerk_user_id, settled_at, favor)`: earned sum (by user), spend charge (`clerk_user_id = ? AND settled_at <= spent_at`, a range search) and the outer `DISTINCT clerk_user_id` (covering scan).
- `idx_aurelle_favor_spends_user_spent ON aurelle_favor_spends(clerk_user_id, spent_at, amount)`.

EXPLAIN on SQLite (real runtime schema): all four reads are `SEARCH/SCAN ... USING COVERING INDEX`, no table scan. Without the indexes the same query shows `SCAN aurelle_settlements` / `SCAN r` / `SCAN s` (control in the test).

## Files
- `drizzle/0051_favor_coup_indexes.sql` and `db/postgres/0051_favor_coup_indexes.sql`: the same two `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`. Indexes only: no table, no data change, nothing destructive; the computed table-count ratchet is unaffected (`tests/postgres-migration.test.mjs` alone: 8/8).
- `lib/aurelle.ts`: `aurelleFavorIndexes` (same statements) and `royalFavorAverageSql(decayAt)` (the coup's average SQL moved here from `lib/aurelle-coup.ts` so it can be tested; same text).
- `lib/db.ts`: creates the two indexes right after the Aurelle tables, so the runtime and the Postgres fixtures (built from the SQLite snapshot) have them.
- `lib/aurelle-coup.ts`: imports `royalFavorAverageSql`; `readFavorAverage` is now exported (QA2 tidy note).
- `tests/postgres-migration-guard.test.mjs`: the inventory assertion now also accepts an index-only migration (it required a table, INSERT or ADD COLUMN).
- `tests/favor-coup-index-616.test.mjs` (3 tests, plan-based, no timings): the two migration files equal each other and `aurelleFavorIndexes`, no CREATE TABLE; SQLite `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` index-backed (with the dropped-index control); PGlite with the real `db/postgres/0051` file applied (twice, so `IF NOT EXISTS` is proven), planner forbidden to seq-scan, plan uses both indexes and no `Seq Scan` (control: without them it seq-scans), and the query still runs. On the Postgres test backend the SQLite-plan test checks the fixture snapshot carries both indexes.
- `tests/favor-spend-decay-585.test.mjs`: follows the moved SQL.

## Flag off
Unaffected: no query text or result changes (indexes only; `royalFavorBalanceSql` and the flat coup query are untouched, and the existing tests that assert both pass).

## Tests run
favor-coup-index-616 (SQLite and Postgres backend), postgres-migration alone, postgres-migration-guard, favor-spend-decay-585, favor-decay-529, aurelle-coup, aurelle-integration, `aurelle.test.py`; eslint clean.

author: darcknight000
body:
### Related issues
## Issue 1: Accordion / Collapsible

Implemented both components in `Accordion.tsx`.

- `Accordion` accepts items with an `id`, title, content, and optional disabled state.
- It supports controlled (`value`) and uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) state. By default, only one item can be open; `multiple` allows several.
- `onValueChange` reports changes as a single ID or an array, depending on the mode.
- `Collapsible` provides the same controlled/uncontrolled choice for a single disclosure, with `onOpenChange` and a disabled option.
- Triggers use native buttons with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; panels are labelled regions and hidden when closed.

`Accordion.test.tsx` covers toggling, callbacks, controlled state, single-open behavior, and multiple-open behavior.

## Issue 2: ExternalLink for Explorers

Added `ExternalLink.tsx`.

- Defaults to opening links in a new tab and adds `noopener noreferrer`.
- Preserves any supplied `rel` values and avoids adding those protections when a link targets the current tab.
- Includes an optional decorative external-link icon, hidden from assistive technology.
- Updated `TransactionToast.tsx` to use it for transaction explorer links.

`ExternalLink.test.tsx` checks new-tab security attributes, preservation of `rel`, and same-tab behavior.

## Issue 3: Responsive Top Navigation

Added `TopNavigationBar.tsx`.

- Accepts a brand, navigation items, optional actions, and configurable accessibility labels.
- Supports active links, external links, explicit targets, and a configurable mobile breakpoint.
- Displays links inline on wide screens and behind an accessible menu toggle on narrow screens.
- Uses `ExternalLink` for external and `_blank` links, and cleans up breakpoint listeners.

`TopNavigationBar.test.tsx` covers desktop rendering, mobile menu interaction, active-link semantics, and secure `_blank` links.

## Issue 4: Toast Notification Provider

Added `ToastProvider.tsx`, exporting `ToastProvider` and `useToast()`.

- `useToast()` provides `showToast`, `dismissToast`, and `dismissAll`.
- Toasts support a message, optional title, `info`/`success`/`warning`/`error` variant, and per-toast duration.
- The provider supports a default duration and four screen positions. A duration of `0` keeps a toast visible until dismissed.
- Errors and warnings use assertive alerts; informational and success notices use polite status announcements.

## Summary

XAI-02 replaces the SHAP-surrogate explanation with an exact decomposition of the Tier 5 composite and evaluates it at the functionally grounded level (Doshi-Velez & Kim 2017) along the Co-12 properties (Nauta et al. 2023). Detection is frozen; the research questions are unchanged.

### Commits
| Commit | Content |
|---|---|
| `f0191ac` | XAI context report |
| `4492b88` | Phase 1: exact agent/feature Shapley, Alert Explanation Records |
| `fb7159b` / `9de7b4e` | Phase 2: METRIC 9 scorecard, surrogate docstrings |
| `ae8c7b7`, `d8cdc62`, `ea1e5bb` | Pre-registration + backfill amendments |
| `2b14011` | Phase 3: bounded 2023-25 KB backfill, retrieval wrapper |
| `0c2cfff` / `41c9746` | Exploratory FP rule (null) |
| `f89f445` / `700d7c3` | Phase 4: pre-registered triage |
| `f0f2253` / `1811dc9` | Phase 5: METRIC 8 refresh (SYNTHETIC) |
| `ee16c70`, `147cc1d`, `12aa383`, `720ebba` | Phase 6: deterministic narratives, dashboard |
| `e42bb14` | Phase 7: Chapter 4 figures |
| `b31c45a`, `e94c6ec` | Phase 8: report, Ch4 notes, stale-claims register, verified bib |
| `112d60f` | Scope decision: E8 removed; retrieval evaluated for integrity only |

### Headline findings
- **Exact attribution is faithful by construction** (efficiency residual ≤ 1.1e-16) and removes the score departure fastest (deletion AUC 0.06–0.17 vs 0.50 random).
- **The deployed SHAP surrogate was unfaithful:** R² −0.32 to −4.39 on the real test windows, deletion AUC at chance (0.49–0.59), same top agent as exact on 1–42% of alert days. Refitting on real data narrows but does not close the gap.
- **Diagnostic value:** the explanation layer exposed a defective retriever (region match 0.00 in 3 regions, duplicates 0.33–0.36, future-dated hits; fixed in the evaluation wrapper), a saturated market agent, and a label the detector's signals do not track (Hormuz).
- **No transferable trust signal:** explanation features did not beat the score for triage (LORO ΔAUC −0.10 to −0.50); Panama's agreement effect (AUC 0.89) reverses in Hormuz; FPs show no more conflict evidence than calm days (lift 1.07 [0.97, 1.15]).
- **METRIC 8 (SYNTHETIC):** hand-tuned 0.937 accuracy; optimized weights fall below the naive baseline (0.578 vs 0.797); the surrogate-driven badge never recommended rerouting.
- **Scope:** retrieval is evaluated for integrity (region, date, de-duplication), not relevance; no human study. `rag_annotation.csv` + `compute_precision_at_3.py` are kept for future human-grounded work.

### Not touched
`thesis/*.tex` and `DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md` are not edited; `STALE_CLAIMS.md` lists the places to revise. Generated CSV/JSON/figures are untracked (rebuild with `python eval/explainability/make_figures.py`).

### Tests
`pytest`: 513 passed.

author: gigurra
body:
## Background / Purpose

Backend for the operator-approved quick-start mock Q2 (tcl-52p3cq, epic tcl-9pgkho). The step list's "Who" picks one of: a specific agent, any member with role R, anyone in the run's scope (prefer idle), you, or a command. The mock also has a fallback for agent steps that no member can take, separate from the role: spawn with profile P (default: the group's default spawn profile), wait, or fail the step. It can be set once for the process and overridden per step.

Until now `Performer.Profile` was both the role matched against members and the profile spawned when `spawn: allowed`. Existing templates must keep working.

The JSON shapes were agreed with proc-ui-kit, which is building the UI (tcl-7p6bgt) against them.

## Implementation

- **Model** (`process/model`)
  - `Performer` gains `role`, `anyone` and `fallback {action: spawn|wait|fail, profile?}`. `Template` gains a top-level `fallback`, the process default for agent steps.
  - Validation (schema plus semantic):
    - agent-only fields
    - at most one of assignee/role/anyone
    - a known action
    - a profile only with spawn
    - no `spawn` together with `fallback`
    - inert-param warnings
- **Engine**
  - `AgentCommand` carries `Role`, `Anyone`, `FallbackAction`/`FallbackProfile`. `AgentCommandFor` builds it, and `AgentCommand.Fallback()` resolves it.
  - Precedence: step fallback, then legacy `spawn: allowed`, then template fallback, then wait. A legacy explicit `spawn: never` doesn't shadow the template fallback.
  - A template that uses none of the new fields binds exactly the command it did before. Commands are compared field by field against persisted checkpoints, so in-flight runs from before the upgrade still re-prepare cleanly.
- **Resolution** (`process_performers.go`)
  - `role` matches only that role. `anyone` admits every active member. Without either, `profile` is the role, as before.
  - Candidates are ordered idle, then online, then offline, and then by fewest open process dispatches ("least busy").
  - Fallback `spawn` uses the step's profile or the group's default spawn profile. With neither it waits, with a reason. `wait` waits. `fail` durably records a performer-less failed report on the dispatch row (`db.FailProcessAgentDispatch`), which the existing recorded-report path applies to the run as the engine actor, so retry and fail routing apply. Wait reasons describe role and anyone.
- **Preview**: `POST /v1/process/resolve-preview {template|source, group}` returns `{nodes: {id: {agentId?, name?, reason, spawnProfile?, waits?, fails?}}}` for agent task steps. A compound task's plan, check and review stages appear under their stage ids.
  - It is an effect-free dry run: no spawn authorization and no rate budget spent.
  - It is gated like the process context: an agent caller sees only its own groups. It is local-only for peer views.
- **Context**: `GET /v1/process/context` now lists every visible, non-archived group, even one without runs, with `defaultSpawnProfile` and `roles: [{role, count}]` (active members, counted in one joined query because the context is polled).
- **Full editor**: the node inspector gains role, "anyone in scope" and the fallback (action, plus a spawn profile field). The clipboard wire accepts the new fields.
- **Docs**: `docs/processes.md` ("Who performs the node") and the process-templates authoring skill.

Not here:
- an editor control for the template-level `fallback` (the Q2 step list owns that row, tcl-7p6bgt). The editor preserves the field.
- giving a spawned performer the step's `role`. It joins with its profile's role.

## Tests

- New flow tests through the daemon mux (`process_performer_selectors_flow_test.go`):
  - the role selector, with the profile ignored for matching
  - anyone: idle beats working, then least busy across two runs
  - a spawn fallback without a profile uses the group default, and waits with a reason when there is none
  - a process-default `fail` fails the run with a `fallback_failed` performer-less report; a step `wait` overrides a process `fail`
  - validation diagnostics through `/v1/process/validate`
  - resolve-preview (member / spawn / fail; agent steps only; unknown group 404) and context (group without runs, default profile, role counts)
- Existing Process/Route/Peer/asset suites in `agentd` and `go test ./pkg/claude/process/...` pass.
- JS: all 443 `process-*.test.mjs` tests pass, including the new mutator test and the updated pinned field list.

## Review

Cold review: a fresh in-harness Claude Code subagent (general-purpose agent via the Task tool, not a tclaude-spawned peer). It was given the diff, a review instruction and this Background / Purpose.

It found no high-severity issues. It confirmed:
- in-flight checkpoint command equality holds for legacy templates
- the `fail` path is durable, happens under the lock, applies once, and is attributed to the engine actor
- the preview and context visibility filters match

Findings:
1. A process fallback was shadowed by an explicit legacy `spawn: never` (medium). **Fixed** in afb288338: only `spawn: allowed` keeps precedence, and a test covers it.
2. The preview missed compound tasks' plan, check and review stages (medium-low). **Fixed**: they are previewed under their stage ids, with a test.
3. Polled context did N+1 reads for roles (low). **Fixed**: one joined query. Per-candidate busy counts in the preview remain; the preview is on demand, not polled.
4. `process.runs.read` holders (incl. group owners) now also see other groups' default profile, role counts and, via the preview, member names and status (low). **Deliberate**: it matches their existing all-groups run visibility.

author: sirkianmj
body:
packaging: PyInstaller desktop proof-of-concept (macOS)

## What

First proof that AeroGrid-XAI can be frozen into a self-contained
executable. No Python environment, no conda, no system libraries
beyond macOS itself.

Verified on macOS 26.6.2 arm64: the frozen binary starts, binds a
port, and answers three probes.

    GET  /health          -> 200  {"status":"healthy"}
    GET  /mission/state   -> 200  9719 bytes (Skyfield)
    POST /discovery/run   -> 200  7158 bytes (Z3)

Bundle size: 289 MB. Boot to first request: ~10 s.

## What this proves

The full scientific stack freezes and runs:
- numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1
- Z3 5.1.0 with its native libz3.dylib
- Skyfield 1.54 with its .npz ephemeris data
- FastAPI 0.115 + uvicorn 0.32
- The three TLE fixtures bundled under app/physics/data/tle/

## What this does not prove

- Not verified on Windows. The spec is macOS-specific.
- Does not produce a .app bundle. The output is a folder with an
  executable. Adding a BUNDLE() section is a follow-up.
- The SaaS layer (backend/app/saas/) still expects PostgreSQL and
  Redis. The three probes above do not touch it. Any /auth/* or
  /saas/* call will fail unless those services are running.
- No code signing. First launch triggers Gatekeeper.

## Files

    desktop_entry.py                     entrypoint
    packaging/aerogrid.spec              PyInstaller spec
    packaging/build_macos.sh             macOS build script
    packaging/requirements-desktop.txt   build-time deps
    packaging/aerogrid-icon-source.png   master icon (2048x2048, PNG)
    packaging/aerogrid.icns              derived macOS icon
    packaging/README.md                  packaging notes

.gitignore gains /build/, /dist/, /packaging/aerogrid.iconset/.

## The two packaging pitfalls, solved in the spec

Two dependencies are missed by PyInstaller's default analysis and
are collected explicitly:

- **Z3 native library.** conda-forge's z3-solver ships
  libz3.dylib in the environment's lib/ directory, not inside the
  Python package. collect_all("z3") only sees the Python package,
  so the shared library is added explicitly.

- **Skyfield ephemeris data.** Skyfield reads .npz files at runtime
  that PyInstaller does not collect by default. collect_data_files
  handles this.

Both omissions produce runtime crashes, not build-time failures.
Documented in packaging/README.md so a Windows port does not
rediscover them.

## Roadmap

Not tied to any roadmap sprint. Off-roadmap packaging work.

author: beatlayer[bot]
body:
## What changed

T56, WP-2.2 part 1: the saved MIDI input work, brought onto current `main` and folded into the routing model that WP-2.19 landed.

- **`bl-core`** gains `midi`: the short MIDI 1.0 messages, `MidiSource` (a port's ID, or the computer keyboard), `PortId` (an FNV-1a hash of the port's name), and the timed `MidiInputEvent` the device layer hands the engine.
- **The model.** A MIDI track's input, its channel, and its monitoring live in the track's routing, as `docs/specs/routing.md` has it. `Input` gains `Port { name }` (one input port, by the name the MIDI system gives it), `Routing` gains `channel: Option<u8>` (1 to 16, or `None` for All Channels), and `routing.set_input` takes the channel alongside the input, so choosing a port and its channel is one undo step. `routing.set_monitor` already existed and changes monitoring. There is no `Track::midi_input`, no `Track::monitoring`, and no `track.set_midi_input` or `track.set_monitoring`: the maintainer's answer on LB-91 folded them into routing. `Input` and `Routing` are no longer `Copy` (a port carries its name); the callers that relied on it now clone.
- **The engine.** `crates/engine/src/midi.rs`: the MIDI input stage. Each block takes messages off the lock-free queue, places each on the sample its stamp gives through the delay-locked block clock, and hands it to every MIDI track whose routing matches (source and channel), with whether the track monitors (its Monitor switch and its arm). A MIDI track's routing travels in the program, so a monitor or arm change recompiles; an input or channel change already did.
- **`bl-midi-io`**: the device trait (`MidiBackend`) with the midir, null, and test backends; `MidiPorts` with each port's Track, Sync, and Remote switches, and the lock-free input queue; `StampClock`, which maps a system's own stamps onto `Instant`s; and the computer MIDI keyboard's layout and state.
- **rtsan**: `rtsan/tests/midi_input.rs` runs the input path under RealtimeSanitizer.

Kept from the saved work: bl-core's messages, the engine's input stage and block clock, and bl-midi-io. Changed from the saved work: the saved `Track.midi_input`/`Track.monitoring` model and its `track.set_midi_input`/`track.set_monitoring` commands are gone, replaced by routing's, per the maintainer's answer. The saved tests are adapted to the routing commands.

## Acceptance points and the tests that prove them

| Acceptance point | Test |
|---|---|
| A message queued with a timestamp lands on the right sample in the next block | `crates/engine/tests/midi_input.rs`, `messages_reach_each_midi_tracks_input_by_source_and_channel_in_the_next_block` (messages 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 ms into block 0 land on frames 48, 96, 144, 192 and 240 of block 1); `a_message_stamped_after_the_block_starts_waits_and_a_late_one_lands_first`; `crates/midi-io/tests/to_the_engine.rs`, `a_ports_notes_and_the_computer_keyboards_reach_their_tracks_inputs` |
| Input reaches only tracks whose input matches | the same engine test: All Ins hears a port and the computer keyboard, a track on port "Keys A" hears only that port, a track on No Input hears nothing, and an audio track has no MIDI input; `crates/midi-io/tests/to_the_engine.rs`, `a_ports_notes...` (a port whose Track switch is off, or with only Remote on, reaches no track) |
| Monitoring In, Auto and Off behave as the spec says | `crates/engine/tests/midi_input.rs`, `input_and_monitoring_edits_reach_the_engine_and_undo` (In hears an unarmed track; a monitor edit reaches the engine and recompiles; undo restores) and `messages_reach...` (an armed track on Auto hears, one on Off does not); `crates/model/src/command.rs`, `a_midi_tracks_input_is_all_ins_or_a_port_with_a_channel`; the routing tests in `crates/model/src/routing.rs` |
| RT tests show no allocation or lock on the input path | every engine test block runs under the allocation trap (`bl_rt::rt_test!`); `crates/engine/tests/midi_input.rs`, `timing_jitter_with_a_real_time_audio_thread_and_a_midi_thread` asserts zero heap operations on the audio thread; `crates/midi-io/tests/to_the_engine.rs`, `timing_jitter_from_a_midi_thread_through_the_test_backend`; `rtsan/tests/midi_input.rs` under RealtimeSanitizer (CI's rtsan job) |

bl-midi-io's own tests cover the ports and their switches, the queue, the stamp clock, the computer keyboard, and the platform backend.

## `cargo xtask check --affected`

```
    ok  format
    ok  clippy
FAILED  tests
    ok  layers
    ok  ui parity reference
    ok  command reference
    ok  keymap
    ok  licences, advisories, bans, sources
    ok  deny self-test
    ok  private terms

Tests (--affected): Cargo.lock changed → testing every package (26 of 26)
1317 tests run: 1316 passed, 1 failed, 4 skipped
FAIL bl-cli::engine engine_smoke_recompiles_during_playback_without_dropouts
```

The one failure is the load-sensitive test the handoff lists: it expects more than 100 recompiles in a second while this shared Mac builds for other agents. Nothing on this branch touches it. CI decides.

`cargo xtask rtsan` needs LLVM 20's RealtimeSanitizer runtime, which isn't installed on this Mac, so the harness was type-checked under its `lspk_rtsan` cfg rather than run; CI's rtsan job is the first sanitizer run.

## Notes for the reviewer

- Two tests in the saved work needed a harness fix rather than a bound change. (1) `crates/midi-io/tests/to_the_engine.rs`'s timing test drove the engine blocks from the test's own thread and passed `Instant::now()` as the callback time, so it measured that thread's scheduling: 14 ms RMS of block-call lateness under this Mac's build load. It now passes the block's due time — what a device's callback gives — and measures 0.28 frames RMS, worst 0.6 frames, with the same bounds. Callback jitter itself is covered by the engine's two jitter tests, one simulated and one on a real-time null device. (2) The saved rtsan test named the old cfg (`bl_rtsan`); it now uses `lspk_rtsan`, as the rest of the harness does.
- `crates/shell/src/routing.rs` still lists All Ins and Computer Keyboard as `pending(WP-2.2)` and lists no ports: the choosers are T57's ("a MIDI track's MIDI From chooser and channel chooser in the In/Out section, fed by the ports"). The model, the commands and the engine carry them from this PR.
- The saved `docs/specs/midi-io.md` ended with two stray tool-output lines (`</content>`, `</invoke>`); they are dropped from the file below.

## Open questions

None that block this change. The decisions the task didn't settle were answered on the issue: fold the saved MIDI input into routing; a port stored by name; the channel rides on `routing.set_input` so one entry change is one undo step.

One reading to confirm: `routing.md` R16 gives the channel chooser as "All Channels with a port", so the model allows a channel only with a port input — a `routing.set_input` that pairs another input with a channel is refused, and a saved set that holds one doesn't load. If Live's channel chooser in fact applies to All Ins and the computer keyboard too, R16 and the model want revisiting; that's one of the spec's "To observe in Live" items.

## Docs changes for the maintainer

1. **New spec**: `docs/specs/midi-io.md`, the whole file below. R7 and R11 are rewritten to point at `routing.md`'s rules and commands instead of defining their own, as the maintainer's answer asked.
2. `docs/specs/routing.md`: R2's MIDI input list gains a port — "a MIDI track All Ins, the computer keyboard, one input port by name, another MIDI track, or nothing" — and R16's `(both disabled, WP-2.2)` and `(disabled, WP-2.2)` for the MIDI From entries, the port and its channel come off when T57 wires the choosers to the ports; the model, the commands and the engine carry them from this PR. R8's "a set saved before WP-2.19 loads with every track at its kind's default" already covers the new channel field.

author: ismaelosuna7824
body:
Space return rescan, focus-ring and Alt+F fixes, an all-day resource pass, and the ring as the default focus indicator. Task IDs and evidence are recorded in `odd/tasks/` (`fluidity.md`, `niri-feel.md` and the per-area records).

## Window management and visuals
- **SR-06**: returning to the managed Space rescans windows and observers before focus adoption and the reflow, so a window moved in from another Desktop is picked up.
- **NF-07**: floating windows get no focus ring (it could not follow their own moves).
- **SM-32/33/34**: Alt+F swaps the overlay faces instantly instead of crossfading. The ring fades with the layers at hand-off, and only the underlay draws the fill, so a shrinking window shows no dark block.
- **NA-05**: window-resize animations are off by default (instant). Settings has a switch to turn them on.
- **NF-08**: the ring is the default `[focus] indicator`. Configs that already set `"dim"` keep it.

## Resource use (PF-T..PF-AB)
- **PF-T**:
  - Snapshot sampling no longer converts the whole capture to another colour space. That was 12-25 ms and ~33 MB kept per capture.
  - Launcher icons are redrawn only for new or changed apps.
- **PF-U**: Gio never attaches an AX observer to its own pid (rule 4). Before, this happened while its main window was open.
- **PF-V**: typing captures wait for a 1.5 s pause and come at most every 5 s per window. Before, steady typing captured every 1-2 s.
- **PF-W**: title-change AX reads are coalesced to one per window per second.
- **PF-X**: the Screen Recording permission check is cached for 10 s. Each check is an IPC to tccd of ~8 ms.
- **PF-Y**: the IPC accept loop backs off on lasting errors instead of spinning.
- **PF-Z**: per-app reconciler state of reaped apps, and dim panels of displays that are gone, are released.
- **PF-AA**: focus-follows-mouse skips the window-list lookup while the pointer stays in the focused window.
- **PF-AB**: the hotkey event tap runs on its own thread, so a hitch on Gio's main thread no longer delays every keystroke and click on the Mac.

Measured:
- Release build at rest: 0.0-0.4 % CPU, ~0 wakeups per second.
- Footprint: flat at 65-67 MB.
- Debug live run under heavy use (357 hotkeys in 150 s, typing, clicks, launcher, overview, trackpad): 4 typing captures (318 in 79 min before PF-V) and no time spent in the permission check.

## Verification
- `swift test`, all bundles with 0 failures:

  | Bundle | Tests |
  |---|---|
  | UI | 312 (53 skipped) |
  | Session | 486 |
  | POC | 7 |
  | Mac | 19 |
  | MacOS | 98 |
  | Core | 1972 |

- Signed `xcodebuild` (Gio, Debug): BUILD SUCCEEDED.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Includes a merge of the current `dev` (PR #8). The suite above was run after that merge.

## Live checks still pending
- SR-06: move a window in from Desktop 2.
- NF-07: a floating window shows no ring.
- SM-32..34 and NA-05: Alt+F.
- PF-Z: change the display arrangement.
- PF-AA: with focus-follows-mouse on.
- NF-08: a fresh config shows the ring.

Already checked live: the tap thread (PF-AB), with keyboard and clicks normal and no `tap re-enabled` line in the log.

The Print section of `docs/mcp.md` said that File → Print writes the job as a print-ready PDF and that there is no printer driver. # Description

Go Tests fail on every pull request to `16.0-stable`: on the GitHub-hosted
runner, the `pkg/debug` test build's download of
`https://www.ezix.org/software/files/lshw-B.02.19.2.tar.gz` gets HTTP 403
(`failed to load cache key: invalid response status 403`). Every 16.0-stable
and 14.5-stable Go Tests run since at least 2026-10-12 has failed this way.
The same download succeeds from the self-hosted runners, which this branch's
build workflow and Go Tests on master and 17.0-stable already use.

This runs the Go Tests job on `zededa-ubuntu-2204`, with a Docker Hub login
using the runner's credentials as on 17.0-stable. It also sets `GH_REF`, which
the existing "Starting Report" step echoes but never defined.

## How to test and validate this PR

This PR changes only `.github/`, so Go Tests skip their test job on it. After
merge, re-run Go Tests on an open 16.0-stable PR (for example #6800) and check
that the `test` job runs on a `zededa-ubuntu-2204` runner and that `make test`
gets past the `pkg/debug` build.

## Changelog notes

None.

## PR Backports

- 17.0-stable: No, it already runs Go Tests on self-hosted runners.
- 16.0-stable: This PR.
- 14.5-stable: Same fix in #6810.
- 13.4-stable: No, its `make test` does not build `pkg/debug`.

author: jfdeev
body:
## Resumo

Trabalho complementar de Análise de Algoritmos: oito funções do Price-Watch reescritas para reduzir a classe de complexidade (ou, em F6–F8, discutir por que ela não muda), mantendo a mesma saída para toda entrada válida.

- O custo dominante do sistema é **I/O de banco e transferência entre back e front**, não laço em memória. As maiores mudanças são de idas ao banco (N+1 → lote) e de linhas lidas (tabela inteira → consulta indexada da fração usada).
- **Meta B:** cinco funções mudam de classe (F1, F2, F3, F4, F5).
- **F6 e F7** são analisadas e documentadas como melhorias que **não** mudam a classe. **F8** muda a classe só no melhor caso da entrada do contrato.
- **Equivalência:** cada função tem um teste que roda a versão original (preservada em `bench/legacy/`) e a nova sobre as mesmas entradas com semente fixa. Nas funções de banco o teste roda em Postgres real e compara também o estado final.
- **Medição:** scripts versionados medem tempo × n, consultas × n e bytes × n. Os gráficos (linear e log-log) estão em `docs/complexidade/graficos/`.
- **Comentários:** o código não tem nenhum; restam só diretivas de ferramenta. Verificação automatizada: `node scripts/check-comments.mjs`.
- **Relatório completo:** [`docs/complexidade/relatorio.md`](https://github.com/Jfdeev/Price-Watch/blob/feat/reducao-complexidade/docs/complexidade/relatorio.md).

## Tabela comparativa

| Função | Arquivo | O antes | O depois | Estratégia adotada |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 `searchProducts` → upsert dos produtos | `backend/src/services/productService.ts`, `productBatchUpsert.ts` | Θ(n) idas ao banco | Θ(1) idas (≤ 6 comandos) | lote: 1 leitura com `= ANY($1)`, 1 INSERT, 1 UPDATE e 1 INSERT de histórico via `jsonb_to_recordset`, numa transação |
| F2 `searchProducts` → produtos excluídos | `backend/src/services/productService.ts` | Θ(D + n) tempo, Θ(D) espaço | O(n log N) tempo, Θ(n) espaço | coluna `normalizedProductUrl` preenchida na escrita + índice `(isDeleted, normalizedProductUrl)` + consulta só das URLs da página |
| F3 `createProduct` | `backend/src/services/productService.ts` | Θ(S) | O(log S) no caminho de sucesso; Θ(S) no pior caso (erro de dono) | índice funcional parcial `lower(name) WHERE isActive`; `LIMIT 1` por igualdade; ILIKE original só como fallback |
| F4 `loadProduct` (favorito) | `frontend/src/pages/ProductDetailPage.tsx`, `favoriteService.ts` | Θ(F) tempo e bytes | O(log F) tempo, Θ(1) bytes | `GET /favorites/product/:productId` no índice único `(userId, productId)` |

## Responsáveis

| Aluno | Funções |
|---|---|
| João Felipe da Rocha Soares | F1, F7 |
| Vithor dos Santos | F2, F5, F8 |
| Paulo Ricardo | F3, F4, F6 |

## Mudanças de banco

- `20261014120000_add_normalized_product_url`: coluna `normalizedProductUrl` e índice `(isDeleted, normalizedProductUrl)`. **Depois de aplicar, rode `npm run db:backfill-normalized-url` uma vez** nos bancos já existentes.
- `20261014130000_add_store_active_lower_name_index`: índice funcional parcial `lower(name) WHERE isActive` em `Store`. É SQL manual; o `prisma migrate diff` confirma que o Prisma não o remove.

### Deploy no banco de produção (Neon)

As medições e os testes rodaram no Postgres local; nada foi aplicado no Neon. No deploy:

1. `npx prisma migrate deploy` com o `DATABASE_URL` do Neon (cria a coluna, o índice composto e o índice funcional parcial);
2. logo em seguida, `npm run db:backfill-normalized-url`. Sem isso, produtos excluídos antes da migration deixam de ser filtrados na busca;
3. recomendado antes de considerar a F3 equivalente em produção: confirmar o locale do banco no SQL Editor do Neon. A equivalência de `lower()` foi verificada só em `en_US.utf8`/libc (achado A3).

## API nova

- `GET /favorites/product/:productId` → `{ id, productId }` ou `null` (autenticado).
- `POST /favorites/lookup` com `{ productIds: string[] }` (até 100) → `[{ id, productId }]` (autenticado; lista inválida → 400).
- `GET /favorites` continua igual.

## Como testar

```bash
docker compose up -d postgres
```

O `npm run bench` da raiz já cria e migra `pricewatch_test`. Para rodar só os testes:

```bash
cd backend && npm run test && npm run test:equivalence && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run build
```

```bash
cd frontend && npm run test && npm run lint && npm run format:check && npm run typecheck && npm run build
```

```bash
npm run check:comments
```

## Como medir

Com o Postgres do `docker-compose` no ar e as dependências instaladas, rode na raiz:

```bash
npm run bench
```

O comando (`scripts/bench-all.mjs`):
1. cria os bancos `pricewatch_test` e `pricewatch_bench` e aplica as migrations;
2. roda os testes de equivalência;
3. mede F1–F8;
4. gera os gráficos e as tabelas.

Os CSVs vão para `docs/complexidade/dados/` e os PNGs para `docs/complexidade/graficos/`.

## Pontos de atenção para a revisão

- **F1:** duplicados de `externalId` na mesma resposta passam a seguir a semântica sequencial; o original dependia de corrida. A falha passou a ser tudo ou nada para a busca (o original isolava por produto). Ambos estão documentados (achados A12–A14).
- **F5:** a falha de favoritos continua derrubando a vitrine, inclusive para visitantes sem login. Isso foi preservado de propósito e registrado como provável bug (A1).
- **F3:** a ressalva de Unicode (`İ` e sigma final) está no achado A3.

author: egoist
body:
On Windows, every renderer (so every window) ran D3DCompile on the first draw of a `ui/shader` shader, and did it again on every launch: 0.14 s for a trivial shader, 1.2 s for `examples/wind/wind.kage` (WARP on windows-latest). Metal already avoids this with its disk cache.

## What changes

- `ui/shader`'s `Compile` calls the new `d3d11.PrecompileEffect` on Windows. It starts compiling the effect's pixel shader on a goroutine; up to NumCPU−1 compile at once. D3DCompile needs no device.
- All renderers share one entry per source (`effectCache`). A renderer that reaches the effect first compiles it itself or waits for the compile already running, so it waits only for what is left.
- The DXBC is kept in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MyGo\ShaderCache\<sha256 of flags + full effect source>.dxbc`. Files are checked for the DXBC magic and the size in the header, written through a temp file and a rename, and removed least-recently-used beyond 32 MB, so `mygo dev` edits don't pile up. There is one directory per user, keyed by content, the same way Windows' own D3DSCache works. A per-app directory would need `App.Name`, which isn't settled yet when shaders compile as package variables.
- The renderer reaches the cache through an atomic hook that only `PrecompileEffect` sets. Effects compiled ahead of time (glass) and apps that draw no shader don't link the cache.

## Measured (temp-runner, windows-latest, WARP; wind.kage, `RenderOffscreen`)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| first draw, 1st renderer, Compile right before, cold cache | 1.30–1.34 s | 1.32 s |
| same, 300 ms between Compile and draw | — | 0.83 s |
| same, 1.5 s between | — | 0.11 s |
| first draw, 2nd and 3rd renderer | 1.30 s each | 0.10–0.11 s |
| next launch (disk cache) | 1.3 s | 0.10–0.14 s |

The ~0.1 s that remains is not D3DCompile. CreatePixelShader of the cached 130 KB DXBC takes 8 ms. A 2×2 draw costs the same as a 224×108 one, so the time isn't spent shading pixels either. It is WARP compiling the DXBC on each new device's first draw (an empty scene's renderer costs 13–30 ms). That is driver work: real GPUs' drivers cache it in D3DSCache. Only sharing one device between windows would avoid it on WARP.

Compiling less doesn't help. The optimization level barely changes D3DCompile's time (wind: O0 1.23 s, O3 1.20 s; only skipping optimization reaches 0.43 s, with slower code). For a trivial shader, most of the 0.1 s is the renderer's head and tail (coverage, clips).

## Size (`-trimpath -tags mygo_noinspector -s -w`, production)

- counter-native and hello: byte-identical before and after, on Windows and macOS.
- wind on Windows: +15 KB.

Tests: `go test ./internal/gpu/d3d11 ./ui/shader ./plugins/glass ./examples/wind ./ui/...` pass on windows-latest. New tests: `TestEffectCache` (compiles once, same code as `CompileEffect`, recompiles a truncated file, reads a file on a later launch) and `TestTrimEffectCache`.

Docs: "Errors and cost" in docs/ui/shaders.md, and the Shaders entry in docs/architecture.md.

body:
Correct the recorded evidence and the numbers that describe the released commit.
`main` is at `cce9ba67` (`Release v0.6.0` run #10 succeeded). The four
intermediate commits this branch originally carried are already on `main`
verbatim — verified by SHA-256 against the contents API, not assumed — so what is
left here is everything that is still missing.

## `code/docs/GITHUB.md` (new)

The reproducible record of the issue, this pull request, the nightly dispatch and
what the CI logs say, with run ids next to every number.

* **`nightly.yml` has never passed.** Run #1 (`38778966871`) failed in 27 s: the
  `run:` block used `\\` for line continuations inside a YAML literal block
  scalar, so bash saw a backslash argument, the command ended at the first line
  and `run_diff.py` died with `the following arguments are required: --cli`. The
  `longrun` job passed 1 000 000 cases per property on both backends. Fixed in
  `cce9ba67`; a green dispatch has still not been observed.
* **The Node oracle had never run in CI.** `oracle_node_bytes.mjs` used a bare ESM
  `import { jsonrepair } from "jsonrepair"`, and the ESM resolver ignores
  `NODE_PATH` (CommonJS-only), so it only resolved when the package sat in a
  `node_modules` above the script. CI installs it under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, so the
  column degraded to `n/a (library not installed)` behind a printed note and
  every published `EVAL_INDEPENDENT.md` lost its third oracle, its 12 strict-oracle
  disagreements and an 8-file table. Fixed in `cce9ba67`; runs #21 (this branch)
  and #22 (`main`) are the first whose differential job logs `jsonrepair 144/188`.
* **Two sites remain open**, documented rather than fixed because the steps are
  not mine to change: `ci.yml` passes `--node-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/node-oracle/node_modules"`
  where the script wants the directory that *holds* `node_modules`, and
  `run_ambiguity.py` is invoked without `--node-dir` at all, so both of its
  reference columns are `n/a` in every run.

## `code/docs/RELEASE_READINESS.md` (new)

A release audit of `cce9ba67` from the run #18 and #22 artifacts, with an
explicit severity call and a cheapest-first fix list.

* **Three documents committed inside the release quote the previous revision.**
  `REPRODUCE.md` says 129 tests and 62 assertions where run #22 measured **170**
  and **77**; it quotes `2371/2661` = 89.1 % library coverage where the released
  commit measures **`2850/3063` = 93.0 %** (`3187/3907` = 81.6 % including
  bench); `TRACEABILITY.md` `NFR-TEST-01` still says `1378/1487` = 92.7 %.
  Coverage is a gate, so the stale line is the one that matters most: a reviewer
  cannot see from it whether the new 288-line `stream_readiness.mbt` is tested.
* **The baseline is stated rather than hidden:** 2 valid documents are repaired
  anyway (both R018), 23 of 188 invalid documents are refused, and the Node

* **The `FR-40` row is still missing** from `TRACEABILITY.md` (`FR-38` and `FR-39`

* §5 is a six-item cheapest-first list; item 1 is the doc corrections, item 2 is

Test count, assertion count and the coverage block now carry run #22's figures

author: hemant-mhalsekar
body:
This PR holds three releases: 11.3.5, 11.3.6 and 11.4.0.

## 11.4.0: Contact group of the new label set

The dashboard now has about 80 label chips (Complete PII Type List). This release covers the Contact group. The list's scope column is deliberately not followed: every type is labeled, including postal codes.

- **Phone numbers are split into two labels.**
  - `Indian Mobile Number`: 10 digits starting 6-9, with an optional +91 / 91 / 0.
  - `International Phone Number`: every other phone, including Indian landlines and toll-free numbers.
  - The country code and brackets are part of the label.
  - Non-Indian numbers are found for the first time: `+1 (415) 732-0198`, `+44 20 7946 0321`, `(11) 3456-7890`, `0812-3456-7890`.
  - A plain run of digits counts only right after a phone word (`Fax: 2345 6789`).
  - Dates, IPs, SSN, CPF, EIN, ZIP+4, CEP, card and Aadhaar numbers are excluded.
- **Postal codes are labeled** (`Postal Code`, `Indonesian Postal Code`, `Brazilian CEP`) when a key or a table / CSV column names the value.
- **Partial addresses count as Address.** A street on its own (`MG Road`, `Rua Augusta 1500`, `Jl. Sudirman No. 12`) is labeled, together with the place names that follow it on the line. A city, state, country or postal code alone is not an address.
- **The mistake check knows the new labels:**
  - A mobile labeled International Phone Number, or the reverse, is a mistake.
  - A phone labeled with the old `Contact Number` chip is a mistake, and the correct new label is shown.
  - A postal code labeled Address is shown as Postal Code.
- **All ~80 chip names are read.** Built-in chip colours are now used only for chips that are on the page.

## 11.3.6: labels that share a colour are not guessed
When several labels have (almost) the same chip colour, every possible label is judged:
- all wrong → a mistake (the badge names every possible label)
- all correct → fine
- mixed → marked "unsure" (amber dashed outline) and counted as not checked

## 11.3.5: "not checked" counts, link fixes
- The bar, tooltip, Alt+Shift+D diagnostics and popup show how many labels could not be checked: the check crashed, the colour could not be read, or the colour is shared. "0 mistakes" no longer looks like the all-clear when nothing could be checked.
- Links:
  - A link wrapped over several lines is recognised.
  - Brackets that belong to a link are kept in it.
  - An e-mail or IP address inside a labeled link is not labeled a second time.
  - A link followed by "." or "," is highlighted.

## Known limitation
On the live dashboard many chips share a colour: Contact Number, Indian Mobile Number and International Phone Number are all orange. The mistake check therefore marks most phone labels "unsure" rather than guessing. The proper fix is to read the label's name from the page instead of its colour. That change will come in a follow-up PR, once we have the page's HTML.

## Testing
- `node scripts/build.js` passed every suite:
  - 266/266 engine checks
  - 251/251 label checks and 238/238 deep label checks
  - 20,000/20,000 mass-generated cases
  - 90/90 new Contact checks (`tests/contact.js`)
- DOM suites: 12/12, 6/6, 79/79 label check, 11/11 Chrome colours, 3/3 extension.

## Notes for reviewers
- The logic is in `src/content.js`. `extension/content.js` and `dist/*.js` are generated copies of it.
- Older tests changed in a few places, because the rules changed:
  - "Contact Number" expectations now use the two new phone labels.
  - "MG Road" is now an address.
  - "Pincode: 560038" is now a Postal Code.
- The rules for these labels are written up in GUIDELINES.md (sections 5.5 and 5.9).

author: malstrom72
body:
`finalize` now fills the data stack, from the end of the globals up to the zero guard, with `0xDEADBEEF`. A local that is read before its first write then gets an obviously wrong value instead of whatever the memory held, which was usually 0 from the host's buffer, or, since #120, stale copies of the constants at the top of the stack.

This is not a promise to programs. A local's value before its first write stays unspecified; the poison is just how this implementation exposes the bug. Zeroing was considered and rejected because it hides such bugs. It costs one pass over the stack per assembly and nothing at run time.

**It already found two.** Running the 26 Permut8 firmwares in `tests/impala/golden` through `tools/runPermut8Firmware.sh`, with and without the poison, changes the output checksums of two of them. A probe build that reports reads of a still-poisoned slot points at uninitialized locals in their sources:
- `miditest_code.impala`, `process`: `j` is never set, only `j = j + 0x10000`, and read in `t^(t-j)`.
- `FFTTest_code.impala`, `process`: `a` is never set, only `a = a + (targetA - a) * rate * 0.1`.

Both used to read 0 by luck. The other 24 firmwares give identical checksums. The build passes: unit tests, the Impala suite and the bounds sweep don't depend on the initial stack contents.

**What the stack held before, per host.** GAZL never wrote the data stack, so it started with the host's buffer. Since #120 the top words of the stack also hold stale copies of the constants.
- **GAZLCmd** (tests, the firmware harness): static arrays, so 0.
- **Permut8 firmware host:** a member array of a freshly `new`-ed machine, created per firmware activation, songs and third-party firmware included. It is not initialized: heap contents in release, `0xCD` in MSVC debug. Stack words from one call stay visible to the next until the next firmware load.
- **Prawn OS / about box:** `new Value[]`, not initialized. Same as Permut8: heap contents in release, `0xCD` in debug, fresh per launch.
- **MidiGAZL** (Synplant 2.5 MIDI scripts): a `std::vector<Value>`, so zeroed, freshly on every assemble.

So on Permut8 and the Prawn OS, a firmware that reads a local before writing it already sees heap garbage. Poisoning makes that deterministic rather than introducing it, and old songs can't have relied on a particular value there. MidiGAZL is the one host where a script could rely on zeros today; a MIDI script that reads a local before writing it would change behaviour. If that is a concern, the alternative is poisoning only in debug builds (`#if !defined(NDEBUG)`).

`miditest_code` and `FFTTest_code` are test fixtures, here and in the permut8-firmwares-sdk repo under `GAZL/tests/impala/`, not shipped firmwares as far as I can tell.

After: 8 bars in the first 8 rows. Same database, 10 km area, first page: 29 ms mixed vs 22 ms unmixed. ## Against the canvas The whole-app canvas ([KRE17t8L8SC8f4M4KFLgZe](https://claude.ai/artifact/KRE17t8L8SC8f4M4KFLgZe)) Discover page was updated for this decision first: `disc-list`, `disc-desk-browse`, and the chips on `disc-map`, `disc-map-close`, `disc-map-opt-c`, `disc-map-opt-d`, plus a green decision note. | Drawn element | Status | |---|---| | Rows from different bars, one per bar first | Built | | Mixed / Nearest switch right of the heading, Mixed by default | Built (ds `Segmented`, pill, as radios) | | Nearest only when there's somewhere to measure from | Built | | Reason tag "New" / "Zero-proof" in the accent | Changed: sits in the row's existing tag slot after the bar line (where "Past ·" tags go), not right after the name, so a row never has two tag places. Needs your OK. | | Phone map sheet: Nearest chip while browsing | Built (Jest); not driven on a phone map in a browser or simulator | | "the classic spec" text on the bar line | Unchanged | ## Gated Adds migration `20261028100000_discover_mixed.sql` (replaces `discover_list`: new signature, same grants as before, authenticated and service_role, not anon). Needs the `human-approved` label. - It was `20261025100000` until #654 took that slot for `item_private_notes`; renamed on 15 Oct to sit above every migration on main (first to `20261025200000`, then to `20261028100000` after #677 and #671 landed newer ones). Main is merged in (no rebase), and Discover keeps main's "Not had yet" filter alongside the mixed list. - **One SQL fix after the first rename (2095d52):** the new `discover_list` had been written from `20261019200000` and missed the hidden-bars filter that `20261020200000` added, so bars a person hid came back into their drinks list (CI's `hidden-bars` test caught it). The filter is restored word for word: a hidden bar's drinks stay off the list except on its own page. ## Checks - Fresh isolated stack: every migration applied. `discover-index`, `discover-drinks`, `discover-near-me`, `discover-ranking` tests: 45 pass, including a new one for the mixed order, paging by place, totals on the first page only, and Nearest never mixed. CI's full security suite runs on the current head. - `lib/discoverDrinks.check.ts`: the place cursor and the reason rules. Jest `components/screens/home`: pass. Typecheck, lint (0 errors), design ratchet, migration order: pass (re-run after merging main). ## Known limits - Mixed measures distance from the area's middle, which the app rounds to about 1 km, so within the first band a bar a block from you can sit a few rows below one 0.3 mi away. Nearest is the exact closest-first view. - The place cursor is a position: a drink added between two pages can shift the next page by a row (`ponytail:` in the SQL). - Not run on iOS or Android; the change is a list header and the server order. ## Next Option B (shelves) is #682, stacked on this one. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01DKaa7ny2kxdJSEsNMrrPcD

author: runyaga
body:
Onto main 2244b44 (#38's squash). Third of three probe PRs for the M3 target.

Each probe or case is mapped through `core_also`; the core run runs them on vm, dart2js and dart2wasm:
- `sp_dump_version_window` (snapshot_version_window): an idle dump and a suspension's dump, with the format version (the u16 after the `MONTY\0` magic) patched to 13, 12, 8 (the 0.0.23 baseline's), 14 and 65535. Only 13 loads. The others are refused with the version window in the message, and the session runs on. This goes through both `load_session` and `load_snapshot`.
- `sp_fixed_offset_timezone` (sandbox_timezone): a fixed-offset `TimeZone` (named, unnamed `UTC+hh:mm`, zero, -86399, an empty name, an IANA-looking name) drives the local clock, `astimezone()`, `tzname`, `time.timezone`, `%Z %z` and the date. An IANA name (`Asia/Kolkata`) resolves with its rules. An offset of a day and an unknown name (`Mars/Olympus`) are refused at checkout, and only the zone check's own refusal, with its text, counts. The row also maps the worker engine's named-zone value cases (`w_tzdb_*`, `worker.also`), but not `w_tzdb_unknown`, whose local-refusal rule does not compare the refusal's text.
- `sp_input_resource_failure` (execution_input_errors): an input over a 70 KB memory limit, nested in a list too, converts. The feed's code starts (it prints first), and then the limit's first check fails the feed with MemoryError (byte counts normalised, structure kept). In 1.1.0 the import path (`object_bridge.rs` `import_node`) allocates without a resource check, so `InvalidInputError`'s resource arm is never produced from a binding's input: the probe pins the behaviour a binding can reach. Upstream keeps the failed input on the heap, so the next feed fails the same way; a small input runs on the next checkout. The probe has its own pool, for the reason below. The row also maps `sp_oversized_input` (`session_also`) and `w_refuse_surrogate_in` (`worker.also`).
- Cases `vf01_repr_numbers`, `vf02_repr_text`, `vf03_format_spec`, `vf04_str_containers`, plus the existing `v_repr` (value_formatting): repr of floats, ints, complex, strings and bytes; format specs; str of containers and singletons; output-only placeholders.

Finding, shared by upstream and core (not a divergence): a worker that served a type-checked session keeps about 3.3 MB of checker state across Reset, and a later session's `max_memory` counts it. With a 70 KB limit, every feed then fails with MemoryError. Upstream pydantic-monty with `max_processes=1` does the same as core. The core run executes probes in sorted order on one shared worker, so `api_reset_type_checker` ran first and the input probe diverged until it got its own pool.

Expected outcomes come from the oracle (pydantic-monty 1.1.0, CPython 3.12): `check_expected.py --write`, with `b11fs_unlink_dir` restored and the manifest recomputed.

**Target** (measured locally at core main 81d96ec; all three engines on vm, dart2js, dart2wasm): 107/123, 103/121, 103/121 (15 failing) -> **111/123, 107/121, 107/121 (3 failing)**. The 3 remaining cells are `install_dependencies`, which needs the core `installDependencies` PR (TGT1 B). `--assert-current` passes.

Checks: `test_target.py`, `test_gate.py`, `check_parity_manifest.py` pass. `dart analyze --fatal-infos` is clean.
