Fixes #103

<!-- issue: Measured catalog figures are hand-written in source and docs, so every type PR conflicts with every other -->

Builds on #115 (measured figures written into stats.json), #171 (per-type default sizes read from stats.json), #84, #146, #57, #45, #30 and #26, which each named #103 and are merged. Those moved the measured figures. What was left of the issue is the one shared table still edited by hand on every type PR, `PRODUCT_TYPE_LABELS` in `type_labels.py` (added by #336), and the numbered steps of `docs/adding-a-type.md`.

## What changes

- `TypeSpec` gains `label`. `type_labels` hooks `typespec.register` (`typespec.on_register`, the slot pattern of `brand_mark.use_marks`): the hook writes it into `PRODUCT_TYPE_LABELS` (now a `RegistryTable`) and refuses a key labelled both there and on a spec. Core imports no domain, so `CORE_EDGES` stays at 19. The older types keep their table entries, so a new type adds a module and no line of a shared file.
- `docs/adding-a-type.md`: the steps of "A new type" are named items (`- **Module.**`, `- **Block.**` ...) not a numbered list, and references to a step are by name, so an inserted step renumbers no neighbour.

Left to CI: the whole suite, golden catalog included. Prior art on this branch: an earlier agent died of an out-of-memory crash with a mutant still applied in `core/typespec.py`; that edit was discarded and is not in the diff (`git diff origin/main --stat` lists the intended files only).

author: bruderj15
body:
Existing shipping APIs accept typed profiles, defaults and listing delivery pushed by the Shopify app, WooCommerce plugin and external non-native producers. Producer repositories own acquisition and mapping. Backend shipping uses the authorized listing source and enabled provider method; it accepts/stores no provider domain and makes no provider HTTP requests.

Profile creation/replacement uses the existing POST/PUT commands. The existing profile list supports an authenticated producer's `objectKey` filter for stable identity recovery. Request metadata separates resource identity, exact retries, acquisition order and explicit observation windows.

Each record commits its assertion and required signals atomically. Manual assertions and clears remain protected; imported components expire independently. Existing source/configuration and authorization changes automatically fence old work. Fresh observations can refresh unchanged terms without semantic events; missing catalog listings remain retryable dependencies.

The migration upgrades stored delivery configuration to `LISTING_DELIVERY_V2`, removes obsolete shipping-domain columns/metadata and preserves listing identity/revision. Immutable historical events retain strict decoding of their prior protocol; their obsolete domain metadata is discarded from the domain model. OpenAPI, changelog, owning contracts and executable producer fixtures describe the same input-only native shipping model. The deployed route catalogue matches the shipping epic baseline.

Validation: focused Rust/PostgreSQL/API/queue tests, including both native producers without domain configuration and the V1-to-V2 persistence upgrade; workspace check and strict Clippy; formatting and dependency rules; infrastructure checks and dev/prod CDK synthesis. TypeScript and PHP clients generate successfully, and canonical fixtures type check against the generated TypeScript models.

Closes #2065

author: robot-head
body:
Fixes #1341.

## What changed

Part of #1341 was already on `main` when this work started (`metadata_last_applied_timestamp_ms`, `metadata_last_applied_lag_ms`, `pending_record_processing_time_us_{avg,max}`), but those gauges departed from Kafka's semantics and were not documented. This PR:

- **Makes the lag match Kafka** (`crates/broker/src/broker/gauges.rs`). `metadata_last_applied_lag_ms` is now the sample time minus the applied append timestamp on **every role**. Before, the active controller was forced to `0`, and so was any node that had not yet applied a record. The new values follow Kafka's `BrokerServerMetrics` reading `MetadataProvenance.EMPTY` (`-1, -1, -1`): before the first record, the offset reads `-1`, the timestamp reads `-1` and the lag reads `now + 1`. The lag is not clamped, so clock skew can make it negative, as in Kafka.
- **Adds `metadata_last_committed_offset`**, the counterpart of `KafkaController.LastCommittedRecordOffset`. It reads `MetadataSource::quorum_committed_offset`, which is `-1` before anything is heard.
- **Splits the derivation into a pure step.** `AppliedRecordGauges::derive(ReportedProgress, now_ms)` makes the clock a parameter. The sampler passes the wall clock and the tests pass a fixed value.
- **Docs**:
  - a new "Metadata quorum health" section in `docs/operations/metrics.md`, which also covers the `raft_*` and `metadata_*` gauges that were missing from the table
  - a `KrabkaMetadataStale` alert: lag above 30 s, guarded on `timestamp > 0`, for 2m
  - a paragraph in the `metadata-quorum-loss` runbook
  - a narrower KIP-835 note in `api_catalog.rs` and `docs/KIP_MATRIX.md`
- `metrics-body.txt` is regenerated.

### Kafka 4.3.1 → krabka mapping

The Kafka side comes from 4.3.1 source: `QuorumControllerMetrics.java`, `ControllerMetadataMetrics.java`, `MetadataLoaderMetrics.java`, `server/.../BrokerServerMetrics.java` and `KafkaRaftMetrics.java`. krabka exports one series per value for every role. Kafka splits each value between `broker-metadata-metrics` and `KafkaController`.

| Kafka metric | krabka series | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `broker-metadata-metrics:last-applied-record-offset`, `KafkaController:LastAppliedRecordOffset` | `krabka_broker_metadata_last_applied_offset` | existing |
| `KafkaController:LastCommittedRecordOffset` | `krabka_broker_metadata_last_committed_offset` | **new** |
| `broker-metadata-metrics:last-applied-record-timestamp`, `KafkaController:LastAppliedRecordTimestamp` | `krabka_broker_metadata_last_applied_timestamp_ms` | existing; now `-1` before the first record |
| `broker-metadata-metrics:last-applied-record-lag-ms`, `KafkaController:LastAppliedRecordLagMs` | `krabka_broker_metadata_last_applied_lag_ms` | existing; **semantics fixed** (leader no longer 0, `now+1` before the first record) |
| `broker-metadata-metrics:metadata-load-error-count` | `krabka_broker_metadata_load_error_count` | existing |
| `BrokerMetadataListener:MetadataBatchProcessingTimeUs` (Mean / Max) | `krabka_broker_pending_record_processing_time_us_avg` / `_max` | existing; mapping documented |
| — (krabka-only: committed − applied) | `krabka_broker_metadata_lag_records` | existing |
| `raft-metrics:current-state`, `current-epoch`, `high-watermark`, `log-end-offset`, `number-of-voters`, `number-of-observers` | `krabka_broker_raft_*` | existing; now documented |
| `broker-metadata-metrics:metadata-apply-error-count`, `KafkaController:MetadataErrorCount` | — | not exported: `MetadataImage::apply` is infallible, and a controller stops on a replay fault instead of counting it |

**For #1392 (recovery deadlines):** use `krabka_broker_metadata_last_applied_lag_ms` together with the guard `krabka_broker_metadata_last_applied_timestamp_ms > 0`. On a healthy node with the default `metadata.max.idle.interval.ms=500`, the lag stays near 500 ms plus the commit delay plus up to one `--gauge-poll-interval` (1 s). For a record-count bound, use `krabka_broker_metadata_lag_records`, which equals `metadata_last_committed_offset − metadata_last_applied_offset`.

### Left open
- `ControllerEventManager:EventQueueTimeMs` / `EventQueueProcessingTimeMs`, plus `TimedOutBrokerHeartbeatCount`, `EventQueueOperations*Count`, `NewActiveControllersCount` and `MetadataLoader:CurrentMetadataVersion`/`CurrentControllerId`/`HandleLoadSnapshotCount`. These live in the same Kafka classes but are not KIP-835 metrics, and krabka's engine loop has no `ControllerEventManager` queue to time directly. They can be a follow-up issue if wanted.
- The lag is computed when the gauge is sampled, not at scrape time, so it can read up to one poll interval low. This is documented.
- `aspect generate-kip-matrix` could not run here: fetching the pinned `krabka-io/tooling` archive returned 403. I hand-applied the KIP-835 row in the generator's format, with test links as `[path::fn](../crates/path)` and the note copied verbatim from `api_catalog.rs`. If the docs job disagrees, I'll fix it.

## Why

Operators need KIP-835's time-based staleness signal, and it has to mean what it means in Kafka. Before this PR, an active controller always reported a lag of 0, even when it had stopped appending `NoOpRecord`s, which is the exact failure KIP-835 exists to catch.

## Checks

- [x] `cargo test -p krabka-broker --lib -- broker::gauges::tests`: 6 passed, including the new table-driven `applied_record_gauges_follow_kafka_units_and_initial_values`. Also `active_controller_lag_is_sample_time_minus_the_applied_append_time`, which drives a real single-voter controller apply and samples it at fixed clock offsets of 0 / 250 / 60 000 ms, comparing the whole gauge struct.
- [x] `cargo test -p krabka-broker --test metrics_contract`: 5 passed, with `metrics-body.txt` regenerated through `KRABKA_METRICS_BODY_OUT`.
- [x] `cargo test -p krabka-broker --lib -- api_catalog`: 38 passed.
- [x] `cargo clippy -p krabka-broker --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean, with no `#[allow]`.
- [x] `cargo +nightly fmt`
- [ ] `bazel test //...`: not run locally (disk/time); CI covers it.
- [x] Tests use `assert2` and exercise behavior.
- [x] No persisted format touched.
- [x] KIP-835 semantics now match Kafka 4.3.1 source.

author: basiltt
body:
## Summary

The SR-122 end-to-end no-token-in-logs test applied only 3 of the 5 `cv-*` secret-shape rules in
`.gitleaks.toml`, so an invite-token-shaped string or a `recovery_codes=[...]` list in the captured
logs went undetected (found while closing out #2103). This lists all five ids in `_SHAPE_IDS` and
adds a parametrised guard that fails when `.gitleaks.toml` gains a `cv-*` rule the tuple does not
list. Test-only: one file, +18/-1 lines, no production code, no edit to the security-owned
`.gitleaks.toml`.

## Related issues

Ticket key: none (QA gap issue filed from the E09-Q06 roll-up #297; no `E*.json` entry)

Closes #2594

Related: Refs #2103 (the SR-122 test itself, In Test; this PR does not close it) and roll-up #297.

## Ticket brief checklist

- [~] I read `## Agent execution brief` — N/A, the issue has no brief; I read `Context` and `Done when` in full and recorded the DoR in the issue (comment "DoR for #2594")
- [x] Repo paths I touched match the ticket; nothing outside `services/api/tests/security/auth/test_no_token_in_logs.py` changed
- [x] No interface changed (test-only)
- [~] I ran every command listed under "Commands" in the brief — N/A, no brief; I ran the `AGENTS.md` §4 backend commands for the touched code (see Test plan)
- [x] The issue's `Done when` criteria are all met (table below); the issue lists no "Do NOT" items
- [~] `blocked_by` tickets — N/A, none (the test and the five rules are already on main)

## Type of change

- [ ] `feat` — new capability
- [ ] `fix` — defect repair
- [ ] `perf` — performance
- [ ] `refactor` — no behaviour change
- [ ] `docs` — documentation / ADR
- [x] `test` — tests only
- [ ] `build` / `ci` / `chore` — tooling, deps, pipeline
- [ ] `security` — security fix or hardening
- [ ] **Breaking change**

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion (issue `Done when`) | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `_SHAPE_IDS` lists all five `cv-*` rule ids from `.gitleaks.toml` | `test_no_token_in_logs.py:39-45`. `pytest tests/security/auth/test_no_token_in_logs.py` gives 6 passed (the main test plus one guard case per rule). Before the change, with the guard added and the tuple untouched, the same run gave 2 failed (`[cv-invite-token]`, `[cv-recovery-code]`), 4 passed |
| A parametrised check in the same module fails if `.gitleaks.toml` gains a `cv-*` rule that `_SHAPE_IDS` does not list | `test_leak_check_applies_every_gitleaks_cv_rule` (`:309-311`) is parametrised over the `cv-*` ids read from the toml (`_gitleaks_cv_rule_ids`, `:79`). Mutation 1: drop `cv-invite-token` from the tuple, 1 failed (`[cv-invite-token]`), 5 passed. Mutation 2: make the toml gain a rule (in memory, `cv-probe-new-rule`), 1 failed (`[cv-probe-new-rule]`), 6 passed |
| Mutation evidence: an injected invite token and an injected recovery-code list each turn the test red | Table below: both stay green with the 3-id tuple and go red with the 5-id tuple |
| Test-only, about 7-20 LOC; PR body says `Refs #2103` | `git diff --stat`: 1 file, +18/-1. `Refs #2103` is in this body; #2103 stays In Test |

Mutation probes. Injection: a throwaway pytest plugin (kept outside the repo, not committed; source in the
details block below) wraps `SessionService.refresh` and emits one structlog event with the synthetic value on
every `/auth/refresh` call, i.e. inside `capture_logs()`. Target:
`test_login_mfa_refresh_stepup_never_log_a_credential`. Values are built at runtime.

| Injected value | 3-id tuple (main) | 5-id tuple (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| none (control) | pass | pass |
| `cvs_` + 44 hex (control, shape already applied) | FAIL | FAIL |
| `cvi_` + 44 hex (invite token) | pass, missed | FAIL, hit `shape:\bcvi_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{` |
| `recovery_codes=['ABCDE-...', ...]` (the 5-5 shape the rule defines) | pass, missed | FAIL, hit `shape:(?i)recovery[_-]?cod` |
| `recovery_codes=[3 codes from generate_recovery_codes(), none consumed by the test]` | pass | pass, see Observations |

<details><summary>Probe plugin and commands (not committed)</summary>

```python
# hw1_probe_plugin.py
import functools, os, secrets
from typing import Any
import structlog
from candleviewer.auth import session_service as ss
from candleviewer.auth.recovery_codes import generate_recovery_codes

_MODE = os.environ.get("HW1_PROBE", "none")

def _detail() -> str | None:
    body = secrets.token_hex(22)  # 44 alphanumeric chars
    if _MODE == "session":
        return "cvs_" + body
    if _MODE == "invite":
        return "cvi_" + body
    if _MODE == "recovery5":
        return "recovery_codes=['ABCDE-" + "FGHIJ', 'KLMNO-" + "PQRST']"
    if _MODE == "recovery_real_other":
        return f"recovery_codes={generate_recovery_codes(3)!r}"
    return None

_orig = ss.SessionService.refresh

@functools.wraps(_orig)
async def _refresh(self: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
    detail = _detail()
    if detail is not None:
        structlog.get_logger("hw1_probe").info("probe", detail=detail)
    return await _orig(self, *args, **kwargs)

ss.SessionService.refresh = _refresh
```

```text
cd services/api
HW1_PROBE=invite PYTHONPATH=<dir with the plugin> .venv/bin/pytest \
  tests/security/auth/test_no_token_in_logs.py -k never_log_a_credential \
  --no-cov -p no:randomly -p hw1_probe_plugin -vv
```

Mutation 2 used a second scratch plugin that appends `{"id": "cv-probe-new-rule", ...}` to the `rules`
list returned by `tomllib.loads` for `.gitleaks.toml`, so the toml on disk is never edited.

</details>

### Test plan

Run from `services/api` in the worktree venv (local Python 3.14, CI uses 3.12):

- `pytest tests/security/auth/test_no_token_in_logs.py --no-cov` gives 6 passed.
- `pytest tests/security/auth/ --no-cov` gives 113 passed, 1 deselected (the directory I touched; the whole backend suite is left to CI).
- `ruff check .` clean; `ruff format --check .` 1218 files already formatted (the CI command); `black --check` on the touched file clean. `black --check .` lists 19 untouched, pre-existing files here (black 26.5.1); none is in this diff.
- `lint-imports`: 76 kept, 0 broken.
- `mypy --strict` on the touched file reports one error at the existing `_collect(logs, ...)` call (`capture_logs()` returns `list[MutableMapping]` under structlog 26.1.0). It is identical on main's copy of the file, and CI type-checks `candleviewer` only (`_job-py.yml:70`). Not touched here (no drive-by edits).
- Semgrep `security/semgrep/auth`: 10 rules, 0 findings (no rule targets `tests/`, so the file matched none; CI scans `services/api/candleviewer`, `apps`, `packages/ui`).
- Secret scan of the diff: none of the 5 `cv-*` or 3 `bybit-*` regexes from `.gitleaks.toml` matches it (the `gitleaks` binary is not installed on this laptop; CI `security / gitleaks` is the real gate).
- commitlint on the commit message: exit 0.
- Level: integration-style test in the `py` lane (real `create_app()` over in-memory fakes) plus a unit-style guard. No network, no sleep, no fixture from Bybit.

## Observations (not in this PR; for orchestrator and security-owner triage)

1. The `cv-recovery-code` rule (`.gitleaks.toml:85-91`) matches `xxxxx-xxxxx` groups, but `generate_recovery_code()` (`services/api/candleviewer/auth/recovery_codes.py:30-53`) mints seven groups of four. The toml regex run on codes from `generate_recovery_codes()` (as `recovery_codes=[...]`, plain and as a structlog event repr) does not match, so applying the rule here only guards the synthetic 5-5 shape (last row of the probe table). The test still catches the one consumed code through its literal set (main `:276`), but a leak of any other minted code is invisible to it. A one-line test-only follow-up would add all ten minted codes to `literals`; aligning the rule with the real format is a security-owned `.gitleaks.toml` change.
2. Minted tokens are un-prefixed `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` values (`invite_service.py:149,184`), so the `cvs_`/`cvr_`/`cvi_` rules cannot match a real token today. The shapes are forward guards; the literal set carries the detection

author: jun-bit-pulse-ai
body:
Refs #75

Follow-up to #134 (OCR plus the ElevenLabs and Deepgram audio providers). This PR adds an upload size limit for audio and file uploads, and fixes the transcription `model` in telemetry, which #134 listed under "What's left".

## What changed
- **`MAX_FILE_PAYLOAD_SIZE_IN_MB`** (opt-in, in `payloadSizeValidator.ts`): applies to `multipart/form-data` POSTs, which cover `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations`, image edits and file uploads.
  - A declared `Content-Length` over the limit gets a 413 before anything reads the form.
  - The handlers buffer the whole form in memory, so while the limit is set, a multipart request without a valid `Content-Length` gets a 411 and is not read unchecked.
  - The JSON limit (`MAX_JSON_PAYLOAD_SIZE_IN_MB`, ported from Portkey 2.0.0) is unchanged.
  - Portkey 2.0.0 has no limit for file uploads, so this one is new code.
- **Transcription and translation `model` in telemetry**:
  - `createTranscriptionHandler` and `createTranslationHandler` now read the form with `c.req.formData()` (Hono's body cache) instead of `c.req.raw.formData()`.
  - A new `requestBodyForTelemetry(c)` in `ps-telemetry.ts` is used by both `ps-telemetry` and `psOtel`. For a multipart body it returns only `{model}` from the form the handler already parsed.
  - It never re-reads or serialises the upload, so no file or prompt content reaches telemetry. Without this change, switching to the cached form would have made `c.req.json()` serialise the whole upload after every request.
  - Events now carry the real model (for example `nova-3` or `scribe_v1`), together with `modality: audio` and `usage_units` in seconds.
- Docs: `README.md` env list, `FORK_NOTICE.md` (the two handlers are added to the modified-upstream list and the payload-limit row is updated) and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Testing
- `payloadSizeValidator.test.ts`: covers multipart 413 and the within-limit case, 411 for a missing, empty, non-numeric or negative `Content-Length`, that the file limit does not apply to JSON, and that nothing changes when the limit is unset.
- `ps-telemetry-hono.test.ts`: a multipart transcription reports `model`, `modality` and seconds, and the `prompt` field is not present in the event. If the handler never parsed the form, telemetry does not read it either (the model is reported as `unknown`).
- Related suites (`audioOcrProviders`, `psOtel`, `ps-telemetry-*`, `payloadSizeValidator`) pass.
- Full `npx jest`: 21 suites and 48 tests fail, the same as `main` (plugins and `tryPost`).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` shows only the expected `plugins/build.ts` `conf.json` error.
- `npm run build` passes.

## What's left (#75)
- Registry and collector: persist `modality`, `usage_units` and `usage_unit_type`. The collector ingest does not read them yet, which is the "Done when" criterion.
- Transcription `response_format=text|srt|vtt` emulation for ElevenLabs and Deepgram.
- OCR on other providers (for example Bedrock).
- The file limit trusts the declared `Content-Length`. Node's HTTP parser stops reading at the declared length, so a body larger than its header is not read past it.

author: daodaonocode
body:
Revises the console for the architecture agreed at the 2026-10-15 kickoff: `ai-grid-backend` (yuvalturg/ai-grid-backend, gRPC) owns every call to the hub, Keycloak and metrics with its own ServiceAccount. The console keeps a thin BFF.

```
browser --JSON--> kube-auth-proxy + bff --gRPC--> ai-grid-backend --> hub API, Keycloak, Thanos
```

## Commits

- **feat(bff)**: drop client-go and the kube/users/clusters packages. New `internal/identity` (proxy headers), `internal/backend` (gRPC client with an identity-forwarding interceptor, plus a bufconn fake for tests). Handlers map `ListManagedClusters` and `ListTenants` to JSON, `/readyz` pings the backend, gRPC codes map to HTTP. The backend module comes through a `replace` to the yuvalturg repo pinned by pseudo-version (its go.mod declares `github.com/osac-project/ai-grid-backend`).
- **feat(frontend)**: `GridCluster` carries what the backend reports; enrolment and locations are gone until an `UpdateManagedCluster` RPC exists. Tenants page, sidebar nav, dev proxy sends `x-forwarded-user`.
- **feat(deploy)**: one pod with kube-auth-proxy, bff and ai-grid-backend over loopback; the backend's ManagedCluster ClusterRole on the console SA; optional Keycloak secret; `hack/dev-backend.sh` and `make dev` run all three locally.
- **docs**: API plan with the RPC behind each endpoint and a table of RPCs still needed; work breakdown split by repository with the kickoff's open questions.
- **fix (review round 1, abe7c7c)**: plaintext gRPC to a non-loopback backend is refused unless `BACKEND_INSECURE`, the backend binds to loopback, `/readyz` no longer echoes backend errors, dev proxy works with `AUTH_TOKEN` alone.
- **fix (review round 2, c76f58f, 7d35a85)**: the BFF binds to `127.0.0.1` too, so nothing on the pod network can bypass kube-auth-proxy with forged identity headers; its readiness probe goes through the proxy (`--skip-auth-route=^/readyz$`). `isProviderAdmin` comes from a `SelfSubjectAccessReview` (patch `managedclusters`) posted to the hub with the caller's own token (`internal/hub`, plain HTTPS, no client-go), as PR 1 did; `PROVIDER_ADMIN_GROUPS` is removed. Plaintext `HUB_API_URL` is accepted for loopback only; the readiness probe gets `timeoutSeconds: 5`. The remaining gap, that the backend calls the hub as its own ServiceAccount instead of as the caller, is recorded in `docs/plan/work-breakdown.md` as the backend's item 2.

## Verification

- `make lint test build`: gofmt clean, vet, golangci-lint 0 issues, `go test -race` green, tsc, vitest 8/8, vite build.
- Live against the dev hub: backend built from the pinned commit running locally with `--kubeconfig`; `hack/smoke.sh` passes (`/readyz`, user, config, clusters from the real `local-cluster`, tenants returning a clean 502 because the hub's Keycloak has no `ai-grid` realm yet). Both pages checked in the browser with playwright-cli.
- `kustomize build` and `oc apply --dry-run=client --validate=strict` pass. Not deployed: no backend image is published anywhere yet; `manifests/` carries a placeholder `quay.io/ai-grid-cloud/ai-grid-backend` and `hack/deploy.sh` takes `BACKEND_IMAGE`.

## Reviewer notes

- The backend does not read the forwarded identity yet, so today everyone who can log in gets the pod ServiceAccount's view. That is the first open question in `docs/plan/work-breakdown.md`.
- The backend container listens on all interfaces so the kubelet can probe it; a NetworkPolicy is listed for when it moves to its own Deployment.

author: maxjay
body:
Phase 3 of the plan: who changed it, with formatting filtered out, grouped by intent.

![Pi's lines, a teammate's commit, your edit, and a reindent filtered out](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maxjay/pi-workbench/feature/origins/docs/screenshots/origins.png)

## What's in it
- **Origin colours.** Every changed line is marked as Pi (teal), you (blue) or others (amber).
  - Pi's lines are matched by content against the `edit` and `write` calls recorded in Pi's session files for this folder, so CLI sessions count too. Session files are cached by mtime.
  - Lines too plain to match, such as brackets and blanks, take their neighbours' origin.
  - "Others" means lines committed by someone other than your `user.email`, from `git blame --porcelain --no-textconv HEAD` mapped onto the current text. Only committed content is read, so no filters run.
- **Formatting filter.** A hunk counts as formatting if it is unchanged once whitespace is ignored. With `difft` installed, a hunk that difftastic's JSON output (`DFT_UNSTABLE=yes`) doesn't touch also counts.
  - Formatting hunks keep a hairline in the margin, have no ghost, and are skipped by Next/Previous.
  - The palette command **Show or hide formatting-only changes** brings them back.
- **Turns.** Sessions now record a `Turn { prompt, before, after }`.
  - `after` is snapshotted when the run ends, before held saves are written, so it captures only Pi's work. A `SaveHold` guard releases the hold even if the session goes away meanwhile.
  - With **Changed** on, the list groups files under each turn (newest first, with its prompt). Everything else goes under "Other changes".
- **Core.** Adds `Repo::changes_between`, `Repo::blame`, `Repo::user_email`, `LineDiff::unchanged_base_line`, `structure::compare` (difftastic), and `sessions::written`. Each has tests.

## Verified on the demo repo

author: kevind003
body:
## What

Fixes the intermittent `db:verify:fresh` failure in `apps/api/tests/facets-integration.test.js` › "orders facets deterministically: count descending, then value" (expected `Snake_town` then `SnakeXtown`, received the reverse).

## Why it flaked

`loadEventFacets` ordered by `count DESC, value ASC` under the database's **default** collation, which depends on how the database was created: on C.UTF-8 `SnakeXtown` sorts before `Snake_town` (0x58 < 0x5F); on an ICU locale it sorts after. The test mirrored the order with `localeCompare` (ICU). The two Snake cities come from `event-search-integration.test.js`, which runs concurrently against the same database, so the test failed only when those rows happened to be present with equal counts.

## Change

- `apps/api/src/lib/facets.js`: every facet value is selected `COLLATE "C"`, so count ties break in byte order on every PostgreSQL. Only tie-break order changes; the web app re-sorts cities for display itself.
- `apps/api/tests/facets-integration.test.js`:
  - the existing ordering assertion is kept at full strength, comparing UTF-8 bytes (`Buffer.compare`) to mirror the SQL;
  - the suite seeds three tie cities of its own (`facettestXtie`, `facettest_tie`, `facettestatie`, two events each) and a new test asserts their exact order, so the case is exercised on every run without depending on another file's rows. The new rows fall under the existing cleanup prefixes.

## Verification

- Reproduced first: a copy of the test with the old `localeCompare` comparator fails against the new fixtures.
- On an ICU (`en`) database: old SQL fails both ordering tests; new SQL passes all 8.
- facets + event-search + traffic together: 10/10 runs green (ICU database), 3/3 after rebasing on current `main`.
- Full API suite with `REQUIRE_DATABASE=1` on a private `desi_event_test_*` database: 3/3 green (171 files, 3909 tests).
- `pnpm db:verify:fresh`: 3/3 green before the rebase, 1/1 green after rebasing on current `main` (Node 22.23.3, per `.nvmrc`).
- ESLint and Prettier clean on both files.

author: akhmialeuski
body:
A write block held the write queue across every await of the service that opened it. Each statement went to the aiosqlite thread and came back through the event loop, and before its first statement the block still had to take a connection from the pool, send `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and be resumed. All that time the next writer waited, although SQLite itself was busy for microseconds. This change runs each unit of work as one synchronous function in one thread, inside one transaction, so the queue is held only for the work itself.

## Why

The first commit splits the wait of a write block into its parts on the `write.block` span. Under the full end-to-end load the parts showed that the start and the release of a block were thread hops and event-loop resumptions, not SQLite. Three ways out were weighed: the SQLAlchemy recipe for SQLite transactions, a dedicated writer connection, and one trip to a thread per transaction. Only the last removes the hops of every statement. A stand with the same blocks under job load cut the median wait of a request block from 97 ms to 8 ms, at the cost of 0.3 to 0.6 ms more event-loop lag at p99.

## What changes

- `UnitOfWork.read`, `change` and `change_book` take a callable over `Repositories` and return its result. Every repository and every service is synchronous inside its unit of work. A nested block is impossible by construction: the work gets repositories, not the unit of work.
- `SqlDatabase` builds two synchronous engines through advanced-alchemy's `SQLAlchemySyncConfig`. The writer has one connection, whose `begin` listener sends `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and the readers share a pool of four that begin with `BEGIN`. The driver's own transaction handling is off (`isolation_level=None`), as the SQLAlchemy documentation recommends for SQLite.
- An anyio `CapacityLimiter(1)` is the write queue. It admits writers in order of arrival, and a writer that waits past its limit gets `BookBusyError` as before. Requests and jobs keep their own limits and now wait in the same queue, so the check that the request limit is shorter than the job limit is removed.
- The `write.block` span carries `wait.ms`, `hold.ms`, `commit.ms` and `block.outcome`. The phase attributes of the first commit are removed with the block start they measured.
- The application supports SQLite only, with the API process as its single writer. The PostgreSQL variants of the tables go: `JSONB`, `COLLATE "C"` and `postgresql_where`.
- Removed: aiosqlite, the async engine, `WriteQueue`, `release_reads` and `NestedChangeError`.
- The in-memory adapter implements the same port, with a lock per book.
- The compare canvas of a step that moves its input, such as Margins, no longer reports itself ready before the place of its two pictures is known. With the faster backend the rows of the step arrived after the pictures, and `compare-placement.spec.ts` measured the first place.

## Effect

The same end-to-end suite with spans, before and after:

| Measure                          | Before   | After, run 1 | After, run 2 |
|----------------------------------|----------|--------------|--------------|
| Wall time of the run, s          | 1351     | 868          | 838          |
| Write lock held, % of the run    | 61.0     | 27.8         | 27.0         |
| Wait for the writer, p50, ms     | 136.78   | 0.77         | 0.74         |
| Wait for the writer, p99, ms     | 2072.24  | 250.10       | 213.66       |
| Wait for the writer, max, ms     | 8606.98  | 1647.31      | 1509.19      |
| Hold of a block, p50, ms         | 69.46    | 21.70        | 20.06        |

`stream-connections.spec.ts`, which failed in the run before the change, passes in every full run after it.

## Known limits

- The worst hold of a block barely moved, 1.6 s against 1.8 s. Shortening the blocks themselves is separate work.
- `processing.spec.ts:127`, Space held over the compare, failed once in three full runs after the change: `data-holding` stayed `false` while the canvas was ready with a picture before. It passed 3 of 3 alone, 9 of 9 with `--repeat-each=3`, and in a full run with a log of the hold hook. The cause is not proven, so nothing was changed for it.

## Tests

- Contract tests of the new port run against both adapters, including the order of waiting writers and the wait limit of a request and of a job.
- New tests of the SQLAlchemy unit of work and of the `write.block` span. The tests of `WriteQueue` and `release_reads` are removed with them.
- Vitest: the compare canvas loads no picture and is not ready while the place is pending, then shows the pictures once at it. It failed without the fix.

```bash
$ uv run pre-commit run --all-files
$ uv run pytest -q
3573 passed, 2 skipped, 653 warnings in 193.13s (0:03:13)
$ npx vitest run
 Test Files  157 passed (157)
      Tests  1821 passed (1821)
$ npx playwright test
  61 passed (12.6m)
```

The 653 warnings come from third-party packages, and the run before the change had the same 653.

author: gs034
body:
## Bottom line

A single-use grant can now be ended before it is spent, by the operator or by kill, and the record says so. This is the library half of work item **L3.7**, assigned by the owner on 15 October: the route-to-production plan's L3.7 is "admin op `revoke` for unconsumed grants, and an admin-socket authorisation stronger than file mode". This ADR and its two PRs build the first half. The second half, an admin peer uid allowlist with its acceptance test, is separate work under the same code and is not touched here. The host's admin operations follow in the next PR.

## Done

Five files, two commits.

- `pep/approval.py`: `ApprovalRecord.revoked_at` with `revoked()` and `outstanding()`; `ApprovalStore.revoke(approval_id)` ends one outstanding grant and returns whether it did, with unknown, spent and already revoked ids returning False and changing nothing; `ApprovalStore.revoke_all(principal=None)` ends every outstanding grant, or those bound to one principal, and returns the count. `consume` checks revocation straight after the principal check and before consumed, expiry, binding, implementation and state, so a stranger still learns only that the id exists. The grant is not consumed.
- `pep/reasons.py`: new additive code `approval_revoked`.
- `pep/evaluate.py`: `PepRuntime.kill` revokes every outstanding grant after engaging the fence and before persisting the halt, so a failed halt write still leaves them revoked in memory; a reason detail for the new code.
- `tests/test_approval.py`: five tests. Revoked grant is DENY `approval_revoked` and stays unspent with the tool not called; revoke is idempotent and refuses unknown and spent grants; `revoke_all` counts and scopes by principal; kill revokes everything and a fresh runtime sharing the store still refuses; revocation takes precedence over mutated args and a later clock while the principal check still comes first.
- `docs/adr/ADR-0011-grant-revocation.md`: Proposed; work item L3.7 first half, with the second half named as separate work. The second commit is this assignment.

## Checks run

- Full suite as a non-root user on the code head, rebased onto main after #61: 496 passed. The second commit is documentation only.
- `python3 scripts/lab_brand_wall.py` on tree and history: clean.

## Review

Not independently reviewed. No different-family reviewer named. Do not merge on the author's say-so. A reviewer should check the order of checks in `consume` and the lock order in `kill` (runtime lock, then store lock, which matches the evaluate path).

## Claim level

A mechanism and its tests. Resume does not clear a revocation; suspend does not revoke. Not persistence across a host restart (L3.8). Not kill reach into a running tool body (L3.10). Not the admin-socket authorisation half of L3.7.

## Needs Go

1. Merge, which accepts ADR-0011.
2. Next in order, each after the previous merges: the host half of revocation, which also names L3.7 in the threat-model legend; then the keyed log library half (ADR-0012, L3.6); then its host half.
3. Later: the second half of L3.7, an admin peer uid allowlist on the admin socket.

## Risks

None beyond the usual for a new reason code: it is additive and no string is reused.

author: spsanps
body:
Closes #373

New implementation crate `omuzaki-settings`: `Paths`, and `Store` implementing `Settings` over a private `Backend` trait with a file backend (`settings.toml` in the config folder for `User` keys, `machine.toml` in the local data folder for `Machine` keys). Design: `docs/design/settings.md` D3, D5, D6, ADR 0026.

## Evidence per acceptance bullet

- **Property tests** (`document.rs`, proptest): any edit set applied to any generated file leaves every unrelated line and comment byte-identical (a comment directly above an edited key belongs to that key); the last edit of a key reads back exactly with its version; applying twice changes nothing more; values round-trip. A mutation of the writer makes them fail. **Migration fixtures**: values stored at version 1, 2 and 3 all load as the same current value; a failed migration reports and keeps the stored value. **Unknown, newer-version and damaged values** survive a write (`comments_order_and_unknown_keys_survive_a_write`, `a_newer_version_is_kept_verbatim...`, `a_bad_value_stays_in_the_file...`).
- **Two stores on one folder**: `two_stores_on_one_folder_are_last_writer_wins_per_key_not_per_file`.
- **Forced interleaving**: a test hook on the file backend pauses store A after its read, under the lock; store B's write waits (asserted not finished), A resumes, and both keys are in the file (`a_store_paused_after_its_read_cannot_lose_the_update...`).
- **Lock held by another process**: the test re-runs its own binary as a child that holds `settings.toml.lock`; the flush waits the bounded time, returns a `Storage` error, the key stays dirty and is listed by `findings()`; once the child exits the next flush lands it.
- **Bench / allocation**: `tests/snapshot_alloc.rs` (counting allocator, per thread) shows 10,000 `snapshot()` + `value()` calls allocate nothing; it fails if a clone-to-string is added. `cargo bench -p omuzaki-settings` on 300 keys: snapshot read about 56 ns; `set_raw` dry run about 0.21 µs; `set_raw` apply including the full snapshot rebuild about 47 µs.

## Notes for review

- Hub line: the root `Cargo.toml` gets one new `[workspace.dependencies]` line, `directories = "6.0"`. A pure addition, ruled exempt from file overlap; **the Director signs the hub line on this PR**.
- Licence: `docs/licensing/deps/directories.toml` (status `conditions` for `option-ext`, MPL-2.0, unmodified). One file, because `lint-licences` rejects separate files for transitive crates (`dirs-sys`, `option-ext`). `register.md` is untouched.
- Locking uses `std::fs::File::try_lock` in a bounded 2 s loop; no locking dependency.
- Deviation: write goes through `omuzaki_core::fsx::write_atomic`, which names its own temp files (`.<hash>-<pid>-<nonce>-<n>.tmp`), so `.<name>.<pid>.tmp` does not exist. Stale temps in the folder are removed by the next lock holder when older than 60 s; std has no portable "is that process alive" check.
- Profiles are not stored here (that is #769): `profiles()` is empty and profile writes return errors. `session()` is an in-memory stand-in until #767. Both are documented in the crate docs.
- Atomic replace retries `PermissionDenied` three times over 100 ms (the Windows rename case in D5).

## Self-review

- Self-review (correctness): every contract bullet has a test above; `set`/`reset`/`reload` follow the trait's dry-run rules (no write, snapshot swap, log entry or event); a no-change write emits no event.
- Self-review (performance): the snapshot read is an `Arc` clone and a map lookup with no allocation (measured); no I/O or blocking on the read path; file I/O only on the writer thread or an explicit `flush`.
- Self-review (architecture): the diff is `crates/omuzaki-settings/**`, the one hub line and the licence file; no API crate changed; depends only on API crates and core; no central list.
- Self-review (good practice): no `unwrap`/`expect` in library code; error texts name their key or file; lock-poisoning is tolerated; no dead code; the dependency has a licence row.
- Self-review (comments and docs): every public item documented; the crate docs list the choices a reviewer may disagree with.

## Gate

| Prod | 2 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​131 | $\color{#cf222e}{\Huge{\mathbf{−}}}$​89 | $\color{#1a7f37}{\Huge{\mathbf{+}}}$​42 |

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

A terminal on a remote machine sometimes sat on "Reconnecting to remote runtime" for minutes after you switched to another workspace and back, even though the connection was fine. Clicking Reconnect fixed it instantly. The terminal now reconnects by itself within about a second.

## What Changed

**Before:** after switching back to a remote workspace, the terminal showed the reconnect banner for about 15 seconds. If you switched a few times in a minute, it sat there for about 3 minutes, then said "Automatic retries stopped" until you clicked Reconnect.
**After:** the terminal reattaches within about a second. Repeated drops slow the retries down instead of stopping them. A connection that is really gone still shows Reconnecting, and after the same ~3 minute window it still offers the Reconnect button.

Older remote hosts (1.4.224 and earlier) end a terminal's output stream when a hidden workspace becomes visible again. The host keeps that terminal running and keeps reporting it as ready. The client handled that end in three slow ways (all in `remote-runtime-pty-transport.ts`):

1. **It waited the whole 15 s window for a "replacement" terminal**, even though the host kept answering that the same one was ready. It now reuses that terminal as soon as the host reports it ready. The exception: if a keystroke sent to it is still unanswered, it keeps waiting, because that send could still come back "stale".
2. **A third drop within 60 s demanded a replacement terminal that never comes.** The retry was then parked with no timer, so the banner spun until the ~3 min deadline. Repeated drops now reuse the same terminal after growing delays (1 s, 2 s, 4 s … 30 s). Only a drop within 10 s of reattaching counts as a repeat. Every reattach resets the recovery deadline, so once that ladder is used up (about a minute of nonstop drops) the pane goes back to waiting for a replacement terminal, and the deadline then offers Reconnect. A terminal that drops forever still surfaces Reconnect and does not retry forever. A terminal the host has actually reported stale still waits for a replacement, as before.
3. **"Unknown" answers parked the retry.** If the host answered without a ready terminal, or the terminal inventory request failed, the retry waited for a network-online or wake-from-sleep event that never fires on a healthy link. These now retry on the normal backoff ladder until the existing deadline. A retry that is still running when the deadline hits stays revivable by online, resume, or Reconnect.

`RemoteRuntimePtyRecoveryState.schedule` takes an optional delay so the repeated-drop pacing reuses the existing recovery timer and deadline.

## Why

- These are client-side fixes, so they also work against released hosts that still end streams this way. Clients and hosts update independently. Nothing on the wire changes.
- The repeated-drop guard from #12003 stays. It still rate-limits a terminal that drops right after every reattach, but it no longer gives up on a terminal the host says is alive. Liveness stays honest: an end proves only that we lost the attachment, and the host's "ready" answer is the live evidence.
- I considered treating "workspace became visible" as a retry trigger. I rejected it because it would only cover the remount path. Scheduling the retries fixes every caller that parked.
- #27698 (community PR) targets the same issue. This PR takes a smaller route to the same three fixes: no new replacement-policy tier and no extra fence loop on the persisted-pane path.

## Linked Issue

Fixes #27178

Also addresses the ~20 s "Reconnect to remote runtime" banner on tab switch in #19647 (same host stream-end + 15 s replacement wait). Not closing it: its second symptom, a frozen pane with no banner while output keeps flowing on the host until a client restart, is a different mechanism this PR does not touch.

## Visual Proof

N/A. The visible behavior is how long the reconnect banner stays up. Fake-timer tests pin that timing. I did not run an end-to-end check against a 1.4.224 host (see Testing).

## Testing

- New `remote-runtime-pty-transport-healthy-link-reattach.test.ts`, red on `main` (5/6 failing) and green with this change:
  - reattaches within 2 s of a stream end when the host reports the handle ready
  - 5 back-to-back ends keep reattaching and never park
  - a resubscribe whose host answered without a ready handle retries and attaches once ready
  - an attach whose host surface stayed pending past 15 s retries and attaches
  - a resubscribe past repeated inventory failures recovers when the host answers again
  - a host that never produces a handle still latches `disconnected` with Reconnect available
- I updated the tests that pinned the old parking behavior. Two-window inventory cap → keeps polling on the ladder until the deadline, then goes quiet. Third flap requires replacement → paced reuse. Pending attach phase `recovering` → `backoff`. The prior-ready-evidence test is now fenced by an unanswered send, so it still covers the end-of-window fallback.
- All `terminal-pane/remote-runtime-*` suites, plus `pty-connection-remote-runtime-attach` and `terminal-remote-runtime-recovery-ui-state`, pass locally (macOS). `pnpm tc:web` and `check:code-quality:changed` are clean.
- Not tested end to end against a real 1.4.224 host.

- [ ] I manually tested these changes locally
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable, or this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

## Notes

- SSH/remote: renderer-only change to the paired remote terminal transport. No RPC or stream frame changes, so it is safe with mixed client and host versions.
- Performance: a pane whose liveness is unknown now keeps polling inside the existing ~3 min deadline instead of idling. That is bounded by the backoff ladder, and it stops at the deadline.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is small and focused
- [x] I explained what changed and why (ELI5, the user-facing before/after, the mechanism, and why over the alternatives)
- [x] Before/after screenshots or videos attached for UI changes, or `N/A` with reason

- [x] Cross-platform, SSH/remote, and path/shortcut impact considered (or N/A)

# TPU: Torch TPU for the TPU well-lit paths, Qwen3.5-397B model guide, GLM-5.2 on TPU7x, Google Cloud TPU landing page

## What this PR does

Moves every Google TPU configuration in the guides to **vLLM on Torch TPU** (native PyTorch on TPU, no JAX layer) and refreshes the TPU content for the Foundations / Models structure (#2665, #2669, #2686). One model per accelerator: **TPU v6e serves `Qwen/Qwen3-32B`**, **TPU7x serves `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8`**.

### Foundations guides (TPU rows)

| Guide | v6e | TPU7x |
| --- | --- | --- |
| optimized-baseline | Qwen3-32B, `2x4` TP=8 | Qwen3.5-397B, `2x2x1` TP=8 EP |
| precise-prefix-cache-routing | Qwen3-32B, `--block-size=256` (TPU router values match) | Qwen3.5-397B, DP=2 × TP=4 EP |
| tiered-prefix-cache | Qwen3-32B, Torch TPU Raiden host tier | Qwen3.5-397B, 100 GiB host tier |

author: dlgreenwald
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Upload Recording dialog appearing with a transparent/white background in dark mode. Also migrates the dropdown menu to the same library for consistency.

## Changes

### Root Cause
Radix DialogPortal renders modal content at document.body as a sibling of #root. CSS custom properties (--background, etc.) set on :root or :root.dark via ThemeProvider do not inherit through the DOM tree to portal content.

Additionally, ThemeProvider used attribute=class by default while shadcn CSS used [data-theme=dark] selectors — a fundamental mismatch meaning dark mode styles never applied.

### Fixes

**1. Headless UI migration (dialog.tsx, dropdown-menu.tsx)**
- Replaced Radix DialogPrimitive + DialogPortal with Headless UI Dialog, DialogPanel, DialogBackdrop, Transition
- Replaced Radix DropdownMenuPrimitive + DropdownMenuPortal with Headless UI Menu
- Both render inline (no portal), so CSS vars cascade naturally
- Dropped the prior getIsDark() / DARK_CSS_VARS hack from dialog.tsx

**2. ThemeProvider attribute (App.tsx)**
- Added attribute=data-theme to match shadcn CSS selectors

**3. Tailwind config (tailwind.config.js)**
- Updated darkMode to [class, [data-theme=dark]] so Tailwind generates [data-theme=dark]: variants

**4. Base bg-background rule (global.css)**
- Added .bg-background { background-color: var(--background); } — light mode via CSS vars; dark modes !important override takes precedence

### Also Included
- Upload Recording button moved from calendar toolbar to sidebar top-left
- UploadModal component (drag-drop, datetime picker, file input, submit)
- api.uploadRecording() — FormData POST to /upload/offline
- UploadModal.test.tsx — 11 tests
- AGENTS.md — test count updated (119 dashboard tests)

## Pre-Existing Session Split Feature
This branch also includes the session-split feature from prior work:

**Server changes (pre-existing in this branch):**
- worker.py: gap-based partitioning for sessions, split reason computation
- database.py: updated recording queries to include split_reason_before/after
- llm.py: enhanced LLM prompt handling for split recordings
- server/alembic/versions/031_split_reasons.py: migration adding split_reason_before/after columns

**Dashboard changes (pre-existing in this branch):**
- types.ts: Recording interface includes split_reason_before/split_reason_after
- RecordingDetail.tsx: renders split reason banners above/below recording sections
- global.css: split-reason-banner styling for dark mode

## Testing
- 137 dashboard tests pass
- 197 server tests pass
- tsc --noEmit clean
- Verified light and dark mode in browser

author: copilot
body:
Replaces the stubbed OpenFlux adapter with real SDK calls. Around it, this adds profile editing with encrypted secrets, reconnect on transport and network failures, IPv6 support and a kill-switch.

**Review first:** there is no public OpenFlux SDK artifact. The PR adds a local `:openflux-sdk` module, a reference client I wrote: length-prefixed frames over TCP/TLS, token auth, keepalive, SNI/ALPN. Its protocol will not work against a real OpenFlux server. Swapping in the real artifact should only require rewriting `OpenFluxAdapterImpl.connect()`. The README documents the swap.

`:app` has not been built. The sandbox can't download the Android Gradle Plugin, so only `:openflux-sdk` was compiled (`javac`). The device checks are still pending and listed in the README.

- **SDK and build**
  - `app` depends on `project(':openflux-sdk')` and `androidx.security:security-crypto`.
  - The SDK calls `SocketProtector.protect()` before `connect()` on every socket it opens, which avoids a routing loop through the VPN.
- **Config and storage**
  - `VpnProfile` and `OpenFluxConfig` gain transport, token, key and keyRef, TLS/SNI/ALPN, DNS, routes, full/split mode, timeouts, an IPv6 TUN address and `killSwitch`.
  - `ProfileStore` keeps `authToken` and `privateKey` in `EncryptedSharedPreferences` (Keystore-backed master key). If that store is unreadable, it is reset.
  - `ProfileValidator` runs both when saving in the editor and again when the service starts. An invalid profile never starts the tunnel.
- **Adapter and reconnect**
  - `OpenFluxAdapterImpl` drives `OpenFluxClient`. Inbound packets go to `PacketCallback`, then `TunPump.inject`.
  - `isConnected()` flips to false on read failure, EOF, keepalive failure or send failure.
  - `OpenFluxController.requestReconnect()` is new. It runs on send failure and network change, and the controller loop notices a drop on its next 500 ms wait, including the backoff wait. I did not add a separate trigger for TUN read failures.
- **Service (`MyVpnService`)**
  - A default-network callback calls `setUnderlyingNetworks` and `requestReconnect()` when the default network changes.
  - The TUN gets IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and full mode always routes `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0`.
- **Kill-switch**
  - The TUN stays up across reconnects, and packets are dropped while the state isn't `CONNECTED`.
  - In split mode with `killSwitch` on, `::/0` is added if the profile has no IPv6 routes, so IPv6 doesn't bypass the tunnel.
  - Android can't enforce this once the process dies or VPN permission is revoked. The README tells users to enable Always-on VPN with "Block connections without VPN".
- **UI**
  - `ProfileEditorActivity` edits all profile fields. Empty optional fields fall back to defaults, and the window uses `FLAG_SECURE`.
- **Docs**
  - The README is rewritten: SDK setup, profile guide, permission/start flow, the testing checklist (pending device runs marked as such) and known limitations.

body:
## What changes

`scripts/check-examples.sh` failed on macOS: its `pack()` tars the tree with bsdtar, which writes an AppleDouble `._name` entry beside every file carrying extended attributes — every checked-out file has `com.apple.provenance`. The fizzy tarball then held `backend/patches/sdl/._0001-….patch` and friends, and the SDL patch step (`run exe patch`) failed with `NoSections`, failing the example-app studio/minimal/endless/dvui builds. CI runs on Linux with GNU tar, so it never saw this.

author: mgreathouse-workbench
body:
*"The budget tab is asking me to pick an edition, which I've already chosen in pages."*

#25 moved the publication/date pickers and the **Load budget** button into the no-edition branch of the shell, because the context bar replaces them once an edition is chosen. The Budget tab's empty state still said:

> Pick a publication and edition, then click Load budget.

naming two controls that were, by then, **not on screen**. There was no way to load a budget for the edition you had already picked.

### Budget

The tab now carries its own button, and it says which edition it will load — *"Load budget for EXT_101726"*, or *"Refresh budget"* once one is loaded.

### Marketplace, same dead end, different cause

It treated **not loaded** and **loading** as one state and returned the spinner for both — and its Refresh button renders further down, *after* that return. So a marketplace that had never been fetched showed "Loading…" forever with no control to load it.

The two states are now separate: a **Load** button when nothing has been fetched, a spinner only while a fetch is actually running.

### The common mistake

Moving a control out of a shared header leaves every screen that referred to it pointing at nothing. An empty state that names a missing button is worse than no empty state at all.

author: livethisdream
body:
Follow-up to #30, which found this and deliberately left it alone.

## Problem

Phase calibration did not repeat. Five runs on kit `phaser-00` on a healthy bench — 85 dB SNR, 33 dB array contrast — returned element 8 offsets spanning **104°**: +8.4, +30.9, +50.6, +95.6, +112.5.

Nothing was wrong with the measurement. Two elements summing give a response ∝ `|1 + exp(jΔ)|`, whose peak is **quadratic**: 20° off the true offset costs 0.26 dB. An argmax over that is reading the flattest part of the curve, so a couple of tenths of a dB of noise moves it tens of degrees — and each pair's answer is held while the next pair sweeps, so the error accumulates. That is exactly the shape of the scatter, growing 17.3° at element 2 to 43.6° at element 8.

## Fix

`φ₀ = angle(Σ P_linear · e^{jφ})` — the first Fourier coefficient of a known one-parameter family. Every sample contributes, including the flanks and the null, which is where the phase information actually lives.

Two properties make it the right estimator rather than just a better one:

- **Immune to an additive pedestal.** A constant is orthogonal to `e^{jφ}`, and the measured response falls to the noise floor rather than to zero. An estimator that cared would have to know where the floor was.
- **Continuous**, so it beats the sweep grid rather than being quantised to it — sub-degree on a sweep coarser than the ADAR's own 2.8125° LSB.

It also yields a free quality metric `|c1|/|c0|`, ~0.33 for a clean response and ~0 for a flat one. That is the only available warning that a pair's sweep carried no phase information; previously an argmax over noise returned a confident number. It reports rather than refuses — a bad fit is still the best estimate available.

## Measured on phaser-00, five runs each

| element | argmax std | fit std | improvement |
| --: | --: | --: | --: |
| 2 | 17.3° | 0.55° | 31.4× |
| 3 | 28.7° | 1.76° | 16.3× |
| 4 | 31.8° | 2.24° | 14.2× |
| 5 | 21.6° | 2.33° | 9.3× |
| 6 | 21.1° | 2.18° | 9.7× |
| 7 | 28.3° | 2.95° | 9.6× |
| 8 | 43.6° | 2.01° | 21.7× |
| **mean** | **27.5°** | **2.00°** | **13.7×** |

The accumulation signature is gone — old scatter grew along the array, new is flat at ~2° past element 3.

**The cleanest evidence** is that verbose output now prints the argmax beside the fit, so both estimators can be compared on the *same captures* with every other variable fixed: **41×** on pair 1→2 (0.55° vs 22.4°) and **10×** on pair 7→8 (2.01° vs 20.6°). Measured quality was 0.312–0.335 on every pair against the theoretical 0.333.

## Tests

`tests/test_phase_estimator.py` — exact recovery on clean sweeps, wrapping, the duplicated sweep endpoint, pedestal immunity, sub-degree accuracy on a coarse sweep, the quality metric at both extremes, graceful degradation, and a Monte Carlo against the argmax at the ~0.4 dB noise level that reproduces the bench's 17° per-pair scatter.

`FakeArray` gains an optional noise term, **defaulted off** so existing tests are untouched. A noiseless fake cannot tell a good phase estimator from a bad one — both land within a step — which is precisely why this went unnoticed in the suite. The new test runs the whole procedure eight times on noisy captures and requires both low scatter *and* the right answer, since a stable-but-biased estimator would pass the first check and still miscalibrate the array.

229 pass.

## Bench note, not a code issue

Received power fell ~12 dB during the session (HB100 search SNR 75.1 → 66.4 dB, source drifting 60 kHz). The kit owner reports the source was likely bumped or moved. Contrast stayed above 30 dB so every run above is valid, and the comparison is internally controlled regardless. But phase cal assumes the source is at **mechanical boresight**, so the `pcal` currently stored on `phaser-00` may carry a geometric steering term and should be re-run once the HB100 is re-aimed.

body:
## Read this first
This branch already contains everything on open PR **#28**, plus the freeform and pgmvox work built on it since. That includes pgmvox up to 0.30.0, the boards under `freeform/lib/boards`, the trial boards, the grammar styles, the x-ray and box renders (WS90) and the plan-review design. Against `main` it adds about 3,800 files. Most are `freeform/lib/boards/`, the worlds under `maps/` and `specs/`. What is new here is three commits:
- `c1fa501b`: the examples as worlds.
- `4097e3e5`: the shape studies, merged in from `ccr-fe3d4854-ws4cd8`.
- `05bbba19`: the studies as worlds.

## Every example that builds a world has one
| Example | World | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `islets` | `maps/koth/islets` | already there, with its map.xml |
| `bridges` | `maps/other/bridges` | six land bridges over a canyon; spawn on the west rim |
| `drop` | `maps/other/drop` | the course, built for the first time (below) |
| `parts` | `maps/other/parts` | every house style, roof form and pattern on one yard |
| `spikes` | `maps/other/spikes` | `forms.spike`'s kinds on one yard |
| `vale` | `maps/other/vale` | every landform on one stretch of ground |
| `layers` | — | holds studio documents, not a world |

- **`drop` gains a `gen.py`.** Each piece is a slab floating at its own top. Each water piece is a pool three deep to its edges, inside a glass rim that stops one block under the surface. The course's audit lands two of its falls on edge cells, and a rim at the waterline would have clipped them. Spawn is (0, 121, 4) on the start slab.
- **`vale`'s spawn stood 26 blocks over the grass,** a fall that kills on arrival. It now stands on the ground at (0, 55, 0).

## Every study is a world, one world a subject
`freeform/lib/studies/worlds.py` builds each form the way its own study builds it, by the study's own functions. It lays a subject's forms side by side, 40 blocks apart and six to a row, with each round in its own band of rows. A sign at each form names its study and form.

| World | Forms | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `maps/other/studies_volcanoes` | round 1's 12 forms, then round 2's 8 | 30 MB |
| `maps/other/studies_winter` | glacier tongue, pack ice, ice shelf, cirques, snowfield | 8 MB |
| `maps/other/studies_combinations` | lava rift, ice rift, somma and ice | 5 MB |
| `maps/other/studies_water` | round 1's 6, then round 2's 6 | 19 MB |
| `maps/other/studies_dungeons` | the six layouts, then the three deep builds | 4 MB |

The volcanoes are in the study's slope-toned wool, as the study draws them. A visitor arrives at a subject's first form; a dungeon's spawn is a floor inside it.

## How the new worlds are written
All eleven new worlds are a `level.dat` and a `region/` with no map.xml, written through the studio's own Anvil writer (`pgmvox.core.world.write`). Each has its row in `maps/INDEX.md`. Every spawn stands on solid ground with two air blocks of headroom over it.

- `check.py` rebuilds every board and example. Only `examples/drop` (new) and `examples/vale` (spawn) move, and those hashes are recorded.
- `check.py --quick` reports nothing broken after merging `main` in.

- The image is built from the same checksum-verified release zip, which `github-release` hands over as a short-lived artifact. The job no longer runs its own untested `installDist`. The zip travels instead of the directory because an artifact upload drops the exec bit on `bin/server`.

**Plugin launcher** (plugin version 1.2.0 → 1.2.1)
- With `server_version: latest`, a failed install of a newly found release (CDN error, `.sha256` not uploaded yet, checksum mismatch) now falls back to the newest installed version with a warning. `latest-release.txt` is written only after a successful install, so the next session retries. A pinned version still fails with the reason.
- Unpacking happens in `<data>/staging/`, outside `dist/`. Only directories named as a version count as installed, so a pre-1.2.1 `<version>.incoming*` leftover is never launched.
- Unpacks abandoned for over an hour are swept on the next install.
- The checksum-missing message now covers a release whose assets are still uploading. Fallback warnings include the cause, e.g. the HTTP status.

**MCPB manifest**
- Adds `read_source` and `search_modules`; the manifest listed 16 of the 18 tools.
- `registerAllTools` is now the single tool list. `McpServerFactory`, `ToolRegistrationTest` and `TraceScenarioTest` use it instead of hand-copied lists.
- New `McpbManifestTest` compares the manifest with the registered tools. The manifest reaches it as a test resource.

**README:** the demo TODO points at `assets/demo.gif`.

## Test plan
- [x] `McpbManifestTest` failed before the manifest fix, reporting `read_source` and `search_modules` missing. It fails again when one entry is removed by hand.
- [x] `gradlew build :server:packageMcpb` passes. `mcpb validate` passes on the generated manifest.
- [x] `actionlint` 1.7.12 is clean on `release.yml` and `ci.yml`.
- [x] `javac -Xlint:all` on the launcher passes. `claude plugin validate --strict` passes on the marketplace and on the plugin.
- [x] Launcher run by hand against scratch data dirs:
  - latest, install fails, older version installed: falls back (the old launcher exits 2)
  - offline, stale `.incoming` dir present: picks the real install (the old launcher launches the partial tree)
  - offline, nothing installed: clear error, exit 2
  - pinned version that does not exist: fails, no fallback
  - real install from GitHub: marker written after the install, aged leftovers swept, a fresh unpack kept
- [ ] The `release.yml` change is exercised for real only by the next tag.

Follow-ups, not in this PR:
- The GitHub release is still published before the image job runs. A failed image push leaves a release without an image or a registry entry.
- The MCPB manifest declares no prompts (`explain_module`).

author: lenaxia
body:
Closes #1687 (client lane). Turns the 4 red-first pins from `poc/sse-live-update-red-pins` (commit e1ce3c2f) green without weakening the guard. Server-side idle-emission gaps (#1666) are out of scope — client lane only.

## The four pins

### Pin 1 — `resync` does not reconcile busy
`SessionActivityProvider.resyncBusy.test.tsx` — RED premise: the broker's `{"type":"resync"}` (broker.go:64, stream_user_events.go:266) is admitted event loss on a **healthy** connection; the dropped set may include the `session.status=idle` that would clear a latched badge, and no `onReconnect` ever fires.
**Fix:** the provider's resync handler runs the same reconciliation as `onReconnect` via a shared module-scope `wipeBusyForEventLoss` core (wipeAt stamp + seed-gate reopen + busy wipe), then invalidates `["sessions"]` **after** the stamp — the #1646 r5 ordering — so the gated re-seed re-derives from REST (test: exactly one connection, badge clears from REST truth).

### Pin 2 — contract `SESSION_STATUS IDLE` never cleared the provider busy map (missing bridge)
`ChatPage.contractIdleBridge.test.tsx` test 1 — RED premise: ChatPage demonstrably receives contract idle (it drives reconcileOnIdle) but nothing fed it into `busySessions`; the user-stream idle frame was the single clear path and is lost to broker drops / reconnect gaps.
**Fix:** new `clearSessionBusy(workspaceId, sessionId)` on the provider context (mirrors the user-stream idle row flip + hung-alert resolution), called from ChatPage's SESSION_STATUS IDLE branch. One stream reporting the turn's end is enough.

### Pin 3 — mid-turn reconnect wipes the live streaming buffer
`ChatPage.midturnReconnect.test.tsx` test 1 (test 2 is the GREEN guard) — RED premise: `onReconnect` called `reconcileOnIdle()` unconditionally, and reconcileOnIdle wiped `sseStreamParts` whenever refetched history was nonempty — mid-turn the in-flight message exists nowhere else.
**Fix:** the wipe (and the optimistic trim) is gated on the viewed session **not being mid-turn per the fold** (`status === BUSY`), read from a ref kept current by `onSnapshot` + the fold-publish effect (stream `onEvent` fires before React commits the fold, so a render closure would be stale). The IDLE handler passes `turnEnded=true` — the event is authoritative over a not-yet-committed fold — which is what keeps the guard green. The reconnect history refetch is kept, and the pre-existing `sse-reconnect-duplicate` regression (fold entry absent + history owns the turn → clear) stays green: an absent fold entry keeps the legacy catch-up rule.

### Pin 4 (compound) — stuck busy silently reroutes sends into the queue
`ChatPage.contractIdleBridge.test.tsx` test 2 — green automatically once Pin 2 lands (the stale busy no longer holds `handleSend`'s gate); kept as the regression pin for symptoms 1+2 together.

## Also in scope — SSE header factory (the #1687 known follow-up)
`sseConnection.ts` destructured `headers` once at creation, so reconnects re-sent the mount-time header set and `Last-Event-ID` replay (implemented server-side, stream_user_events.go:92) never fired post-mount. `headers` now accepts a **factory**, re-evaluated on every connect; `useUserEventStream` passes `buildHeaders` and its stale r2 NOTE is updated to record the resolution. This is the systematic fix for reconnect-gap event loss on the user stream.

## Synergy with #1685
The 15-min busy nudge should become retirable once this lands: all three of its feeding symptoms (stuck badge, queue-held sends, mid-turn wipe) are fixed at the root here.

## Harness notes (no pin weakened)
- Provider-mocking ChatPage tests gain a `useClearSessionBusy` stub — the mock must mirror the module surface ChatPage now consumes.
- `hookcount` expectation 72 → 75 (+`useClearSessionBusy`, +fold ref, +fold-sync effect) — the pin's own instruction for intentional hook additions.
- `contractIdleBridge` pin: one compile-only fix (`?.onEvent?.`) — `TS2722` pre-existed on the pins branch and blocked the required clean `tsc --noEmit`. No assertion or semantic change.
- `sse-reconnect-duplicate` and `optimistic-survival` regressions were load-bearing design inputs for Pin 3's gate shape (see above) and pass unchanged.

## Verification
- Pins: `npx vitest run src/providers/SessionActivityProvider.resyncBusy.test.tsx src/pages/ChatPage.contractIdleBridge.test.tsx src/pages/ChatPage.midturnReconnect.test.tsx` → **5 passed** (4 pins + guard).
- Full frontend suite after `npm ci`: **191 files / 2104 tests passed**.
- `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings, identical to the pins branch).

body:
Closes #64

## What
**`/admin/import`** ("Import recruits" in the admin nav)
1. **Paste** from Google Sheets (tabs) or **upload** the Forms CSV; "first row contains column names"
2. **Columns**: Name (several columns joined – first + last name), E-mail, Sections, Language (optional) – **guessed from the headers** (imię/nazwisko, e-mail, sekcj…, język…)
3. **Form answers → sections**: each distinct answer (checkbox answers split on `,`/`;`) mapped to an app section (exact name match pre-selected, otherwise "not mapped" or ignore); language values → Polski/English (`en…`/`ang…` guessed as English)
4. **Expiry**, **Send invitation e-mails** (disabled with a hint when e-mail isn't configured) → **Preview** → table with New / Already invited / Error per recruit (source row numbers) → **Create N links & send N e-mails** → summary with links to Booking links / E-mail status

**`POST /api/booking-links/import`** `{rows: [{line, name, email, sectionIds, language}], expiresAt, dryRun, sendEmails}`
- rows **merged by e-mail** (lower-cased): sections united, first name kept
- errors: missing/invalid e-mail, no section, unknown section, unsupported language, name too long
- **already invited** = an active, unexpired link **or** an active interview → skipped, so **re-importing the same file creates nothing**
- commit: recruits upserted, one personal link per recruit (language set), invitations queued via `Invitations.QueueAsync` – all in **one transaction**
- refuses to send when e-mail or `Club:PublicUrl` isn't configured

**Fixes found while testing**
- Booking an **anonymous** link didn't attach the recruit to it → the import couldn't see that person as invited. Booking now sets `link.Recruit`; the interview check covers older data
- Default templates greeted with the full name ("Cześć Zofia Nowak!") → new `{firstName}` placeholder → "Cześć Zofia!"

**Also**: `frontend/src/csv.ts` – RFC 4180 + Sheets-paste parser, checked by `npm test`; `docs/EMAIL.md` – recommended setup: **dedicated sending account, replies to the university address**.

## Verified
- Import script (DB backed up and restored): preview → commit (3 links, 3 mails) → re-import (all "already invited"); merged Zofia got **one** Polish mail with both sections, the English row got the English mail; Kasia (booked via anonymous link) → "already invited"
- `npm test` (parser: Forms CSV with BOM/quoted commas/escaped quotes/line breaks, Sheets paste, `;` CSV, empty rows)
- Backend **25/25**, frontend build + lint clean

Que cada consulta nueva llegue por email (épica #20). El aviso es de mejor esfuerzo: un fallo de Resend no pierde la consulta.

Ninguna.

author: maycon-rodrigues
body:
Fixes #31

## Problema

Todo redeploy no Railway deixava o log do Postgres assim, em todas as conexões do pool ao mesmo tempo:

```
LOG:  SSL error: unexpected eof while reading
LOG:  could not receive data from client: Connection reset by peer
```

O `PrismaService` **já** implementava o hook de desconexão (`src/infra/prisma/prisma.service.ts:10`), mas sem `app.enableShutdownHooks()` o Nest não liga os sinais do processo ao ciclo de vida. O node recebia o SIGTERM, não tinha handler, e a ação default encerrava o processo na hora — o `$disconnect()` nunca rodava.

## Solução

Uma linha em `src/main.ts`, antes do `app.listen()`:

```ts
app.enableShutdownHooks();
```

Com os hooks ligados o Nest para de aceitar conexões novas, deixa as requisições em voo terminarem e só então fecha — rodando o `onModuleDestroy` do Prisma no caminho.

## Impacto

- **Cosmético:** os `unexpected eof` saem do log do Postgres.
- **Real:** requisições em voo deixam de ser cortadas no meio a cada deploy. É o que mais importa aqui: num fluxo de ramp, uma requisição morta entre a chamada à BlindPay e o `INSERT` deixa registro remoto órfão sem linha local.

## Correção de uma premissa da issue

A issue #31 afirmava que o `npm` repassa sinais de forma imperfeita, e sugeria trocar o `CMD` do Dockerfile para o node receber o SIGTERM direto. **Medi, e isso está errado** — deixo o teste aqui porque a informação errada já está registrada na issue:

```
# via npm run (exatamente o que o Dockerfile faz hoje)
$ npm run start:migrate --silent &  ; kill -TERM $!
node pronto, pid=853080
NODE RECEBEU SIGTERM -> shutdown limpo
exit=0
```

O npm 10 repassa o SIGTERM corretamente, e o `sh -c "a && b"` também (o shell faz `exec` implícito no último comando). O sinal **sempre chegou** ao node — o que faltava era só o handler.

Então cheguei a alterar o `CMD` e **revertí**: mudar o entrypoint do container de um backend de pagamentos, para ganho cosmético, sem necessidade funcional comprovada, não se justifica. O Dockerfile fica intocado e o PR é de um arquivo.

## Fora de escopo

O `CMD` roda `prisma migrate deploy && node dist/main`. Se um SIGTERM cair **durante** a migration, o Prisma pode deixar uma linha em `_prisma_migrations` como iniciada-e-falha e travar todo deploy seguinte. Não é o que causava este sintoma e não mexi nisso — merece issue própria, junto com a decisão de tirar migration do boot.

- `tsc --noEmit` limpo
- **638 testes passando, 45 suites** (suíte completa)
- `eslint src/main.ts`: 1 warning pré-existente no `bootstrap();` (floating promise), nenhum erro novo

Como confirmar depois do merge em dev: no próximo deploy, os `unexpected eof while reading` devem desaparecer do log do Postgres. É o sinal de que o `$disconnect()` passou a rodar.

author: wolf31o2
body:
The pump already redials every batch and retries forever once `TXPUMP_STARTUP_TIMEOUT` is 0. A node that hangs or dies mid-batch still cost one timeout per remaining transaction, and those failures were logged as rejections.

- A submission that fails for any reason other than a ledger rejection marks the connection broken and ends the batch, so the pump redials.
- Transport failures are logged with status `error` and as `submit failed`; only ledger rejections use `rejected`.
- A transaction whose submit failed on the wire may still have been accepted; the wallet is replaced from the node snapshot at the start of the next batch, which settles it.
- Tests: an unreachable node is retried until it returns, the pump resumes after a node dies following readiness, and the backup is used while the primary is down.

Tested: build, vet, lint, nilaway and race tests pass.
