author: jampat000
body:
Addresses #1003 and #1006.

## What was untested
- Nothing showed an alert reaching a listening receiver: the webhook body, the Discord embed, the headers, a 4xx or 5xx answer, or a switched-off channel being left alone. Delivery was only tested against a recording stand-in for the poster.
- Of a rule set's settings the contract round trip saved two. Nothing showed the rest reaching `RulesConfigFor`, and the real passes in the suites only ever ran the built-in default.

## What proves it now
- `AlertDeliveryTests`, `AlertOnJobOutcomeTests` (contract): a test send and a real finished or failed file reach a receiver served on this PC. Webhook members and headers, the Discord embed (title, description, colour 0x2ECC71 or 0xE74C3C, Module and Job ID fields, footer), one post per channel that is switched on and subscribed and none for one switched off (switch it on and a post arrives), and a refusing receiver is asked once and said so plainly in the log.
- `ExternalJsonPosterStandInTests`, `NotificationDispatcherTests`, `NotificationPayloadTests`, `WebhookJobNotificationsTests` (unit): the request that arrives, redirect and 4xx/5xx handling, the address rules still applying, the exact payload shapes, the switched-off channel (red against a dispatcher that ignores `enabled`: seen failing).
- `RuleSetFieldsRoundTripTests` (contract): the settings come from the OpenAPI schema, so a new one fails until it has a value here. All set to non-default values and read back; changed one at a time with the others unchanged; defaults checked against the documented ones.
- `RuleSetEveryFieldMappingTests` (unit): every column of `ProcessingRuleSetRecord` changes `RulesConfigFor` (reflection, so a new column fails until it maps), plus the field families.
- `RuleSetRealPassTests` (contract, real ffmpeg and ffprobe, skipped without them): languages and the default slot, commentary, audio order and preference mode, subtitle keep-selected with the forced and default marks, subtitle order, each metadata removal alone and all together, and the original language with its other-languages and untagged-track options, on films generated with every kind of track and tag.

## Product bugs found and fixed (each with a failing test first)
1. A file that failed for good sent "A file finished" and never "A file failed for good". A file's failure is recorded by its pass and the job still ends normally, so the alert said finished (and a file only waiting or being tried again said it too). The pass now tells the job what to alert (`JobAlert`): finished only for a file that was done, failed for good for a failure with no retry owed, nothing for a wait, a retry, a skip or a refusal.
2. "Send test" said it worked when the receiver answered 4xx or 5xx. It now says so in plain words. A refusing receiver in a real alert is logged in plain words too ("The alert ... was not delivered, and Weir will not send it again").
3. The saved subtitle order never reached a real pass or the preview (`RulesConfigFor` left `subtitle_sorters_json` out).
4. "Mark as default: third choice" acted as the first choice; the third slot is now honoured (and the named slot is found even when an earlier slot is left empty).
5. "Other metadata" on its own made every file fail its checks ("planned the track to be tagged 'eng', output is tagged 'und'"): ffmpeg's `-map_metadata -1` takes the language tags with it, and language tags are a separate choice. The command now writes the plan's languages back unless "Language tags" is on. The four golden argv cases that change are patched in `GoldenDivergences`, as the earlier deliberate changes are.

## A test-only setting
`WEIR_NOTIFICATION_STAND_IN_PORT` sends every alert's connection to that port on the same PC after the address passes the same public-address checks (the name resolves to a public address, a number is checked as written). Like `WEIR_LIBRARY_SWAP_HOLD_AT` it is refused at start when `WEIR_ENV` is production, and a value that is not a port is refused too. There was no existing allowance, and a loopback bypass in the check itself would have meant the test never ran the check. This is a new setting in the product binary, so worth a look from the owner.

## Owner decisions (found, not changed)
- **Two original-language options change nothing a pass writes.** "Keep one track per language" (`original_language_keep_only_first`) and "Use audio preferences if no match is found" (`original_language_first_if_none`) both end in the same single audio track: only the first preferred track is ever read, and a missing original falls back either way (only the wording of a note differs). "Other languages to keep" only picks a track when the original is missing, and the original language is not read at all when "Audio tracks kept" is "best of each language". The screen promises more than that. What should each do?
- **"Keep forced subtitles" and "Keep default subtitles" keep a mark, not a track.** A forced track in a language that is not listed is still removed (the golden corpus records it); the toggles only decide whether kept tracks keep their forced or default flag. The labels read as if they keep the tracks.
- The saved default for `audio_sorters_json` is the full default order, while the OpenAPI schema documents `""`.

## Not covered, and why
- The Discord shape is taken from Discord's documented webhook fields, not from a post recorded on the golden VM (off limits here), and no recording exists; none was invented. The checks hold the shape Weir writes, field for field.
- With mkvmerge present the Matroska writer is mkvmerge; this PC has only ffmpeg, so the real-pass tests ran here with the ffmpeg writer. CI installs mkvmerge and runs them with it.

## Results
Local: Core 2347, Infrastructure 2816 (14 skipped), Api 948, contract areas harness 92, system 240, libraries 280, processing 88, all passed. `dotnet build apps/server/Weir.slnx -warnaserror` clean. Register: 707 gaps, was 717 at origin/main (10 rows proved, 1 added). check-agent-docs, check-public-privacy, check-wall-clock-waits, check-contract-areas, check-no-python pass.

author: johncarmack1984
body:
Labels pitched or rotated with the map turn and foreshorten with it, but native still collides them as the screen-aligned box around the projected anchor. A variable anchor's shift is also rotated by the bearing for collision and by the pitch when drawing, so those labels collide as boxes they don't fill and get drawn off their own axes. GL JS replaced both in maplibre/maplibre-gl-js#4071 (`_projectCollisionBox`, `getShiftedAnchor`), and native never got that change.

This ports it:

- The collision box of a label with a map rotation or pitch alignment is eight samples along the label's axes, in tile units when it's pitched, projected to the screen.
- When the label is drawn, its variable-anchor shift runs along the same axes: the skew vectors for a pitched label that stays aligned with the viewport, the projected east vector for a map-rotated label that isn't pitched.
- As in GL JS, a pitched label without a variable anchor gets the shader's perspective size correction and one on a variable anchor doesn't, even with a zero shift. Icon boxes follow the text's alignment, and take the text's shift only when they're fitted to text on a variable anchor.

Screen-aligned labels collide exactly as before.

I found this working on #4533. It's on main, so it gets its own PR. It's the first of two: the next one makes symbols collide and lay out where `*-translate` puts them, the rest of #4071.

Tests:

- `text-variable-anchor/rotated-with-map`, `text-variable-anchor-offset/rotated-with-map` and `text-pitch-alignment/map-text-rotation-alignment-viewport` take GL JS's images from #4071. Main still had the earlier ones and renders them; with this change it matches GL JS's exactly.
- `text-variable-anchor/pitched-with-map` and `text-variable-anchor-offset/pitched-with-map` take GL JS's images too, allowing 0.1% for a corner label the old images had as well.

Checked:

- Full render manifests on Metal, Linux OpenGL (llvmpipe), Vulkan (lavapipe) and WebGPU (Dawn). With main's code exactly these five tests fail on Metal; with this change nothing fails but what main fails in the same Docker setup (`fill-extrusion-pattern/function-2`, `color-relief/rainbow` and `combinations/symbol-translucent--fill-translucent` on OpenGL, the last on Vulkan).
- Unit tests on Linux OpenGL, the collision, placement and symbol unit tests on Metal, and clang-tidy on `collision_index.cpp` and `placement.cpp`.
- Not in an app.

Collision of a map-aligned box now projects up to ten points instead of one.

Semver: patch. No API change. Labels pitched or rotated with the map can be placed differently.

author: gonuts-patch-worker[bot]
body:
Fixes #36

### Trigger

Bug report https://github.com/cody-raves/Gonuts/issues/36 (build `unknown`, Minecraft ``): Hive: per-account order/auction slot settings revert to 18 on both accounts

### Root cause

Tuning treats a setting as "this client's own" only if the key already happens to appear in doughbay-local.json (plus the hard-coded reports.auto_critical). The slot counts slots.max and orders.bid_slots are therefore written by Tuning.set -> saveShared into the shared tuning.json, which the accounts of a hive share. Whichever client saved last — a manual change, or the automatic rank learning in MarketWatcher/AutomatedExecutionDriver that calls Tuning.set("slots.max", learned) — published its own number, and the other account picked it up on its next read (startup or pollExternalChanges), so the account on 45 silently fell back to the other's 18. SettingsCode.PER_ACCOUNT and Tuning's own javadoc already documented these as per-account, but nothing enforced it for file storage.

### Fix

Added Tuning.ACCOUNT_OWN = {"slots.max", "orders.bid_slots"} and made loadLocalFrom seed LOCAL_KEYS with it unconditionally, the same way reports.auto_critical is already seeded. saveShared then skips those keys (they are never written into the shared tuning.json) and saveLocal writes them into this client's doughbay-local.json, which wins over the shared file on every load and poll. Existing values are not lost: a number already in tuning.json is still read at startup and stands until this client next saves, at which point it is written into the client's own file. session.wind_down, although listed in SettingsCode.PER_ACCOUNT for export purposes, was deliberately left shared because its own setting text documents that accounts sharing a settings file wind down together.

### Validation

- `dev.doughbay.fabric.HiveSlotSettingsTest` fails on main (1 failing)
- `dev.doughbay.fabric.HiveSlotSettingsTest` passes with the fix
- `.\gradlew.bat build` passed (916 tests across all modules, JDK 25 toolchain for the mod)
- mod jar `doughbay-0.1.1-staffwatch+26.2.jar` version 0.1.1-staffwatch+26.2 depends on Minecraft ~26.2, entrypoint dev.doughbay.fabric.DoughBayClient, no test or smoke classes, built without smoke flags
- validated against main 0413a359df

### Why this is a draft

- triage confidence 0.72 is below 0.85

This change needs a human review before it can merge; the worker will not merge it.

author: this-is-npc
body:
## Before
- The 0.2.0 package pinned every Qt dependency to qt6-base's minor release. Built with qt6-base 6.12 and qt6-webengine 6.11, it required `qt6-webengine>=6.12`, which Arch does not have, so `pacman -U` refuses it on an up-to-date system.
- A release carried only the package and its `SHA256SUMS`. A recipe that builds from source, such as the one omarchy-pkgs keeps, had no source archive whose checksum the release states.

## After
- Each Qt module is pinned to the version it was built against (`qt6-webengine>=6.11` beside `qt6-base>=6.12`), so the package installs wherever those modules are.
- Each release also carries `omafiles-<version>.tar.gz`, the archive of the tag, named in `SHA256SUMS` beside the package. A recipe can follow releases from `SHA256SUMS` alone, without downloading anything to learn a checksum.

## Summary of changes
| Aspect | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Package | `package()` reads each `qt6-*` dependency's own installed version for its `>=` pin |
| Release | The package job archives the tagged `HEAD` with a `omafiles-<version>/` prefix, adds it to `SHA256SUMS` and uploads it with the package |
| Install script | Unchanged; a new test proves it still picks the package when the source archive is listed first |

## Files updated
- `pkgbuild/PKGBUILD`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `tests/test_install_script.py`

## Validation
| Scenario | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `mise run check` on each commit | Pass |
| Published 0.2.0 package | Its `.PKGINFO` requires `qt6-webengine>=6.12`, and the current Arch qt6-webengine is 6.11.2. A package built with the same pins failed to install in a current `archlinux` container with "unable to satisfy dependency" |
| Source archive of `v0.2.0` built alone, with a recipe in the omarchy-pkgs form (`source=` the archive, its checksum pinned, out-of-tree qmake build, this repository's file list), in the pinned `archlinux:base-devel` image | `makepkg --verifysource` passes; the package builds without the `.git` directory |
| That package with the fixed pins | Requires `qt6-webengine>=6.11` and `>=6.12` for the other modules; installs; no unresolved shared library in the five binaries; `omafiles --version` prints 0.2.0; `pacman -R` leaves nothing behind |
| `tests/test_install_script.py` | Four cases pass; loosening the package filter in `install.sh` makes the new case fail |

## Deviations
| Criterion | Deviation | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release workflow | Not run on GitHub before merge | It runs only when a release is created; the archive and checksum commands were exercised locally and in a container |

## Risks / follow-ups
- Merging this releases 0.2.1, the first package that installs on an up-to-date Arch.
- The recipe in omarchy-pkgs is not changed here; following releases there needs its own pull request with an `upstream` block naming `omafiles-{pkgver}.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS`.

body:
## What changed

**Date picker → sheet in the month picker's design**
The stock Material date range dialog is replaced by `DateRangeSheet`. It has a From | To connected pair (the end that the next tap sets is ringed), quick picks (Last 7 days, This week, Last 30/90 days, This year), the same connected `‹ October 2026 ›` stepper as the month sheet, and round day tiles: the first and last days are filled, a band joins the days between, and today is ringed. Days after the latest allowed date can't be picked. It's used by Insights, People and the transaction filter.

**Updates: a dedicated page + download notification**
- *Check for updates* (Settings) and *Check now* (Automatic updates) open a new **App update** page. The page asks GitHub when it opens, unless an update is already found, downloading or waiting.
- A download shows its progress in a notification with **Cancel**. A download the user started runs in a foreground service (`UpdateDownloadService`, type `dataSync`), so it keeps going with the app closed. When it finishes, the notification says it's ready, with **Install**.
- The *Update available* notification gets **Download**, which downloads without opening the app. Tapping any update notification opens the update page; *Install* opens it and starts the install, and Android asks for confirmation as usual.
- New permissions: `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` and `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC`.

**Linux window animation**
The motion did run (the tests show it), but nobody could see it. It scaled from 90% to 100% on Material's emphasized-decelerate curve, which covers about 75% of the movement in the first ~55 ms. A new page's first frames go to building it, so the window had already opened before it was drawn. Now pages, tabs and sheets grow from 80–85% over 340 ms on an ease-out curve, and close over 240 ms with a late fade.

**Splash**
On a cold start, "NormPix" appears letter by letter: each letter rises with a little spring, "Pix" is in the accent colour, and a tagline follows. Then the splash fades into the app, which comes forward underneath it. It waits for the data to load (up to 2.5 s). The update offer, shared drafts, reminder alerts and the lock prompt wait until it's gone. It's skipped when animations are turned off.

**Categories missing after an update**
Default categories were only seeded on first install. The 11 families added in 1ebcad9 (Personal care, Fitness, Events, Kids, Pets, Insurance, Loans & EMI, Taxes, Investments, Family support, Donations) never reached existing installs. Database version 11 adds them once, with their sub-categories. Any name already in use is skipped, so nothing is doubled or moved. Databases that were first set up with the new list are left alone, so a family the user deleted doesn't come back.

**README with app screenshots**
- `README.md` is now laid out as an app page: icon, tagline, badges, links, about, a 3×3 screenshot grid (light and dark), highlights, all features and recent changes (collapsed), install, FAQ and project structure. The build, CI, release and signing sections are kept as they were.
- The screenshots come from the real screens running on the app's **sample data**. `ReadmeScreenshots` (Robolectric, native graphics) renders Home, Activity, Budgets, Insights and Wallet in light and dark. Normal test runs skip it; `-Pscreenshots=<folder>` turns it on.
- `.github/workflows/screenshots.yml` renders them whenever the app changes. On `main` it commits them to `docs/screenshots` if they changed. For a pull request it pushes them to `readme-screenshots/<branch>` and never to the PR's own branch, so the PR's checks stay its own.

**Smaller items**
- The receipt preview no longer shows the attached picture; the editor shows it.
- The picture viewer now opens and closes in the chosen page transition style.
- The "Plans & Transactions" tab is now "Plans & Activity", and its history view is "Activity", so the pill label is no longer cut off.

## Testing
The first CI run built the release APK; two new update-page tests and one lint error failed. All three are fixed in 0c78334, and the latest CI run is the check.

New and updated tests:
- `DateRangeSheetTest`: day picking, a tap before the first day, quick picks, the latest-date cap.
- `CategoryCatalogMigrationTest`: missing families added, nothing doubled, a deleted family isn't brought back.
- `LaunchSplashTest`
- `UpdateUiTest`: the page, the Settings entry points, notification requests, Install.
- `AppUpdaterTest`: progress reporting, the "ready" notice when the app is off screen, `downloadNow()`.
- `PageTransitionsTest`: one test renamed for the new close motion.
- Label updates in the navigation tests.

author: bengschulz
body:
## Summary

Fifth and last PR of the Wind chat renderer stack (MST-16566). The Wind composer placeholder from R-1 is replaced by apollo-wind's `ChatComposer`, wired to the service as Material's input is.

- **Draft**: the composer follows the service prompt (`getPrompt` at mount, `SetPrompt` after) and writes edits back with `setPrompt`; an empty draft clears it, as in Material. `SetInputFocused` focuses the field.
- **Send**:
  - Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line; the primitive leaves IME composition alone.
  - Sending goes through the service `Request` intercept with the prompt text and the attachments, then clears the draft and the attachments.
  - Focus returns to the field after a send from the button.
  - Sending is held back during the initial skeleton load and while an attachment is still loading.
  - A parity test checks that the `Request` payload from Wind matches Material's.
- **Stop**: while a reply is awaited or streams, the send button stops it, unless `disabledFeatures.stopResponse` is set, in which case it stays a disabled send button and Enter does not send. Same as Material. The button stays filled in both states (`variant="default"`), as Material's does; the primitive's ghost stop button faded its fill out on every send and read as a flicker.
- **Attachments** (chips sized as Material's: 30px tall, at most half the row, name truncated with the full name as a tooltip only when cut off, on messages and in the composer; a sent message's attachment row is capped to the message so it scrolls inside the panel):
  - They come in through the attach button, a panel-wide `DropzoneOverlay` drop, and paste anywhere on the panel, checked against `allowedAttachments`: MIME types and their extensions, max size, and the max count minus what is already attached (`maxCount: 0` means no limit, as in Material).
  - Paste is handled by Wind with apollo-wind's `validateFiles`: it takes over the paste only when a file passes, so text pasted alongside a refused file still lands, and the refused file is named in the error.
  - While the panel cannot take files (attachments disabled, no composer, chat closing), a file dropped on it is still caught so the browser does not open it in the tab.
  - Removing a chip while the host uploads it publishes `SetAttachments` with it in `removed` and drops it from the draft; finishing the upload never brings it back, so the remove button stays available while uploading.
  - Chips use the file type icons from the message list, show as uploading while the service marks them loading, and can be removed.
  - The attach button lists the limits in a tooltip and to screen readers, as Material's does.
  - Hidden, and drops ignored, when `disabledFeatures.attachments` is set.
- **Errors and footer**:
  - The service error (error or `warn`) shows above the field as `ChatComposerError` (`role="alert"`), rendered as markdown like Material's, and dismissing it clears the error and keeps focus in the field.
  - The footer disclaimer comes from the shared `useChatLabels` at 10px, as in Material, hidden with `disabledFeatures.footer`.
- **Compact and read-only**:
  - `spacing.compactMode` sets the composer's compact density, and `spacing.promptBox` sets the textarea rows.
  - Read-only hides the composer, as R-1 already did and as Material does.

## Hoisted into `src/chat/headless`

| Helper | What it carries | Material change |
|---|---|---|
| `hooks/use-attachment-intake.ts`: `useAttachmentIntake`, `getAcceptedFileTypes` | Material's dropzone rules and messages: one file at a time when `multiple` is off, the whole batch refused when over `maxCount`, oversized and wrongly typed files named, the rest parsed and attached, the error cleared when nothing was refused. Takes neutral rejection reasons, so both react-dropzone and apollo-wind's checks feed it | `dropzone.tsx` maps react-dropzone codes onto it (its own handling removed) |
| `hooks/use-composer-send.ts`: `useComposerSend` | In-flight state, whether stop is allowed, send (ending dictation first) and stop | `chat-input.tsx` submit uses it |
| `hooks/use-attachment-intake.ts`: `checkAttachmentFiles` | Picked files checked as the drop targets check them: type by MIME or extension, size, then the count left | `chat-input-actions.tsx` attach button now validates types, size and count through it and the intake hook, like the dropzone (its size message is now the dropzone's) |
| `hooks/use-attachment-limits.ts`: `useAttachmentLimits` | The attach limits text (max files, max size, allowed types) | `chat-input-actions.tsx` tooltip and screen-reader description |

## Storybook

`pnpm storybook:design`, then **Apollo React / Chat / Playground**, **Compare renderers**:

- **Attachments** (chips sized as Material's: 30px tall, at most half the row, name truncated with the full name as a tooltip only when cut off, on messages and in the composer; a sent message's attachment row is capped to the message so it scrolls inside the panel): a user turn with files, then a draft with an attachment placed in both composers through `setPrompt`. Attach more with the button, by dropping files on the panel, or by pasting.
- **Error** and **Warning**: the alert above the composer, with markdown and a dismiss button.
- **`autoReply`** `echo` or `stream`: send from either composer. The message mirrors to the other chat and both reply. Stop while streaming, or turn on `disableStopResponse` to see a disabled send button instead.
- **`compactMode`**: the compact composer.
- **`disableAttachments`**, **`disableFooter`**, **`inputPlaceholder`** and **`footerDisclaimer`**.

## Tests

- `vitest --run src/chat src/material/components/ap-chat src/material/components/ap-tool-call`: 47 files, 266 tests pass. New tests cover:
  - the intake rules: accepted plus named rejections, the whole batch refused when over the count, one file at a time, the accept list;
  - the composer:
    - Enter and Shift+Enter;
    - focus after send;
    - following the service prompt;
    - stop, and stop disabled;
    - the error alert as markdown, with warn and dismiss;
    - picked files sent with the prompt;
    - an oversized file named;
    - drop and paste on the panel;
    - attachments disabled;
    - compact and the footer;
  - the `Request` payload parity test against Material.
- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- **Known gap (W-10)**: apollo-wind's `DropzoneOverlay` takes a single hint string, so Wind's drop overlay cannot list the max count, size and types as Material's does. Composer chips also take no title or tooltip from the primitive, so the truncation tooltip is a native `title`.
- `biome check` on touched files: clean.
- New strings, in `en.json` only: `input.label` ("Message", the field's accessible name) and `input.error.dismiss` ("Dismiss"). Everything else reuses Material's ids with Material's source messages.

## Stack

1. R-1 Wind shell: #1371
2. R-2 message list: #1372
3. R-3 markdown renderer: #1375
4. R-4 tool-call and tree renderers: #1376
5. **R-5 composer: this PR**

author: vortiago
body:
## What changes

Before: a scene that sets an `AtlasTexture` on `light_projector`, `area_texture`, `PointLight2D.texture` or a `Decal` texture, or a `PlaneMesh` on `CSGMesh3D.mesh`, gets no diagnostic.

After: the new `resource-type-excluded-by-hint` file diagnostic warns on each node property whose reference resolves to a class its `PROPERTY_HINT_RESOURCE_TYPE` hint excludes with a `-` prefix. The message names the type, the declaring class and property, and the hint.

The editor erases the exact excluded name from the classes it offers (`editor_resource_picker.cpp:827-833`), and the setter keeps the value, so the value is outside the UI hint: a warning (ADR-0032). Godot 4.6.3 confirms it: a scene with an `AtlasTexture` on `OmniLight3D.light_projector` loads, keeps the texture and prints the `light_3d.cpp:212` warning.

How:
- `pnpm nodes:base-types` writes the seven excluding slots of the 4.6.3 captures, and any nearer declaration of such a slot, to `godot/classdb/resourceTypeExclusions.generated.ts`. The linter reads this small table, not the full ClassDB property table, which would add 246 KB to the CLI bundle.
- `godot/classdb/resourceTypeHint.ts` is the one parse of a hint string. It imports nothing, so the generator, `acceptedResourceTypes` and the linter all use it.
- `godot/classdb/excludingHint.ts` finds a slot's excluding hint through `findInClassChain`.
- `godot/classdb/uncataloguedProperties.ts` holds the five 4.7.2 `AreaLight3D` rows the pinned ClassDB lacks. Hover and completion read them too, and a test drops them once the captures hold the class.
- The new fixture `unit-area-light-atlas-texture.tscn` carries the warning. It and `unit-decal-atlas-texture.tscn`, whose AtlasTexture and CanvasTexture decals now warn, are allowlisted in `fixtureLint.test.ts`.
- `clearedResourceSlot.test.ts` reads a value bound by a loop over `Object.entries` as every key, and a row checks that `null` and an absent slot agree for the new sweep.
- The seven comparison sheets of the affected nodes name the warning.

## How you checked it

- `pnpm test:unit`, `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm type-check:tests`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm check:bundle-size`, and the pre-push checks.
- The linter over all of `scenes/` reports the new warning only on the two fixtures above.

Closes #731

author: xalcker
body:
Fase 6 de Xalcker/retrorecomp#59 ([docs/PLAN.md](docs/PLAN.md)): el juego recompilado en el navegador y en Android. No necesita cambios en retrorecomp: usa `web/` y `android/` de `shared/` tal cual.

## Qué cambia

- **El proyecto generado** lleva `platform/web.mk`, `platform/shell.html` y `platform/android/` (embebidos como en los otros cuatro). Su `Makefile` define `make web` y `make apk`.
  - La copia de la ROM lleva la extensión del juego (`rom.sms` o `rom.gg`), así el runtime elige el modelo igual que en el escritorio.
  - `LEEME.txt` explica cómo usarlos.
- **El mando en pantalla** ya venía en la ventana desde la fase 3 (`player_touch.h`): la cruz, 1, 2 y, arriba, la Pausa (Master System) o el Start (Game Gear).
- **`make webtest` y `make apktest`** recompilan la ROM mínima (`mkcontrato --minima`) y arman su proyecto. Si no hay Emscripten o SDK, usan Docker con las imágenes fijas de `shared/`. Los dos corren en el CI de Linux.
- **`make test`** comprueba que el proyecto lleve `make web` y `make apk`, y que un `.gg` dé `rom.gg`.
- **`PAGE_SIZE` pasa a llamarse `SMS_PAGE_SIZE`.** En Android esa macro ya es el tamaño de página de la memoria, y el clang del NDK avisaba que se redefinía. Si un encabezado del sistema se incluía después de `sms.h`, el mapper habría usado 4096.
- **PLAN, ARQUITECTURA y README** con la fase 6.

## Probado (macOS, con Docker)

- **`make webtest` y `make apktest`** pasan con la ROM mínima y con el juego del contrato. La APK trae `libmain.so` para arm64-v8a y x86_64, y el NDK no da ningún aviso.
- **Dragon Blaster recompilado en el navegador** (Chrome): carga la ROM con `?rom=` y se puede jugar. Con el tamaño de un teléfono, al tocar la pantalla aparece el mando.
- **`make test`** completo (71 pruebas) y **`golden.sh`**, igual en los 21 casos.

Sin probar: la APK instalada en un teléfono o en el emulador de Android (solo se comprobó que se arma).

body:
## Resumen de cambios

Este PR atiende la revisión de seguridad solicitada para roles administrativos y el endurecimiento perimetral del importador de productos en Excel.

### 1. Hardening de Roles Administrativos (Fail-Closed)
- **Fail-Closed en `normalizeAdminRole`**: Devuelve `AdminRole | null`. Cualquier rol desconocido, nulo, vacío o con casing incorrecto devuelve `null` (sin acceso).
- **Control perimetral en proxy**: `src/proxy.ts` redirige a `/admin/login` y elimina las cookies de sesión si el rol es inválido.
- **Resolución activa desde BD con caché**: `src/server/services/admin-role.service.ts` consulta el rol actual en tiempo real en la base de datos (con caché corta en memoria de máx 60s) para que cualquier degradación de privilegios surta efecto de inmediato.
- **Sesiones antiguas**: Se resuelve el rol activo desde la BD por `userId`. Si no existe o falla, se niega el acceso.
- **`scripts/create-admin.ts`**: Exige la variable `ADMIN_ROLE` explícita y valida contra los roles conocidos.
- **Migración aditiva**: `20261015180000_admin_user_default_role_inventory_operator` para establecer el default de `AdminUser.role` a `INVENTORY_OPERATOR` sin tocar registros existentes.

### 2. Endurecimiento de Seguridad en Importador Excel
- **SheetJS 0.20.3 fijada desde CDN oficial**: Reemplazo de `xlsx@0.18.5` vulnerable (CVE-2023-30533, CVE-2024-22363) por la versión corregida `0.20.3` con hash de integridad SHA-512 verificado y bloqueado en `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
- **Validación previa a memoria**: `validateImportFile` valida tamaño (máx 2 MB), extensión estricta (`.xlsx`, rechaza `.xlsm`, `.xls`, etc.) y tipo MIME compatible **antes** de llamar a `file.arrayBuffer()`.
- **Protección contra Zip Bomb**: Uso de `fflate` para inspeccionar los tamaños descomprimidos declarados en el directorio central sin descomprimir el archivo. Rechaza elementos > 20 MB o total > 50 MB.
- **Límites de contenido**: Lectura exclusiva de la primera hoja (`sheets: 0`), máximo 5.000 filas de datos (sin truncar en silencio), máximo 40 columnas y 5.000 caracteres por celda.
- **Prevención de Prototype Pollution**: Construcción de registros con `Object.create(null)` e ignorando claves peligrosas (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`), protegiendo también `matchHeader`.
- **Auditoría CI**: Paso en `.github/workflows/ci.yml` con `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high`.

### Verificación y Calidad
- [x] `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` (0 errores)
- [x] `pnpm lint` (0 errores, 0 warnings)
- [x] `pnpm test` (144 suites pasadas, 1.211 tests pasados)
- [x] Cobertura global > 80% (services > 92%, product-import.service > 95%)

andy-esch
body:
## Outcome

Make the sport registry's input vocabulary explicit while preserving today's Strava categorization and public config response. The internal version-2.0 registry places existing inclusion/exclusion lists under `mappings["strava.sport_type"]`; Go and Python support only that vocabulary. Category keys, metadata, stored values and fallback/monitoring behavior stay unchanged.

The API projects the registry into the existing version-1.0 `/v1/sports/config` response, retaining `stravaTypes` and `excludedTypes` for settings, map styles and cached clients. The drift checker consumes the new internal structure, and docs describe the vocabulary/provenance distinction. OpenAPI now documents the endpoint's existing wrapper and metadata accurately.

## Compatibility and validation

A frozen pre-change config checks the complete public response and every existing forward/reverse Strava mapping. Python verifies memberships/exclusions, TypeScript validates the shared public contract, and HTTP tests check the legacy fields without exposing internal mappings.

- `just sync-schemas` and `just verify-schemas` — passed.
- `just test` against a disposable PostGIS database with all 15 migrations — 746 Python tests passed (one existing xfail), all three Go modules passed, 2,270 web tests passed.
- `just lint` and `just typecheck` — passed.
- Focused Pants config/checker lint, check and test — passed with its golangci-lint skipped; native Go lint passed separately.
- Scoped Markdown lint and `git diff --check` — passed.

The optional Pants Go HTTP target still has shared-module archive failures reproduced on clean main. Its pinned golangci-lint also predates Go 1.27 support. Those independent tooling problems are outside this refactor; CI's native Go quality path passes. The disposable database and baseline checkout were removed after verification.

## Adversarial review

Independent review checked every existing mapping and metadata value, runtime consumers, packaging and docs. A compiler-valid mapping mutation was caught by the frozen-fixture regression. Review fixes preserve explicit empty chart-interval overrides and emit `excludedTypes: []` when the optional registry list is omitted; permanent regressions failed before these fixes and pass after them. The package schema example and endpoint reference are updated. Independent re-review found no remaining actionable issues in the fixes.

One small presentation change remains: Go sorts category keys, and the current activity/chart chips inherit that order. A tracked set previously displayed as Cycling, Running, Hiking, Yoga now appears as Cycling, Hiking, Running, Yoga. The projection keeps standard JSON encoding; a deliberate UI ordering policy is a separate follow-up.

Validation of the fixes passed through `just`: config/sports/activities Go race tests and native lint, Pants config lint/check/test with the known linter skip, schema verification and scoped docs lint. Independent review also passed 146 focused frontend tests, TypeScript checking, and Python config/monitor tests and quality checks. The full integration suite listed above was not repeated for these Go projection/doc fixes.

author: yeraze
body:
Fixes #5824

## Problem
"Show MQTT/Bridge Messages" was one browser-global localStorage key (`showMqttMessages`). Flipping it on one source flipped it everywhere, and a fresh or private browser reset it to hidden.

Note: the issue says "Show MQTT Nodes" is already per source. It isn't: it's per user on the server (`user_map_preferences` has no `sourceId`). This PR makes the message toggle truly per user **and** per source, as decided with the maintainer.

## Change
- **Migration 205** adds `user_map_preferences.show_mqtt_messages_by_source` (TEXT, JSON `{ sourceId: boolean }`) on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. Idempotent via the shared helpers.
- **`POST /api/user/map-preferences`** accepts `{ showMqttMessages, sourceId }` and updates only that source's entry (read-modify-write). It returns 400 for a non-boolean value or a missing `sourceId`, and 404 for an unknown source, so the map cannot grow without bound. **GET** returns `showMqttMessagesBySource`.
- **`UIContext`**:
  - Reads a per-source local cache (`showMqttMessages:<sourceId>`), falling back to the old global key so nobody loses their setting on upgrade.
  - Applies the server value when it loads.
  - Saves each toggle both locally and to the server. Anonymous users keep the local cache.
  - A toggle made before the server read returns is not overwritten.

## Mesh impact
None. This is a display preference only; it sends no packets, notifications or timers.

## Tests
- Migration 205: adds the column, idempotent, existing rows read NULL.
- Schema maps the column on all three backends; `parseBooleanMap` handles malformed input.
- Route (real harness): per-source isolation, survives other preference saves, empty map by default, 400/404 cases.
- `UIContext` (jsdom, mocked API): per-source cache, legacy fallback, server wins, local kept when server has no entry, save payload, a slow server read doesn't undo a toggle.
- Full Vitest suite: 33,007 passed, 0 failed (PostgreSQL and MySQL suites skipped locally; CI covers them). `tsc` (client and server) clean; `lint:ci` OK.

No UI change beyond persistence, so no screenshot.

Style application repeatedly runs wildcard matching for literal rules, incompatible anchored prefixes, equal compatibility fields and another WindowID. This batch reduces that work and fixes a parser defect that dropped WindowID when Name preceded it.

- Prepare literal/universal selector metadata once per immutable rule.
- Reject incompatible anchored prefixes before the existing wildcard matcher.
- Match equal resource/class/title values once per lookup.
- Reject a mismatched WindowID before string work.
- Enforce the existing Name/WindowID conjunction in both documented orders.

Ordered traversal, wildcard semantics, configuration syntax and update/grab barriers are preserved. Rule metadata owns no pointers; window strings are borrowed only within one synchronous operation. The new unit checks 799776 differential cases. Paired actual-core controls cover matching costs, precedence, UseStyle/merge/removal lifetimes and existing geometry/update ordering. No universal elapsed-speedup claim is made.

All four affected matching/filter/core/update checks pass ten compiler/feature profiles across six targets. Core/update probes pass four BSD default X servers; scoped sanitizer coverage passes four affected entries. Original full runs pass 1967/1976 standard and 433/433 optional entries. Nine fresh stages validate 135 code/88 catalog identities; staged geometry passes 18 invocations/126 cases. Portable checks pass 166 with eleven explicit native-Meson skips. The two affected manuals render and their new examples are readable at 80 columns; formatter lint limitations remain explicit in the report.

Native-CPU/hardware/release coverage remains separate; VESA #93 stays deferred.

Five substantive improvements share one frozen checkpoint and one broad matrix run. ## O que mudou

- Opções `ckanext.mpb.*` declaradas no plugin e expostas no `.env.example` como `CKANEXT__MPB__*`.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md`: as pipelines autenticam com token de API do usuário de serviço, gerado por sysadmin e entregue pelo armazenamento de segredos.
- Testes do comando e das permissões do usuário de serviço; fixtures de leitura do `.env.example` movidas para `conftest.py`.

## Motivo
Completa a atividade "Configurar autenticação, autorização e plugins necessários ao escopo": com as permissões restritas do #12, as pipelines precisam de um usuário com papel definido para publicar, sem privilégios de sysadmin.

## Como validar
- CI: job `Extension and API tests`.
- Local: copiar o bloco `# Portal organization and pipeline service user` do `.env.example` para o `.env`, rodar `bin/compose up -d --build --wait` e conferir no log `Usuário mpb-pipelines é editor da organização movimento-pela-base.`
- Opcional: `bin/ckan user token add mpb-pipelines teste`, publicar um dataset com `owner_org=movimento-pela-base` usando o token e depois revogá-lo com `bin/ckan user token revoke <id>`.

body:
# 笔记 / 画板 / 导图落盘临时件不再固定同名：两处同时存不再扑空

## 变更摘要

- **问题**：`book_notes._write_json` / `_write_text`、`board._write_json` / `_write_bytes`、
  `mindmap._write_json` 都把临时件写死成 `path + ".tmp"`，而这三条保存路**都没走
  `ui_server._WRITE_LOCK`**，后端又是 `ThreadingHTTPServer`：
  - `/api/mindmap` 的保存与 AI 画图任务线都会调 `mindmap.save_map`，同一本书被两处同时存；
  - `/api/board` 的保存与导出（或同一块板的两次保存）可以同时进来；
  - `/api/mynotes` 的自动保存与 `/api/mynotes/export` 各写一份。

  两个写手同时进来时，先收尾的那个 `os.replace` 把共用的临时件整个搬走，后一个轮到自己
  那一句时临时件已不在 —— 抛 `FileNotFoundError`，界面看到「保存失败」，可前一笔其实已经
  落盘；反过来后开的那个也可能把前一份截断，两份内容交织着顶成正式文件。
- **收口**：临时件名统一改成「进程号 + 一小串随机」（`<名>.<pid>.<rand>.tmp`），与
  `ui_server._write_json` / `_write_bytes` 同一把尺子。写失败时先把临时件收干净再抛，
  旧档始终完整（`book_notes` 原先没有这层清理，一并补上）。
- **purge 同步**：`board.delete_board(purge=True)` 连新的唯一临时名与旧的固定名
  `b1.json.tmp` 一起收（被强杀留下的那一份只有磁盘看得见），且不碰别的板的临时件。
- 涉及文件：`board.py`、`book_notes.py`、`mindmap.py`，新增门禁
  `tests/check_write_tmp_unique.py` 并登记进 `tests/run_all.sh`。

改动规模：4 个文件、`+67 / -12` 行（不含新增的门禁套件内容），未新增依赖、未动锁文件 /
依赖清单 / `.github/` / 密钥。

## 验证情况

- **新门禁** `tests/check_write_tmp_unique.py`（42 条断言，全部通过），钉四面 + 一条旁证：
  - A：四个写口每次的临时件名都不一样、带本进程号、以 `.tmp` 收尾，写完目录无残件；
  - B：对照 —— 两个写手共用固定临时件名时，后一个 `os.replace` 当场
    `FileNotFoundError`（证明这道闸不是空转）；
  - C：写入失败照旧抛，临时件收干净，旧档逐字节不动；
  - D：画板 purge 把旧固定名与新的唯一临时名都收走，且不碰别的板；
  - E：四个线程并发存，无写手抛异常、无 `.tmp` 残件、最后落地那份解得动。
- **非空转取证**：把 `board.py` / `book_notes.py` / `mindmap.py` 临时 stash 回改前版本，
  同一条门禁报 11 条红，正是 `FileNotFoundError: ... notes.json.tmp -> notes.json` 这一形状；
  改后 42/42 通过。
- **全量门禁**：在仓库内新建 `.venv` 并装好 `requirements.txt`（playwright / feedparser /
  genanki / pypdf / yt-dlp）后，`bash tests/run_all.sh --fast` 输出
  **静态门禁：通过 176 项，失败 0 项**（第九轮基线 175 项，本次 +1 为新增套件）。
- 相关既有套件单独复跑均绿：`check_board_store`、`check_mindmap_store`、
  `check_notes_surrogate`、`check_board`、`check_mindmap`、`check_gate_wiring`。

## 已知问题

- 没有改任何既有测试或断言；`tests/run_all.sh` 只新增了一行登记（`check_gate_wiring`
  要求新建套件必须挂进门禁）。
- 唯一临时名带来的一个已知代价：进程被 `SIGKILL`（不是异常、不走 `except`）时，会留下
  一个孤儿 `.tmp`，不会被下次写入复用。画板那条有 purge 兜底，笔记 / 导图目录里目前没有
  主动清扫这些残件的口子；`sync._finished_file` 按后缀排除它们，不会上云，但会占盘。这是与

author: commanderx-code
body:
Roadmap item 5; completes v0.4.0 and sets the workspace version to 0.4.0, so the release after this merges is **v0.4.0**.

**Checks** (`helixforge-engine/src/doctor.rs`), read-only, each a `Diagnosis` with an id, health (OK, notice, problem), summary, evidence, advice, and a repair or a catalog entry where one is supported:
- Network: a default route in `/proc/net/route`.
- DNS: a lookup of github.com with a 5-second limit; the name servers as evidence; repair restarts systemd-resolved or NetworkManager, whichever is active. Skipped when offline.
- Services: `systemctl --failed` for the system and the user, one diagnosis per unit with its last journal lines; repair restarts that unit.
- Graphics: each PCI display controller's driver from sysfs; none in use is a problem, nouveau a notice; the Nvidia drivers entry (Arch) or the general GPU drivers entry addresses them.
- Package database: a pacman lock with no pacman, paru, yay, pamac or packagekitd running (repair removes it; while one runs, a notice); unfinished `dpkg --audit` (repair `dpkg --configure -a`).
- Home permissions: the home folder, and items in `~`, `~/.config`, `~/.local/share`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.cache`, owned by root; repair `chown -R` back to the user for exactly those paths.
- Boot: each installed kernel's initramfs (Arch by package base, Debian and Fedora by version); repair with mkinitcpio, dracut-rebuild, update-initramfs or dracut, whichever exists. A GRUB configuration without a generated menu (repair `grub-mkconfig`/`grub2-mkconfig`). The EFI partition's room.
- Disk space on `/`; repair clears package caches (paccache plus a journal vacuum, `apt-get clean`, `dnf clean packages`).

Machine access goes through a `System` trait: `Here` for the machine, `Fake` for tests. Repairs are commands of quoted words, run as a one-step plan with their own confirmation.

**Menu**: Helix Doctor (sidebar and the dashboard's Run System Doctor) opens the checks, run on a background thread, with the area's reports (Machine Summary, System Diagnostics, System Report) listed below them. `Enter` shows a check's evidence and what to do, or runs a report; `f` runs the repair or the entry; `r` checks again. The title column fits the longest title.

**Command line**: `helixforge doctor` prints every check with evidence for the ones that are not OK; `helixforge doctor --repair <id> [--dry-run] [--yes]`.

On this machine every check is OK except one: `~/.local/share/Shelly` belongs to root.

**Tests**: every check against made-up machines in its healthy and broken forms, including a quoted path; the menu screen's evidence, repair confirmation and reports; Distributions runs `helixforge doctor` on Arch, Debian, Ubuntu and Fedora and refuses an unknown repair.

author: pyflat-jr
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets both widgets show devices that other providers publish to Macro Deck's battery catalog (SDK beta.17, `IIntegrationContext.Batteries`), such as the phones from the built-in ADB integration, next to this plugin's own devices.

- **Picker:** the widget's device list shows this plugin's devices first, then every catalog device from another provider, labelled `device - provider`. This plugin's own catalog entries are filtered out by the id it published.
- **Rows:** a picked external device is drawn like our own devices, with level, charging state, time to full and our icon for its kind. A disconnected device shows as stale.
- **Storage:** a widget stores an external device by its catalog id (`provider:id`). The colon keeps those ids from ever clashing with our own device ids.
- **Existing widgets:** an empty selection still means this plugin's devices only, so existing widgets don't gain rows.
- **Widgets only:** external devices get no `battery_<id>_*` variables, no events and no trend.
- **Row keys:** a widget element key can't contain a colon, so external rows are keyed by a short SHA-256 hash of the catalog id (`ExternalBatteryDevices.RowKey`). A test opens a real widget session to cover this.
- **Live updates:** the host drops a context `Changed` handler on every re-initialization, and widget sessions stay open across that. So the integration re-subscribes in `InitializeAsync` and raises its own `BatteryCatalogChanged`, which the sessions listen to.
- **Mapping back:** headphones become our headset icon, laptop becomes the system icon, and watch and unknown kinds become other. `NotCharging` reads as Full at 100 % and Unknown below, matching our macOS and Linux sources.
- **Docs:** README, AGENTS.md and the `sourceIds` description in the widget data schema are updated. There is one new string, `Widgets.Config.Devices.External`.

## Why

- After a reboot the dashboard crash-looped under systemd (restart counter 39). The stored Gmail token had been revoked, so `gmail_auth.interactive_auth` asked for a callback URL. With no console attached, `input()` raised `EOFError` and the process exited. The screen kept showing the last frame from before the crash, so the Claude and Codex numbers looked wrong.

author: greeng3
body:
The feature this fork was for. Previously every duplicate in a group could be marked **except** the group's representative (the first row, `group.ref`), which was auto-chosen and force-kept — so the survivor was picked by happenstance. Now the user chooses which file to keep.

### Behavior
- **The representative is markable** like any other member; you pick the survivor by leaving one unmarked.
- **Reference-folder files stay protected.** `dupe.is_ref` (files from user-designated reference folders) remain unmarkable — only the *arbitrary* group representative becomes markable.
- **A group can never be fully marked.** `mark_toggle` refuses to mark the last unmarked member, so at least one survivor always remains (no way to delete every copy). The sole remaining survivor's checkbox is disabled via a new `Results.can_mark()`.
- **Bulk ops keep the representative as survivor.** `mark_all`/`mark_invert` act on non-representative dupes only (they can no longer use mark-inversion, which would now mark representatives too). Markable totals use `_counts_as_markable` so the stat line is unchanged.
- **Groups are visually separated** by alternating per-group background shading (`QPalette.AlternateBase`), driven by a new `DupeRow.is_group_odd`.

### Tests
New core tests: representative is markable, last-survivor guard, reference-folder files stay unmarkable, `mark_all` keeps representatives, group-parity shading, and representative-row markability. Full suite: **520 core/hscommon pass**, **3 GUI tests pass**, pre-commit clean.

### Worth a human eye
- This changes a core safety/UX contract of dupeGuru, so please sanity-check the marking logic.
- The visual result — alternating shading + the disabled checkbox on the survivor — is best confirmed with a **manual click-through of a real scan** (the automated GUI test can't reach a populated results table, as noted in the PyQt6 PR).

Closes #15

1. **Lean Hardened Runtime** (`runtimes/python/3.12/wolfi/Dockerfile`):
   - Non-root execution via numeric `USER 1001:1001`.
   - Tamper-resistant filesystem with `umask 022`, root-owned `/app` (`0755`), and restricted state directories (`/var/lib/app`, `/var/cache/app` at `0750`).
   - Lean virtual environment created with `python3.12 -m venv --without-pip /opt/venv`, removing `pip` and build tools from the production runtime.
   - Standard OCI and build metadata labels.
2. **Dev / Builder Image** (`runtimes/python/3.12/wolfi-dev/Dockerfile`):
   - Includes Python 3.12 along with `py3.12-pip`, `py3.12-setuptools`, and `py3.12-wheel`.
   - Pre-configures `/home/appuser`, `/app`, and `/opt/venv` owned by `1001:1001` to enable non-root package builds in multi-stage Dockerfiles.
3. **Workflow Support** (`.github/workflows/runtime-build-publish.yml` and `.github/workflows/validate.yml`):
   - Added automated detection of `-dev` variants.
   - Generates tags for runtime (`:3.12`, `:latest`, `:3.12-bXX-YYYY.MM`) and dev (`:3.12-dev`, `:latest-dev`, `:3.12-dev-bXX-YYYY.MM`).
   - Passes OCI build args (`IMAGE_VERSION`, `VCS_REF`, `SOURCE_URL`, `BUILD_LABEL`).
   - Adds functional test assertions verifying the presence of `pip` in dev images and the absence of `pip` in production runtime images.

## Validation Executed
- **Hadolint**: Passed on both Dockerfiles with zero errors.
- **Workflow YAML & Action Pinning**: Validated YAML syntax and verified all third-party GitHub Actions are pinned to full 40-character commit SHAs.
- **Local Container Build & Verification**: Built both images locally; verified `pip` presence in the dev image and `pip` absence in the runtime image.
- **Multi-Stage Application Build**: Verified an end-to-end multi-stage build using `wolfi-dev` to install dependencies into `/opt/venv`, copying the venv into `wolfi` runtime, and executing as non-root user `1001:1001`.

## CI & Publishing Impact
- Opening this PR triggers the `PR Validation` workflow (`validate.yml`) for static analysis, local Docker build, functional tests, and Trivy scan.
- No external image publication will occur until this PR is merged to `main`.

author: nicolas-peiffer
body:
#### Proposed Changes ####

**RSA-PSS options are checked before they reach the token.**
- A negative `PSSOptions.SaltLength` other than the `Auto` and `EqualsHash` sentinels went to
  pkcs11-go's `NewPSSParams`, which panics on a negative salt. So `Sign` panicked instead of
  returning an error. It is now an error wrapping `errUnsupportedRSAOptions`, as crypto/rsa
  makes it.
- An explicit salt longer than the modulus can carry is `rsa.ErrMessageTooLong`, as in
  crypto/rsa.
- A digest whose length is not the hash's size is an error, as on the PKCS#1 v1.5 path, instead
  of being left to the token.
- The resolution moves into `pssSaltLength`, which can be tested without a token.

**HMAC.**
- `hmacInfos` listed SHA-384 with a 64-byte block, so `BlockSize()` was wrong. It is 128 bytes.
- `NewHMAC` accepted any `_GENERAL` output length. Zero made every `Sum` panic on the empty MAC,
  and a negative length reached the token as a huge `CK_ULONG`. Lengths outside 1 to the hash's
  full size are now rejected with `errInvalidMACLength`, before a session is taken.

#### Types of Changes ####

Bugfix.

#### Verification ####

- `go vet` and `golangci-lint` (v2.14.0, repo config): 0 issues.
- The full suite passes on SoftHSM2 2.6.1.

#### Testing ####

- New PSS subtests in `testRsaSigningPSS`, run for every hash and for both token and native keys:
  `NegativeSaltLength`, `OversizedSalt`, `WrongDigestLength`. Each asserts an error and no panic.
- `TestPSSSaltLength` covers the salt resolution without a token, including keys found without a
  public half.
- `TestHmacInfoSizesMatchDigests` now checks every table entry's size, block size and `_GENERAL`
  flag against Go's own hash implementations. That catches the SHA-384 block size, and would have
  caught the earlier MD5 size bug.
- `TestNewHMACRejectsInvalidLength` needs no token.

#### Linked Issues ####

None.

#### User-Facing Change ####
```release-note
RSA-PSS Sign returns an error instead of panicking for a negative SaltLength, and rejects
oversized salts and wrong-length digests as crypto/rsa does. HMAC: BlockSize for SHA-384 is
128, and NewHMAC rejects _GENERAL output lengths outside 1..full size.
```

#### Further Comments ####

The commit is signed with Claude's SSH signing key and authored as
`Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`. It has no `Signed-off-by` trailer: the DCO sign-off is the
maintainer's to give. The Eclipse ECA check will not match that author email, so this needs
re-authoring or a squash-merge under a maintainer's identity.

author: jameskermode
body:
### Problem

A float32 bundle gets float32 *absolute* positions, so a model that forms a pair vector as `x_j - x_i` rounds it to about ulp(|x|). That error grows with distance from the origin, whatever the pair's length: about 1e-5 at 100 length units, 1e-4 at 1000. For a well-conditioned float32 model at scale this is the dominant force error.

Measured with an ACE silicon potential on an RTX A4500 (lammps-jax float32 bundle against a float64 reference):

| box | relative force error |
|---|---|
| 43 Å | 2.3e-5 |
| 87 Å | 3.3e-5 |
| 174 Å | 5.7e-5 |

The same evaluator with float64 displacements gives 1.9e-5 at every size. KOKKOS ML-PACE in `mixed`/`single` precision shows the same growth; there `x` is `KK_FLOAT`, so presumably LAMMPS itself holds positions in float.

### Change

- **`export_model(split_positions=True)`** (float32 only) appends a `positions_lo[max_atoms, 3]` input after the box. The pack kernel fills it with the rounding residual `x - float32(x)`, formed from LAMMPS's double positions. The model receives it as `graph.positions_lo`.
- **`lammps_jax.export.pair_vectors(positions, graph, i, j)`** returns `(hi_j - hi_i) + (lo_j - lo_i)`.
  - For atoms within a cutoff and away from the origin, `hi_j - hi_i` is exact (Sterbenz), so the vector is accurate to about an ulp of itself.
  - The program stays float32, which matters on GPUs with little fp64 throughput.
  - Gradients flow through `positions` as before.
  - With no split (or a duck-typed graph) it is the plain gathered difference.
- **Built-in models:** the EAM evaluators (analytic, setfl energy and edge-force), MACE and the LJ example now use `pair_vectors`. Models that ignore the residual are unchanged.
- **Format tag:** a `"+split-positions"` suffix, so an older plugin rejects the bundle instead of calling the program one input short. The loader also checks that the tag and the contract flag agree, and that the bundle is float32.
- **Example:** `examples/export_model.py --split-positions`.

The residual carries information only when LAMMPS stores positions in double (`KOKKOS_PREC=double`, the default and what the plugin builds against today); the README notes this.

### Tests

- `tests/test_export.py`:
  - ABI arity with and without the box;
  - the format tag and contract key;
  - float64 rejection;
  - `pair_vectors` equal to the plain difference without a split;
  - emulated forces 1000 units from the origin: plain float32 error above 1e-5, split below 2e-6.
- `tests/test_lammps.py`: a new deck, `eam_far_static`, is the EAM static deck translated about 1700 units from the origin.
  - The translation uses `change_box ... remap` after `displace_atoms random`, whose per-atom seeding from coordinates would otherwise give different configurations per decomposition.
  - The new static case `eam_far_split_static` passes the 1/2-rank and dense float64 checks.
  - `test_split_positions_far_box` compares it with the plain bundle: max force error against dense float64 is 5.5e-5 plain (over `MAX_DENSE_FORCE_ERROR` = 5e-5) and 1.5e-7 split.

Local results (moriarty, RTX A4500, LAMMPS develop of 25 Sep 2026, jax 0.11.2):
- Unit suite on CPU: 89 passed.
- `test_lammps.py`: 25 passed, 3 skipped.
- The only failures are the Pallas cases, which fail the same way on `main` here. Their export path refuses jaxlib > 0.10.1.

author: arturomanzoli
body:
**Problem:**

- Saving any transforming function (dragging or adding a point of interest, a point of interest synced from another operator, saving a function on the Data Lake page) cleared every transforming-function value for up to a second while they were rebuilt.
- A joystick event inside that window sent MANUAL_CONTROL with the throttle at 0, which is full down on ArduSub, and it stayed there until the next joystick event.

**Fix:**

- Saving a function keeps the current value of every function whose expression did not change; only the edited one starts empty and re-evaluates, as before (`src/libs/actions/data-lake-transformations.ts:251`).
- Rebuilt functions are evaluated right away instead of 1000 ms later, so an edited axis output has a value before the next joystick event (`src/libs/actions/data-lake-transformations.ts:160`).

**Test plan:**

- [ ] In Cockpit Standalone with a DualSense controller and a disarmed ArduSub vehicle, keep the throttle at neutral, drag a point of interest on the map and move the right stick right away: MANUAL_CONTROL `z` in BlueOS's MAVLink Inspector stays at 500.
- [ ] Repeat by adding a point of interest, and by saving a user function in Settings > Data Lake: `z` stays at 500.
- [ ] Edit the "Axis Z Output" expression in Settings > Data Lake (append ` * 1`) and move the right stick right after saving: `z` keeps following the throttle stick.
- [ ] With two points of interest on the map, drag one: the other stays put and the dragged one lands where it was dropped.
- [ ] Reload Cockpit: the joystick axes and the points of interest behave as before.

**Checks:**

- Reproduced in Cockpit Lite on master: the next joystick event after any of those saves sent `z` = 0 (5 of 5 runs), and `z` stayed 0 after the output came back until another event. With this branch, `z` stays 500 at every point from 0 to 1100 ms after a save.

Closes #3226

author: myst1ck
body:
## Summary

Review-hardening fixes plus a module split of the two monolithic API files. 13 commits on top of `a206388`.

**Hardening fixes (new)**
- Clamp negative item quantity to zero — a negative parsed count inverted the decrement-on-use / delete-at-zero invariant.
- Refuse to guess an unparseable schema version — raise `SchemaCorruptError` instead of migrating or rebuilding a database of unknown format.
- Keep negative damage totals (`[DAMAGE:1d6-100]`) from healing — damage never restores HP.
- Strip `class_concept` fence escapes before prompt interpolation (missing placeholder name let user text escape into instruction position).
- Clamp item tooltip position inside the viewport (max-first clamping for over-wide tooltips).
- Guard item actions against in-flight turns — bidirectional race with the turn's state snapshot.
- Surface transcript load failures instead of silently rendering a phantom line.

**Earlier review sweep on this branch**
- Isolate CORS tests from the dev database; close backend races/SSRF gap/probe ordering; surface frontend failures and guard busy states; drop unused api client exports; remove duplicate inventory chips from the sheet.

**Refactor**
- Split `backend/src/open_tavern/api/routes.py` (937 lines) into `api/routes/` + `guards.py` / `llm.py` / `runtime.py`.
- Split `frontend/src/api.ts` (527 lines) into `frontend/src/api/` modules.
- Extraction hardening: LLM error text is sanitized in 502 responses, `X-Base-Url` requires a caller-supplied `X-API-Key` (the server key never reaches a caller-chosen host), and lifespan shutdown releases the executor, storage, and state cache. SETUP.md documents the BYO-key rule.

## Test status
- backend: `uv run --extra dev pytest` — **392 passed**
- backend: `uv run --extra dev ruff check .` — clean
- frontend: `pnpm build` (tsc + vite + PWA) — clean
- frontend: `pnpm lint` — clean

## UI notes
No visual redesign. Behavior-only: item tooltip stays inside the viewport when wider than it; item actions and turn submission disable while the other is in flight; transcript load errors show in the play view.

## Integration note — merge conflicts expected
Branch is based on `a206388`; `main` has since gained 22 commits including backend features that touch the files this PR splits (`api/routes.py`, `frontend/src/api.ts`): DM narration style presets, player turn kinds, keyless local models, OpenRouter base-URL mapping. A test merge against current `main` conflicts in `backend/src/open_tavern/api/routes.py` and `backend/tests/test_client.py`. Merging needs main's additions ported into the new module layout (`api/routes/*`, `api/*` client modules) — not a plain conflict resolution.

Closes #243

## Conflicts

All six conflicts come from upstream `81493efb7` "chore: change product branding from Alpha to Beta (#20032)". Upstream changed the stage label on the same lines where the fork replaced the `T3 Code` base name with `T3 Hermes`. Each hunk keeps the fork's base name and identity and takes upstream's new stage label:

| File | Fork side | Upstream side | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/package.json` | `productName: "T3 Hermes (Alpha)"` | `"T3 Code (Beta)"` | `"T3 Hermes (Beta)"` |
| `apps/desktop/scripts/electron-launcher.mjs` | `T3 Hermes (Dev)` / `T3 Hermes (Alpha)` | `T3 Code (Dev)` / `T3 Code (Beta)` | `T3 Hermes (Dev)` / `T3 Hermes (Beta)`. The fork's `com.nateweav.t3hermes` bundle IDs and `assets/hermes` icons on neighbouring lines merged cleanly and are unchanged. |
| `apps/desktop/src/app/DesktopAppIdentity.test.ts` | `T3 Hermes Alpha` / `T3 Hermes (Alpha)` | `T3 Code Beta` / `T3 Code (Beta)` | `T3 Hermes Beta` / `T3 Hermes (Beta)`, matching `DesktopEnvironment.ts`, which now resolves `Beta` |
| `apps/desktop/src/app/DesktopPreReadyPlatform.test.ts` | `Name=T3 Hermes (Alpha)` | `Name=T3 Code (Beta)` | `Name=T3 Hermes (Beta)`. The `com.nateweav.T3Hermes.desktop` assertion is kept. |
| `apps/web/index.html` | `<title>T3 Hermes (Alpha)</title>` | `<title>T3 Code (Beta)</title>` | `<title>T3 Hermes (Beta)</title>` |
| `scripts/build-desktop-artifact.test.ts` (2 hunks) | `T3 Hermes (Alpha)` / `T3 Hermes (Nightly)`; DMG `T3 Hermes (Alpha) 1.2.3 Installer` | `resolveDesktopProductName("0.1.0")` → `T3 Code (Beta)`; DMG `T3 Code (Beta) …` | Upstream's `0.1.0` input with `T3 Hermes (Beta)` / `T3 Hermes (Nightly)`; DMG `T3 Hermes (Beta) 1.2.3 Installer` |

These upstream changes merged cleanly with no manual edits: `DesktopEnvironment.ts`, `branding.ts`, mobile `BrandMark.tsx`/`mobileBranding.ts`, contracts `DesktopAppStageLabel` (now includes `Beta`), and `docs/operations/release.md`.

Left unchanged on purpose: the desktop user-data **legacy** profile name `T3 Hermes (Alpha)` in `DesktopUserData.ts` (and its tests). Other test fixtures that still say `(Alpha)` (`DesktopLinuxUrlHandler`, `DesktopPreReadyFileSystem`, `branding.test.ts`) are also left alone, as upstream left them.

No Hermes functionality was touched. The provider, ACP, text generation, panels, usage, and the other FORK.md rows are outside this diff. Besides the six conflict resolutions, the merge commit changes only files that upstream changed.

## 第 13 步 13b — 策略引擎：`ubos-authz` 嵌入 Cedar，内核全部执行点接入（DEC-073）

### 做了什么
- **新 crate `crates/ubos-authz`**：嵌入 `cedar-policy` 4.13（DEC-065，工作区锁定）；由类注册表生成实体模型（DSN-DVM-802）：`UBOS::User`（处于其 `Role` 中）、`VAE`、`Branch`（kind）、`Class`，以及 `UBOS::Model::<类名>` 每个业务类一个实体类型，属性只含 policy-visible 字段（分级 `public`/`internal` 的标量字段）加 `class`/`slug`/`branch`/`state`；动作 = STD-ISA-005 的授权动作 + 模型中声明的端口权限 + `query`/`merge`/`approve`/`export`；上下文 = STD-LGS-031 的决策上下文（principal_kind、channel、vae、branch_kind、role、auth_level）。策略解析、按 schema 校验（严格模式）、编译集、决策函数。

body:
## What this adds (render-ops only; nothing dispatched)

Owner direction, relayed by PM on Issue #6 (6202060028): restore `sportsassets-db` from `basic_4gb` to its prior plan, `4c-16g`. It must be a targeted change, not a reset, a recreate or a Blueprint sync.

- **`db-plan-set` [R99]**, modelled on `db-recover-storage`. Every gate refuses with "nothing was sent".
  - **Inputs:** `confirm=DO`; `service=sportsassets-db` only; `arg` must be exactly `4c-16g` (the one allow-listed value).
  - **Which database:** resolved by name, which must match exactly one database, and its id must match a pinned sha256. The id is never taken from input and never printed.
  - **Preconditions:** plan `basic_4gb`, status `available`, `not_suspended`. Because the plan must read `basic_4gb`, a second dispatch after a restore is refused.
  - **The change:** ONE `PATCH /postgres/{id}` with body exactly `{"plan":"4c-16g"}`, never retried.
    - A 4xx is final.
    - A 5xx or no response is INDETERMINATE: the arm only watches, and does not resend.
  - **The watch:** a 15 s timeline, at most 80 reads and 20 min. It stops on `recovery_failed` or a suspension.
  - **The report:** BEFORE and AFTER records from an allow-list of fields. Every other field is compared, unchanged or CHANGED, values not printed, and any CHANGED field fails the run.
- **`db-metrics` [R100]**, read-only. The database's CPU, memory, connections and disk series, with ids and IPs masked. Neither existing action could read current database metrics.

## Why not a Blueprint sync or PR #133

- Every record puts the Blueprint on `claude/session-njaewf`, whose render.yaml still declares `plan: basic-4gb`.
- PR #133 targets `claude/release-api`, so merging it neither changes the database nor stops a re-sync.
- A sync also re-applies declared env literals, including those on the owner-operated SAM service.
- An API PATCH on this Blueprint-managed database is proven: `db-recover-storage`, 2026-10-11, HTTP 200.

## Tests

- New `backend/tests/test_render_ops_db_plan_set.py`: **65 passed**. It runs the bash arms against stubbed Render calls. It covers:
  - every gate, every refusal and the impostor id;
  - exactly one write, with the exact body;
  - the timeline;
  - 4xx, 5xx and no-response paths;
  - the read bound;
  - recovery_failed and suspension stops;
  - other-field change detection;
  - redaction;
  - mutation controls: a widened body and a widened allow-list are both caught.
- All 53 render-ops / `workflow_source` test files: head 1075 passed / 19 failed / 67 skipped, against base `34dd479a` 1011 / 19 / 67. The 19 failures are the same tests on both, already failing on the base (`sql` preset ordering pins). The change adds nothing to that list.
- `scripts/check_workflows.py .`: 60/60 workflows pass.

## Expected effect when dispatched (not part of this PR)

- Render documents a few minutes of unavailability for a database without high availability.
- PAPER pauses until the ext_pinnacle writer lease is re-taken: about 13–17 min typical, up to about 20.
- Storage stays 75 GB. No credential, service, env var, branch or Blueprint change. No rollback or recreate.

This is a draft and is not to be merged. The arm runs from this branch ref.

author: dajiaohuang
body:
## Problem

The README advertises Angular 19, but its Universal integration still instructs importing removed transfer-state modules and a legacy module-map loader. The section labelled “Standalone Example” is actually another NgModule declaration. The two loader snippets also fail strict TypeScript checking because `Observable.create` leaves `observer` implicitly `any`; the transfer-state keys describe numbers although SVG text is stored.

Separately, the callback description says the SVG is already in the DOM. `setSvg` actually calls the callback before appending the clone and inserts the callback's returned element. The import package for `inject`/`signal` is also misspelled.

## Change

- Use the existing module/provider APIs for Angular 19 server configuration, with an actual standalone configuration example.
- Keep filesystem imports server-only, type the Observable/string transfer data, and describe the old external Universal project as historical rather than current setup instructions.
- Correct the callback timing/arguments/return value and the Angular core import name.

No library runtime changes or new Angular-version compatibility claim.

## Validation

Against Angular 19.2.25 and RxJS 6.6.7:
- Original loader snippets: strict TypeScript fails with TS7006 for both observers. Revised loader and integration snippets compile under strict TypeScript with application-specific scaffolding and the built library.
- Bundled Node SSR fixtures render a synthetic local SVG using the documented filesystem loader through module and standalone registration; SVG text is transferred, and the browser loader reuses it without requesting HTTP again.
- Production library build passes on this branch.

The SSR fixture is bundled with esbuild: direct Node ESM execution with the repository's RxJS 6 dependencies encounters directory-import resolution errors. Browser hydration, deployed applications, earlier/later Angular versions and upstream CI were not tested. The external example site/project was not fetched or modified.

author: bedatty
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #908, from looking at the live comment on #906.

The alert block described the situation in prose, so you had to read it to know what it was. Now a 💥 sits in an `##` heading inside the block, which makes the state legible from the PR timeline before anyone opens anything.

```
> [!IMPORTANT]
> ## 💥 Breaking change detected
>
> **This pull request needs a decision.** Merging it makes the next release a
> **major** version — often deliberate, so this just asks someone to confirm it.
```

The table gains marks on the three rows that matter, so it can be scanned instead of read:

| | |
|:--|:--|
| 💥 **Breaking commit** | … |
| 👤 **Who can decide** | … |
| ⬜ **Author acknowledgement** | missing *(✅ when present)* |

And each state now gets the alert that fits it, instead of a plain heading:

| State | Alert | Mark |
|---|---|---|
| waiting | `[!IMPORTANT]` | 💥 Breaking change detected |
| approved | `[!NOTE]` | ✅ Breaking change approved |
| rejected | `[!CAUTION]` | ⛔ Breaking change rejected |
| unresolved | `[!WARNING]` | 💥 decision not recorded |

Colour and icon come from GitHub's own alert rendering; the emoji says what the block is about. `CAUTION` is reserved for the rejection, since that is the only state where something was actually taken away — the pull request was closed.

## Type of Change

- [x] `feat`: New workflow or new input/output/step in an existing workflow

## Breaking Changes

None. Presentation only; no input, output or job name changes.

## Testing

- [x] YAML syntax validated locally
- [ ] Triggered a real workflow run on a caller repository using `@this-branch` or the beta tag
- [x] Verified all existing inputs still work with default values
- [x] Confirmed no secrets or tokens are printed in logs
- [x] Checked that unrelated workflows are not affected

All four states rendered locally from the composite's own shell body and read end to end. `actionlint`, `composite-schema` and `typos` clean; 72 wiring tests, one new pinning each state to its alert and mark.

**Caller repo / workflow run:** the comment this replaces is live on #906.

body:
GitHub stays the project's home; the maintainer's self-hosted GitLab holds a copy, set up the same way as the homelab stack repos.

- `.gitlab-ci.yml`: a scheduled `mirror` job fetches `main` and the tags from GitHub and pushes them to GitLab, fast-forward only (a commit made on GitLab stops the mirror instead of being overwritten), with a project access token in the masked, protected `MIRROR_TOKEN` CI/CD variable. The mirror repo is bare, so the fetch into `main` works wherever `init.defaultBranch=main`. Every commit that arrives gets the daemon-free part of "Dashboards + config": `compose-config` (the five compose invocations, same env as ci.yml), `checks` (ruff, ruff format, yamllint, pytest + coverage floor, `check_dashboards.py`, then `promql_tests.py`, whose output goes as an artifact to) `promtool` (config, web-config, PromQL tests), `alloy-fmt`, `blackbox-config`, `hadolint`, `actionlint`. Images pinned by tag and digest (the same pins as ci.yml and the Dockerfiles), bumped by hand.
- Stays GitHub-only: the image builds and the Grafana boot test (they need a daemon), the Loki config check (its image has no shell, which a GitLab job needs) and the snmp_exporter one (ci.yml runs it unpinned).
- Two Argus-specific differences: `check_dashboards.py` and the tests run `git ls-files`, which the slim Python image lacks, so the `checks` job installs `git` from Debian's signed archive; and ci.yml's hadolint image is `FROM scratch` with no shell, so the GitLab job uses the same release's `-alpine` variant (also hadolint 2.15.1), pinned by digest. The forbidden patterns come from an `ARGUS_FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS` CI/CD variable on GitLab, as from the repo secret on GitHub; without it the check still runs, with its warning.
- Docs: CHANGELOG, CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING, GOVERNANCE (token row, forbidden-patterns row), docs/architecture.md, docs/dependencies.md.

Checked locally: each GitLab job run in its pinned image against a clone of this branch (compose-config ok; checks ok: ruff, yamllint, 204 tests at 100 % coverage, check_dashboards with the forbidden patterns loaded, 16 PromQL test files; promtool, alloy-fmt, blackbox-config, hadolint, actionlint ok), and alloy-fmt, hadolint, blackbox-config and promtool each fail on a broken input; the mirror script in the pinned `alpine/git` image against bare repos (first push with tags, no-op, fast-forward, diverged refused). author: tvanepps
body:
Proposes a 2x `funder_recognition` multiplier on `time_weight` for members who add the Protocol Guild funder table to their GitHub profile README.

**Why:** While the leaderboards on our website, Dune dashboard, and tweets are a good start for donor recognition, we should try to increase the visibility footprint. This will help to maintain momentum on the funding flywheel. Member profile READMEs are visible wherever members commit, review, and open PRs across Ethereum's repos.

**Changes to `docs/01-membership.md`:**
- `time_weight` = `SQRT`((`start_date` - `months_inactive`) * `full_or_part_time`) * `funder_recognition`
- new component 5. `funder_recognition`: 2.0x with the table, 1.0x without
- PG Ops maintains the table and sends quarterly PRs to each member; the table is checked at each quarterly membership update, and the multiplier drops off the following quarter if it is removed

**Examples:** [github.com/protocolguild](https://github.com/protocolguild) (org profile) and [github.com/tvanepps](https://github.com/tvanepps) (member profile).

Also open to something visually smaller in the readme, eg. a bulleted list:

> - **Funding Distributed**: ⭐ EigenLayer, ⭐ Ether.fi, ⭐ Taiko Labs, Arbitrum DAO, LayerZero, Lido DAO, Uniswap DAO, ENS DAO, Moloch DAO, Nouns DAO
> - **Funding Remaining**: ⭐ Ether.fi, LayerZero, ⭐ EigenLayer, ⭐ Aztec, ⭐ Aligned Layer, Starknet, ⭐ Taiko Labs, Octant, Delivery at Dawn, ⭐ Puffer
> - **Recent Donations**: wagumi.eth, ⭐ Aligned Layer, Cosmic Signature, 0x969e...f4f4, 0x67ee...fde1, Octant, 0x512a...3d66, TheDAO, 0xc647...83ba, 0x799d...ae39

Since the pool is fixed, the effect depends on how much total weight opts in: at 10% opt-in, participating members get 1.82x their plain time-weight share and others 0.91x; at 100% opt-in, shares return to plain time-weighting. As previously discussed, this also has the benefit of injecting some need-weighting into the allocation. Future iterations of this policy can consider higher multipliers for teams, given they are higher visibility.

Proposed to go live in the Q4 November update.
