author: srozov
body:
## Problem

A workflow that must apply the same step to every item of a list known only at run time (one review per document, per record, per repository) could only loop inside one agent task. One session then accumulated every item's context, one failing item failed the whole task and every item ran again, and every view showed a single task. Closes #29.

## Approach

A task can declare `map: { over, key, concurrency }`:

```yaml
  review:
    executor: reviewer
    dependsOn: [list]
    map: { over: $tasks.list.output.docs, key: id, concurrency: 3 }
    inputs: { doc: $item }
    prompt: |
      Review the document in your inputs.
```

- **Each item is an ordinary attempt** of the task, tagged with its `item` key, so launching, settling, transcripts, interactions, cancellation and `outputSchema` work per item without new machinery.
- **The task keeps one attempt of its own per round.** Every existing rule keyed on a task's latest attempt (dependencies, reruns, resume, `when`, run status) sees that attempt as the task, unchanged.
- **One place starts items:** the scheduler starts items in list order into free slots, the next one whenever one ends, and settles the task's attempt once no item is active or waiting.
- **Rounds make resume per item:** every attempt records its round (`roundId`). A plain `resume` continues the round and reruns only the items that did not complete; `resume --from` the map task, or a rerun upstream of it, starts a new round.

`src` grows by 71 lines.

## Behavior changes

- New task field `map` (all three keys required) and the `$item` / `$item.<path>` references, in a map task's `inputs` only. `over` reads a dependency's output or the run input.
- The task's output is `{ "<key>": <item output> }`. An empty list completes the task at once with `{}`.
- A list that is not a list of objects with unique non-empty string keys fails the task before any item starts: `map_items_invalid`.
- An item that fails, blocks or is cancelled leaves its siblings running. Once all items have ended, the task is `blocked` with `map_items_incomplete`.
- Attempts gain `item` and `roundId` (null on every other attempt). A map task's `attempts` lists its own attempts and its items' attempts, in creation order. Item attempts take the task's next attempt numbers, so numbers stay unique per task.
- `task.status_changed` events and interactions of an item carry its `item`.
- While a map runs, its run is `running`, even when all its active items wait for answers.
- Validation rejects `rerun` or `session: continue` on a map task and continuing a map task's session (`invalid_map`), and `$item` outside a map task's inputs. `cancel-task` on a map task's own attempt fails with `invalid_task_state`; cancel an item or the run.
- `task_runs` gains two nullable columns (`item_key`, `round_id`), added in place to an existing database. Inserts now name their columns.

## Tests and checks

- `pnpm check`, `pnpm build`: clean. `pnpm test`: 91/91, 8 of them new:
  - the issue's acceptance: 36 items, 3 at a time; one fails, the other 35 keep their results; a resume reruns only that item; the task lists all 36 item attempts; the maximum observed concurrency is exactly 3;
  - empty, invalid and guarded lists from the run input;
  - a daemon restart in the middle of a map, then a resume;
  - cancelling one item, and the rejected cancel of the map task's own attempt;
  - `resume --from` the map task (a new round);
  - an item's permission request carrying `item`;
  - the database upgrade;
  - validation.
- Two deliberate mutations (every resume starting a fresh round; one item more than `concurrency`) were each caught by the tests.
- Manual run on a throwaway daemon: a 36-item process map with `concurrency: 3` never had more than 3 items running, blocked on the one failing item, and completed after `resume` reran only that item; `watch` showed the item's events with `item`.

## Known limitations and follow-ups

- No nested maps, and no concurrency limit across tasks, runs or workflows.
- Items that have not started yet are not listed while the map runs; once it has ended, every item has an attempt.
- A client that treats a task's highest attempt number as its latest attempt will pick an item's attempt for a map task. Grouping by `item` gives the per-item view.
- **Rolling back after deploying:** a build from before this change inserts attempts without naming their columns, so it cannot write to a database this build has upgraded. Back up the database before deploying it.

author: zehang0228
body:
## Why

Live rotation (and generated rounds) could still schedule two men against two women. The gender rule in `lib/domain/gender-balance.ts` only protected a woman who was at least 150 points (one realm) below both men. When the levels were close, men against women was simply the most even split. Friends brought to an activity had no gender and always counted as men.

The club asked to avoid men against women whenever a mixed split exists, and to allow it only when both women are two realms stronger.

## What changed

- **Pairing rule:** a pair of men facing a pair of women counts as a mismatch for both women, unless both women are at least `womenPairGapPoints` (300, two realms) above both men. Mismatches outrank every other preference, so two men and two women are always split into two mixed pairs. The existing one-realm rule for a much weaker woman is unchanged. This applies everywhere `genderMismatches` is used: live rotation, round and planned generation, fixed-partner opponents.
- **Friends' gender:** a new friend must be given a gender (male or female) at signup, stored as `guestGender`. Friends still have no profile. The server rejects a new friend without one.
- **Correcting it:** the registrant, the activity organiser or an administrator can change it with the new `guestGender` command, from a new 改性别 button in the activity's friend list. Friends added before this have no gender; the list opens and shows how many still need one, since they count as men until filled in.

## Tests

- New gender-rule cases: even levels, a 299 vs 300 gap, either side, and two mixed pairs.
- Two men and two women of similar level are split into mixed pairs by round/planned grouping (20 seeds) and by live rotation; without the rule the men would be paired.
- A friend's `guestGender` is used for pairing.
- Signup requires a gender and leaves no orphan friend on rejection. `guestGender` permissions cover the registrant, an admin, another member (403) and a non-friend.
- The form asks for gender for new friends only. UI tests cover the gender prompt and form.
- With the old rule, the three new pairing tests fail.
- `npm run verify` passed locally: 903 unit tests, integration and UI tests, and the production build.

author: osamafelfel
body:
A stored developer key needs evidence that the provider accepted it for the current approved definition. This adds an internal validator for the existing OpenAI/Anthropic cloud formats. It sends one fixed one-token request and issues an owner/model/fingerprint-bound verification only after fresh definition checks. It also supplies a transaction-scoped current-definition check for the next storage slice.

An owned Python worker receives the key through stdin, discards output and caps the provider response at 64 KiB. Its provider-exchange wall deadline includes DNS and response reading; timeout kills and reaps the worker. Redirects, retries and proxies are disabled. Management reads receive no provider secret and use one five-second socket timeout each, not a total wall deadline. HTTPS is required, with an explicit loopback-only HTTP option for synthetic fixtures. Unknown provider parameters/policy envelopes fail before key contact.

No HTTP/CLI admission, storage write or inference dispatch is connected. Fingerprint persistence, account-removal cleanup and the exact protected native publication envelope remain separate follow-ups. A successful check does not promise future key acceptance or model quality.

Validation: 73 focused isolated checks pass, including 16 new real localhost HTTP cases for both protocols, refusal, redirects, malformed/oversized responses, outages, killed/reaped deadline cleanup and definitions changed during validation/before commit checking. Ruff, migration drift and diff checks pass; final formatting preserves identical ASTs. No paid provider, model weights, shared previews or containers were used. Native/runtime and combined full regression remain queued for the next coordinated wave. Stacked on the internal personal-choice branch; #50 remains frozen.

Additional isolated native validation at frozen #54 edb3af36d82d5d68fbcffbebfc7d9af0d8be8da6 also passed (validator source unchanged from #53): cached immutable image sha256:e7f203d6526d8c1d3968686718f3eed181d669cdc62411bcae3c042d0b285afe, network disabled, read-only root, UID 65532. Django check/migrate through 0004, three actual synthetic HTTP exchanges through the stdin worker, two-owner bound-key replacement/removal and actual 0700/0600/65532:65532 file ownership passed. Unique container cleanup confirmed. This is separate from the still-coordinated combined regression and is not a gateway-release claim.
